docs.title: Zero to Hero: the path from zero to production
docs.text:
This route takes you from an empty directory to a production-ready Django application with a WebSocket chat, Docker Compose, authentication and CI.

Each step solves one specific problem and leaves behind a working application.

docs.title: Route map
docs.text:
[0] Environment ──► [1] Hello Django ──► [2] First model ──► [3] CRUD + arch
                                                                      │
                                                                      ▼
[9] Deployment ◄── [8] Celery ◄── [7] WebSocket ◄── [6] Tests ◄── [5] Auth ◄── [4] Forms + UI

Steps 1–4 are standalone learning projects. Steps 5–9 develop notes_chat_app (the final production application).

docs.title: Route projects
docs.text:
hello_project        ← Step 1  — one view, SQLite, no models
bootstrap_notes      ← Step 2  — the first model, Django Admin
notes_project        ← Step 3  — CRUD, selectors/services, PostgreSQL
crispy_notes         ← Step 4  — ModelForm, Bootstrap 5, template inheritance
notes_chat_app       ← Steps 5–9 — auth, testing, WebSocket, Celery, Docker, CI

Each standalone project is a separate repository, not a branch of notes_chat_app. It shows only the concept needed at that step.

docs.title: Summary table of steps
docs.text: # Name Project New concept Knowledge Completion criterion 0 Environment — Python, pyenv, Docker — python -c "import django; print(django.__version__)" 1 Hello Django hello_project MTV, URLconf, HttpResponse I, II curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/ → 200 2 First model bootstrap_notes ORM, migration, Admin III a DB record through Admin 3 CRUD + arch notes_project selectors/services, PostgreSQL VI a unit TestCase passes 4 Forms + UI crispy_notes ModelForm, Bootstrap 5 IV, V a crispy form in the browser 5 Auth + security notes_chat_app IDOR, Q-filter, Groups VII the IDOR test fails without the fix and passes after it 6 Testing notes_chat_app TransactionTestCase, Selenium VIII 200+ tests green 7 WebSocket notes_chat_app Channels, Redis, ASGI IX the consumer test passes 8 Celery notes_chat_app Celery Worker, Beat, Redis broker, HTTP polling IX reminders arrive by email + toast in the browser 9 Deployment notes_chat_app Docker Compose, Nginx, CI X GitHub Actions: green

docs.title: Step 0. Environment
docs.text:
Problem: nothing runs.

What we install: Python (through pyenv), Git, Docker Desktop, VS Code + the Python extension.

Check:

python --version        # 3.12.x
docker version          # Engine: 24+
git --version           # 2.x
python -c "import django; print(django.__version__)"  # 5.2.x

New concepts: virtual environment, PATH, Docker daemon.

docs.title: Step 1. Hello Django
docs.text:
Tutorial: 01: The first Django page · In detail: README_1

Problem: how do you make a browser get a response from Python?

What we build: hello_project, an empty Django project with one view.

django-admin startproject hello_project .
python manage.py runserver

Architecture at this step:

Browser → urls.py → view function → HttpResponse

New concepts: MTV, URLconf, HttpResponse, DEBUG, INSTALLED_APPS.

Common mistakes: - ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'django': the virtual environment is not activated - Error: That port is already in use: another runserver is running

Notes Chat App: a similar structure notes_project/urls.py → notes_app/views.py, but with 15+ views instead of one.

docs.title: Step 2. The first model
docs.text:
Tutorial: 02: The first model · In detail: README_2

Problem: data disappears after the server restarts.

What we build: bootstrap_notes, a project with a Note model, migrations and Django Admin.

class Note(models.Model):
    title   = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    content = models.TextField()
    created = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

python manage.py makemigrations
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py createsuperuser

Architectural change: stateless HTTP → data is stored in SQLite between requests.

New concepts: models.Model, migration graph, __str__, ForeignKey, on_delete, Django Admin, QuerySet.

Common mistakes: - Forgetting makemigrations after changing a model - IntegrityError: NOT NULL constraint: a required field without a default

Notes Chat App: notes_app/models.py has 10 models with ForeignKey, M2M and on_delete=CASCADE / SET_NULL. SQLite is replaced by PostgreSQL starting from Step 3.

docs.title: Step 3. CRUD and architecture
docs.text:
Tutorial: 03: CRUD · In detail: README_3 · CBV: README_4

Problem: the view gets fat: ORM queries, validation and HTTP logic are mixed in one function.

What we build: notes_project, CRUD with selectors.py and services.py, PostgreSQL.

Pedagogical evolution:

def note_list(request):
    notes = Note.objects.filter(user=request.user)  # ORM in the view
    ...

# Duplicated in 5 views → we extract it:

# selectors.py
def get_notes_for_user(user):
    return Note.objects.filter(user=user)  # read only

# services.py
def create_note(user, title, content):
    return Note.objects.create(user=user, title=title, content=content)  # mutation only

Moving from SQLite → PostgreSQL:

SQLite: no full FOREIGN KEY constraints, limited concurrent writes
PostgreSQL: transactions, indexes, ON DELETE CASCADE/SET NULL, UNIQUE constraints

New concepts: PRG (Post/Redirect/Get), thin view, selector (read-only), service (mutation), get_object_or_404.

Common mistakes: - Returning a lazy QuerySet from a selector → SynchronousOnlyOperation in an async context - A mutation in a selector (a layer violation) - TypeError if the view and service parameters do not match

docs.title: Step 4. Forms and Bootstrap
docs.text:
Tutorial: 04: Templates + Bootstrap · In detail: README_5

Problem: HTML forms look bad, and validation is duplicated in the view and the template.

What we build: crispy_notes: ModelForm, crispy-forms, Bootstrap 5, a SaaS dashboard.

class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model  = Note
        fields = ['title', 'content', 'priority']

    def clean_title(self):
        title = self.cleaned_data['title']
        if len(title) < 3:
            raise ValidationError("Заголовок занадто короткий.")
        return title

Template inheritance:

templates/base.html           ← DOCTYPE, head, navbar
└── templates/layouts/dashboard.html  ← sidebar, content block
    └── notes_app/note_list.html       ← a specific page

FBV vs CBV:

FBV: explicit if request.method == 'POST': more code, but more transparent
CBV: CreateView, UpdateView: less boilerplate, but harder to debug
→ notes_chat_app chooses FBV for explicitness and flexibility with permissions

New concepts: ModelForm, clean_<field>, CSRF, {{ form|crispy }}, {% extends %}, {% block %}, {% include %}.

docs.title: Step 5. Authentication and security
docs.text:
Tutorial: 05: Auth and security · In detail: README_6

Problem: anyone can read and edit other people's notes (IDOR).

What we add to notes_chat_app:

  • @login_required: only authenticated users see notes
  • Object-level permissions: Note.user == request.user OR group
  • UserProfile (1:1 to User)
  • Group sharing: several users have shared access
  • Password reset flow

The IDOR attack and the defense:

# VULNERABLE: only login is checked, not ownership
@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)  # any note at all!
    ...

# SAFE: Q-filter by owner and group
def get_note_for_user(pk, user):
    user_groups = user.groups.all()
    return get_object_or_404(
        Note,
        Q(pk=pk) & (Q(user=user) | Q(group__in=user_groups))
    )

New concepts: request.user, login_required, sessions, UserProfile, Q objects, IDOR, AbstractBaseUser, password hashing, authenticate().

Common mistakes: - @login_required ≠ an object-level permission → IDOR - Checking note.user == request.user without accounting for group sharing

docs.title: Step 6. Testing
docs.text:
Tutorial: 06: Testing · In detail: README_7

Problem: refactoring breaks things nobody notices.

Test suite architecture:

test_models.py    — check constraints, __str__, on_delete behaviour
test_services.py  — check the return value + persistence
test_forms.py     — valid data, invalid data, custom clean_
test_views.py     — Client + force_login, status codes, redirect targets
test_consumers.py — WebsocketCommunicator + TransactionTestCase (not TestCase!)
test_selenium.py  — E2E in a real browser (StaticLiveServerTestCase)

Critical: TransactionTestCase for consumer tests:

TestCase wraps each test in a transaction → rollback after the test.
An async consumer reads the DB from a separate worker thread —
  that transaction is invisible to it → the setUp objects "disappear".
ALWAYS use TransactionTestCase for consumer tests.

Running:

# Unit + integration + consumer
docker compose run --rm web python manage.py test \
  notes_app.tests.test_models notes_app.tests.test_services \
  notes_app.tests.test_forms notes_app.tests.test_views \
  notes_app.tests.test_consumers -v 2

# Selenium E2E (requires the stack to be running)
docker compose up -d
docker compose exec web python manage.py test notes_app.tests.test_selenium -v 2

New concepts: AAA (Arrange/Act/Assert), setUp, force_login, WebsocketCommunicator, StaticLiveServerTestCase, CI YAML.

docs.title: Step 7. Async and WebSocket
docs.text:
Tutorial: 07: Async and WebSocket · In detail: README_8 · README_9

Problem: HTTP request/response is not suitable for real time: 100 clients = 100 requests/sec with polling.

Pedagogical evolution:

HTTP polling
  setInterval(() => fetch('/new-messages/'), 1000)
  → 100 clients = 100 requests/sec: inefficient

WebSocket
  → one long-lived connection
  → the server can push events without a request from the client
  → Django Channels: an ASGI handler for WS
  → Redis channel layer: broadcast to a group

The ASGI stack:

Browser WS connect
  → Nginx (proxy_pass ws://)
  → Daphne ASGI server
  → ProtocolTypeRouter (asgi.py)
  → AuthMiddlewareStack  (reads the session cookie → scope["user"])
  → URLRouter (routing.py: /ws/groups/<pk>/chat/)
  → GroupChatConsumer

Critical implementation details:

# asgi.py: get_asgi_application() BEFORE importing notes_app
django.setup() → get_asgi_application() → from notes_app.consumers import ...

# consumers.py: never call the sync ORM directly
history = await database_sync_to_async(
    lambda: list(ChatMessage.objects.filter(group=group_pk).values(...))
)()  # list() materializes the QuerySet BEFORE leaving the worker

# RedisChannelLayer (settings.py):
CHANNEL_LAYERS = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "channels_redis.core.RedisChannelLayer",
        "CONFIG": {"hosts": [REDIS_URL], "socket_timeout": None},
        #                                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
        #                     None = no timeout for idle WS
    }
}

New concepts: asyncio, coroutine, await, ASGI vs WSGI, AsyncWebsocketConsumer, channel layer, group_send, database_sync_to_async.

docs.title: Step 8. Celery and background tasks
docs.text:
Tutorial: 08: Celery and background tasks

Problem: Django cannot send an email at exactly the scheduled time: a view runs only in response to a request.

Two levels of reminders:

Email (Celery Worker)
  Celery Beat → every 60 sec → @shared_task send_reminder_notifications()
  → Reminder.filter(remind_at__lte=now, is_sent=False)
  → send_mail() → reminder.is_sent = True
  → _schedule_next() → a new Reminder if repeat_pattern ≠ none

Browser Toast (HTTP polling)
  reminders.js → every 60 sec → GET /reminders/check/
  → JsonResponse({reminders: [...]})
  → Bootstrap Toast for new ones (sessionStorage for deduplication)

Redis DB allocation:

Redis DB 0 — Django Channels channel layer (WebSocket)
Redis DB 1 — Celery broker and result backend

Docker Compose services:

celery-worker:
  command: celery -A notes_project worker -l info --concurrency=2
celery-beat:
  command: celery -A notes_project beat -l info   # exactly 1 instance!

New concepts: @shared_task, Celery Beat, broker, CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE, relativedelta, HTTP polling, Bootstrap Toast API, sessionStorage, @override_settings(EMAIL_BACKEND=...), mail.outbox.

docs.title: Step 9. Deployment and CI
docs.text:
Tutorial: 09: Deployment · In detail: README_9

Problem: the application only works locally.

The Docker Compose stack:

services:
  db:       # PostgreSQL + PostGIS
  redis:    # the channel layer for Channels
  web:      # Django (Daphne ASGI)
  nginx:    # reverse proxy, SSL termination, static files
  ngrok:    # a public HTTPS tunnel for development
  selenium: # Selenium Grid for E2E tests

Production checklist:

✓ DEBUG=False
✓ SECRET_KEY — from env, not in the code
✓ DATABASE_URL — missing → Exception (no SQLite fallback!)
✓ ALLOWED_HOSTS — specific domains
✓ Static files — through Nginx, not Django
✓ DebugExceptionMiddleware — only if DEBUG=True
✓ HTTPS — CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE

GitHub Actions CI:

jobs:
  test:       # unit + integration + consumer tests
  selenium:   # E2E in Selenium Grid

New concepts: Dockerfile, multi-service docker-compose.yml, ENTRYPOINT, Nginx proxy_pass, collectstatic, the .env file, GitHub Actions workflow.

docs.title: Architectural evolution across the whole route
docs.text: Step DB Auth Forms Tests Deploy Background process 1 SQLite (not used) — — — runserver — 2 SQLite — Admin — runserver — 3 PostgreSQL — raw HTML TestCase runserver — 4 PostgreSQL — ModelForm + crispy Form tests runserver — 5 PostgreSQL login_required + Q-filter ModelForm IDOR test runserver — 6 PostgreSQL ✓ ✓ 200+ tests runserver — 7 PostgreSQL ✓ ✓ + consumer Daphne ASGI — 8 PostgreSQL ✓ ✓ + test_tasks Daphne ASGI Celery Worker + Beat 9 PostgreSQL ✓ ✓ + Selenium Docker + Nginx + CI Celery Worker + Beat

docs.title: Tutorial 01 — My first Django project
docs.text:
This tutorial takes you from an empty folder to a full-fledged Django site with view functions, URL routing, an admin panel, and your first model.

Result: 

http://localhost:8000/        →  Hello, Django!
http://localhost:8000/about/  →  This is my first Django page!
http://localhost:8000/admin/  →  Admin panel (superuser)

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
Theory (read before the code) - 01 · HOW DJANGO HANDLES A REQUEST — from the browser to the response - 02 · PROJECT STRUCTURE — what each file means - 03 · MANAGE.PY — Django's command center - 04 · SETTINGS.PY — anatomy of the configuration - 05 · URL PATTERNS — how Django finds a view

Step-by-step implementation 1. Step 1 — Virtual environment 2. Step 2 — Install Django 3. Step 3 — Create the project 4. Step 4 — Apply migrations 5. Step 5 — Create a superuser 6. Step 6 — Create an app 7. Step 7 — Write view functions 8. Step 8 — URL routes 9. Step 9 — Check in the browser 10. Bonus — Your first model and the Django shell

docs.title: 01 · How Django handles a request
docs.text: The most important question: what happens when you type http://localhost:8000/ into the browser?

docs.title: The full Request/Response cycle
docs.text:
Browser                    runserver (manage.py)              Django
   │                              │                              │
   │  GET /about/  ───────────────►                              │
   │                              │  ProtocolTypeRouter          │
   │                              │  (WSGI or ASGI)              │
   │                              │         │                    │
   │                              │  SecurityMiddleware          │
   │                              │  SessionMiddleware           │
   │                              │  CommonMiddleware            │
   │                              │  CsrfViewMiddleware          │
   │                              │  AuthenticationMiddleware    │
   │                              │  MessageMiddleware           │
   │                              │         │                    │
   │                              │  URLconf → hello_project/urls.py
   │                              │         │                    │
   │                              │  include → hello_app/urls.py │
   │                              │         │                    │
   │                              │  path('about/', about_view)  │
   │                              │         │                    │
   │                              │  about(request)              │
   │                              │         │                    │
   │                              │  HttpResponse("This is my...")
   │                              │         │                    │
   │  ◄───────────── 200 OK  ─────│         │                    │
   │  (body: "This is my first...")                              │

docs.title: Three participants
docs.text:
URLS.PY            → "Who will respond?"   path('about/', views.about)
VIEWS.PY           → "What to respond?"    return HttpResponse("...")
TEMPLATE/RESPONSE  → "What will it look like?"   a string or HTML

A restaurant analogy: - urls.py = the host: "Table 5 — your waiter is Marko" - views.py = the cook: receives the order and prepares the dish - HttpResponse = the plate that goes back to the guest

docs.title: 02 · Project structure
docs.text:
After django-admin startproject hello_project . and startapp hello_app you will have:

./
├── manage.py               ← CLI: running the server, migrations, shell, tests
│
├── hello_project/          ← Project configuration (one for the whole project)
│   ├── __init__.py         ← Empty: makes the folder a Python package
│   ├── settings.py         ← All settings: DB, INSTALLED_APPS, TEMPLATES...
│   ├── urls.py             ← The main URLconf: includes the apps' urls.py
│   ├── wsgi.py             ← Entry point for WSGI servers (Gunicorn, uWSGI)
│   └── asgi.py             ← Entry point for ASGI servers (Uvicorn, Daphne)
│
├── hello_app/              ← An app (one of possibly several)
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── admin.py            ← Registering models in the Django Admin
│   ├── apps.py             ← AppConfig configuration
│   ├── models.py           ← Models: Python class → DB table
│   ├── views.py            ← View functions: request → response
│   ├── urls.py             ← The app's URLs (must be created by hand)
│   ├── forms.py            ← ModelForm and Form classes (must be created)
│   ├── migrations/         ← Automatically generated migration files
│   │   └── __init__.py
│   └── templates/          ← HTML templates (must be created)
│       └── hello_app/
│           └── index.html
│
└── db.sqlite3              ← The DB file (appears after migrate)

docs.title: Why are hello_project/ and hello_app/ different things?
docs.text:
hello_project/   = CONFIGURATION
  One for the whole site.
  settings.py, urls.py, wsgi.py.
  Contains no business logic.
  You rarely edit it after the initial setup.

hello_app/       = FUNCTIONALITY
  There can be several (notes_app, users_app, chat_app).
  models.py, views.py, forms.py, templates/.
  This is where all the application code lives.
  Each app = an isolated unit of functionality.

Rule: one app = one responsibility. notes_app → notes. users_app → profiles. Don't mix everything into one big app.

docs.title: 03 · manage.py
docs.text: manage.py is Django's CLI orchestrator. All interaction with the project goes through it.

docs.title: The most important commands
docs.text:
# ── Development server ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python manage.py runserver                 # http://localhost:8000/
python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8080   # a different port and host (for the network)

# ── Migrations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python manage.py makemigrations            # Generates a migration plan from models.py
python manage.py makemigrations hello_app  # Only for one app
python manage.py migrate                   # Applies all migrations to the DB
python manage.py migrate hello_app 0002    # Roll back to a specific migration
python manage.py showmigrations            # Show the state of all migrations

# ── Administration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python manage.py createsuperuser           # Create a superuser interactively
python manage.py changepassword alice      # Change a user's password

# ── Code generation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python manage.py startapp blog_app         # A new app
python manage.py startproject config .     # A new project configuration

# ── Interactive shell ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python manage.py shell                     # A Python shell with the Django context
python manage.py shell -i bpython          # Or ipython/bpython if installed

# ── SQL ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python manage.py sqlmigrate hello_app 0001 # Show the SQL that a migration will run
python manage.py dbshell                   # psql / sqlite3 shell

# ── Checks ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python manage.py check                     # Check the configuration without running
python manage.py check --deploy            # Check the production settings

# ── Tests ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python manage.py test                      # All tests
python manage.py test hello_app            # Tests of a specific app
python manage.py test hello_app.tests.test_models -v 2

# ── Static files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python manage.py collectstatic             # Collect static files into STATIC_ROOT

# ── Data ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
python manage.py dumpdata hello_app.Note   # Export data to JSON
python manage.py loaddata fixtures.json   # Import data

docs.title: How does manage.py know about your project?
docs.text:
# manage.py — the first line after the shebang:
os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'hello_project.settings')
# ↑ Tells Django where to look for settings.py
# When running in Docker, this is often overridden via an ENV variable

docs.title: 04 · settings.py
docs.text: settings.py is Django's brain. Read every setting, don't just copy it.

docs.title: The full anatomy of settings.py
docs.text:
# hello_project/settings.py

# ── Security ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SECRET_KEY = 'django-insecure-...'   # The secret for CSRF, sessions, signatures
# In production: read it from os.environ or a .env file!
# os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY') — never store it in git

DEBUG = True
# True:  detailed error pages with a traceback → ONLY in development
# False: Production → a generic error without a traceback → configure LOGGING

ALLOWED_HOSTS = []
# A list of domains that may access the site
# DEBUG=True → ALLOWED_HOSTS is not checked (localhost is always allowed)
# Production: ['example.com', 'www.example.com']
# ngrok/Docker: add their domain here or via env


# ── Installed apps ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    # Django built-ins — THE ORDER MATTERS for some operations:
    'django.contrib.admin',         # /admin/ — the admin panel
    'django.contrib.auth',          # The User model, login/logout
    'django.contrib.contenttypes',  # ContentType framework (generic relations)
    'django.contrib.sessions',      # Sessions: the django_session table
    'django.contrib.messages',      # Flash messages
    'django.contrib.staticfiles',   # Static files: /static/

    # Third-party (installed via pip):
    'django_bootstrap5',
    'crispy_forms',
    'crispy_bootstrap5',

    # Your apps — always AT THE END:
    'hello_app',
]
# If an app is listed here → Django looks for models, views, templates, static in it


# ── Middleware — the request processing chain ────────────────────────────────
MIDDLEWARE = [
    'django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware',
    # ↑ HTTPS redirect, HSTS, XSS protection headers

    'django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware',
    # ↑ Loads the session from the DB → request.session

    'django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware',
    # ↑ Adds the trailing slash, APPEND_SLASH

    'django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware',
    # ↑ Checks the CSRF token in POST requests → 403 if it is missing

    'django.contrib.auth.middleware.AuthenticationMiddleware',
    # ↑ Reads the session → sets request.user
    # IMPORTANT: after SessionMiddleware!

    'django.contrib.messages.middleware.MessageMiddleware',
    # ↑ Flash messages: messages.success(request, ...)

    'django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware',
    # ↑ X-Frame-Options: DENY → protection against clickjacking
]
# The order is critical! Middleware is called in sequence (request↓, response↑)


# ── URL configuration ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ROOT_URLCONF = 'hello_project.urls'
# Relative to DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE


# ── Templates ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TEMPLATES = [{
    'BACKEND': 'django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates',
    'DIRS': [BASE_DIR / 'templates'],  # Global templates (not in an app/)
    'APP_DIRS': True,                  # Look for templates/ in every app
    # APP_DIRS: True → django looks for hello_app/templates/hello_app/*.html
    'OPTIONS': {
        'context_processors': [
            'django.template.context_processors.debug',
            'django.template.context_processors.request',
            # ↑ request is available in the template as {{ request }}
            'django.contrib.auth.context_processors.auth',
            # ↑ {{ user }} and {{ perms }} are available in all templates
            'django.contrib.messages.context_processors.messages',
            # ↑ {{ messages }} is available in all templates
        ],
    },
}]


# ── Database ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DATABASES = {
    'default': {
        'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.sqlite3',
        'NAME': BASE_DIR / 'db.sqlite3',
    }
}
# SQLite: a single file, ideal for development, not for production
# PostgreSQL (production): ENGINE = 'django.db.backends.postgresql'


# ── Static files ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
STATIC_URL = '/static/'
# The URL prefix for static files: CSS, JS, images
# In a template: {% load static %} + {% static 'css/style.css' %}


# ── Language and time zone ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
LANGUAGE_CODE = 'uk'            # The language of the admin panel and built-in messages
TIME_ZONE = 'Europe/Kyiv'       # The time zone for DateTimeField
USE_I18N = True                 # Internationalization
USE_TZ = True                   # Store datetimes in UTC in the DB
# USE_TZ=True: datetimes in the DB are always in UTC → converted on display
# USE_TZ=False: datetimes are stored "as is" → dangerous when the TZ changes


# ── Auto primary key ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD = 'django.db.models.BigAutoField'
# BigAutoField → id: bigint (64-bit)
# AutoField     → id: int (32-bit, may overflow with billions of records)

docs.title: 05 · URL Patterns
docs.text: urls.py is the site map. Each URL leads to a specific view function.

docs.title: Anatomy of path()
docs.text:
from django.urls import path, include, re_path
from . import views

urlpatterns = [
    # path(route, view, kwargs=None, name=None)
    path('about/', views.about, name='about'),
    #      ↑          ↑               ↑
    #   URL string   callable        a unique route name
    #   (no / at the start  (a function or CBV.as_view())
    #   if included via include)
]

docs.title: Path Converters — capturing values from the URL
docs.text:
urlpatterns = [
    # <int:pk> — capture an integer
    path('notes/<int:pk>/', views.note_detail, name='note_detail'),
    # /notes/42/ → the view receives pk=42

    # <str:username> — capture a string (does not include '/')
    path('users/<str:username>/', views.user_profile, name='user_profile'),
    # /users/alice/ → the view receives username='alice'

    # <slug:slug> — only letters, digits, hyphens
    path('articles/<slug:slug>/', views.article, name='article'),
    # /articles/my-first-post/

    # <uuid:pk> — UUID format
    path('orders/<uuid:pk>/', views.order_detail, name='order_detail'),

    # <path:file_path> — includes '/'
    path('files/<path:file_path>/', views.serve_file, name='serve_file'),
    # /files/images/2026/photo.jpg → file_path='images/2026/photo.jpg'
]

docs.title: A two-level URLconf — include()
docs.text:
# hello_project/urls.py (the main one)
from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import path, include

urlpatterns = [
    path('admin/', admin.site.urls),

    # include() plugs in another app's URLconf
    path('', include('hello_app.urls', namespace='hello_app')),
    # '' → all URLs without a prefix go to hello_app.urls
    # namespace='hello_app' → for {% url 'hello_app:index' %}

    # Or with a prefix:
    path('notes/', include('hello_app.urls', namespace='hello_app')),
    # Then /notes/ + '' (in hello_app.urls) = /notes/
]

# hello_app/urls.py (the modular one)
from django.urls import path
from . import views

app_name = 'hello_app'   # ← Required when there is a namespace in include()!
# Without app_name: ImproperlyConfigured: Specifying a namespace in include() without providing an app_name

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.index, name='index'),        # ← '' here
    path('about/', views.about, name='about'),
]

docs.title: reverse() — generating URLs programmatically
docs.text:
# In a view:
from django.urls import reverse
from django.shortcuts import redirect

def some_view(request):
    # Instead of hardcoding '/notes/':
    url = reverse('hello_app:note_list')
    return redirect(url)

# Or directly:
return redirect('hello_app:note_list')

# In a template:
# {% url 'hello_app:note_detail' pk=note.pk %}
# → /notes/42/

Why reverse() instead of hardcoding /notes/? If you change the URL in urls.py, reverse() automatically generates the new URL. With a hardcoded /notes/ → you have to search and replace it across the whole codebase.

docs.title: Step 1 — Virtual environment
docs.text:
A virtual environment is an isolated Python environment. The packages you install into it do not affect other projects or the system Python.

# Create a venv in the current folder
python -m venv venv

# Activate — Linux / macOS
source venv/bin/activate

# Activate — Windows PowerShell
venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

# Activate — Windows Command Prompt
venv\Scripts\activate.bat

After activation, (venv) will appear in the terminal prompt: 

(venv) ~/projects/hello_django $

Activate it every time you open a new terminal in the project. Forgot to activate it? pip install django will install into the system Python → version conflicts.

# Deactivate (return to the system Python):
deactivate

# Check that the correct Python is being used:
which python    # macOS/Linux → should be .../venv/bin/python
where python    # Windows

docs.title: Step 2 — Install Django
docs.text:
# Upgrade pip (recommended)
python -m pip install --upgrade pip

# Install Django (the latest stable version)
pip install django

# Or a specific version:
pip install django==5.2.2

# Save the dependencies to requirements.txt
pip freeze > requirements.txt
# Contents: Django==5.2.2 (and other dependencies)

# Install from requirements.txt (for another developer):
pip install -r requirements.txt

Check the installation: 

python -m django --version
# → 5.2.2

docs.title: Python and Django compatibility
docs.text:
Python Django Note 3.10 – 3.13 5.1.x or 5.2.x A stable pair 3.14+ only 5.2+ 5.1 does not support Python 3.14 3.9 4.2.x (LTS) Old, but supported

Check: python --version

docs.title: Step 3 — Create the project
docs.text:
django-admin startproject hello_project .

The dot . at the end is required!

With the dot: hello_project/ and manage.py in the current folder ✓ Without the dot: Django will create hello_project/hello_project/ → unnecessary nesting ✗

Result: 

./
├── hello_project/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── settings.py   ← configuration
│   ├── urls.py       ← the main router
│   ├── asgi.py       ← for uvicorn/daphne
│   └── wsgi.py       ← for gunicorn
└── manage.py         ← the CLI orchestrator

docs.title: Step 4 — Apply migrations
docs.text:
python manage.py migrate

Django includes built-in apps (django.contrib.auth, django.contrib.admin, and so on). Each of them has tables in the database. migrate creates these tables in db.sqlite3.

docs.title: What exactly Django creates
docs.text:
Operations to perform:
  Apply all migrations: admin, auth, contenttypes, sessions
Running migrations:
  Applying contenttypes.0001_initial... OK        # ← Django ContentType framework
  Applying auth.0001_initial... OK                # ← auth_user, auth_group, auth_permission
  Applying admin.0001_initial... OK               # ← django_admin_log
  Applying sessions.0001_initial... OK            # ← django_session

docs.title: Tables that Django creates automatically
docs.text:
Table What it stores auth_user Users: username, password (a PBKDF2+SHA256 hash), email, is_staff, is_superuser auth_group Groups/roles: name auth_permission Permissions: name + model (add_note, change_note, delete_note, view_note) auth_user_groups M:N: user ↔ group auth_user_user_permissions M:N: user ↔ permission django_session Sessions (the sessionid cookie → a record in the DB) django_admin_log A log of actions in the admin panel (who changed what and when) django_migrations Which migrations have already been applied (so they are not repeated) django_content_type A registry of all models (for generic FKs)

Without migrate the admin panel crashes: OperationalError: no such table: auth_user

docs.title: Step 5 — Create a superuser
docs.text:
python manage.py createsuperuser

Django will ask: 

Username (leave blank to use 'niko'): admin
Email address: admin@example.com
Password:
Password (again):
Superuser created successfully.

docs.title: User types in Django
docs.text:
Superuser  → is_superuser=True, is_staff=True
             All permissions automatically.
             Bypasses permission checks.
             Access to /admin/ and all objects.

Staff user → is_staff=True, is_superuser=False
             Can log in to /admin/, but only with the assigned permissions.
             Does not see models without explicit permissions.

Regular    → is_staff=False, is_superuser=False
             An ordinary user. No access to /admin/.
             Can use the application's frontend.

docs.title: Django permissions (automatic)
docs.text:
Django automatically generates 4 permissions for each model:

hello_app.add_note      ← can create notes
hello_app.change_note   ← can edit
hello_app.delete_note   ← can delete
hello_app.view_note     ← can view

# In a template:
{% if perms.hello_app.add_note %}
    <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_create' %}">+ New</a>
{% endif %}

# In a view:
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import permission_required
@permission_required('hello_app.add_note')
def note_create(request): ...

# Checking in Python:
request.user.has_perm('hello_app.add_note')

docs.title: Step 6 — Create an app
docs.text:
python manage.py startapp hello_app

This command creates: 

hello_app/
├── __init__.py
├── admin.py        ← Registering models for the Django Admin
├── apps.py         ← HelloAppConfig — the app configuration
├── models.py       ← Models (empty)
├── tests.py        ← Tests (better turned into a tests/ package)
├── views.py        ← View functions (empty)
└── migrations/
    └── __init__.py

Register the app in hello_project/settings.py:

INSTALLED_APPS = [
    'django.contrib.admin',
    'django.contrib.auth',
    'django.contrib.contenttypes',
    'django.contrib.sessions',
    'django.contrib.messages',
    'django.contrib.staticfiles',
    'hello_app',    # ← ADD THIS LINE
]

Why do you need to register it? Django knows about an app only if it is in INSTALLED_APPS. Without that: - Django does not look for templates in hello_app/templates/ - python manage.py makemigrations ignores hello_app/models.py - The Django Admin does not know about the models from hello_app/ - management commands from hello_app/management/ are not available

docs.title: Step 7 — Write view functions
docs.text:
Open hello_app/views.py:

from django.http import HttpResponse
from django.shortcuts import render


def index(request):
    """Home page."""
    return HttpResponse("Hello, Django!")


def about(request):
    """About page."""
    return HttpResponse("This is my first Django page!")

docs.title: Anatomy of a view function
docs.text:
def index(request):
    #       ↑
    #  HttpRequest object — contains:
    #    request.method   → 'GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE'
    #    request.GET      → QueryDict: the parameters ?q=search&page=2
    #    request.POST     → QueryDict: the POST form body
    #    request.user     → the logged-in User or AnonymousUser
    #    request.session  → dict-like: the user's session
    #    request.META     → HTTP headers: REMOTE_ADDR, HTTP_HOST...
    #    request.FILES    → uploaded files
    #    request.COOKIES  → browser cookies

    return HttpResponse("Hello!")
    #         ↑
    #  HttpResponse — the response to the browser:
    #    status_code=200 (by default)
    #    content_type='text/html; charset=utf-8'
    #    body: 'Hello!'

docs.title: Response types
docs.text:
from django.http import (
    HttpResponse,            # 200 OK with any content
    HttpResponseRedirect,    # 302 Redirect
    Http404,                 # raised as an exception → 404 page
    JsonResponse,            # 200 OK with a JSON body
)
from django.shortcuts import render, redirect, get_object_or_404

# The most common ones in views.py:
return render(request, 'hello_app/index.html', {'key': value})
# → renders an HTML template with a context → 200

return redirect('hello_app:note_list')
# → 302 Redirect to a URL from reverse()

return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=42)
# → 302 Redirect with an argument

raise Http404("Not found")
# → Django returns the 404 page

note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)
# → Note.objects.get(pk=pk) but instead of DoesNotExist → Http404

docs.title: Step 8 — URL routes
docs.text:
Create a new file hello_app/urls.py:

from django.urls import path
from . import views

app_name = "hello_app"    # ← The namespace

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.index, name='index'),        # → /
    path('about/', views.about, name='about'),  # → /about/
]

Why app_name? Without it, the link {% url 'hello_app:index' %} does not work. Django raises: ImproperlyConfigured: Specifying a namespace in include() without providing an app_name

Plug it into the main hello_project/urls.py:

from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import path, include

urlpatterns = [
    path('admin/', admin.site.urls),
    path('', include('hello_app.urls', namespace='hello_app')),
    #     ↑                              ↑
    #   empty prefix →               the namespace for {% url %}
    #   hello_app URLs start
    #   right from the root /
]

docs.title: How Django finds the view for the request GET /about/
docs.text:
GET /about/
    ↓
hello_project/urls.py:
  path('', include('hello_app.urls', ...))
  → prefix '' → PASS

hello_app/urls.py:
  path('about/', views.about, name='about')
  → 'about/' == 'about/' → MATCH!

views.about(request) is called
  → HttpResponse("This is my first page...")

docs.title: The Django admin panel
docs.text:
The Django Admin is an automatically generated web interface for managing data. It is built into Django: django.contrib.admin in INSTALLED_APPS.

What you see after logging in: 

Django administration                         Logged in as: admin
  AUTHENTICATION AND AUTHORIZATION
    Groups    → add / edit groups
    Users     → all users, password changes, permissions

docs.title: 1. Describe the model in hello_app/models.py
docs.text:
from django.db import models


class Note(models.Model):
    title      = models.CharField(max_length=200, verbose_name='Title')
    content    = models.TextField(blank=True, verbose_name='Text')
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True, verbose_name='Created')
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True, verbose_name='Updated')

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title

    class Meta:
        verbose_name        = 'Note'
        verbose_name_plural = 'Notes'
        ordering            = ['-created_at']   # Newest first

docs.title: Field types and what they mean
docs.text:
# CharField — a short string, max_length is required
title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
# SQL: title VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL

# TextField — a long string, with no length limit
content = models.TextField(blank=True)
# blank=True: not required in Django forms
# SQL: content TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''

# DateTimeField — date and time
created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
# auto_now_add=True: set on CREATE, never changes
# SQL: created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()

updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)
# auto_now=True: updated on every SAVE

# BooleanField
is_pinned = models.BooleanField(default=False)
# SQL: is_pinned BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE

# IntegerField with choices
PRIORITY_CHOICES = [(1, 'Low'), (2, 'Medium'), (3, 'High')]
priority = models.SmallIntegerField(choices=PRIORITY_CHOICES, default=1)
# SQL: priority SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1

# ForeignKey — an N→1 relationship
user = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='notes')
# SQL: user_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES auth_user(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

docs.title: 2. Register it in the admin panel (hello_app/admin.py)
docs.text:
from django.contrib import admin
from .models import Note


@admin.register(Note)
class NoteAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    list_display   = ('title', 'created_at')     # Columns in the list
    search_fields  = ('title', 'content')        # Search by fields
    list_filter    = ('created_at',)             # Filters on the right
    ordering       = ('-created_at',)            # Sorting
    readonly_fields = ('created_at', 'updated_at') # Not editable

Result: http://localhost:8000/admin/hello_app/note/ — full CRUD for notes.

docs.title: 3. Create and apply a migration
docs.text:
python manage.py makemigrations

Output: 

Migrations for 'hello_app':
  hello_app/migrations/0001_initial.py
    - Create model Note


python manage.py migrate

Output: 

Operations to perform:
  Apply all migrations: admin, auth, contenttypes, hello_app, sessions
Running migrations:
  Applying hello_app.0001_initial... OK

docs.title: The two-step rule
docs.text:
# After ANY change to models.py → always two steps:
python manage.py makemigrations   # Record the plan of changes
python manage.py migrate          # Apply it to the DB

# makemigrations WITHOUT migrate:
# → the Python class exists, the DB table does not → OperationalError on the first query

docs.title: What happens between models.py and the DB
docs.text:
models.py (Python class)
    ↓ python manage.py makemigrations
migrations/0001_initial.py  (a plan of changes in the form of Python operations)
    ↓ python manage.py migrate
     ↓ sqlmigrate shows the real SQL:
CREATE TABLE "hello_app_note" (
    "id"         bigint NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY,
    "title"      varchar(200) NOT NULL,
    "content"    text NOT NULL,
    "created_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
    "updated_at" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL
);
    ↓
http://localhost:8000/admin/hello_app/note/   ← the model is now available

docs.title: 4. Django shell — ORM queries
docs.text:
python manage.py shell

from hello_app.models import Note

# CREATE — INSERT INTO
Note.objects.create(title="First note", content="Hello Django!")
Note.objects.create(title="Django ORM", content="Very powerful!")

# READ — SELECT
Note.objects.all()                          # → QuerySet [<Note: First note>, ...]
Note.objects.count()                        # → 2
Note.objects.filter(title__icontains='django')  # → QuerySet (case-insensitive)
Note.objects.get(id=1)                      # → <Note: First note> or DoesNotExist
Note.objects.first()                        # → the first object
Note.objects.order_by('-created_at')        # → sorting: newest first

# UPDATE — UPDATE SET
note = Note.objects.get(id=1)
note.title = "Changed note"
note.save()                                 # → UPDATE hello_app_note SET title=... WHERE id=1

# DELETE — DELETE FROM
note.delete()                               # → DELETE FROM hello_app_note WHERE id=1
Note.objects.filter(id__gt=5).delete()     # → Delete all with id > 5

# QuerySets are lazy:
qs = Note.objects.all()   # ← SQL IS NOT EXECUTED YET
print(qs)                  # ← Only here is the SQL executed!
# SELECT * FROM hello_app_note

# Useful lookups:
Note.objects.filter(title__icontains='first')   # icontains = case-insensitive
Note.objects.filter(title__startswith='Django')
Note.objects.filter(created_at__year=2026)
Note.objects.filter(id__in=[1, 2, 3])
Note.objects.exclude(title='secret')            # exclude = NOT

docs.title: Common mistakes

docs.title: Tutorial 02 — Bootstrap Notes: ModelForm, CRUD and Templates
docs.text:
This tutorial turns a simple Django project into a full-fledged Bootstrap 5 application with a Navbar, cards, forms and flash messages.

Result: 

http://localhost:8000/notes/           →  Notes list — Bootstrap Cards Grid
http://localhost:8000/notes/new/       →  Create form (ModelForm)
http://localhost:8000/notes/1/         →  Note detail
http://localhost:8000/notes/1/edit/    →  Edit form (instance=note)
http://localhost:8000/notes/1/delete/  →  Delete confirmation (POST only)

Prerequisites: you have completed Tutorial 01 — you have a Note model and a Django project.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
Theory (read before the code) - 01 · ModelForm — an automatic form from a model - 02 · The PRG pattern — why redirect after POST - 03 · Django Messages — flash messages - 04 · Template Inheritance — blocks and inheritance - 05 · Bootstrap 5 — Grid and components - 06 · Django Template Filters and Tags

Step-by-step implementation 1. Step 1 — Bootstrap dependencies 2. Step 2 — base.html — the base template 3. Step 3 — NoteForm (ModelForm) 4. Step 4 — CRUD views with PRG 5. Step 5 — URL routes 6. Step 6 — The list template (Card Grid) 7. Step 7 — The form template 8. Step 8 — The delete template 9. Step 9 — The detail template

docs.title: 01 · ModelForm
docs.text: ModelForm — Django automatically generates an HTML form from a Python model. One class replaces 50 lines of HTML.

docs.title: Without ModelForm vs With ModelForm
docs.text:
# ❌ WITHOUT ModelForm: you describe every field by hand
class NoteFormManual(forms.Form):
    title   = forms.CharField(max_length=200, label='Заголовок')
    content = forms.CharField(widget=forms.Textarea, required=False, label='Текст')
    # + duplication with the model — when models.py changes → you must edit here too

# ✅ WITH ModelForm: one line fields = [...]
class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model  = Note
        fields = ['title', 'content']
        # Django itself looks at Note.title (CharField(max_length=200))
        # and generates forms.CharField(max_length=200)
        # Synchronization is automatic when the model changes

docs.title: What ModelForm does automatically
docs.text:
Note model                      NoteForm generates
─────────────────────────       ────────────────────────────────────
CharField(max_length=200)   →   forms.CharField(max_length=200)
                                widget=TextInput
                                → <input type="text" maxlength="200">

TextField(blank=True)       →   forms.CharField(required=False)
                                widget=Textarea
                                → <textarea rows="10"></textarea>

SmallIntegerField(choices)  →   forms.TypedChoiceField(choices=...)
                                widget=Select
                                → <select><option>...</option></select>

BooleanField(default=False) →   forms.BooleanField(required=False)
                                widget=CheckboxInput
                                → <input type="checkbox">

ForeignKey(Notebook)        →   forms.ModelChoiceField(
                                    queryset=Notebook.objects.all())
                                widget=Select
                                → <select> with all notebooks

ManyToManyField(Tag)        →   forms.ModelMultipleChoiceField(
                                    queryset=Tag.objects.all())
                                widget=SelectMultiple

docs.title: The form cycle: GET → POST → redirect
docs.text:
def note_create(request):

    # GET request → show an empty form
    if request.method == 'POST':
        # POST request → a filled-in form

        form = NoteForm(request.POST)
        # ↑ request.POST: QueryDict {'title': ['Нотатка'], 'content': ['']}
        # NoteForm is bound to the data → bound form

        if form.is_valid():
            # is_valid() does:
            # 1. Converts strings from request.POST into Python types
            # 2. Runs the validators of each field
            # 3. Runs clean_<field>() if present
            # 4. Runs form.clean() (cross-field validation)
            # If there are errors → is_valid() = False → form.errors is filled

            note = form.save()
            # form.save() = form.instance.save()
            # Executes INSERT INTO hello_app_note (...) VALUES (...)
            # Returns the saved object

            return redirect('hello_app:note_list')
    else:
        form = NoteForm()
        # ↑ Unbound form — empty

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {'form': form})
    # If is_valid() = False → we return THE SAME form with errors
    # form.errors: {'title': ['Це поле обов\'язкове.']}
    # The template shows errors under each field

docs.title: form.save() and form.save(commit=False)
docs.text:
# form.save() — saves and returns the object
note = form.save()   # INSERT INTO + return Note instance

# form.save(commit=False) — does not save, returns an unsaved object
note = form.save(commit=False)
note.user = request.user   # ← add fields that are not in the form
note.save()                # ← now we save

# Why commit=False?
# The NoteForm form does not include the user field (protection against IDOR)
# So the view adds user = request.user manually before saving

docs.title: A form with instance — editing
docs.text:
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)

    # instance= passes an existing object into the form:
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note)
        # ↑ Bound form + existing object
        # form.save() → UPDATE instead of INSERT
    else:
        form = NoteForm(instance=note)
        # ↑ The form is filled with the current data of note

    # Without instance: form.save() always does INSERT (duplicate!)
    # With instance: form.save() → UPDATE hello_app_note SET ... WHERE id=note.id

docs.title: 02 · The PRG pattern
docs.text: POST/Redirect/Get — the standard for handling forms. Protects against duplicates on F5.

docs.title: The problem without PRG
docs.text:
User → POST /notes/new/ (create the note "Shopping")
  ↓ The view saves the note, returns 200 with a confirmation
  ↓ The browser shows the page
  ↓ The user presses F5 (refresh)
  ↓ The browser REPEATS the POST request ← PROBLEM!
  ↓ A second "Shopping" note is created!

Result: 2 identical notes.
Press F5 again → 3 notes. This is the "Double Submit" problem.

docs.title: The solution — PRG
docs.text:
User → POST /notes/new/
  ↓ The view saves the note
  ↓ The view returns 302 REDIRECT → /notes/
  ↓ The browser does GET /notes/ (follows the redirect automatically)
  ↓ The browser shows the list of notes
  ↓ F5 → repeats GET /notes/ (safe!)

Result: only one note. F5 = reloading the list.

# ✅ Correct — PRG:
def note_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = form.save()
            return redirect('hello_app:note_list')   # ← 302, not 200!
    else:
        form = NoteForm()
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {'form': form})

# ❌ Wrong — without redirect:
def note_create_bad(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = form.save()
            return render(request, 'success.html', {'note': note})
            # ↑ The browser stays on the POST URL
            # F5 → browser: "Resubmit the POST request?" → duplicate!

docs.title: 03 · Django Messages
docs.text: Flash messages are one-time messages that disappear after a single view. Ideal for "Note saved" after a redirect.

docs.title: How Messages work
docs.text:
1. POST /notes/new/
   messages.success(request, "Нотатку збережено!")
   → the message is stored in the SESSION (not in the response)
   ↓
2. redirect → GET /notes/
   template: {% for message in messages %}{{ message }}{% endfor %}
   → the message is displayed
   → the SESSION is cleared (used once!)
   ↓
3. F5 → GET /notes/ again
   messages = empty → the message is gone

docs.title: Message levels and Bootstrap classes
docs.text:
# Django levels → Bootstrap Alert classes
from django.contrib import messages

messages.debug(request, 'Налагоджувальне повідомлення')
messages.info(request, 'Інформаційне повідомлення')
messages.success(request, 'Нотатку успішно збережено!')
messages.warning(request, 'Нотатку видалено.')
messages.error(request, 'Помилка при збереженні.')

# MESSAGE_TAGS in settings.py:
from django.contrib.messages import constants as messages
MESSAGE_TAGS = {
    messages.DEBUG:   'secondary',   # → alert-secondary
    messages.INFO:    'info',        # → alert-info
    messages.SUCCESS: 'success',     # → alert-success
    messages.WARNING: 'warning',     # → alert-warning
    messages.ERROR:   'danger',      # → alert-danger (Bootstrap uses danger!)
}

docs.title: Messages in the template
docs.text:
{% if messages %}
    {% for message in messages %}
    <div class="alert alert-{{ message.tags }} alert-dismissible fade show" role="alert">
        <!--
            message.tags → 'success' / 'warning' / 'danger'
            alert-{{ message.tags }} → Bootstrap class alert-success / alert-warning...
        -->
        {{ message }}
        <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-bs-dismiss="alert">
        </button>
        <!-- data-bs-dismiss="alert": Bootstrap JS closes the alert -->
    </div>
    {% endfor %}
{% endif %}

docs.title: 04 · Template Inheritance
docs.text: A single base.html contains the Bootstrap CDN, Navbar and Footer. All other pages only fill in blocks.

docs.title: How the Django template engine processes templates
docs.text:
1. render(request, 'hello_app/note_list.html', context)

2. Django finds the template:
   APP_DIRS=True → looks in hello_app/templates/hello_app/note_list.html
   (APP_DIRS looks for templates/ in every INSTALLED_APP)

3. Encounters {% extends 'base.html' %}
   → loads base.html
   → finds all {% block name %}...{% endblock %} in base.html

4. For each block:
   → if the child template overrides it → uses the child content
   → if not → uses the base content (if any)

5. {{ variable }} → replaced with the context value
   {% tag %} → executes the template tag
   {{ var|filter }} → applies the filter

docs.title: base.html blocks and their purpose
docs.text:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="uk">
<head>
    <!-- The Bootstrap CDN is ALWAYS here -->
    <title>{% block title %}Bootstrap Notes{% endblock %}</title>
    <!--
        block title: the child template overrides it:
        {% block title %}Мої нотатки{% endblock %}
        → <title>Мої нотатки</title>
    -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="...bootstrap.min.css">
    {% block extra_css %}{% endblock %}
    <!--
        extra_css: an empty block — a child can add page-specific CSS
        For example: <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'css/editor.css' %}">
    -->
</head>
<body>
    <nav>...</nav>

    <main>
        {% block content %}{% endblock %}
        <!--
            content: the MAIN block — each page fills in its own
            base.html defines nothing here → empty by default
        -->
    </main>

    <footer>...</footer>
    <script src="...bootstrap.bundle.min.js"></script>
    {% block extra_js %}{% endblock %}
    <!--
        extra_js: a child can add page-specific JS
        for example: <script>...</script> for a Leaflet map, Chart.js, etc.
    -->
</body>
</html>

docs.title: {{ block.super }} — inheriting block content
docs.text:
{# Base template #}
{% block extra_css %}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="global-styles.css">
{% endblock %}

{# Child template #}
{% block extra_css %}
    {{ block.super }}  {# ← inserts the content from base.html #}
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="page-specific.css">
{% endblock %}

{# Result: BOTH CSS lines, not only page-specific #}

docs.title: 05 · Bootstrap 5
docs.text: Bootstrap 5 is a CSS framework. Classes → ready-made styles without writing CSS.

docs.title: Bootstrap Grid System
docs.text:
Bootstrap Grid = 12 columns in a row
Total width of columns = 12 (or less)

col-md-4 + col-md-4 + col-md-4 = 12 ✓  (3 equal columns)
col-md-6 + col-md-6 = 12 ✓              (2 equal halves)
col-md-8 + col-md-4 = 12 ✓              (sidebar layout)
col-md-12 = 12 ✓                         (full width)

Breakpoints:
  no suffix → always (from 0px)
  sm  → ≥576px   (larger phone)
  md  → ≥768px   (tablet)
  lg  → ≥992px   (laptop)
  xl  → ≥1200px  (monitor)
  xxl → ≥1400px  (large monitor)

<!-- Card Grid — responsive: 1 column → 2 → 3 -->
<div class="row row-cols-1 row-cols-md-2 row-cols-lg-3 g-4">
    <!--
        row-cols-1:    mobile      → 1 card per row
        row-cols-md-2: tablet      → 2 cards per row
        row-cols-lg-3: laptop/PC   → 3 cards per row
        g-4:           gap (spacing between cards) = 1.5rem
    -->
    {% for note in notes %}
    <div class="col">
        <div class="card h-100 shadow-sm">
            <!-- h-100: height = 100% of the row (equal cards) -->
            <!-- shadow-sm: a light shadow -->
            <div class="card-body">
                <h5 class="card-title">{{ note.title }}</h5>
                <p class="card-text text-muted">{{ note.content|truncatechars:80 }}</p>
            </div>
            <div class="card-footer">
                <!-- Actions: edit / delete -->
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>
    {% endfor %}
</div>

docs.title: Common Bootstrap classes
docs.text:
Spacing:
  m-{n}   → margin all sides    mt-3 → margin-top: 1rem
  p-{n}   → padding all sides   px-4 → padding-left+right: 1.5rem
  mb-4    → margin-bottom: 1.5rem
  gap-2   → gap between flex elements

Flex:
  d-flex                  → display: flex
  justify-content-between → space-between
  align-items-center      → vertically center
  flex-grow-1             → takes up all free space

Text:
  text-muted   → gray color
  text-center  → text-align: center
  fw-bold      → font-weight: bold
  small        → font-size: 0.875em
  display-1    → large heading

Color:
  bg-dark   → background: dark
  text-white → color: white
  bg-primary → Bootstrap blue

Buttons:
  btn btn-primary      → blue button
  btn btn-outline-secondary → outlined gray
  btn-sm               → small button
  btn-group btn-group-sm → button group

Alerts:
  alert alert-success    → green
  alert alert-warning    → yellow
  alert alert-danger     → red
  alert-dismissible      → close button
  fade show              → appearance animation

Utilities:
  shadow-sm     → shadow
  border-0      → no border
  rounded       → rounded corners
  h-100         → height: 100%
  min-vh-100    → min-height: 100vh
  overflow-auto → overflow: auto

docs.title: Sticky Footer — a technical detail
docs.text:
Problem: with little content the footer moves up and does not stay at the bottom.

Solution with Flexbox:
  body {
    display: flex;         → body = flex container
    flex-direction: column → vertical axis
    min-height: 100vh;     → at least 100% of the window height
  }
  main {
    flex-grow: 1;          → main takes up all free space between nav and footer
  }

<body class="d-flex flex-column min-vh-100">
    <nav>...</nav>
    <main class="container my-4 flex-grow-1">...</main>
    <footer>...</footer>  ← always at the bottom!
</body>

docs.title: Filters — transform values
docs.text:
{# Syntax: {{ variable|filter:argument }} #}

{{ note.title }}                      → "Дуже довга назва нотатки..."
{{ note.title|truncatechars:30 }}     → "Дуже довга назва нотатк..."

{{ note.content|truncatechars:100 }}  → the first 100 characters
{{ note.content|linebreaks }}         → \n → <br><p>
{{ note.content|safe }}               → do not escape HTML (CAREFUL: XSS)
{{ note.content|escape }}             → escape HTML (default)

{{ note.created_at }}                 → 2026-06-13 10:00:00
{{ note.created_at|date:"d.m.Y" }}   → 13.06.2026
{{ note.created_at|date:"H:i" }}      → 10:00
{{ note.created_at|timesince }}       → 5 hours ago
{{ note.created_at|naturalday }}      → today / yesterday

{{ notes|length }}                    → 42
{{ notes|first }}                     → the first element
{{ notes|last }}                      → the last element

{{ note.title|upper }}                → UPPERCASE TITLE
{{ note.title|lower }}                → lowercase title
{{ note.title|capfirst }}             → First letter capitalized

{{ note.priority|default:"не вказано" }}  → if None/False → the default
{{ note.priority|default_if_none:"—" }}   → only if None

{% load static %}
{% static 'css/style.css' %}          → /static/css/style.css

docs.text:
{# Conditions #}
{% if notes %}
    ...
{% elif archived_notes %}
    ...
{% else %}
    <p>Немає нотаток</p>
{% endif %}

{% endfor %}

{% block content %}...{% endblock %}

docs.title: Step 3 — NoteForm
docs.text:
Create hello_app/forms.py:

from django import forms
from .models import Note


class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    """
    ModelForm for Note.
    Django automatically generates fields from the model:
      title (CharField(max_length=200)) → TextInput
      content (TextField(blank=True))   → Textarea
    """

    class Meta:
        model  = Note
        fields = ['title', 'content']
        # We do NOT include: created_at (auto_now_add), updated_at (auto_now)
        # Django sets them automatically — the user should not see them

        widgets = {
            'title': forms.TextInput(attrs={
                'class':       'form-control',     # Bootstrap class
                'placeholder': 'Введіть назву...',
                'autofocus':   True,               # Cursor goes straight to this field
            }),
            'content': forms.Textarea(attrs={
                'class': 'form-control',
                'rows':  6,
                'placeholder': 'Текст нотатки...',
            }),
        }
        labels = {
            'title':   'Заголовок',
            'content': 'Зміст',
        }
        help_texts = {
            'title':   'Коротка і описова назва (до 200 символів)',
            'content': 'Основний вміст нотатки. Поле необов\'язкове.',
        }

    def clean_title(self):
        """
        A custom validator for the title field.
        clean_<field_name>() is called after the standard validators.
        """
        title = self.cleaned_data.get('title', '').strip()
        if len(title) < 3:
            raise forms.ValidationError('Заголовок має бути мінімум 3 символи.')
        return title   # ← IMPORTANT: return the cleaned value!

docs.title: Step 4 — CRUD views
docs.text:
hello_app/views.py:

from django.shortcuts import render, redirect, get_object_or_404
from django.contrib import messages

from .models import Note
from .forms import NoteForm


def index(request):
    """Home → redirect to the list."""
    return redirect('hello_app:note_list')


def note_list(request):
    """List of all notes."""
    notes = Note.objects.all()              # SELECT * FROM hello_app_note
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_list.html', {'notes': notes})


def note_detail(request, pk):
    """Detail of a single note."""
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)   # get() or 404
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_detail.html', {'note': note})


def note_create(request):
    """
    GET  → empty form
    POST → validation → saving → redirect (PRG)
    """
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = form.save()
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" успішно створено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_list')
    else:
        form = NoteForm()

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form':   form,
        'action': 'Створити',
        'title':  'Нова нотатка',
    })


def note_edit(request, pk):
    """
    GET  → form filled with the current data (instance=note)
    POST → update (UPDATE, not INSERT)
    """
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note)
        if form.is_valid():
            form.save()
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" оновлено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(instance=note)   # Fill with the current data

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form':   form,
        'note':   note,
        'action': 'Зберегти зміни',
        'title':  f'Редагувати: {note.title}',
    })


def note_delete(request, pk):
    """
    GET  → confirmation page
    POST → deletion → redirect (DELETE only via POST!)

    Why only POST?
    If DELETE worked via GET: <img src="/notes/1/delete/"> or <a href=...>
    would delete the note when the page loads (CSRF attack, search bots).
    POST requires a form with csrf_token → protected.
    """
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        title = note.title   # Save before deleting
        note.delete()
        messages.warning(request, f'Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_list')

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

docs.title: get_object_or_404 — protection against KeyError / DoesNotExist
docs.text:
# ❌ Without get_object_or_404:
note = Note.objects.get(pk=pk)   # If not found → DoesNotExist → 500 Internal Error

# ✅ With get_object_or_404:
note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)   # If not found → Http404 → 404 page

# You can filter by several fields:
note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
# → 404 if the note either does not exist or belongs to another user
# This is protection against IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference)!

docs.title: Step 5 — URL routes
docs.text:
hello_app/urls.py:

from django.urls import path
from . import views

app_name = 'hello_app'

urlpatterns = [
    path('',                        views.index,       name='index'),
    path('notes/',                  views.note_list,   name='note_list'),
    path('notes/new/',              views.note_create, name='note_create'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/',         views.note_detail, name='note_detail'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/edit/',    views.note_edit,   name='note_edit'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/delete/',  views.note_delete, name='note_delete'),
]

Important: the order notes/new/ before notes/<int:pk>/

'notes/new/' → does not match <int:pk> because 'new' is not an int → OK
'notes/42/'  → <int:pk> → pk=42 → OK

If the order were reversed:
'notes/<int:pk>/' → 'new' → int('new') → ValueError → error!
Django checks urlpatterns FROM TOP TO BOTTOM → the first match wins.
More specific patterns — at the top!

{% extends 'base.html' %}

{% block title %}{{ title }}{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
    <div class="col-12 col-md-8 col-lg-6">
        <div class="card shadow-sm">

            <div class="card-header bg-white border-bottom">
                <h1 class="h4 mb-0">
                    <i class="bi bi-journal-plus me-2"></i>{{ title }}
                </h1>
            </div>

            <div class="card-body">
                <form method="post" novalidate>
                    <!--
                        novalidate: disables browser HTML5 validation
                        → Django validates on the server (more reliable)
                        → Browser validation can be bypassed with curl/Postman
                    -->
                    {% csrf_token %}
                    <!--
                        csrf_token: REQUIRED for every POST form!
                        Django generates: <input type="hidden" name="csrfmiddlewaretoken" value="...">
                        Without it: 403 Forbidden from CsrfViewMiddleware
                    -->

                    {% for field in form %}
                    <div class="mb-3">
                        <label for="{{ field.id_for_label }}" class="form-label fw-semibold">
                            {{ field.label }}
                            {% if field.field.required %}
                            <span class="text-danger" title="Обов'язкове поле">*</span>
                            {% endif %}
                        </label>
                        {{ field }}
                        {#
                            field.widget already has class="form-control" (from the widgets in forms.py)
                            → {{ field }} generates <input class="form-control"> or <textarea ...>
                        #}

                        {% if field.help_text %}
                        <div class="form-text text-muted">{{ field.help_text }}</div>
                        {% endif %}

                        {% for error in field.errors %}
                        <div class="invalid-feedback d-block">
                            <i class="bi bi-exclamation-circle me-1"></i>{{ error }}
                        </div>
                        {% endfor %}
                    </div>
                    {% endfor %}

                    <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-4">
                        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">
                            <i class="bi bi-check-lg me-1"></i>{{ action }}
                        </button>
                        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}"
                           class="btn btn-outline-secondary">
                            <i class="bi bi-x-lg me-1"></i>Скасувати
                        </a>
                    </div>

                </form>
            </div>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

docs.title: How it all connects — the full cycle
docs.text:
CRUD operations and HTTP methods:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CREATE:  GET  /notes/new/     → note_create view → empty form
         POST /notes/new/     → form.save() → redirect → flash message
         GET  /notes/         → list with the new note + flash message

READ:    GET  /notes/         → note_list view → QuerySet → template
         GET  /notes/42/      → note_detail view → get_object_or_404 → template

UPDATE:  GET  /notes/42/edit/ → note_edit view → form with instance=note
         POST /notes/42/edit/ → form.save(instance) → UPDATE → redirect

DELETE:  GET  /notes/42/delete/  → note_delete view → confirmation
         POST /notes/42/delete/  → note.delete() → redirect → flash message
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
