docs.title: Step 7 — Architecture: Services & Selectors
docs.text:
Detailed documentation (read separately): - DJANGO_SERVICES_SELECTORS.md — the full architecture: View→Service→Selector→ORM, data flow, anti-patterns, a responsibility table - DJANGO_SELECTORS.md — an in-depth look at Selectors: CQRS-light, naming convention, QuerySet vs evaluated list, centralizing N+1 - DJANGO_SERVICES.md — an in-depth look at Services: stateless functions, @transaction.atomic, on_commit(), Celery as a transport layer

🧠 Mental model: A View is a traffic controller, not a worker. It accepts an HTTP request, delegates the work and returns a response. If a View runs all the DB queries itself, it is a "fat view", and a month later the code becomes unreadable. Selector = reading. Service = writing/changing.

📚 Why Services/Selectors: The same DB query is needed in a View, in a Celery task, in an API, in a test. Without a Selector you copy the QuerySet into 10 places. Change the business logic → 10 places to update. With a Selector → 1 function.

🌐 Architectural split: - selectors.py — ONLY reading (SELECT). No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. - services.py — ONLY writing (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE). No direct SELECTs in the View. - views.py — ONLY HTTP logic. Calls selectors and services.

❌ Common mistake: Note.objects.filter(user=user) directly in a View is a violation. All QuerySets → into selectors.

docs.title: The hello_app/selectors.py file:
docs.text:
# hello_app/selectors.py
"""
Selectors — the data READING layer.
All SELECT queries live here.
Views, Tasks, API — they all use selectors.
"""
from django.db.models import Count, Q, Prefetch
from django.utils import timezone

from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag, TodoList, TodoItem, ShoppingList, Reminder


def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False, notebook=None, tag=None, search=None):
    """
    The user's list of notes with filters.
    select_related + prefetch_related — solves the N+1 problem.
    """
    qs = Note.objects.filter(
        user=user,
        is_archived=archived
    ).select_related(
        'notebook'           # FK → JOIN (1 query instead of N)
    ).prefetch_related(
        'tags'               # M:N → a 2nd query (not N+1)
    )

    if notebook:
        qs = qs.filter(notebook=notebook)

    if tag:
        qs = qs.filter(tags=tag)

    if search:
        qs = qs.filter(
            Q(title__icontains=search) | Q(content__icontains=search)
        )

    return qs.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')


def get_note_detail(user, note_id):
    """
    Note detail — with all relationships.
    Raises Note.DoesNotExist if not found or not the owner.
    """
    return Note.objects.select_related(
        'notebook', 'user'
    ).prefetch_related(
        'tags',
        Prefetch(
            'reminders',
            queryset=Reminder.objects.filter(
                remind_at__gte=timezone.now()
            ).order_by('remind_at')
        )
    ).get(id=note_id, user=user)


def get_user_notebooks(user):
    """All notebooks with their note count."""
    return Notebook.objects.filter(user=user).annotate(
        note_count=Count('notes', filter=Q(notes__is_archived=False))
    ).order_by('-is_default', 'title')


def get_user_tags(user):
    """Tags with their note count."""
    return Tag.objects.filter(user=user).annotate(
        note_count=Count('notes')
    ).order_by('name')


def get_user_todo_lists(user):
    """To-do lists with progress."""
    return TodoList.objects.filter(
        user=user
    ).annotate(
        total_items=Count('items'),
        done_items=Count('items', filter=Q(items__is_done=True))
    ).prefetch_related('items').order_by('is_completed', '-created_at')


def get_pending_reminders():
    """For the Celery worker: reminders that need to be sent."""
    return Reminder.objects.filter(
        is_sent=False,
        remind_at__lte=timezone.now()
    ).select_related('note__user')

docs.title: The hello_app/services.py file:
docs.text:
# hello_app/services.py
"""
Services — the data WRITING layer.
All the business logic lives here: CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE.
Services may call selectors, but not the other way around.
"""
from django.db import transaction
from django.db.models import F
from django.utils.text import slugify

from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag, TodoItem, Reminder


def create_note(*, user, title, content='', notebook=None, priority=1, tag_ids=None):
    """
    Creating a note with tags.
    transaction.atomic() — either the Note and its tags are saved together, or nothing is.
    """
    with transaction.atomic():
        note = Note.objects.create(
            user=user,
            title=title,
            content=content,
            notebook=notebook,
            priority=priority,
        )
        if tag_ids:
            # Check that the tags belong to this user (security!)
            valid_tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=user)
            note.tags.set(valid_tags)

    return note


def update_note(note, *, title=None, content=None, priority=None,
                notebook=None, is_pinned=None, tag_ids=None):
    """
    Updating a note — only the given fields.
    update_fields → generates an UPDATE only for the changed columns.
    """
    changed_fields = []

    if title is not None:
        note.title = title
        changed_fields.append('title')
    if content is not None:
        note.content = content
        changed_fields.append('content')
    if priority is not None:
        note.priority = priority
        changed_fields.append('priority')
    if notebook is not None:
        note.notebook = notebook
        changed_fields.append('notebook')
    if is_pinned is not None:
        note.is_pinned = is_pinned
        changed_fields.append('is_pinned')

    if changed_fields:
        note.save(update_fields=changed_fields)

    if tag_ids is not None:
        valid_tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=note.user)
        note.tags.set(valid_tags)

    return note


def archive_note(note):
    """Archiving a note (not deleting it)."""
    Note.objects.filter(pk=note.pk).update(is_archived=True)


def delete_note(note):
    """Deleting a note. CASCADE will delete the Reminders automatically."""
    note.delete()


def toggle_todo_item(item_id, *, user):
    """
    Check/uncheck a list item.
    select_for_update() — prevents a race condition on simultaneous clicks.
    """
    with transaction.atomic():
        item = TodoItem.objects.select_for_update().get(
            id=item_id,
            todo_list__user=user   # access-permission check via FK traversal
        )
        item.is_done = not item.is_done
        item.save(update_fields=['is_done'])
    return item


def mark_reminder_sent(reminder_id):
    """
    Atomically mark a reminder as sent.
    F() + update() — race condition safe.
    """
    Reminder.objects.filter(pk=reminder_id).update(is_sent=True)


def create_tag(*, user, name, color='#808080'):
    """Creating a tag with a uniqueness check."""
    tag, created = Tag.objects.get_or_create(
        user=user,
        name=name.lower().strip(),
        defaults={'color': color}
    )
    return tag, created

docs.title: Step 8 — Views and templates
docs.text:
🧠 Mental model: A View is a thin layer. It: (1) parses the HTTP request, (2) calls a selector or a service, (3) renders a template or returns a redirect. No business logic, no QuerySets directly in the View.

📚 The PRG pattern: Post/Redirect/Get is the standard for forms. GET → show the form. POST → process it → redirect (not render). Why? Without a redirect: the user presses F5 → the browser repeats the POST → a duplicate record. With a redirect → F5 repeats the GET → safe.

❌ Common mistake: Note.objects.filter(...) directly in a View. This breaks the architectural split. 3 months later the same query is needed in a Celery task → you copy it → duplication → things get out of sync.

# hello_app/views.py
from django.shortcuts import render, redirect, get_object_or_404
from django.contrib import messages
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required

from .models import Note
from .forms import NoteForm
from . import selectors, services


@login_required
def note_list(request):
    """
    The current user's list of notes.
    The View only: gets the filters from GET → calls a selector → renders.
    """
    search = request.GET.get('q', '')
    tag_id = request.GET.get('tag')
    notebook_id = request.GET.get('notebook')

    # The Selector decides WHICH query, the View decides WHICH parameters
    notes = selectors.get_user_notes(
        request.user,
        search=search or None,
        tag=tag_id or None,
    )
    notebooks = selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user)
    tags = selectors.get_user_tags(request.user)

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_list.html', {
        'notes': notes,
        'notebooks': notebooks,
        'tags': tags,
        'search': search,
        'active_tag': tag_id,
    })


@login_required
def note_detail(request, pk):
    """Note detail. The Selector raises Note.DoesNotExist if the user is not the owner."""
    try:
        note = selectors.get_note_detail(request.user, pk)
    except Note.DoesNotExist:
        from django.http import Http404
        raise Http404("Нотатку не знайдено")

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_detail.html', {'note': note})


@login_required
def note_create(request):
    """
    PRG: GET → an empty form. POST → service.create_note() → redirect.
    """
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = services.create_note(
                user=request.user,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', 1),
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" створено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm()

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'action': 'Створити',
        'title': 'Нова нотатка',
    })


@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    """Editing. The Service runs an UPDATE only for the changed fields."""
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note)
        if form.is_valid():
            services.update_note(
                note,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', note.priority),
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" оновлено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(instance=note)

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'note': note,
        'action': 'Зберегти',
        'title': f'Редагувати: {note.title}',
    })


@login_required
def note_delete(request, pk):
    """
    Deletion via POST (not GET!).
    GET → a confirmation page. POST → service.delete_note() → redirect.
    """
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        title = note.title
        services.delete_note(note)
        messages.warning(request, f'Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_list')

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% load static %}

{% block title %}Мої нотатки{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
<div class="container py-4">
    <div class="row">
        <!-- Sidebar: filters -->

            <div class="card mb-3">
                <div class="card-header fw-bold">📓 Записники</div>

                        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}" class="text-decoration-none">

                <div class="card-body">
                    {% for tag in tags %}
                    <a href="?tag={{ tag.id }}"
                       class="badge text-decoration-none me-1 mb-1"
                       style="background-color: {{ tag.color }};">
                        #{{ tag.name }}
                        <small>({{ tag.note_count }})</small>
                    </a>
                    {% endfor %}
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>

        <!-- Main content -->
        <div class="col-md-9">
            <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
                <h2>📝 Нотатки</h2>
                <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_create' %}" class="btn btn-primary">

                </a>

            <!-- Search -->
            <form method="get" class="mb-3">
                <div class="input-group">
                    <input type="text" name="q" value="{{ search }}"
                           class="form-control" placeholder="Пошук нотаток...">
                    <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-secondary">🔍</button>
                </div>
            </form>

            <!-- Django Messages -->
            {% for message in messages %}
            <div class="alert alert-{{ message.tags }} alert-dismissible" role="alert">
                {{ message }}
                <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-bs-dismiss="alert"></button>
            </div>
            {% endfor %}

            <!-- List of notes -->
            {% if notes %}
            <div class="row row-cols-1 row-cols-md-2 g-3">
                {% for note in notes %}
                <div class="col">
                    <div class="card h-100 {% if note.is_pinned %}border-warning{% endif %}">
                        <div class="card-body">
                            <div class="d-flex justify-content-between">
                                <h5 class="card-title">
                                    {% if note.is_pinned %}📌 {% endif %}
                                    <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_detail' note.pk %}"
                                       class="text-decoration-none text-dark">
                                        {{ note.title }}
                                    </a>
                                </h5>
                                <!-- Priority -->
                                <span class="badge
                                    {% if note.priority == 4 %}bg-danger
                                    {% elif note.priority == 3 %}bg-warning text-dark
                                    {% elif note.priority == 2 %}bg-info text-dark
                                    {% else %}bg-light text-dark{% endif %}">
                                    {{ note.get_priority_display }}
                                </span>
                            </div>

                            <p class="card-text text-muted small">
                                {{ note.content|truncatechars:100 }}
                            </p>

                            <!-- Tags (loaded via prefetch_related — no N+1!) -->
                            <div class="mb-2">
                                {% for tag in note.tags.all %}
                                <a href="?tag={{ tag.id }}"
                                   class="badge text-decoration-none"
                                   style="background-color: {{ tag.color }};">
                                    #{{ tag.name }}
                                </a>
                                {% endfor %}
                            </div>
                        </div>

                        <div class="card-footer d-flex justify-content-between">
                            <small class="text-muted">
                                📁 {{ note.notebook.title|default:"Без записника" }}
                                · {{ note.updated_at|date:"d.m.Y" }}
                            </small>
                            <div>
                                <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_edit' note.pk %}"
                                   class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary">✏️</a>
                                <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_delete' note.pk %}"
                                   class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">🗑️</a>
                            </div>
                        </div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                {% endfor %}
            </div>

            {% else %}
            <div class="text-center py-5">
                <div class="display-1">📝</div>
                <p class="text-muted">
                    {% if search %}
                        Нотаток за запитом "{{ search }}" не знайдено.
                    {% else %}
                        У вас ще немає нотаток.
                    {% endif %}
                </p>
                <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_create' %}" class="btn btn-primary">
                    Створити першу нотатку
                </a>
            </div>
            {% endif %}
        </div>
    </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

docs.title: Step 8.5 — Detailed tutorial: every function explained
docs.text: Here we will go through EVERY function from selectors.py, services.py, views.py and forms.py step by step — what happens inside and why.

docs.title: get_user_notes(user, *, archived, notebook, tag, search)
docs.text:
What it does: returns the user's filtered list of notes
Where it is called: views.note_list()

Step by step:

# Step 1: The base QuerySet (LAZY — the SQL has not run yet!)
qs = Note.objects.filter(user=user, is_archived=archived)
#    SQL so far: WHERE note.user_id=? AND note.is_archived=?
#    But the SQL is NOT executed — Django waits until someone iterates the QuerySet!

# Step 2: select_related('notebook') — attach the FK with one JOIN
qs = qs.select_related('notebook')
#    The SQL becomes: LEFT JOIN hello_app_notebook nb ON note.notebook_id = nb.id
#    Consequence: note.notebook.title → does NOT trigger a new SELECT (already in memory!)
#
#    WITHOUT select_related: for note in qs: print(note.notebook.title)
#                        → 1 SELECT + N SELECTs = the N+1 problem!
#    WITH select_related: 1 SELECT with a JOIN — always!

# Step 3: prefetch_related('tags') — load the M:N
qs = qs.prefetch_related('tags')
#    QUERY 1: SELECT * FROM note WHERE ...
#    QUERY 2: SELECT tag.* ... WHERE note_id IN (1, 2, 3, ...)
#    Python: Django joins them by itself
#    Consequence: note.tags.all() → already in the cache, NOT a new SELECT!

# Step 4: Optional filters — a CHAIN (lazy)
if notebook is not None:
    qs = qs.filter(notebook=notebook)
    # SQL gets: AND note.notebook_id = ?

if tag is not None:
    qs = qs.filter(tags=tag)
    # SQL: AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM note_tags WHERE note_id=? AND tag_id=?)

if search:
    qs = qs.filter(Q(title__icontains=search) | Q(content__icontains=search))
    # SQL: AND (note.title ILIKE '%search%' OR note.content ILIKE '%search%')

# Step 5: Ordering and return (still LAZY!)
return qs.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')
# SQL: ORDER BY is_pinned DESC, priority DESC, updated_at DESC
# The SQL runs only when the View passes notes to the template and {% for note in notes %}!

docs.title: get_note_detail(user, note_id)
docs.text:
What it does: loads ONE note with all its relationships for the detail page
Where it is called: views.note_detail()

The key difference from get_user_notes:

# get_user_notes → a QuerySet (a list, not executed yet)
# get_note_detail → ONE object (already executed!)

note = Note.objects.select_related('notebook', 'user')  # JOIN for the FKs
.prefetch_related(
    'tags',         # M:N: 2 queries
    Prefetch(       # A FILTERED prefetch!
        'reminders',
        queryset=Reminder.objects.filter(
            remind_at__gte=timezone.now()  # only FUTURE reminders
        ).order_by('remind_at'),
        to_attr='upcoming_reminders'  # store it in a SEPARATE attribute!
    )
).get(id=note_id, user=user)  # .get() → EXECUTES the SQL + checks permissions

# Why Prefetch with to_attr?
# WITHOUT to_attr:  note.reminders.all()         → NEW QuerySet (another SELECT!)
#              note.reminders.filter(...)      → NEW QuerySet (a different SELECT!)
# WITH to_attr:   note.upcoming_reminders        → list[Reminder] (already in memory!)
#   In the template: {% for r in note.upcoming_reminders %}  ← NOT a SELECT!

docs.title: get_user_notebooks(user) and get_user_tags(user)
docs.text:
What they do: notebooks/tags with the NUMBER of notes in a single SQL
Where they are called: views.note_list() → sidebar

Why annotate and not a separate count():

# ❌ WRONG: N+1!
notebooks = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user)
for nb in notebooks:
    count = nb.notes.filter(is_archived=False).count()  # a separate SELECT!
# 10 notebooks → 11 SQL queries!

# ✅ RIGHT: a single GROUP BY
notebooks = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user).annotate(
    note_count=Count('notes', filter=Q(notes__is_archived=False))
)
# SQL: SELECT nb.*, COUNT(note.id) FILTER (WHERE note.is_archived=FALSE) AS note_count
#      FROM notebook nb LEFT JOIN note ON note.notebook_id=nb.id
#      WHERE nb.user_id=? GROUP BY nb.id
# 1 SQL! nb.note_count → a number, already in memory!

docs.title: get_user_todo_lists(user) — double annotation
docs.text:
TodoList.objects.filter(user=user).annotate(
    total_items=Count('items'),                                    # total items
    done_items=Count('items', filter=Q(items__is_done=True))       # done ones
)
# SQL: SELECT todolist.*,
#             COUNT(item.id) AS total_items,
#             COUNT(item.id) FILTER (WHERE item.is_done=TRUE) AS done_items
#      FROM todolist LEFT JOIN todoitem item ON item.todo_list_id = todolist.id
#      WHERE todolist.user_id = ? GROUP BY todolist.id
#
# In the template:
# todo.total_items → 5 (without a single SELECT!)
# todo.done_items  → 3 (without a single SELECT!)
# Progress: 3/5 = 60%

docs.title: get_pending_reminders() — for Celery
docs.text:
# This function is NOT for a View — it is for a background task!
Reminder.objects.filter(
    is_sent=False,                  # not sent yet
    remind_at__lte=timezone.now()   # the time has come (remind_at <= now)
).select_related('note__user')      # traversal THROUGH TWO FKs
# SQL JOIN: reminder → note → user
# reminder.note.user.email → without a single extra SELECT!

# Usage in Celery:
# @shared_task
# def send_reminders():
#     for r in selectors.get_pending_reminders():
#         send_email(to=r.note.user.email, ...)  ← no N+1!
#         services.mark_reminder_sent(r.id)

docs.title: create_note(*, user, title, content, notebook, priority, tag_ids)
docs.text:
What it does: atomically creates a note + attaches tags
Where it is called: views.note_create() after form.is_valid()

Step by step:

# Why the asterisk * before the arguments?
# def create_note(*, user, title, ...)
# → all arguments are KEYWORD-ONLY (no positional ones after *)
# → call: services.create_note(user=user, title="Test")  ✓
# → call: services.create_note(user, "Test")             ✗ TypeError!
# Why? More readable, fewer mistakes when refactoring.

with transaction.atomic():  # SQL: BEGIN;
    # Step 1: INSERT the note
    note = Note.objects.create(user=user, title=title, ...)
    # SQL: INSERT INTO note (...) VALUES (...) RETURNING id, created_at, ...

    if tag_ids:
        # Step 2: Check the tags (SECURITY!)
        valid_tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=user)
        # SQL: SELECT * FROM tag WHERE id IN (1,2,3) AND user_id=?
        # Without user=user: Alice could add Bob's tag to her own note!

        # Step 3: Set the M:N relationship
        note.tags.set(valid_tags)
        # SQL: INSERT INTO hello_app_note_tags (note_id, tag_id) VALUES (?,?), ...

# Step 4: COMMIT (or ROLLBACK if any operation failed!)
# If tags.set() raises an Exception → automatic ROLLBACK for the Note too!
return note  # after COMMIT: note.id is available

docs.title: update_note(note, *, title, content, priority, ...) — partial update
docs.text:
# The "partial update" pattern:
# - If the argument=None → the field is NOT updated
# - If the argument is passed → we update it

changed_fields = []
if title is not None:
    note.title = title
    changed_fields.append('title')
# ... for each field ...

if changed_fields:
    note.save(update_fields=changed_fields)
    # update_fields=['title'] → SQL: UPDATE note SET title=? WHERE id=?
    # Without update_fields:      → SQL: UPDATE note SET title=?, content=?,
    #                                priority=?, is_pinned=?, ... (ALL fields!)
    # With update_fields: only the changed ones! Safer for concurrent writes.

# M:N: a separate operation (not in update_fields!)
if tag_ids is not None:  # None = "don't change", [] = "remove all"
    note.tags.set(Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=note.user))

docs.title: toggle_todo_item(item_id, *, user) — race condition prevention
docs.text:
# WHY select_for_update()?
# The problem without locking:
#   Thread A: SELECT item WHERE id=5 → is_done=False
#   Thread B: SELECT item WHERE id=5 → is_done=False  (THE SAME VALUE!)
#   Thread A: UPDATE item SET is_done=True
#   Thread B: UPDATE item SET is_done=True  ← both set True!
#   Bug: the second click should have unchecked it!

with transaction.atomic():  # select_for_update REQUIRES atomic!
    item = TodoItem.objects.select_for_update().get(
        id=item_id,
        todo_list__user=user  # SECURITY: check access permission via the FK!
    )
    # SQL: SELECT ... FROM todoitem
    #      JOIN todolist ON todoitem.todo_list_id = todolist.id
    #      WHERE todoitem.id=? AND todolist.user_id=?
    #      FOR UPDATE  ← locks the row!

    item.is_done = not item.is_done
    item.save(update_fields=['is_done'])
# COMMIT → releases the row lock

docs.title: create_or_get_tag(*, user, name, color) — an idempotent operation
docs.text:
tag, created = Tag.objects.get_or_create(
    user=user,
    name=name.lower().strip(),  # normalization: "Python" → "python"
    defaults={'color': color}   # color is set ONLY on CREATE
)
# get_or_create:
#   1. SELECT WHERE user=? AND name=?
#   2. If found → return (existing_tag, False)
#   3. If not found → INSERT → return (new_tag, True)
#
# Atomic! The UNIQUE constraint (user, name) protects against a race condition.
# Two simultaneous requests: one INSERT wins, the other gets the SELECT.

return tag, created
# views.py: tag, created = services.create_or_get_tag(user=user, name='python')

docs.title: complete_todo_list(todo_list) — bulk update
docs.text:
with transaction.atomic():
    # Step 1: mark the list
    todo_list.is_completed = True
    todo_list.save(update_fields=['is_completed'])

    # Step 2: mark all items in bulk
    todo_list.items.filter(is_done=False).update(is_done=True)
    # SQL: UPDATE todoitem SET is_done=TRUE
    #      WHERE todo_list_id=? AND is_done=FALSE
    #
    # WRONG:
    # for item in todo_list.items.all():
    #     item.is_done = True
    #     item.save()  # N queries instead of 1!
    #
    # RIGHT: .update() → 1 SQL for all rows!

    # Step 1: initialize the parent ModelForm

        self.fields['notebook'].queryset = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user)
        # Now the dropdown shows ONLY this user's notebooks!
        self.fields['tags'].queryset = Tag.objects.filter(user=user)

        self.fields['tags'].queryset = Tag.objects.none()

# Calls:

def clean_name(self):
    # Validation Pipeline:
    # 1. to_python("  Python  ") → str "  Python  "
    # 2. validate("  Python  ") → OK (required, max_length)
    # 3. run_validators → (no custom ones)
    # 4. clean_name(self) ← WE ARE HERE
    #    self.cleaned_data['name'] = "  Python  " (the string that passed validate)

    name = self.cleaned_data['name']
    normalized = name.lower().strip()   # "  Python  " → "python"

    if not normalized:
        raise forms.ValidationError("Назва тегу не може бути порожньою.")

    return normalized  # ← you MUST return it!
    # cleaned_data['name'] = "python" (normalized!)

docs.title: note_list(request) — a GET request with filters
docs.text:
URL: GET /notes/?q=python&notebook=3&tag=7

# Step 1: Read the filters from the URL
search = request.GET.get('q', '').strip()  # '' if missing
tag_id = request.GET.get('tag')            # '7' or None

# Step 2: Convert id → objects (with a permission check!)
tag = None
if tag_id:
    try:
        tag = Tag.objects.get(id=int(tag_id), user=request.user)
        #                          ↑                ↑
        #              string→int conversion    only your own tag!
    except (Tag.DoesNotExist, ValueError):
        pass  # invalid id → just ignore it

# Step 3: Get the data via a selector
notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user, search=search or None, tag=tag)
# '' → None: so the selector knows search is absent (not an empty string)

# Step 4: Render (this is where the QuerySet is executed!)
return render(request, 'hello_app/note_list.html', {'notes': notes, ...})
# During rendering: {% for note in notes %} → the SQL SELECT is executed!

docs.title: note_create(request) — the PRG pattern
docs.text:
GET  /notes/new/  → show an empty form
POST /notes/new/  → process the form → redirect

if request.method == 'POST':
    # 1. Bind the POST data to the form (the form becomes "bound")
    form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)

    # 2. Validation Pipeline:
    #    to_python → validate → run_validators → clean_<field> → clean
    if form.is_valid():
        # 3. Extract tag_ids from the M:N field
        tags = form.cleaned_data.get('tags')   # QuerySet[Tag] or None
        tag_ids = [t.id for t in tags] if tags else None  # [1, 3] or None

        # 4. Business logic → a Service (not here in the View!)
        note = services.create_note(
            user=request.user,
            title=form.cleaned_data['title'],  # a typed str (validated!)
            tag_ids=tag_ids,
            ...
        )

        # 5. PRG: messages + redirect (not render!)
        messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" створено!')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
        # HTTP 302 → GET /notes/42/ → safe, F5 does not duplicate!
    # If is_valid=False → we fall through to the render below

else:  # GET
    form = NoteForm(user=request.user)  # an empty form

# Render for GET and for a POST with errors:
return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {'form': form, ...})

docs.title: note_delete(request, pk) — why POST only
docs.text:
GET  /notes/42/delete/  → confirmation page
POST /notes/42/delete/  → deletion → redirect

# Why can't GET delete?
# Browsers, bots, antivirus software make GET requests AUTOMATICALLY
# (prefetch links, availability checks, etc.)
# If GET /notes/42/delete/ deleted things → notes would disappear "by themselves"!

note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
# SQL: SELECT WHERE id=42 AND user_id=request.user.id
# 404 if not found → Alice cannot delete Bob's notes!

if request.method == 'POST':  # the form in the confirmation template
    title = note.title  # save it BEFORE deletion
    services.delete_note(note)
    # CASCADE: deleting the note → automatically deletes the Reminders
    messages.warning(request, f'Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
    return redirect('hello_app:note_list')

# GET → show the page with a warning and a confirmation form
return render(request, 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

docs.title: select_related — solving N+1 for FKs
docs.text:
# ❌ N+1: 100 notes + 100 queries for user + 100 for category = 201 queries
notes = Note.objects.filter(is_archived=False)[:100]
for note in notes:
    print(note.user.username, note.notebook.title)  # new SQL for each one!

# ✅ select_related: 1 query with a JOIN
notes = Note.objects.select_related(
    'user', 'notebook'
).filter(is_archived=False)[:100]
for note in notes:
    print(note.user.username, note.notebook.title)  # already in memory

docs.title: prefetch_related — for M:N and reverse FKs
docs.text:
# ✅ 2 queries: one for notes, one for tags
notes = Note.objects.prefetch_related('tags').all()[:50]
for note in notes:
    print([t.name for t in note.tags.all()])  # already in memory!

# ✅ A combination (the most efficient for note_list)
notes = (
    Note.objects
    .select_related('user', 'notebook')     # FK → SQL JOIN (1 query)
    .prefetch_related('tags', 'reminders')  # M:N + reverse FK (2 queries)
    .filter(is_archived=False)
    .order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')
)

docs.title: F() — atomic operations
docs.text:
from django.db.models import F

# ✅ Atomic increment (race-condition safe!)
# UPDATE hello_app_note SET views_count = views_count + 1 WHERE id = 42
Note.objects.filter(pk=42).update(views_count=F('views_count') + 1)

# ✅ Comparing two fields with each other
Note.objects.filter(views_count__gt=F('likes_count'))
# WHERE views_count > likes_count  (comparing COLUMNS, not values)

# ❌ Dangerous with concurrent requests:
note = Note.objects.get(pk=42)
note.views_count += 1   # reads in Python
note.save()             # writes it back → race condition!

docs.title: select_for_update() — preventing race conditions
docs.text:
with transaction.atomic():
    # SELECT ... FOR UPDATE → locks the row until the end of the transaction
    note = Note.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=note_id)
    if not note.is_archived:
        note.is_archived = True
        note.save(update_fields=['is_archived'])
    # COMMIT → the lock is released

# nowait=True: raises DatabaseError instead of waiting if the row is already locked
try:
    note = Note.objects.select_for_update(nowait=True).get(pk=note_id)
except DatabaseError:
    return JsonResponse({'error': 'Ресурс зайнятий, спробуйте пізніше'}, status=409)

docs.title: What CBVs are and why
docs.text:
FBV (Function-Based Views) — a view as a function:

def note_list(request):
    notes = Note.objects.filter(user=request.user)
    return render(request, 'note_list.html', {'notes': notes})

CBV (Class-Based Views) — a view as a class:

class NoteListView(LoginRequiredMixin, ListView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_list.html'
    context_object_name = 'notes'

Why CBVs?

Problem with FBVs Solution with CBVs @login_required has to be added to every function LoginRequiredMixin once in the class Note.objects.filter(user=request.user) is repeated in 5 places UserQuerySetMixin.get_queryset() — once if request.method == 'POST': form = ...; if form.is_valid(): ... — boilerplate code CreateView/UpdateView do this automatically No standard way to extend the logic We override hooks: get_queryset(), form_valid(), get_context_data()

Important: CBVs do not replace the architecture. Selectors/Services stayed exactly where they were — only the calls moved from functions into class methods.

docs.title: Why a class can't be put directly into urls.py
docs.text:
The Django router expects a callable (a function):

# ❌ DOES NOT WORK — NoteListView is a class, not a callable
path('notes/', views.NoteListView, name='note_list')

# ✅ CORRECT — .as_view() returns a callable wrapper function
path('notes/', views.NoteListView.as_view(), name='note_list')

docs.title: What as_view() does
docs.text:
as_view() is a classmethod that Django calls once when the server starts. It returns an ordinary wrapper function view. On every HTTP request this function:

  1. Creates a new instance of the class (a new one every time — thread-safe!)
  2. Copies request, args, kwargs onto the instance
  3. Calls instance.dispatch(request, *args, **kwargs)
# Simplified pseudocode of what as_view() does inside Django:
@classmethod
def as_view(cls, **initkwargs):
    def view(request, *args, **kwargs):
        self = cls(**initkwargs)          # 1. new instance
        self.request = request            # 2. copy the request
        self.args = args
        self.kwargs = kwargs
        return self.dispatch(request, *args, **kwargs)  # 3. dispatch
    return view

docs.title: What dispatch() does
docs.text:
dispatch() is the main router of a CBV. It looks at the HTTP method of the request and delegates the call to the corresponding class method:

# Pseudocode of dispatch() from the base View:
def dispatch(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
    method = request.method.lower()          # 'get', 'post', 'put', ...
    handler = getattr(self, method, None)    # self.get, self.post, ...
    if handler:
        return handler(request, *args, **kwargs)
    return HttpResponseNotAllowed(...)       # 405 Method Not Allowed

In FBVs, parameters were passed into the function or hardcoded inside it. In CBVs we declare them as class attributes:

    template_name = 'hello_app/note_list.html'  # ← which template to render
    context_object_name = 'notes'            # ← what to call the list in the template
                                             #   (instead of the default 'object_list')

docs.title: Why the order in the parentheses is critically important
docs.text:
Python determines the method lookup order through the MRO (Method Resolution Order). When Django calls dispatch(), Python looks it up along the MRO from left to right:

NoteListView → LoginRequiredMixin → ListView → View

LoginRequiredMixin.dispatch() checks authentication first — before ListView.dispatch() does anything at all.

# ✅ CORRECT: LoginRequiredMixin first → the auth check comes FIRST
class NoteListView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, ListView):
    ...

# ❌ WRONG: ListView first → the auth check comes AFTER the data is loaded
class NoteListView(UserQuerySetMixin, ListView, LoginRequiredMixin):
    ...

    classDef success  fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32,stroke-width:2px;
    classDef warning  fill:#fff8e1,stroke:#e65100,stroke-width:2px;

    class R,D,C step;
    class A decision;
    class L warning;
    class T success;

By default the redirect goes to /accounts/login/?next=/notes/. You can change this via login_url and redirect_field_name on the class.

docs.title: The problem: duplicating the user filter
docs.text:
Without a mixin, every Detail, Update, Delete view has to repeat:

# In NoteDetailView:
queryset = Note.objects.filter(user=self.request.user)

# In NoteUpdateView:
queryset = Note.objects.filter(user=self.request.user)

# In NoteDeleteView:
queryset = Note.objects.filter(user=self.request.user)

This is not just code repetition — it's a security hole: if you forget it in one place, Alice will see Bob's notes.

docs.title: The solution: a custom mixin
docs.text:
class UserQuerySetMixin:
    """
    Mixin for automatically filtering the QuerySet by the current user.
    """
    def get_queryset(self):
        # super().get_queryset() → returns model.objects.all()
        # .filter(user=...) → restrict to this user's objects only
        return super().get_queryset().filter(user=self.request.user)

docs.title: How Django uses get_queryset() for protection
docs.text:
DetailView, UpdateView, DeleteView load the object via get_object():

# Pseudocode of get_object() in DetailView:
def get_object(self, queryset=None):
    queryset = self.get_queryset()        # ← our filtered queryset!
    pk = self.kwargs.get('pk')
    return queryset.get(pk=pk)           # SQL: WHERE id=pk AND user_id=current_user

If Alice tries to open Bob's note (/notes/42/): - get_queryset() returns Note.objects.filter(user=Alice) - get_object() does .get(pk=42) on this queryset - SQL: SELECT * FROM note WHERE id=42 AND user_id=<Alice_id> → nothing found - Django raises Note.DoesNotExist → Http404

Alice sees a 404, not Bob's data.

docs.title: MRO with UserQuerySetMixin
docs.text:
class NoteDetailView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, DetailView):
    ...

# Python MRO:
# NoteDetailView → LoginRequiredMixin → UserQuerySetMixin → DetailView → View
#
# When get_queryset() is called:
#   1. Finds UserQuerySetMixin.get_queryset()
#   2. super().get_queryset() → goes further → DetailView.get_queryset()
#   3. DetailView.get_queryset() → returns Note.objects.all()
#   4. UserQuerySetMixin adds .filter(user=self.request.user)
#   Result: Note.objects.all().filter(user=self.request.user)

docs.title: Step 5 — ListView: a list of notes with filters
docs.text: NoteListView is the most complex view in the project: it supports search and filtering by tag and notebook.

docs.title: Class attributes
docs.text:
class NoteListView(LoginRequiredMixin, ListView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_list.html'
    context_object_name = 'notes'   # instead of the default 'object_list'

docs.title: get_queryset() — which collection to return
docs.text:
In FBVs we read the GET parameters right inside the function. In CBVs we do it in get_queryset() via self.request.GET:

def get_queryset(self):
    self._get_filters()       # parse GET params once (cached on self)
    return selectors.get_user_notes(
        self.request.user,
        search=self.search or None,
        tag=self.active_tag,
        notebook=self.active_notebook,
    )

The architecture is preserved: the selector does all the ORM logic. get_queryset() only delegates.

docs.title: get_context_data() — what data to pass to the template
docs.text:
ListView automatically adds to the context: - notes (or object_list) — the result of get_queryset() - page_obj — if there is pagination - is_paginated — a boolean

We extend the context via super():

def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
    self._get_filters()
    ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)   # ← already contains 'notes'!
    ctx['notebooks'] = selectors.get_user_notebooks(self.request.user)
    ctx['tags'] = selectors.get_user_tags(self.request.user)
    ctx['search'] = self.search
    ctx['active_tag'] = self.active_tag
    ctx['active_notebook'] = self.active_notebook
    return ctx

Always call super().get_context_data(**kwargs) and add to the dictionary — don't replace it.

docs.title: _get_filters() — a private helper for DRY
docs.text:
Both methods (get_queryset and get_context_data) need the same GET parameters. To avoid parsing them twice — a private helper that caches on self:

def _get_filters(self):
    if hasattr(self, '_filters_parsed'):   # already parsed earlier
        return
    self._filters_parsed = True

    self.search = self.request.GET.get('q', '').strip()

    tag_id = self.request.GET.get('tag')
    self.active_tag = None
    if tag_id:
        try:
            # check permissions! user=request.user
            self.active_tag = Tag.objects.get(id=int(tag_id), user=self.request.user)
        except (Tag.DoesNotExist, ValueError):
            pass   # invalid id → simply ignore it

docs.title: Step 6 — DetailView: object detail
docs.text:
class NoteDetailView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, DetailView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_detail.html'
    context_object_name = 'note'

docs.title: What DetailView does automatically
docs.text:
1. Reads pk from self.kwargs['pk'] (from the URL pattern <int:pk>)
  2. Calls get_object() → get_queryset().get(pk=pk)
  3. Passes the object to the template as 'note' (our context_object_name)
  4. Renders template_name
  5. If not found → 404 automatically

docs.title: Overriding get_object() for Prefetch
docs.text:
In our project the selector loads the note with Prefetch(to_attr='upcoming_reminders'). So we override get_object() to use the selector instead of the standard queryset.get(pk=pk):

def get_object(self, queryset=None):
    try:
        return selectors.get_note_detail(self.request.user, self.kwargs['pk'])
    except Note.DoesNotExist:
        raise Http404("Нотатку не знайдено")

Http404 is a standard Django exception. It automatically returns a 404 page.

docs.title: get_context_data() — adding reminders
docs.text:
def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
    ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
    # upcoming_reminders is set via Prefetch(to_attr=) in the selector
    ctx['reminders'] = getattr(self.object, 'upcoming_reminders', [])
    return ctx

self.object is the loaded object (always available after get_object()).

docs.title: Step 7 — CreateView and get_form_kwargs()
docs.text:
class NoteCreateView(LoginRequiredMixin, CreateView):
    model = Note
    form_class = NoteForm
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_form.html'

docs.title: What CreateView does automatically
docs.text:
GET request: 1. get_form() → form_class(**get_form_kwargs()) → an empty form 2. get_context_data() → adds {'form': form} 3. Renders the template

POST request: 1. get_form() → a form with data=request.POST 2. form.is_valid(): - True → calls form_valid(form) - False → calls form_invalid(form) → renders the template with errors

docs.title: The problem: how to pass user= into the form
docs.text:
NoteForm.__init__ needs user= to filter the QuerySet for the notebook and tags fields:

# FBV:
form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)

# CBV: how do we do this if CreateView builds the form automatically?

docs.title: The solution: get_form_kwargs()
docs.text:
CreateView builds the form via get_form():

# Inside CreateView (simplified):
def get_form(self):
    return self.form_class(**self.get_form_kwargs())

get_form_kwargs() returns a dictionary of arguments for the form. We extend it:

def get_form_kwargs(self):
    kwargs = super().get_form_kwargs()
    # super() returns: {'data': request.POST, 'files': request.FILES, ...}
    kwargs['user'] = self.request.user   # ← add user=
    return kwargs
    # Result: NoteForm(data=POST, files=FILES, user=request.user)

docs.title: get_initial() — initial values for the form
docs.text:
TagCreateView supports ?name=python — it pre-fills the field:

def get_initial(self):
    initial = super().get_initial()
    name = self.request.GET.get('name')
    if name:
        initial['name'] = name
    return initial

get_initial() returns a dictionary of initial values. CreateView passes them into the form as initial=.

docs.title: Step 8 — UpdateView: editing with an instance
docs.text:
class NoteUpdateView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, UpdateView):
    model = Note
    form_class = NoteForm
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_form.html'

docs.title: What UpdateView does automatically (compared with CreateView)
docs.text:
UpdateView does everything CreateView does, plus:

  • Before rendering on GET: loads the existing object via get_object()
  • Passes instance=object into the form → all fields are pre-filled
  • UserQuerySetMixin.get_queryset() → 404 if the object belongs to someone else
# Inside UpdateView (simplified):
def get_form_kwargs(self):
    kwargs = super().get_form_kwargs()
    kwargs['instance'] = self.object    # ← the key difference from CreateView
    return kwargs

docs.title: get_form_kwargs() — passing user=
docs.text:
def get_form_kwargs(self):
    kwargs = super().get_form_kwargs()
    kwargs['user'] = self.request.user
    return kwargs
    # Result: NoteForm(data=POST, instance=note, user=request.user)

docs.title: get_context_data() — breadcrumbs
docs.text:
def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
    ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
    ctx['note'] = self.object           # for breadcrumbs in the template
    ctx['action'] = 'Зберегти зміни'
    ctx['title'] = f'Редагувати: {self.object.title}'
    return ctx

docs.title: Step 9 — DeleteView: safe deletion via POST only
docs.text:
class NoteDeleteView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, DeleteView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html'
    success_url = reverse_lazy('hello_app:note_list')
    context_object_name = 'note'

docs.title: Why DELETE only via POST?
docs.text:
Deleting via GET violates HTTP semantics:

GET /notes/42/delete/   ← Dangerous!
  • The browser may prefetch these URLs — deleting without a click!
  • A search bot crawls the links — deleting all records!
  • <img src="/notes/42/delete/"> in an email — deletes when it's opened!

DeleteView automatically requires POST for the actual deletion: - GET → renders the confirmation page ("Are you sure?") - POST → deletes and redirects

docs.title: form_valid() — the POST confirmation hook
docs.text:
def form_valid(self, form):
    note = self.get_object()
    title = note.title    # save it BEFORE deletion!
    services.delete_note(note)
    messages.warning(self.request, f'🗑️ Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
    return redirect(self.success_url)

We save title before services.delete_note() — after deletion note.title may be unavailable.

docs.title: get_context_data() — showing a warning
docs.text:
In NotebookDeleteView we add the number of notes that will be left without a notebook:

def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
    ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
    ctx['note_count'] = self.object.notes.count()
    return ctx

The template shows: "Deleting will not delete the notes, they will be left without a notebook".

docs.title: Step 10 — get_success_url() and reverse_lazy
docs.text: After a successful save/delete, the CBV needs to know where to redirect.

docs.title: Option 1: success_url — a static URL
docs.text:
class NoteDeleteView(..., DeleteView):
    success_url = reverse_lazy('hello_app:note_list')

Why reverse_lazy and not reverse()?

success_url = reverse('hello_app:note_list') is executed when the class is loaded (when Django starts), before the URL patterns are registered. This leads to NoReverseMatch.

reverse_lazy('hello_app:note_list') is executed lazily, only when the attribute is actually needed (during a request). By then the URL patterns are already registered.

docs.title: Option 2: get_success_url() — a dynamic URL
docs.text:
When the URL depends on the object's state or on request parameters:

# In TagCreateView: support the ?next= parameter
def get_success_url(self):
    return self._get_next_url()

def _get_next_url(self):
    return (
        self.request.GET.get('next')     # ?next= in GET
        or self.request.POST.get('next') # next in the POST form
        or 'hello_app:note_create'       # default if missing
    )

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: success_url get_success_url() When a static URL known in advance the URL depends on the object or the request Example the list of notebooks the detail page of a just-created note reverse_lazy required not needed (called during the request)

docs.title: Step 11 — Services architecture in CBVs
docs.text: In FBVs, Services/Selectors were called directly inside the view function. In CBVs — in hooks.

docs.title: form_valid() instead of form.save()
docs.text:
Key rule: if you have services.py, never call super().form_valid() in CreateView/UpdateView — inside it is form.save(), which bypasses your business logic.

class NoteCreateView(LoginRequiredMixin, CreateView):
    ...

    def form_valid(self, form):
        # ❌ DON'T: super().form_valid(form) → it contains form.save()!

        # ✅ DELEGATE to the service — it has transaction.atomic(), business rules
        tags = form.cleaned_data.get('tags')
        tag_ids = [t.id for t in tags] if tags else None

        note = services.create_note(
            user=self.request.user,
            title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
            content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
            priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', 1),
            notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
            tag_ids=tag_ids,
        )
        messages.success(self.request, f'✅ Нотатку "{note.title}" створено!')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)

docs.title: get_queryset() instead of direct queries in get_context_data()
docs.text:
In NoteListView we don't run queries in get_context_data() except for the sidebar data. The main list comes from get_queryset(). This lets pagination work correctly.

# ✅ CORRECT: the list of notes via get_queryset()
def get_queryset(self):
    return selectors.get_user_notes(self.request.user, ...)

# ✅ CORRECT: sidebar data via get_context_data()
def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
    ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
    ctx['notebooks'] = selectors.get_user_notebooks(self.request.user)
    return ctx

docs.title: Full table of hooks
docs.text: Hook Where we override it What for get_queryset() ListView, UserQuerySetMixin which collection to return get_object() NoteDetailView loading with Prefetch via the selector get_context_data() all extra data for the template get_form_kwargs() NoteCreateView, NoteUpdateView pass user= into the form get_initial() TagCreateView initial field values form_valid() all Create/Update/Delete call a service instead of form.save() get_success_url() TagCreateView dynamic redirect after saving

docs.title: Step 12 — CBVs in urls.py
docs.text:
# hello_app/urls.py
from django.urls import path
from . import views

app_name = "hello_app"

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.IndexView.as_view(), name='index'),

    # Notes
    path('notes/', views.NoteListView.as_view(), name='note_list'),
    path('notes/new/', views.NoteCreateView.as_view(), name='note_create'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/', views.NoteDetailView.as_view(), name='note_detail'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/edit/', views.NoteUpdateView.as_view(), name='note_edit'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/delete/', views.NoteDeleteView.as_view(), name='note_delete'),

    # Notebooks
    path('notebooks/', views.NotebookListView.as_view(), name='notebook_list'),
    path('notebooks/new/', views.NotebookCreateView.as_view(), name='notebook_create'),
    path('notebooks/<int:pk>/edit/', views.NotebookUpdateView.as_view(), name='notebook_edit'),
    path('notebooks/<int:pk>/delete/', views.NotebookDeleteView.as_view(), name='notebook_delete'),

    # Tags
    path('tags/new/', views.TagCreateView.as_view(), name='tag_create'),
]

docs.title: FBV vs CBV in urls.py
docs.text:
# FBV: views.note_list is already a callable function
path('notes/', views.note_list, name='note_list')

# CBV: views.NoteListView is a class (not callable!)
path('notes/', views.NoteListView.as_view(), name='note_list')
#                              ^^^^^^^^^^^ required!

docs.title: IndexView — a base View without Generic
docs.text:
class IndexView(View):
    """The simplest CBV — the base View."""
    def get(self, request):
        return HttpResponse("Hello, Django ORM!")

The base View doesn't render a template automatically — you have to implement get() and post() by hand. It's suitable for simple pages or API endpoints.

docs.title: List
docs.text:
# FBV
@login_required
def note_list(request):
    notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user, ...)
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_list.html', {'notes': notes})

# CBV
class NoteListView(LoginRequiredMixin, ListView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_list.html'
    context_object_name = 'notes'

    def get_queryset(self):
        return selectors.get_user_notes(self.request.user, ...)

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
# FBV
@login_required
def note_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = services.create_note(user=request.user, ...)
            messages.success(request, '...')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(user=request.user)
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {'form': form})

# CBV
class NoteCreateView(LoginRequiredMixin, CreateView):
    model = Note
    form_class = NoteForm
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_form.html'

    def get_form_kwargs(self):
        kwargs = super().get_form_kwargs()
        kwargs['user'] = self.request.user
        return kwargs

    def form_valid(self, form):
        note = services.create_note(user=self.request.user, ...)
        messages.success(self.request, '...')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
# FBV
@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            services.update_note(note, ...)
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(instance=note, user=request.user)
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {'form': form, 'note': note})

# CBV
class NoteUpdateView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, UpdateView):
    model = Note
    form_class = NoteForm
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_form.html'

    def get_form_kwargs(self):
        kwargs = super().get_form_kwargs()
        kwargs['user'] = self.request.user
        return kwargs

    def form_valid(self, form):
        note = self.get_object()
        services.update_note(note, ...)
        return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
# FBV
@login_required
def note_delete(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
    if request.method == 'POST':
        services.delete_note(note)
        messages.warning(request, f'Нотатку видалено.')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_list')
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

# CBV
class NoteDeleteView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, DeleteView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html'
    success_url = reverse_lazy('hello_app:note_list')
    context_object_name = 'note'

    def form_valid(self, form):
        note = self.get_object()
        services.delete_note(note)
        messages.warning(self.request, f'Нотатку видалено.')
        return redirect(self.success_url)

docs.title: How to run
docs.text:

source ../notes_project/venv/bin/activate   # or your own venv

docs.title: Bootstrap forms in templates
docs.text: The templates of this project (note_form.html, notebook_form.html, tag_form.html) render Django forms by hand with Bootstrap 5 — without django-crispy-forms. This gives full control over the HTML and helps you understand how Django and Bootstrap interact.

docs.title: 1. Structure of a form template (Template Inheritance)
docs.text:
Every form template starts the same way:

{% extends 'hello_app/base.html' %}   {# inherit base: navbar, footer, Bootstrap CDN #}

{% block title %}{{ title }}{% endblock %}  {# title comes from the CBV context #}

{% block extra_css %}
    {% load static %}   {# load the {% static %} tag — without this line the tag doesn't work #}
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'hello_app/css/forms.css' %}">
    {# forms.css: .form-card, .tag-label, .pin-toggle, .tag-checkbox-item {display:none} #}
{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
    ...form...
{% endblock %}

{% block extra_js %}
    <script>/* live preview JS */</script>
{% endblock %}

Why separate blocks:

Block Purpose {% block extra_css %} CSS only for this page — doesn't pollute all the others {% block content %} The main HTML content of the page {% block extra_js %} JS only for this page, included after </body>

{% load static %} loads a tag library, not a file. Without it {% static '...' %} raises the error Invalid block tag: 'static'. You have to load it in every template where it's used.

docs.title: 2. Context variables — what comes from the CBV into the template
docs.text:
The note_form.html template is used by two CBV classes. Both pass the same keys via get_context_data():

# views.py — NoteCreateView
def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
    ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
    ctx['action'] = 'Створити'       # submit button text
    ctx['title']  = 'Нова нотатка'  # form heading
    return ctx
    # ctx['form'] is added automatically by CreateView/UpdateView!
    # ctx['note'] = None (we don't pass it) → the template checks {% if note %}

# views.py — NoteUpdateView
def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
    ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
    ctx['note']   = self.object            # Note instance for the breadcrumb
    ctx['action'] = 'Зберегти зміни'
    ctx['title']  = f'Редагувати: {self.object.title}'
    return ctx
    # ctx['form'] is already filled with instance=note automatically!

The following variables are available in the template:

Variable in the template Type Where it comes from Usage {{ form }} NoteForm CreateView/UpdateView automatically {{ form.title }}, {% for checkbox in form.tags %} {{ title }} str get_context_data() <h2>{{ title }}</h2> {{ action }} str get_context_data() <button>{{ action }}</button> {{ note }} Note or None get_context_data() {% if note %} in the breadcrumb {{ request }} HttpRequest context processor {{ request.path }} for ?next=

{{ request }} is available because settings.py has django.template.context_processors.request in TEMPLATES → Django automatically adds request to every template.

docs.title: 3. How a Widget passes the Bootstrap class
docs.text:
A Django form renders a field via a Widget. In forms.py every field is given attrs:

# forms.py — Widget attrs set the Bootstrap class
class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        widgets = {
            'title':    forms.TextInput(attrs={
                            'class': 'form-control',    # Bootstrap: styles the <input>
                            'placeholder': 'Назва нотатки...',
                            'autofocus': True,          # the browser focuses the field automatically
                        }),
            'content':  forms.Textarea(attrs={
                            'class': 'form-control',
                            'rows': 8,                  # textarea height in rows
                        }),
            'priority': forms.Select(attrs={
                            'class': 'form-select',     # Bootstrap: styles the <select>
                        }),
            'notebook': forms.Select(attrs={
                            'class': 'form-select',
                        }),
            'is_pinned': forms.CheckboxInput(attrs={
                            'class': 'form-check-input', # Bootstrap: styles the checkbox
                        }),
        }
Bootstrap class HTML element Effect form-control <input>, <textarea> Full width, border, padding, focus ring form-select <select> Dropdown arrow, padding, border form-check-input <input type="checkbox"> Custom checkbox style form-control-color <input type="color"> Special style for the color picker

docs.title: 4. Rendering a single field — the full anatomy of a BoundField
docs.text:
This is real code from note_form.html, line by line:

<div class="mb-3">
    <!--
      form.title — a BoundField: an object that combines the form field + the current value + the form.
      .id_for_label → the string 'id_title' (Django: prefix 'id_' + field name)
      Browser: clicking <label for="id_title"> focuses <input id="id_title">
    -->
    <label for="{{ form.title.id_for_label }}" class="form-label">
        <i class="bi bi-type me-1"></i>  {# Bootstrap Icon: an icon next to the label #}
        {{ form.title.label }}           {# → 'Заголовок' (from Meta.labels in forms.py) #}
        <span class="text-danger ms-1">*</span>  {# red asterisk = required field #}
    </label>

    <!--
      {{ form.title }} calls BoundField.__str__() → Widget.render()
      Result: <input type="text"
                        name="title"
                        id="id_title"
                        class="form-control"
                        placeholder="Назва нотатки..."
                        autofocus
                        maxlength="200">
      All the attributes (class, placeholder, autofocus) came from Meta.widgets!
    -->
    {{ form.title }}

    <!--
      form.title.help_text — hint text from Meta.help_texts.
      No help_text is set for title → the block is not shown.
      For notebook: help_text = 'Залиш порожнім — нотатка буде без записника.'
    -->
    {% if form.title.help_text %}
    <div class="form-text">{{ form.title.help_text }}</div>
    {% endif %}

    <!--
      form.title.errors — an ErrorList (a list of strings with error messages).
      Empty after a GET request. Filled if POST + is_valid() = False.
      For example: ['Це поле обов'язкове.'] or ['Не більше 200 символів.']
    -->
    {% if form.title.errors %}
    <ul class="errorlist">
        {% for error in form.title.errors %}<li>{{ error }}</li>{% endfor %}
    </ul>
    {% endif %}
</div>

docs.title: 5. BoundField — all the attributes used in templates
docs.text:
form.field_name in a template is a BoundField object (not just a string!). It knows the current value, the errors, and the metadata.

Expression in the template Python type Example value Description {{ form.title }} str (HTML) <input type="text" ...> Renders the Widget → a full HTML tag {{ form.title.id_for_label }} str 'id_title' id for <label for="">, auto-generated {{ form.title.label }} str 'Заголовок' Label text (from Meta.labels) {{ form.title.help_text }} str 'Залиш порожнім...' Hint (from Meta.help_texts) {{ form.title.html_name }} str 'title' The name attribute <input name="title"> {{ form.title.errors }} ErrorList ['Це поле обов'язкове.'] List of errors, iterable {% if form.title.errors %} bool True / False Checks whether there are errors form.title.field Field CharField(max_length=200) The form field object (not the Widget!) form.title.value() str 'Назва нотатки' Current value (from initial or POST)

docs.title: 6. Bootstrap Grid in a form + help_text + form.instance
docs.text:
The Bootstrap Grid lets you place several fields in one row. A real block from note_form.html:

<!--
  Bootstrap Grid: row + col-* = 12 columns.
  col-6 + col-6 = 12 → two fields take exactly one row.
  g-3 = gap between columns (Bootstrap 5 gutter).
-->
<div class="row g-3 mb-3">

    <div class="col-6">
        <label for="{{ form.priority.id_for_label }}" class="form-label">
            <i class="bi bi-flag me-1"></i>{{ form.priority.label }}
        </label>
        {{ form.priority }}  {# → <select class="form-select" name="priority">...</select> #}
        <!--
          priority-hint — an extra hint with colored icons.
          NOT part of the Django form — plain HTML for UX.
        -->
        <div class="priority-hint mt-1">
            <span class="bg-secondary bg-opacity-25">🟢 Низький</span>
            <span class="bg-warning bg-opacity-25">🟠 Високий</span>
            <span class="bg-danger bg-opacity-25">🔴 Терміново</span>
        </div>
    </div>

    <div class="col-6">
        <label for="{{ form.notebook.id_for_label }}" class="form-label">
            <i class="bi bi-journals me-1"></i>{{ form.notebook.label }}
        </label>
        {{ form.notebook }}  {# → a <select> with notebooks filtered by user #}
        <!--
          form.notebook.help_text → 'Залиш порожнім — нотатка буде без записника.'
          Rendered only if help_text is not empty.
        -->
        {% if form.notebook.help_text %}
        <div class="form-text">{{ form.notebook.help_text }}</div>
        {% endif %}
    </div>

</div>

form.instance in the template — access to the current model object (only with UpdateView):

<!-- notebook_form.html — color preview strip -->
<div class="color-preview-strip" id="colorStrip"
     style="background: {{ form.instance.color|default:'#4A90E2' }};"></div>
<!--
  form.instance → the Notebook ORM object (when editing) or an empty object (when creating).
  .color → the value of the color field from the database.
  |default:'#4A90E2' → Django filter: if color is empty → '#4A90E2'.
-->

docs.title: 7. Why novalidate on the <form>
docs.text:
<form method="post" novalidate>
    {% csrf_token %}
    ...
</form>

novalidate turns off the browser's HTML5 validation (required, minlength, type="email", etc.).

Why this is correct: - Browser validation looks different in Chrome, Firefox, Safari - It doesn't know about Django-specific rules (for example clean_name()) - Django validates on the server: always the same way, with your error messages - After a POST with errors → the template is rendered again with form.errors → a single error style

{% csrf_token %} → inserts a hidden input: 

<input type="hidden" name="csrfmiddlewaretoken" value="abc123XYZ...">
Django rejects a POST without this token with 403 Forbidden. Protection against Cross-Site Request Forgery.

docs.title: 8. A custom checkbox for tags (M:N) — in detail
docs.text:
ManyToManyField(Tag) → Django renders it as a group of <input type="checkbox">. The problem: the default look is ugly. The solution — iterate over the checkboxes manually, hide the native input, and style the label as a badge.

Real code from note_form.html:

<div class="tags-grid">
{% for checkbox in form.tags %}
    <!--
      form.tags — a BoundWidget for CheckboxSelectMultiple.
      Iteration: each checkbox is a separate SubWidget with its own data.
    -->
    <div>
        <!--
          The native checkbox: functional (the browser sends its value on submit),
          but INVISIBLE via CSS: .tag-checkbox-item { display: none; }

          name="{{ form.tags.html_name }}"
            → 'tags' (the same for all checkboxes in the group!)
            → Django receives: POST['tags'] = ['1', '3'] (a list of pks of the selected tags)
            → Why not Django's auto-name? Because we render the input by hand, outside the Widget.

          value="{{ checkbox.data.value }}"
            → the tag pk: '1', '2', '3'...
            → checkbox.data is a dictionary: {'value': '1', 'label': 'python', 'selected': False}

          id="{{ checkbox.id_for_label }}"
            → unique: 'id_tags_0', 'id_tags_1', 'id_tags_2'...
            → linked with the <label for="..."> below

          {% if checkbox.data.selected %}checked{% endif %}
            → if the tag is already attached to the note (when editing) → the checkbox will be checked
        -->
        <input type="checkbox"
               class="tag-checkbox-item"
               name="{{ form.tags.html_name }}"
               value="{{ checkbox.data.value }}"
               id="{{ checkbox.id_for_label }}"
               {% if checkbox.data.selected %}checked{% endif %}>

        <!--
          <label for="id_tags_0"> — clicking the label toggles <input id="id_tags_0">!
          This is standard HTML behavior: label + input with matching id ↔ for.
          Since the input is hidden (display:none), the user sees only the label badge.

          checkbox.choice_label → the tag text: 'python', 'django', 'work'
          style="--tag-color: #7c6efa;" → a CSS custom property (CSS variable)
            → forms.css uses var(--tag-color) for the badge color
        -->
        <label for="{{ checkbox.id_for_label }}" class="tag-label"
               style="--tag-color: #7c6efa;">
            <i class="bi bi-tag-fill" style="font-size:0.7rem;"></i>
            {{ checkbox.choice_label }}
        </label>
    </div>

{% empty %}
    <!--
      {% empty %} — runs if the form.tags queryset is empty.
      That is, if this user has no tags at all.
      We show a link to create a tag with ?next={{ request.path }}
    -->
    <span class="text-muted small fst-italic">
        Немає тегів.
        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:tag_create' %}?next={{ request.path }}"
           class="text-primary">Створити тег</a>
    </span>
{% endfor %}
</div>

What checkbox.data is: 

# For each tag, the Python object in checkbox.data looks like this:
{
    'value':    '1',        # tag pk (a string!)
    'label':    'python',   # tag name
    'selected': False,      # whether it's selected (True when editing if the tag is attached)
    'index':    '0',        # position in the group
    'disabled': False,
    'type':     'checkbox',
    'attrs':    {'id': 'id_tags_0'},
}

docs.title: 9. JavaScript live preview in {% block extra_js %}
docs.text:
notebook_form.html and tag_form.html have an <input type="color"> for picking a color. To show a preview immediately on selection, we add JS in {% block extra_js %}.

The key point: Django inserts id_for_label directly into the JS code while rendering the template:

{% block extra_js %}
<script>
/*
  Live preview of the notebook color.
  Updates the preview strip on every change of the color picker.
*/
(function() {
    /*
      '{{ form.color.id_for_label }}' → Django renders this as the string 'id_color'
      before sending the HTML to the browser.
      The browser receives: document.getElementById('id_color')  — ready-made JS!
    */
    const colorInput = document.getElementById('{{ form.color.id_for_label }}');
    const colorStrip = document.getElementById('colorStrip');  {# id in the template #}

    if (colorInput && colorStrip) {
        colorInput.addEventListener('input', function() {
            /*
              The 'input' event: fires on every change (not only after blur).
              this.value → a HEX string: '#FF5733'
            */
            colorStrip.style.background = this.value;
        });
    }
})();  {# IIFE: Immediately Invoked Function Expression — doesn't pollute the global scope #}
</script>
{% endblock %}

tag_form.html has a more complex live preview: it syncs both the color and the tag name:

function update() {
    const color = colorInput ? colorInput.value : '#808080';
    const name  = nameInput  ? (nameInput.value.trim() || 'назва') : 'назва';
    if (strip) strip.style.background = color;        // updates the strip
    if (badge) badge.style.background = color;        // updates the badge
    if (badgeName) badgeName.textContent = name;      // updates the badge text
}

if (colorInput) colorInput.addEventListener('input', update);
if (nameInput)  nameInput.addEventListener('input', update);
update();  // initial state on load

docs.title: 10. Redirect pattern: hidden next input (tag_form.html)
docs.text:
A tag can be created right from the note form — so you don't lose an unsaved note. URL: /tags/new/?next=/notes/new/

<!-- tag_form.html -->
<form method="post" novalidate>
    {% csrf_token %}
    <!--
      The hidden input stores the URL for the redirect after saving.
      next = '{{ next }}' → Django inserts the value from the context.

      Where does next in the context come from?  TagCreateView.get_context_data():
        ctx['next'] = self.request.GET.get('next') or 'hello_app:note_create'

      After submit:  TagCreateView.get_success_url():
        return self.request.POST.get('next') or 'hello_app:note_create'
        → redirect back to the note form!
    -->
    <input type="hidden" name="next" value="{{ next }}">
    ...
</form>

Also: the "Cancel" button leads to the same next: 

<a href="{{ next }}" class="btn btn-outline-secondary">
    <i class="bi bi-x me-1"></i>Скасувати
</a>

The "Create tag" link in note_form.html passes the current path: 

<a href="{% url 'hello_app:tag_create' %}?next={{ request.path }}">Створити тег</a>
<!--
  request.path → '/notes/new/' (the current URL without the domain)
  {% url 'hello_app:tag_create' %} → '/tags/new/'
  Full URL: '/tags/new/?next=/notes/new/'
-->
