docs.title: CrispyNotes — Django Templates + Crispy Forms
docs.text:
This tutorial walks you through the evolution of Django forms: HTML by hand → widget attrs → FormHelper + Layout.

The project is a notes manager with a SaaS Dashboard: the same Note model as in notes_project, but form rendering has been switched to django-crispy-forms. Three levels of form rendering — from {{ form.as_p }} to {% crispy form %} — show why crispy.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
Architectural foundation (read before the code) - 01 · TEMPLATE SOUP — the problem of duplicated HTML - 02 · TEMPLATE INHERITANCE — a 3-level hierarchy - 03 · FORMS EVOLUTION — 3 levels of rendering - 04 · FORMHELPER + LAYOUT — crispy architecture - 05 · DASHBOARD ARCHITECTURE — sidebar, topbar, context

Step-by-step implementation 1. Step 0 — Running the project 2. Step 1 — Settings: enabling crispy 3. Step 2 — Level 1: base.html (the HTML shell) 4. Step 3 — Level 2: layouts/dashboard.html (Sidebar + Topbar) 5. Step 4 — Level 3: Pages (note_list, note_form...) 6. Step 5 — Forms Tier 1: form.as_p (Raw Django) 7. Step 6 — Forms Tier 2: Manual Bootstrap HTML 8. Step 7 — Forms Tier 3: FormHelper + Layout (Crispy) 9. Step 8 — Sidebar Context Processor 10. Step 9 — Components (pagination, empty_state, modal) 11. Project file structure

docs.title: 01 · TEMPLATE SOUP
docs.text: "Template Soup" is when templates contain repeated blocks of HTML: <nav>, <header>, the Bootstrap CDN — copied into every file. When the navigation changes → you edit 20 files.

docs.title: The problem: duplication at the template level
docs.text:
<!-- notes_form.html — 80 lines for 5 fields -->
<div class="mb-3">
  <label for="id_title" class="form-label fw-semibold">
    Заголовок
    <span class="text-danger">*</span>
  </label>
  <input type="text"
         name="title"
         id="id_title"
         class="form-control {% if form.title.errors %}is-invalid{% endif %}"
         autofocus>
  {% if form.title.errors %}
    {% for error in form.title.errors %}
    <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ error }}</div>
    {% endfor %}
  {% endif %}
</div>

<!-- ... repeat for every field ... -->

This is Tier 2 — manual Bootstrap HTML. The problems:

Problem Example Duplication 15 lines per field × 6 fields = 90 lines just for the form Changing a class Want form-control-lg → edit every <input> in every template Synchronization Added a field in models.py → don't forget to update the template No system Every developer writes it "a little differently"

docs.title: The solution: separation of responsibilities
docs.text:
BEFORE (Tier 2):
  forms.py:    fields + widget attrs + validation
  template:    label + input + error + help_text   ← 80 lines of HTML

AFTER (Tier 3):
  forms.py:    fields + FormHelper + Layout           ← structure described in Python code
  template:    {% crispy form %}                    ← 1 line

Key idea: A form is a Python object. Its structure is described in Python code (Layout), not in HTML in the template. The template becomes thin — it only says where to render.

docs.title: 02 · TEMPLATE INHERITANCE
docs.text: "Don't repeat HTML — inherit it." Django lets you build templates as a tree: the parent defines the structure, the child provides the content.

docs.title: A 3-level hierarchy (the SaaS Dashboard pattern)
docs.text:
base.html                          ← Level 1: the HTML shell
│  Bootstrap CDN, meta, <body>
│  {% block body %}
│
└── layouts/dashboard.html        ← Level 2: the application layout
       Sidebar + Topbar
       Django Messages
       {% block content %}
       {% block topbar_title %}
       │
       ├── hello_app/note_list.html       ← Level 3: page content
       ├── hello_app/note_form.html
       ├── hello_app/notebook_list.html
       └── hello_app/tag_form.html

docs.title: What it looks like in code
docs.text:
base.html — only the HTML skeleton: 

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <!-- Bootstrap CDN, CSS -->
</head>
<body>
  {% block body %}{% endblock %}   ← the whole application goes here
</body>
</html>

layouts/dashboard.html — the layout (extends base): 

{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% block body %}
  <div class="d-flex vh-100">
    <nav><!-- Sidebar --></nav>
    <div class="flex-grow-1">
      <header>{% block topbar_title %}{% endblock %}</header>
      <main>{% block content %}{% endblock %}</main>
    </div>
  </div>
{% endblock %}

note_list.html — a page (extends dashboard): 

{% extends 'layouts/dashboard.html' %}
{% block topbar_title %}Мої нотатки{% endblock %}
{% block content %}
  <!-- only content, the sidebar/topbar already come from the parent -->
{% endblock %}

docs.title: The inheritance flow
docs.text:
Request /notes/
     │
     ▼
views.note_list()
  └─► render('hello_app/note_list.html', context)
           │
           ▼
      Django Template Engine
           │
      note_list.html extends dashboard.html
           │
      dashboard.html extends base.html
           │
      base.html — the root template
           │
           ▼
      Assembly: base → dashboard → note_list → HTML
           │
           ▼
      200 OK  ·  a full HTML page

Advantages: - A navigation change → only dashboard.html, all pages are updated - A new page → you only write {% block content %}, the rest comes for free - No duplication of the Bootstrap CDN in every file

docs.title: Comparison: with inheritance vs without
docs.text: Without inheritance With a 3-level hierarchy A new page Copy all the HTML 5 lines of {% extends %} + content A navigation change Edit every file Only dashboard.html Bootstrap CDN In every file Only base.html Sidebar Copy into every file Once in dashboard.html

docs.title: 03 · FORMS EVOLUTION
docs.text: Three levels of form evolution — from "it just works" to "beautiful and without duplication".

docs.title: Comparison table
docs.text:
Tier Where to look Method HTML in the template Where the Bootstrap classes are 1 — Raw notes_project/forms.py {{ form.as_p }} ~5 lines Nowhere (no styles) 2 — Manual django_bootstrap_project/ Manual HTML ~80 lines In the template, by hand 3 — Crispy this project /notes/new/ {% crispy form %} 1 line In forms.py via Layout

All three approaches pass the same NoteForm. The difference is only in how it's rendered.

docs.title: Tier 1: Raw Django — {{ form.as_p }}
docs.text:
# views.py — nothing special
def note_create_raw(request):
    form = NoteForm(user=request.user)
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form_raw.html', {'form': form})

<!-- note_form_raw.html -->
<form method="post">
  {% csrf_token %}
  {{ form.as_p }}      ← Django generates <p><label><input></p> without classes
  <button type="submit">Зберегти</button>
</form>

What gets generated: 

<p>
  <label for="id_title">Заголовок:</label>
  <input type="text" name="title" id="id_title" required>
</p>

Not a single class="form-control", no Bootstrap styles at all. Validation works, but it looks bad.

When to use it: only for debugging. Never in production.

docs.title: Tier 2: Manual Bootstrap HTML
docs.text:
# forms.py — set Bootstrap classes via widget attrs
class NoteFormManual(forms.ModelForm):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.fields['title'].widget.attrs.update({'class': 'form-control'})
        self.fields['content'].widget.attrs.update({'class': 'form-control', 'rows': 8})
        self.fields['priority'].widget.attrs.update({'class': 'form-select'})
        # ... repeat for every field

<!-- note_form_manual.html — ~80 lines of HTML for 5 fields -->
<form method="post">
  {% csrf_token %}

  <!-- Field: title -->
  <div class="mb-3">
    <label for="{{ form.title.id_for_label }}" class="form-label fw-semibold">
      {{ form.title.label }}
      {% if form.title.field.required %}<span class="text-danger">*</span>{% endif %}
    </label>
    <input type="text"
           name="{{ form.title.html_name }}"
           id="{{ form.title.id_for_label }}"
           value="{{ form.title.value|default:'' }}"
           class="form-control {% if form.title.errors %}is-invalid{% endif %}"
           autofocus>
    {% if form.title.errors %}
      {% for error in form.title.errors %}<div class="invalid-feedback">{{ error }}</div>{% endfor %}
    {% endif %}
  </div>

  <!-- ... another ~60 lines for priority, notebook, content, tags, is_pinned ... -->
</form>

Problems with Tier 2: - 80 lines of HTML just for the form - When you add a field in models.py → you have to add it to the template by hand - When the Bootstrap version changes → edit every template - 10 forms in the application = 800 lines of duplication

Where this approach is used: in notes_project (the previous lesson) — that's exactly how the forms are written there. It's a perfectly fine approach for small projects. Crispy is an upgrade for scale.

docs.title: Tier 3: Crispy Forms — {% crispy form %}
docs.text:
# forms.py — ALL the Bootstrap markup is described here, in Python code
from crispy_forms.helper import FormHelper
from crispy_forms.layout import Layout, Row, Column, Fieldset, Submit, Field

class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.helper = FormHelper()
        self.helper.form_method = 'post'
        self.helper.layout = Layout(
            Fieldset('Основна інформація',
                Field('title', placeholder='Назва нотатки...', autofocus=True),
                Row(Column('priority', css_class='col-md-4'),
                    Column('notebook', css_class='col-md-8')),
            ),
            Fieldset('Зміст нотатки',
                Field('content', rows=8, placeholder='Текст нотатки...'),
            ),
            Submit('submit', 'Зберегти нотатку', css_class='btn btn-primary me-2'),
        )

<!-- note_form.html — 1 line instead of 80 -->
{% load crispy_forms_tags %}
{% crispy form %}

What gets generated automatically: - <form method="post"> + the CSRF token - <div class="mb-3"> for every field - <label class="form-label"> with the required asterisk - <input class="form-control"> or <select class="form-select"> - <div class="invalid-feedback"> for errors - <div class="form-text"> for help_text - <fieldset> with <legend> for a Fieldset - <div class="row"> for a Row, <div class="col-md-4"> for a Column

docs.title: 04 · FORMHELPER + LAYOUT
docs.text: FormHelper is an object attached to the form that describes: - The attributes of the <form> tag (method, action, id, class) - The rendering behavior - The Layout — the structure and order of the fields

docs.title: FormHelper architecture
docs.text:
NoteForm
│
├── fields (Django standard)
│   ├── title     CharField
│   ├── content   TextField
│   └── ...
│
└── helper = FormHelper()          ← crispy adds this
    ├── form_method = 'post'       ← <form method="post">
    ├── form_id = 'note-form'      ← <form id="note-form">
    ├── form_tag = True            ← render <form>...</form>
    └── layout = Layout(...)       ← the field structure
        ├── Fieldset(...)          ← <fieldset><legend>
        │   ├── Field('title')     ← an individual field with attrs
        │   └── Row(...)           ← <div class="row">
        │       ├── Column(...)    ← <div class="col-md-4">
        │       └── Column(...)    ← <div class="col-md-8">
        ├── Submit(...)            ← <button type="submit">
        └── HTML('<hr>')           ← arbitrary HTML

docs.title: The rendering pipeline
docs.text:
{% crispy form %}
     │
     ▼
crispy_forms templatetag
     │  Finds form.helper
     │  Finds form.helper.layout
     ▼
Layout.render(form, context)
     │
     ├── Fieldset.render()
     │   ├── Field('title').render()  → field.html template
     │   └── Row.render()
     │       └── Column.render()
     ├── Submit.render()              → baseinput.html template
     └── HTML.render()               → direct string
     │
     ▼
Bootstrap 5 HTML
(form-control, mb-3, row, col-md-4, invalid-feedback...)

docs.title: Attributes of Layout objects
docs.text:
# kwargs → HTML attributes
Field('title', placeholder='Підказка')   # placeholder="Підказка"
Field('title', autofocus=True)           # autofocus
Field('title', data_custom="val")        # data-custom="val" (underscore → hyphen)
Field('title', css_class="extra")        # an extra CSS class
Field('title', type="hidden")            # a hidden input

# The wrapping div
Field('title', wrapper_class="mt-3")     # class for <div class="mb-3 mt-3">

docs.title: Where crispy vs where manual HTML — the rule
docs.text: Situation Approach The form takes up the whole page {% crispy form %} — full control via Layout A quick prototype {{ form\|crispy }} — no FormHelper, just Bootstrap styles A single field embedded in a page {{ form.title\|as_crispy_field }} A form without Bootstrap (API, email) {{ form.as_p }} or form.cleaned_data directly

docs.title: 05 · DASHBOARD ARCHITECTURE
docs.text: SaaS Dashboard is a UI pattern for applications: a fixed sidebar on the left, a topbar at the top, scrollable content in the center. Gmail, Notion, Linear — all built on this pattern.

docs.title: Sidebar Context Processor
docs.text:
The sidebar shows notebooks and tags — they're needed on EVERY page. But passing them from every view by hand is duplication:

# ❌ Bad — duplication in every view
def note_list(request):
    notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user)
    notebooks = selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user)  # duplication
    tags = selectors.get_user_tags(request.user)            # duplication
    return render(request, '...', {'notes': notes, 'notebooks': notebooks, 'tags': tags})

def note_create(request):
    notebooks = selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user)  # duplication again
    tags = selectors.get_user_tags(request.user)            # duplication again
    ...

The solution — context_processors.py:

# ✅ Good — once, automatically for all views
def sidebar_context(request):
    if not request.user.is_authenticated:
        return {}
    return {
        'sidebar_notebooks': selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user),
        'sidebar_tags': selectors.get_user_tags(request.user),
    }

# settings.py — register the processor
TEMPLATES = [{
    'OPTIONS': {
        'context_processors': [
            ...
            'hello_app.context_processors.sidebar_context',  # ← here
        ]
    }
}]

Now {{ sidebar_notebooks }} and {{ sidebar_tags }} are available in every template automatically.

docs.title: Active state in the navigation
docs.text:
<!-- Highlight the active menu item via request.resolver_match -->
<a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}"
   class="nav-link text-white {% if request.resolver_match.url_name == 'note_list' %}active{% endif %}">
  Всі нотатки
</a>

request.resolver_match.url_name returns the name of the current URL — without any extra variables in the View.

docs.title: Step 1 — Settings
docs.text:
# hello_project/settings.py

INSTALLED_APPS = [
    'django.contrib.admin',
    'django.contrib.auth',
    ...
    'crispy_forms',        # ← 1. the base package
    'crispy_bootstrap5',   # ← 2. the template pack for Bootstrap 5
    'debug_toolbar',
    'hello_app',
]

# Configure crispy
CRISPY_ALLOWED_TEMPLATE_PACKS = "bootstrap5"
CRISPY_TEMPLATE_PACK = "bootstrap5"

# Where to look for templates — critical for the 3-level hierarchy
TEMPLATES = [{
    'BACKEND': 'django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates',
    'DIRS': [BASE_DIR / 'templates'],   # ← global templates (base.html, layouts/)
    'APP_DIRS': True,                   # ← templates in hello_app/templates/hello_app/
    'OPTIONS': {
        'context_processors': [
            'django.template.context_processors.request',  # ← for request.user, request.resolver_match
            'django.contrib.auth.context_processors.auth',
            'django.contrib.messages.context_processors.messages',
            'hello_app.context_processors.sidebar_context', # ← sidebar notebooks/tags
        ],
    },
}]

# Django Messages → Bootstrap alert classes
from django.contrib.messages import constants as messages_constants
MESSAGE_TAGS = {
    messages_constants.DEBUG: 'secondary',
    messages_constants.INFO: 'info',
    messages_constants.SUCCESS: 'success',
    messages_constants.WARNING: 'warning',
    messages_constants.ERROR: 'danger',  # ← Bootstrap: alert-danger (not alert-error!)
}

LOGIN_URL = '/accounts/login/'
LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL = '/notes/'

Why 'DIRS': [BASE_DIR / 'templates']? base.html and layouts/dashboard.html are global templates, not tied to an app. Django looks for templates in two places: DIRS (global) and APP_DIRS (inside each app).

docs.title: Step 2 — base.html
docs.text:
Location: crispy_notes_project/templates/base.html

base.html is the HTML skeleton. It contains ONLY: - DOCTYPE, <head>, <body> - Bootstrap 5 CDN - Bootstrap Icons CDN - Global CSS - A single {% block body %} — the whole application goes here

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="uk">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>CrispyNotes</title>

  <!-- Bootstrap 5 CSS -->
  <link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css" rel="stylesheet">
  <!-- Bootstrap Icons -->
  <link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/font/bootstrap-icons.min.css" rel="stylesheet">
</head>
<body>

  {% block body %}{% endblock %}    ← the whole application goes here

  <!-- Bootstrap JS -->
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js"></script>
</body>
</html>

Rule: base.html knows nothing about the sidebar, navigation, or content. It is responsible only for: "I am a correct HTML5 document with Bootstrap".

docs.title: Step 3 — layouts/dashboard.html
docs.text:
Location: crispy_notes_project/templates/layouts/dashboard.html

Level 2 of the hierarchy. It: - Extends base.html - Fills {% block body %} with the full Dashboard markup - Provides two slots for child templates: - {% block topbar_title %} — the title in the topbar - {% block content %} — the main page content

{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% load static %}

{% block body %}
<div class="d-flex vh-100 overflow-hidden">

  <!-- ════════════════════ SIDEBAR ════════════════════ -->
  <nav id="sidebar" class="sidebar d-flex flex-column p-3 text-bg-dark" style="width: 260px;">

    <!-- Brand -->
    <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}" class="d-flex align-items-center text-white mb-3">
      <i class="bi bi-journal-text fs-4 me-2"></i>
      <span class="fs-5 fw-semibold">CrispyNotes</span>
    </a>
    <hr>

    <!-- NOTES section -->
    <p class="sidebar-label text-uppercase fw-semibold mb-1 px-2">Нотатки</p>
    <ul class="nav nav-pills flex-column mb-3">
      <li>
        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:notebook_list' %}"
           class="nav-link {% if 'notebook' in request.resolver_match.url_name %}active{% endif %}">
          <i class="bi bi-collection me-2"></i>Записники
        </a>
      </li>
      <li>
        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}"
           class="nav-link {% if request.resolver_match.url_name == 'note_list' %}active{% endif %}">
          <i class="bi bi-journal-text me-2"></i>Всі нотатки
        </a>
      </li>
      <li>
        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_create' %}"
           class="nav-link {% if request.resolver_match.url_name == 'note_create' %}active{% endif %}">
          <i class="bi bi-plus-circle me-2"></i>Нова нотатка
        </a>
      </li>
    </ul>

    <!-- TASKS section -->
    <p class="sidebar-label text-uppercase fw-semibold mb-1 px-2">Задачі</p>
    <ul class="nav nav-pills flex-column mb-3">
      <li>
        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:todo_list' %}"
           class="nav-link d-flex justify-content-between {% if 'todo' in request.resolver_match.url_name %}active{% endif %}">
          <span><i class="bi bi-check2-square me-2"></i>Список справ</span>
          {% if sidebar_todo_count %}
          <span class="badge bg-primary rounded-pill">{{ sidebar_todo_count }}</span>
          {% endif %}
        </a>
      </li>
      <li>
        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:shopping_list' %}"
           class="nav-link d-flex justify-content-between {% if 'shopping' in request.resolver_match.url_name %}active{% endif %}">
          <span><i class="bi bi-cart me-2"></i>Покупки</span>
          {% if sidebar_shopping_count %}
          <span class="badge bg-secondary rounded-pill">{{ sidebar_shopping_count }}</span>
          {% endif %}
        </a>
      </li>
    </ul>
    <hr>

    <!-- Notebooks (a list, from sidebar_context — a context processor!) -->
    {% if sidebar_notebooks %}
    <p class="sidebar-label text-uppercase fw-semibold mb-1 px-2">Записники</p>
    <ul class="nav nav-pills flex-column mb-3">
      {% for nb in sidebar_notebooks %}

           class="nav-link py-1 d-flex justify-content-between">

          <span class="badge bg-secondary">{{ nb.note_count }}</span>

      {% for tag in sidebar_tags %}

      {% endfor %}

    {% endif %}

        </a>

  </nav>
  <!-- /SIDEBAR -->

  <!-- ════════════════════ MAIN ════════════════════ -->
  <div class="d-flex flex-column flex-grow-1 overflow-auto">

    <!-- TOPBAR: title | search | user dropdown -->
    <header class="topbar d-flex align-items-center px-4 py-2">
      <h6 class="mb-0 me-auto fw-semibold">
        {% block topbar_title %}Нотатки{% endblock %}   ← child templates fill in the title
      </h6>
      <form class="d-flex me-3" method="get" action="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}">
        <input type="search" name="q" class="form-control form-control-sm" placeholder="Пошук нотаток...">
        <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary ms-1" type="submit">
          <i class="bi bi-search"></i>
        </button>
      </form>
      <!-- Profile / Logout (dropdown on the right) -->
      <div class="dropdown">
        <a href="#" class="d-flex align-items-center text-decoration-none dropdown-toggle"
           data-bs-toggle="dropdown">
          <i class="bi bi-person-circle fs-5 me-1"></i>
          <span class="small fw-semibold">{{ request.user.username }}</span>
        </a>
        <ul class="dropdown-menu dropdown-menu-dark dropdown-menu-end shadow">
          <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="{% url 'hello_app:notebook_list' %}">Мої записники</a></li>
          <li><hr class="dropdown-divider"></li>
          <li>
            <form method="post" action="{% url 'logout' %}">
              {% csrf_token %}
              <button type="submit" class="dropdown-item text-danger">Вийти</button>
            </form>
          </li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </header>

    <!-- Django Messages → Bootstrap Alerts -->
    {% if messages %}
    <div class="px-4 pt-3">
      {% for message in messages %}
      <div class="alert alert-{{ message.tags }} alert-dismissible fade show">
        {{ message }}
        <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-bs-dismiss="alert"></button>
      </div>
      {% endfor %}
    </div>
    {% endif %}

    <!-- PAGE CONTENT -->
    <main class="flex-grow-1 p-4">
      {% block content %}{% endblock %}   ← child templates fill in the content
    </main>

  </div>
  <!-- /MAIN -->

</div>
{% endblock %}

docs.text:
Goal: show what Django provides "out of the box", without any styles.

Tier 1 is implemented in notes_project — the forms there have no crispy. The code below is for comparing the concepts.

# views.py
@login_required
def note_create_raw(request):

docs.title: Step 6 — Tier 2: Manual
docs.text:
Goal: show the full Bootstrap HTML — to understand what Tier 3 saves you from.

Tier 2 is implemented in django_bootstrap_project — the forms there use manual Bootstrap HTML. The code below is for comparing the concepts.

<!-- note_form_manual.html — look how much code there is for ONE field -->
<form method="post">
  {% csrf_token %}

  <!-- Field: title  ← 14 lines of HTML for just one field -->
  <div class="mb-3">
    <label for="{{ form.title.id_for_label }}" class="form-label fw-semibold">
      {{ form.title.label }}
      {% if form.title.field.required %}<span class="text-danger">*</span>{% endif %}
    </label>
    <input type="text"
           name="{{ form.title.html_name }}"
           id="{{ form.title.id_for_label }}"
           value="{{ form.title.value|default:'' }}"
           placeholder="Назва нотатки..."
           class="form-control {% if form.title.errors %}is-invalid{% endif %}"
           autofocus>
    {% if form.title.errors %}
      {% for error in form.title.errors %}
      <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ error }}</div>
      {% endfor %}
    {% endif %}
  </div>

  <!-- ... another ~65 lines for priority, notebook, content, tags, is_pinned ... -->

  <button type="submit" class="btn btn-secondary">Зберегти</button>
</form>

Line count: 

title:     14 lines
priority:  12 lines (select)
notebook:  14 lines (select + queryset)
content:   12 lines (textarea)
tags:      14 lines (multiple select)
is_pinned: 10 lines (checkbox)
buttons:    3 lines
─────────────────
TOTAL:    ~80 lines of HTML just for the form

Multiply by 5 forms in the application → 400 lines of duplication. Changed the Bootstrap version → you edit 400 lines.

docs.title: Step 7 — Tier 3: Crispy
docs.text: Goal: replace 80 lines of HTML with 10 lines of Python.

docs.title: forms.py — the full NoteForm code
docs.text:
# hello_app/forms.py
from django import forms
from crispy_forms.helper import FormHelper
from crispy_forms.layout import (
    Layout, Submit, Row, Column,
    Fieldset, HTML, Div, Field
)
from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag


class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Note
        fields = ['title', 'content', 'priority', 'notebook', 'tags', 'is_pinned']
        # ↑ NO widget attrs at all — crispy adds the Bootstrap classes automatically!

    def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        # Security: filter the FK by the current user
        if user is not None:
            self.fields['notebook'].queryset = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user)
            self.fields['tags'].queryset = Tag.objects.filter(user=user)

        # FormHelper — describe the form in Python code
        self.helper = FormHelper()
        self.helper.form_method = 'post'
        self.helper.form_id = 'note-form'

        # Layout — the field structure
        self.helper.layout = Layout(
            # Section 1: basic information
            Fieldset('Основна інформація',
                Field('title', placeholder='Назва нотатки...', autofocus=True),
                Row(
                    Column('priority', css_class='col-md-4'),
                    Column('notebook', css_class='col-md-8'),
                ),
            ),
            # Section 2: content
            Fieldset('Зміст нотатки',
                Field('content', rows=8, placeholder='Текст нотатки...'),
            ),
            # Section 3: tags and options
            Fieldset('Теги та параметри',
                'tags',
                Div(Field('is_pinned'), css_class='form-check mt-2'),
            ),
            # Divider
            HTML('<hr class="my-4">'),
            # Buttons
            Submit('submit', 'Зберегти нотатку', css_class='btn btn-primary me-2'),
            HTML('<a href="javascript:history.back()" class="btn btn-outline-secondary">Скасувати</a>'),
        )

docs.title: note_form.html — the whole template
docs.text:
{% extends 'layouts/dashboard.html' %}
{% load crispy_forms_tags %}

{% block topbar_title %}{{ title }}{% endblock %}

{% block content %}
<div class="row">
  <div class="col-lg-8">
    <div class="card shadow-sm">
      <div class="card-header bg-primary text-white">
        <h6 class="mb-0"><i class="bi bi-journal-plus me-2"></i>{{ title }}</h6>
      </div>
      <div class="card-body">

        {% crispy form %}

        {# ↑ One tag instead of 80 lines of HTML.
           FormHelper + Layout in forms.py describe ALL the Bootstrap markup. #}

{% endblock %}

docs.title: What {% crispy form %} does, step by step
docs.text:
1. {% load crispy_forms_tags %} — registers the tag

2. {% crispy form %} — calls do_uni_form() in crispy_forms_tags.py

3. Finds form.helper — our FormHelper with the Layout

4. Renders form.helper.layout:
   ├── Fieldset('Основна інформація', ...) →
   │     <fieldset>
   │       <legend>Основна інформація</legend>
   │       ...fields...
   │     </fieldset>
   │
   ├── Field('title', placeholder='...') →
   │     <div class="mb-3">
   │       <label for="id_title" class="form-label">Заголовок *</label>
   │       <input type="text" name="title" id="id_title"
   │              class="form-control" placeholder="Назва нотатки..."
   │              autofocus>
   │     </div>
   │
   ├── Row(Column('priority', css_class='col-md-4'), ...) →
   │     <div class="row">
   │       <div class="col-md-4">...priority field...</div>
   │       <div class="col-md-8">...notebook field...</div>
   │     </div>
   │
   └── Submit('submit', 'Зберегти') →
         <input type="submit" value="Зберегти" class="btn btn-primary me-2">

5. Adds <form method="post"> and {% csrf_token %} automatically

docs.text:
# views.py — the view for Tier 3 is no different from Tier 2!
# Crispy is purely the PRESENTATION layer, not business logic.

@login_required
def note_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = services.create_note(
                user=request.user,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content=form.cleaned_data['content'],
                priority=form.cleaned_data['priority'],
                notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                tag_ids=[t.pk for t in form.cleaned_data.get('tags', [])],
                is_pinned=form.cleaned_data.get('is_pinned', False),
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" створено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(user=request.user)

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'title': 'Нова нотатка',
        'current_tier': 'crispy',
    })

Conclusion: services.create_note() is the same function as in notes_project. Crispy doesn't change the business logic. It only changes how the form looks.

docs.title: Pattern: form_tag = False — embedded forms
docs.text:
Sometimes a form is part of a larger page, not a separate page. For example: a task list + an inline form for adding a new task on the same page.

The problem: if the template already has <form action="/todo/5/items/add/">, and crispy also renders a <form> — you get a nested <form> — invalid HTML, and browsers ignore the inner <form>.

The solution: self.helper.form_tag = False — crispy renders only the fields and buttons, but not the <form>...</form> wrapper. The template provides the form tag itself.

# forms.py — TodoItemForm: embedded inside a <form> that exists in the template
class TodoItemForm(forms.Form):
    text = forms.CharField(max_length=500, label='Завдання')
    due_date = forms.DateField(required=False, widget=forms.DateInput(attrs={'type': 'date'}))

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.helper = FormHelper()
        self.helper.form_tag = False          # ← don't render <form>...</form>
        self.helper.form_show_labels = False  # ← no labels (compact look)
        self.helper.layout = Layout(
            Row(
                Column(Field('text', placeholder='Нове завдання...'), css_class='col-md-7'),
                Column(Field('due_date'), css_class='col-md-3'),
                Column(Submit('submit', '+ Додати', css_class='btn btn-primary w-100'),
                       css_class='col-md-2'),
            ),
        )

<!-- todo_detail.html — the template provides the <form> tag, crispy only the fields -->
<form method="post" action="{% url 'hello_app:todo_item_add' list.pk %}">
  {% csrf_token %}
  {% crispy item_form %}   ← renders a Row with fields and a button, but WITHOUT <form>
</form>
Scenario form_tag The form takes a separate page (note_create, note_edit) True (default) The form is embedded in a page (inline add item) False

docs.title: Step 8 — Context Processor
docs.text:
# hello_app/context_processors.py
from django.db import OperationalError
from django.db.models import Q
from .models import TodoList, ShoppingList
from . import selectors


def sidebar_context(request):
    """
    Automatically adds sidebar_notebooks, sidebar_tags and task counters to every template.
    Runs on every request for authenticated users.
    """
    if not request.user.is_authenticated:
        return {
            'sidebar_notebooks': [], 'sidebar_tags': [],
            'sidebar_todo_count': 0, 'sidebar_shopping_count': 0,
        }

    user = request.user

    # try/except — protection in case the migration hasn't been applied yet (new M2M tables)
    try:
        todo_count = TodoList.objects.filter(
            Q(user=user) | Q(shared_with=user), is_completed=False
        ).distinct().count()
        shopping_count = ShoppingList.objects.filter(
            Q(user=user) | Q(shared_with=user)
        ).distinct().count()
    except OperationalError:
        todo_count = 0
        shopping_count = 0

    return {
        'sidebar_notebooks': selectors.get_user_notebooks(user),
        'sidebar_tags': selectors.get_user_tags(user),
        'sidebar_todo_count': todo_count,       # ← badge on "Список справ"
        'sidebar_shopping_count': shopping_count,  # ← badge on "Покупки"
    }

Why try/except OperationalError? A context processor runs on every request. If the migration for a new table hasn't been applied yet (for example, during development after a git pull), the QuerySet will fail with OperationalError: no such table. The guard lets the server keep working — the counters simply return 0 instead of a 500 error.

Registration in settings.py: 

'context_processors': [
    'django.template.context_processors.request',
    'django.contrib.auth.context_processors.auth',
    'django.contrib.messages.context_processors.messages',
    'hello_app.context_processors.sidebar_context',   # ← ours
],

Usage in any template (without passing it from the View): 

{% for nb in sidebar_notebooks %}
  <a href="?notebook={{ nb.pk }}">{{ nb.title }}</a>
{% endfor %}

Important: A context processor runs on every HTTP request. So the selector must be efficient — select_related, annotate, no N+1.

docs.title: CrispyNotes — Django Authentication and Security
docs.text:
This tutorial walks you through the full security stack of a Django application: login/logout → password reset → object protection → groups for shared access.

The project is the same notes manager from the previous lesson (crispy forms + SaaS Dashboard). In this lesson we add security layers on top of a finished application. You will see how security is "woven into" real code rather than existing separately.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
Architectural foundation (read before the code) - 01 · AUTH BASICS — Authentication vs Authorization - 02 · SESSIONS — How Django remembers the user - 03 · PASSWORD SECURITY — Resetting and changing a password - 04 · OBJECT-LEVEL PERMISSIONS — Protection against IDOR - 05 · GROUP SHARING — Shared access via Django Groups - 06 · SECURITY SETTINGS — What and why

Step-by-step implementation 1. Step 0 — Running the project 2. Step 1 — Settings: auth + security 3. Step 2 — URLs: wiring up the built-in auth views 4. Step 3 — Login / Register templates 5. Step 4 — Password Reset Flow (5 templates) 6. Step 5 — Password Change 7. Step 6 — Object-Level Permissions in views.py 8. Step 7 — Models: Group FK 9. Step 8 — Selectors: Q-filter for group access 10. Step 9 — Services: Group CRUD 11. Step 10 — Group Views + URLs 12. Step 11 — Group Templates 13. Project file structure

docs.title: 01 · AUTH BASICS
docs.text:
The main question: Who are you and what are you allowed to do?

These two questions are the foundation of any security system. Django answers them with two different systems.

docs.title: Analogy — a passport and a concert ticket
docs.text:
• Passport = Authentication (AuthN): "Who are you?" — confirms identity. The security guard checks the document and makes sure it is genuine.
  • Ticket = Authorization (AuthZ): "Where are you allowed to go?" — defines rights. The cashier checks the ticket and decides where you can sit (VIP or the stalls).

At the airport: security checks your passport (AuthN), then your boarding pass (AuthZ). A passport without a ticket — you won't get in. A ticket without a passport — neither.

docs.title: Table: AuthN vs AuthZ
docs.text: Authentication (AuthN) Authorization (AuthZ) Question Who are you? What are you allowed to do? Answer Password check Permission check Django tool authenticate(), login() @login_required, get_object_or_404 Where it is checked AuthenticationMiddleware In each view separately What if it fails Form with an error 302 Redirect or 404/403

docs.title: Django Auth components
docs.text:
from django.contrib.auth import authenticate, login, logout
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required

# 1. Check credentials (AuthN):
user = authenticate(request, username='alice', password='secret')
# → Django: looks up a User with username='alice'
# → Checks the PBKDF2 password hash in the DB
# → Returns the User object if it matches, or None

# 2. Start a session after a successful login:
if user is not None:
    login(request, user)   # ← creates a session_id in the DB + a cookie in the browser
    # Now request.user = alice in all subsequent requests

# 3. End the session:
logout(request)   # ← deletes the session record from the DB + forcibly clears the cookie

docs.title: Middleware chain: who sets request.user
docs.text:
Every request passes through the ENTIRE middleware chain:

1. SecurityMiddleware       — HTTPS redirect, HTTP security headers
2. SessionMiddleware        — reads Cookie: sessionid=... → loads the session from the DB
3. CommonMiddleware         — trailing slash, Content-Type
4. CsrfViewMiddleware       — checks csrfmiddlewaretoken in POST
5. AuthenticationMiddleware — reads the session → sets request.user
   │                          If there is a session → request.user = User(id=42)
   │                          If not                → request.user = AnonymousUser
6. MessageMiddleware        — Django messages flash framework
7. XFrameOptionsMiddleware  — X-Frame-Options: DENY header
   │
   ▼
View function (request.user is already set!)

docs.title: @login_required — what it does and where it lives
docs.text:
# hello_app/views.py
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required

@login_required   # ← decorator, checks request.user.is_authenticated
def note_list(request):
    # If request.user = AnonymousUser:
    #   → redirect to LOGIN_URL (settings.py) + ?next=/notes/
    #   → 302 /accounts/login/?next=/notes/
    # If request.user = User(id=42):
    #   → runs the view normally
    notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user)
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_list.html', {'notes': notes})

# settings.py — where to redirect users who are not logged in:
LOGIN_URL = '/accounts/login/'
LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL = '/notes/'         # where to go AFTER a successful login
LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL = '/accounts/login/'  # where to go AFTER logout

Important: @login_required is only AuthN ("are you logged in?"). It does NOT check whether this particular note belongs to you. That requires a separate AuthZ step in the view.

docs.title: 02 · SESSIONS
docs.text: The problem: HTTP is a stateless protocol. Every request is as if it were the "first". The server does not know who you are unless you send proof.

docs.title: Analogy — a loyalty card at a café
docs.text:
Imagine a café where you earn points for every coffee. Without a card, the waiter forgets you after every visit. With a card, the points add up.

Session cookie = loyalty card: the browser stores it and automatically presents it with every request.

docs.title: Step-by-step flow: Login → Cookie → Next request
docs.text:
STEP 1: Alice clicks "Log in"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser:  POST /accounts/login/  {username: 'alice', password: 'secret'}
Django:   authenticate('alice', 'secret') → User(id=42) ✓
          login(request, user)
            → INSERT INTO django_session (session_key='xK9mPq', user_id=42, expire=...)
          Response: 302 /notes/
          Header:    Set-Cookie: sessionid=xK9mPq; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

STEP 2: The browser stores the cookie. Alice sees /notes/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser stores: sessionid=xK9mPq (in protected storage)

STEP 3: Alice's next request (/notes/)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser:  GET /notes/
Header:   Cookie: sessionid=xK9mPq   ← automatically!
          Django SessionMiddleware:
            SELECT * FROM django_session WHERE session_key='xK9mPq'
            → user_id = 42
          Django AuthenticationMiddleware:
            SELECT * FROM auth_user WHERE id=42
            → request.user = User(id=42, username='alice')
View:     request.user.is_authenticated → True ✓
          notes = Note.objects.filter(user=request.user)

STEP 4: Logging out (Logout)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser:  POST /accounts/logout/  (with the CSRF token)
Django:   logout(request)
            → DELETE FROM django_session WHERE session_key='xK9mPq'
          Response: 302 /accounts/login/
          Header:    Set-Cookie: sessionid=; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970...
Browser:  Deletes the cookie. request.user → AnonymousUser.

docs.title: Cookie settings in settings.py
docs.text:
# settings.py:

SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True
# ↑ JS cannot read sessionid via document.cookie
#   Protection against XSS attacks that try to steal the cookie

SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE = "Lax"
# ↑ "Lax": the cookie is sent only from the same site
#   Protection against CSRF (evil.com cannot send a request with your cookie)
#   "Strict" — stricter, but can break OAuth flows
#   "None" — dangerous without the Secure flag

CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = False
# ↑ False: JS can read csrftoken (needed for fetch/axios requests)
#   If you don't use JS for forms → True for strict protection

# Production HTTPS (uncomment when you have an SSL certificate):
# SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True   # cookie only over HTTPS
# CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True

docs.title: 03 · PASSWORD SECURITY
docs.text: Django provides a complete password management system "out of the box" via django.contrib.auth. You don't need to write a single view for login, logout, password reset or change.

docs.title: What include('django.contrib.auth.urls') wires up
docs.text:
# hello_project/urls.py:
path("accounts/", include("django.contrib.auth.urls")),

This automatically registers the following URLs:

URL View Name Template (you must create it) /accounts/login/ LoginView login registration/login.html /accounts/logout/ LogoutView logout (redirect) /accounts/password_change/ PasswordChangeView password_change registration/password_change_form.html /accounts/password_change/done/ PasswordChangeDoneView password_change_done registration/password_change_done.html /accounts/password_reset/ PasswordResetView password_reset registration/password_reset_form.html /accounts/password_reset/done/ PasswordResetDoneView password_reset_done registration/password_reset_done.html /accounts/reset/<uidb64>/<token>/ PasswordResetConfirmView password_reset_confirm registration/password_reset_confirm.html /accounts/reset/done/ PasswordResetCompleteView password_reset_complete registration/password_reset_complete.html

Conclusion: 8 URLs + 7 views = you only write the templates!

docs.title: Password Reset Flow — 5 steps
docs.text:
Step 1: /accounts/password_reset/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Alice forgot her password → enters her email in the form
→ password_reset_form.html

Step 2: Django processes the POST
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Django looks up a User with that email
Generates a unique token: sha1(user_pk + timestamp + SECRET_KEY)
Sends an email with the link:
  /accounts/reset/<uidb64>/<token>/

[DEV: email → console (EMAIL_BACKEND = console)]
[PROD: email → SMTP server]

Step 3: /accounts/password_reset/done/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Django shows: "Check your email"
→ password_reset_done.html

Step 4: /accounts/reset/<uidb64>/<token>/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Alice follows the link from the email
Django: checks the token (valid? 72 hours, single-use?)
If OK → form for the new password
→ password_reset_confirm.html

Step 5: Success → /accounts/reset/done/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Password saved (PBKDF2-hashed) → sessions reset
→ password_reset_complete.html

docs.title: Password Validators — Django protects against weak passwords
docs.text:
# settings.py — 4 built-in validators:
AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS = [
    # Is the password similar to the username / email / name?
    {"NAME": "django.contrib.auth.password_validation.UserAttributeSimilarityValidator"},
    # At least 8 characters (by default):
    {"NAME": "django.contrib.auth.password_validation.MinimumLengthValidator"},
    # Is it in the list of the 20,000 most common passwords? ("password", "123456"...)
    {"NAME": "django.contrib.auth.password_validation.CommonPasswordValidator"},
    # Does it consist only of digits?
    {"NAME": "django.contrib.auth.password_validation.NumericPasswordValidator"},
]

docs.title: 04 · OBJECT-LEVEL PERMISSIONS
docs.text: The most common vulnerability in web applications (OWASP A01): Broken Access Control — a user gains access to someone else's data.

docs.title: What IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) is
docs.text:
Alice is registered. She sees the URL of her note: /notes/42/edit/
She thinks: "What happens if I change 42 to 43?"
Alice navigates to: /notes/43/edit/
If the view doesn't check the owner → Alice edits BOB's note!

This is an IDOR attack — direct access to an object by ID without a permission check.

docs.title: The difference between AuthN and AuthZ (by example)
docs.text:
# PROBLEM: @login_required is only AuthN, not AuthZ!
@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)   # ← IDOR vulnerability!
    # Alice is logged in → @login_required lets her through
    # But note 43 belongs to Bob → Alice edits someone else's data!

# SOLUTION: add user= to get_object_or_404
@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)   # ← AuthZ ✓
    # pk=43 + user=Alice → Django looks for Note WHERE pk=43 AND user_id=Alice.id
    # No such record (43 belongs to Bob) → 404 for Alice

Golden rule: 

@login_required        = "are you logged in?"     (AuthN)
get_object_or_404(     = "is this object yours?"  (AuthZ)
    Note, pk=pk,
    user=request.user
)

docs.title: Pattern for your own objects
docs.text:
# Applies to: note_edit, note_delete, note_detail,
# notebook_edit, notebook_delete, shopping_edit, shopping_delete, etc.

@login_required
def note_delete(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
    #      ↑ If note.user != request.user → 404 (not 403, so as not to reveal that it exists)
    if request.method == 'POST':
        note.delete()
        messages.warning(request, 'Нотатку видалено.')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_list')
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

# For notes with a group — a more complex check:
from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied
from django.db.models import Q

@login_required
def note_detail(request, pk):
    user_groups = request.user.groups.all()
    note = get_object_or_404(
        Note.objects.filter(
            Q(user=request.user) | Q(group__in=user_groups)
        ),
        pk=pk
    )
    # Alice sees the note if:
    #   note.user == Alice (personal)
    #   OR note.group in Alice.groups.all() (group)
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_detail.html', {'note': note})

docs.title: 05 · GROUP SHARING
docs.text: The idea: Alice wants to share notes with her family. She creates the group "Family" and adds Bob to it. Notes tagged with this group are visible to both.

docs.title: Django's built-in Group model
docs.text:
Django already has a ready-made Group model in django.contrib.auth:

from django.contrib.auth.models import Group

# Every Group has:
#   id       — PK
#   name     — name ('Сімя', 'Команда', 'Клас')
#   users    — M2N relation to User (via django_auth_user_groups)
#   permissions — M2N relation to Permission (for role-based access — NOT our case)

# In our project we use Group for DATA SHARING,
# not for the Django Permission System.

docs.title: Q-filter: "mine or the group's"
docs.text:
# selectors.py — a clever query:
from django.db.models import Q

def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False, ...):
    user_groups = user.groups.all()   # all of Alice's groups
    qs = Note.objects.filter(
        Q(user=user) |               # own notes OR
        Q(group__in=user_groups),    # notes of groups where Alice is a member
        is_archived=archived,
    ).select_related('notebook', 'group').prefetch_related('tags')
    return qs.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')

Alice is in the groups: [Сімя(id=1), Робота(id=3)]

SQL (simplified):
  SELECT * FROM note
  WHERE (user_id = 42)                          -- Alice's personal ones
     OR (group_id IN (1, 3))                    -- notes of her groups
  AND is_archived = FALSE
  ORDER BY is_pinned DESC, priority DESC, updated_at DESC

docs.title: 06 · SECURITY SETTINGS
docs.text: Django has many security settings. Most of them are "off" by default so as not to break localhost development. In production they must be turned on.

docs.title: Table: each setting and what it protects against
docs.text: Setting Value What it protects against SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True JS doesn't read the cookie XSS attacks for session hijacking SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE = "Lax" Cookie only from the same site CSRF via cross-site forms CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = False JS reads csrftoken (False = for fetch/axios) X_FRAME_OPTIONS = "DENY" Bans <iframe> Clickjacking attacks SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF = True Don't "guess" MIME XSS via forged files DEBUG = False Hides stack traces Leaking SECRET_KEY and code ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['mysite.com'] Only this domain HTTP Host header attacks

docs.title: What leaks with DEBUG = True in production
docs.text:
A server error with DEBUG=True shows:
  ✗ The full stack trace (file paths, function names)
  ✗ The values of ALL local variables at the moment of the error
  ✗ SECRET_KEY (a leak = anyone can forge session cookies!)
  ✗ All SQL queries are kept in memory → memory leak
  ✗ INSTALLED_APPS, DATABASES, MIDDLEWARE — the whole config is visible

Rule: DEBUG = False ALWAYS in production.

docs.title: Production HTTPS (uncomment on the server)
docs.text:
# settings.py — commented out in dev, enable in production:

# SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True
# ↑ The cookie is sent ONLY over HTTPS (not over HTTP)
# Without this, a man-in-the-middle attacker can intercept sessionid

# CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True
# ↑ The same for the CSRF cookie

# SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True
# ↑ Any HTTP request → 301 Moved Permanently → HTTPS

# SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 31536000  # 1 year
# ↑ The browser remembers: this site is HTTPS ONLY, never HTTP
# (Strict-Transport-Security header)

docs.title: Step 6 — Object-Level Permissions
docs.text:
The pattern is applied in every view that takes a pk parameter.

# hello_app/views.py — the general pattern for your OWN objects:

@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    # get_object_or_404 with user=request.user:
    #   1. Looks for Note WHERE pk=<pk> AND user_id=<request.user.id>
    #   2. If not found → 404 (not 403! — we don't reveal that the object exists)
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            cd = form.cleaned_data
            services.update_note(
                note,
                title=cd['title'],
                content=cd.get('content', ''),
                priority=cd.get('priority', note.priority),
                notebook=cd.get('notebook'),
                is_pinned=cd.get('is_pinned', False),
                tag_ids=[t.pk for t in cd.get('tags', [])],
            )
            messages.success(request, 'Нотатку оновлено.')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(instance=note, user=request.user)

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form, 'title': 'Редагування нотатки',
    })

# Before (vulnerable to IDOR):
note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)   # ← any pk!

# After (protected):
note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)  # ← only your own pk!

from django.contrib.auth.models import User, Group

class Note(models.Model):
    user = models.ForeignKey(
        User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='notes'

        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,  # ← if the group is deleted → the note becomes personal
        null=True,                   # ← NULL = personal note (by default)
        blank=True,                  # ← the field is optional in the form
        related_name='notes',
    )
    # ── the rest of the fields ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    content = models.TextField(blank=True)
    priority = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(default=1)

docs.title: Why SET_NULL and not CASCADE?
docs.text:
CASCADE: deleting a group → ALL of the group's notes are deleted
         → Alice deletes the group → Bob loses all shared notes!

SET_NULL: deleting a group → the notes remain, but become personal (group=NULL)
          → Alice deletes the group → the notes move to the owner's personal space
          → Bob sees that there are no more shared notes, but the original owners kept theirs

docs.title: Step 8 — Selectors
docs.text:
Location: hello_app/selectors.py

from django.db.models import Q, Count
from django.contrib.auth.models import Group


def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False, notebook=None, tag=None, search=None):
    """Returns the user's notes + notes of groups where they are a member."""
    user_groups = user.groups.all()
    qs = Note.objects.filter(
        Q(user=user) | Q(group__in=user_groups),   # ← the key Q-filter
        is_archived=archived,
    ).select_related('notebook', 'group').prefetch_related('tags')

    if notebook is not None:
        qs = qs.filter(notebook=notebook)
    if tag is not None:
        qs = qs.filter(tags=tag)
    if search:
        qs = qs.filter(Q(title__icontains=search) | Q(content__icontains=search))

    return qs.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')


def get_user_groups(user):
    """The user's groups with the member count (for display on group_list)."""
    return user.groups.annotate(
        member_count=Count('user')   # ← annotate = we add a member_count field to the queryset
    ).order_by('name')


def get_group_with_members(group_id, user):
    """Returns the group with its members ONLY if the user is a member of it."""
    try:
        group = Group.objects.prefetch_related('user_set').get(pk=group_id)
        # Membership check — if the user is not in the group → return None
        if not group.user_set.filter(pk=user.pk).exists():
            return None
        return group
    except Group.DoesNotExist:
        return None

from django.contrib.auth.models import Group, User


def create_group(*, name, creator):
    """Creates a group and automatically adds the creator as the first member."""
    group = Group.objects.create(name=name)
    group.user_set.add(creator)   # ← the creator becomes the first member
    return group


def add_user_to_group(group, username):
    """Adds a user to the group by username. Returns (True, '') or (False, 'message')."""
    try:
        user = User.objects.get(username=username)
    except User.DoesNotExist:
        return False, f'Користувача «{username}» не знайдено.'

    if group.user_set.filter(pk=user.pk).exists():
        return False, f'«{username}» вже є членом цієї групи.'

    group.user_set.add(user)
    return True, ''


def remove_user_from_group(group, user):
    """Removes a user from the group."""
    group.user_set.remove(user)


def delete_group(group):
    """Deletes the group. The group's notes become personal (group=NULL via SET_NULL)."""
    group.delete()
    # Django automatically performs SET_NULL for Note.group and ShoppingList.group

docs.text:
Location: hello_app/views.py

from django.contrib.auth.models import Group
from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied
from . import selectors, services
from .forms import GroupCreateForm, GroupAddMemberForm


@login_required
def group_list(request):
    """List of the groups the current user belongs to."""
    groups = selectors.get_user_groups(request.user)
    return render(request, 'hello_app/group_list.html', {'groups': groups})


@login_required
def group_create(request):
    """Creating a new group. The creator automatically becomes the first member."""
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = GroupCreateForm(request.POST)
        if form.is_valid():
            group = services.create_group(
                name=form.cleaned_data['name'],
                creator=request.user,       # ← request.user = the first member
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Групу «{group.name}» створено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:group_detail', pk=group.pk)
    else:
        form = GroupCreateForm()
    return render(request, 'hello_app/group_form.html', {
        'form': form, 'title': 'Нова група',
    })


@login_required
def group_detail(request, pk):
    """Group view: members, add/remove, leave."""
    group = selectors.get_group_with_members(pk, request.user)
    if group is None:
        raise Http404('Групу не знайдено або у вас немає доступу.')
    # ↑ If the user is not a member → Http404 (not 403, so as not to reveal that the group exists)

    add_form = GroupAddMemberForm()
    error = None

    if request.method == 'POST':
        action = request.POST.get('action')   # 'add' / 'remove' / 'leave'

        if action == 'add':
            add_form = GroupAddMemberForm(request.POST)
            if add_form.is_valid():
                ok, msg = services.add_user_to_group(
                    group, add_form.cleaned_data['username']
                )
                if ok:
                    messages.success(request, 'Користувача додано до групи.')
                    return redirect('hello_app:group_detail', pk=pk)
                else:
                    error = msg   # ← "Not found" or "already a member"

        elif action == 'remove':
            remove_pk = request.POST.get('user_pk')
            try:
                target = User.objects.get(pk=remove_pk)
                services.remove_user_from_group(group, target)
                messages.success(request, f'«{target.username}» видалено.')
            except User.DoesNotExist:
                pass
            return redirect('hello_app:group_detail', pk=pk)

        elif action == 'leave':
            services.remove_user_from_group(group, request.user)
            messages.info(request, f'Ви покинули групу «{group.name}».')
            return redirect('hello_app:group_list')

    return render(request, 'hello_app/group_detail.html', {
        'group': group,
        'members': group.user_set.all(),
        'add_form': add_form,
        'error': error,
    })


@login_required
def group_delete(request, pk):
    """Deleting a group (only if the user is a member)."""
    group = get_object_or_404(Group, pk=pk)
    if not group.user_set.filter(pk=request.user.pk).exists():
        raise PermissionDenied   # ← 403 (we know the group exists, but the user is not a member)
    if request.method == 'POST':
        name = group.name
        services.delete_group(group)
        messages.warning(request, f'Групу «{name}» видалено. Спільні нотатки стали особистими.')
        return redirect('hello_app:group_list')
    return render(request, 'hello_app/group_confirm_delete.html', {'group': group})

The key pattern in group_detail:

One view — three actions through a single POST:

action = request.POST.get('action')

'add'    → add a member by username
'remove' → remove a specific member (by user_pk)
'leave'  → the current user leaves the group

Why a single view? All the group logic is in one place — easier to read and maintain.

{% extends 'layouts/dashboard.html' %}
{% load crispy_forms_tags %}
{% block topbar_title %}Група: {{ group.name }}{% endblock %}
{% block content %}

<div class="row g-4">
  <!-- Member list -->
  <div class="col-md-6">
    <div class="card shadow-sm">
      <div class="card-header">
        <h6 class="mb-0">Учасники ({{ members.count }})</h6>
      </div>
      <ul class="list-group list-group-flush">
        {% for member in members %}
        <li class="list-group-item d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center">
          <span>
            {{ member.username }}
            {% if member == request.user %}
              <span class="badge bg-success ms-1">Ти</span>
            {% endif %}
          </span>
          {% if member != request.user %}
          <!-- Remove a member (action=remove) -->
          <form method="post">
            {% csrf_token %}
            <input type="hidden" name="action" value="remove">
            <input type="hidden" name="user_pk" value="{{ member.pk }}">
            <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-danger btn-sm">
              <i class="bi bi-x"></i>
            </button>
          </form>
          {% endif %}
        </li>
        {% endfor %}
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Actions: add a member, leave, delete -->
  <div class="col-md-6">
    <!-- Add a member (action=add) -->
    <div class="card shadow-sm mb-3">
      <div class="card-header"><h6 class="mb-0">Додати учасника</h6></div>
      <div class="card-body">
        {% if error %}<div class="alert alert-danger small">{{ error }}</div>{% endif %}
        <form method="post">
          {% csrf_token %}
          <input type="hidden" name="action" value="add">
          {% crispy add_form %}
        </form>
      </div>
    </div>

    <!-- Danger zone: leave or delete -->
    <div class="card border-danger shadow-sm">
      <div class="card-body">
        <h6 class="text-danger mb-3">Небезпечна зона</h6>
        <!-- Leave the group (action=leave) -->
        <form method="post" class="d-inline">
          {% csrf_token %}
          <input type="hidden" name="action" value="leave">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-danger btn-sm me-2"
                  onclick="return confirm('Покинути групу?')">
            Покинути групу
          </button>
        </form>
        <!-- Delete the group (separate URL) -->
        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:group_delete' group.pk %}"
           class="btn btn-danger btn-sm">
          Видалити групу
        </a>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

docs.title: CrispyNotes — Django Testing from A to Z
docs.text:
This tutorial walks you through the full testing stack of a Django application: unit tests → services → forms → integration (views) → E2E (Selenium).

The project is the same CrispyNotes from the previous lessons (crispy forms + auth + groups). In this lesson we write tests for an application that is already finished. You will see how each level of tests protects a different layer of the system.

Result: 129 tests — 123 pass + 6 Selenium

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
Theory (read before the code) - 01 · WHY TESTS — an alarm system instead of manual checking - 02 · THE PYRAMID — unit vs integration vs E2E - 03 · DJANGO TESTCASE — how it works under the hood - 04 · THE TEST DATABASE — isolation and rollback - 05 · THE AAA PATTERN — the structure of every test - 06 · READING THE OUTPUT — PASSED / FAILED / ERROR

What we test and why - 07 · MODELS — constraints, defaults, SET_NULL - 08 · SERVICES — business logic and security - 09 · FORMS — validation and queryset filtering - 10 · DJANGO TEST CLIENT — integration tests - 11 · SELENIUM — tests through the browser

Step-by-step implementation 1. Step 0 — Running the project 2. Step 1 — Structure of the tests/ package 3. Step 2 — test_models.py 4. Step 3 — test_services.py 5. Step 4 — test_forms.py 6. Step 5 — test_views.py 7. Step 6 — test_selenium.py 8. Step 7 — Running and understanding the results 9. Step 8 — GitHub Actions CI 10. File structure

docs.title: 01 · WHY TESTS
docs.text:
The main question: How do you know that nothing broke after your changes?

The answer without tests: run it manually, click around the site, hope for the best. The answer with tests: run one command and see everything in 30 seconds.

docs.title: Analogy — a fire alarm
docs.text:
A house without an alarm: you discover the fire when it's already burning. A house with an alarm: you learn about the spark BEFORE everything goes up in flames.

Tests = your code's alarm system. They check "is everything still correct" on every change.

WITHOUT TESTS                           WITH TESTS
──────────────────────────────────────  ──────────────────────────────────────
You write a new feature                 You write a new feature
You manually click through 10+ pages   You run: manage.py test
"Looks ok"                              FAIL: test_note_visible_only_to_owner
git push → deploy                       You see EXACTLY what broke
A week later: "Bug in production!"      You fix it BEFORE deploying
You turn detective — hunting the cause git push → deploy → all green

docs.title: A real scenario: you change selectors.py
docs.text:
# OLD version (correct):
def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False):
    user_groups = user.groups.all()
    return Note.objects.filter(
        Q(user=user) | Q(group__in=user_groups),   # ← own + group notes
        is_archived=archived,
    )

# NEW version after "refactoring" (bug!):
def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False):
    return Note.objects.filter(
        user=user,    # ← forgot the Q-filter for groups!
        is_archived=archived,
    )

Without tests: All group notes disappear for all users. Customers discover it a week after the production deployment.

With tests: test_selectors.py immediately reports: 

FAIL: test_group_notes_visible_to_members
AssertionError: <Note: Team meeting> not found in queryset for bob
You fix it in 2 minutes before committing.

docs.title: What else tests give you
docs.text: Benefit Explanation Documentation test_create_notebook_default_unsets_previous_default explains the invariant better than a comment Fearless refactoring You changed the implementation → the tests confirm the behavior is the same Finding edge cases While writing a test you think: "what if it's None? what if it's empty?" Protection against regressions Bug fixed + test written = the bug never comes back Security checks test_notebook_queryset_excludes_other_user_notebooks — IDOR is impossible

docs.title: 02 · THE TESTING PYRAMID
docs.text:
Not all tests are equal. Different levels have different costs and speeds.

              ╱╲
             ╱E2E╲          Selenium, Playwright
            ╱──────╲        Real browser, full scenario
           ╱ Integr. ╲      Slow (seconds/test), brittle
          ╱────────────╲    Django Test Client: requests → DB → response
         ╱     Unit      ╲  Medium (100ms/test)
        ╱──────────────────╲ pytest/TestCase: function → result
       ╱────────────────────╲ Fast (1-10ms/test), reliable

      70% Unit | 20% Integration | 10% E2E

    new = services.create_notebook(user=alice, title='New', is_default=True)
    old.refresh_from_db()

docs.title: 03 · DJANGO TESTCASE
docs.text: django.test.TestCase is unittest.TestCase + Django magic.

docs.title: What makes Django TestCase different
docs.text:
import unittest
from django.test import TestCase

# unittest.TestCase — basic, no DB
class PureUnitTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_math(self):
        assert 2 + 2 == 4   # OK, no DB

# django.test.TestCase — with the full Django stack
class DjangoTest(TestCase):
    def test_with_db(self):
        user = User.objects.create_user('alice')  # ← requires the test DB
        self.assertEqual(user.username, 'alice')

docs.title: What Django TestCase gives you automatically
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Before ALL tests of the class:                                 │
│    → Creates the test DB in memory                              │
│    → Applies all migrations                                     │
│                                                                 │
│  Before EACH test:                                              │
│    → Opens a transaction                                        │
│    → Calls setUp()                                              │
│                                                                 │
│    ┌─── THE TEST RUNS ─────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│    │  User.objects.create(...)  ← records in the test DB   │   │
│    │  Note.objects.create(...)  ← isolated from the real one│  │
│    └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                                 │
│  After EACH test:                                               │
│    → ROLLBACK of the transaction (all records disappear!)       │
│    → Calls tearDown()                                           │
│                                                                 │
│  After ALL tests:                                               │
│    → Deletes the test DB                                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Why rollback is a good thing
docs.text:
class MyTest(TestCase):
    def test_first(self):
        User.objects.create_user('alice')    # ← alice EXISTS
        self.assertEqual(User.objects.count(), 1)
        # After the test → ROLLBACK → alice is gone

    def test_second(self):
        # alice does NOT exist — every test starts from a clean state
        self.assertEqual(User.objects.count(), 0)  # ← 0, not 1!

Without rollback tests would affect each other: - test 1 creates alice → test 2 sees alice → results are unpredictable - The order in which tests run would affect the result

With rollback every test is isolated → the result does not depend on the order.

docs.title: setUp — preparation before each test
docs.text:
class NoteServiceTest(TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        """Runs BEFORE each test. The DB is clean."""
        self.alice = User.objects.create_user('alice', password='pass123')
        self.bob   = User.objects.create_user('bob',   password='pass123')
        # These users will exist in every test of this class
        # After each test → ROLLBACK → they disappear → the next setUp creates them again

    def test_something(self):
        # self.alice and self.bob already exist here
        note = services.create_note(user=self.alice, title='Test')
        ...

docs.title: 04 · THE TEST DATABASE
docs.text: The most important rule: Tests never touch your working DB.

docs.title: How Django creates the test DB
docs.text:
$ python manage.py test hello_app.tests

Creating test database for alias 'default' ...
#  ↑ Django creates test_<db_name> or an in-memory one (SQLite)
#    All the data is there — not in your db.sqlite3!

Found 82 test(s).
...

Destroying test database for alias 'default' ...
#  ↑ The test DB is deleted after completion

docs.title: Three kinds of isolation at once
docs.text:
1. ISOLATION FROM THE REAL DB:
   db.sqlite3 (your working one) ≠ test DB (separate, temporary)
   Tests cannot break your real data.

2. ISOLATION BETWEEN TESTS:
   Each test — its own transaction → rollback.
   Test A does not see Test B's data.

3. ISOLATION FROM EXTERNAL SYSTEMS:
   Email: EMAIL_BACKEND = console (not actually sent)
   Files: not changed in production
   API: needs a mock (unittest.mock.patch)

docs.title: 05 · THE AAA PATTERN
docs.text:
Every test has three distinct parts. This is the standard in all languages.

def test_create_note_assigns_tags(self):

    # ── ARRANGE: preparing the state ──────────────────────────────────────
    # What does the test need? We create the minimal required state.
    tag1 = Tag.objects.create(user=self.alice, name='work')
    tag2 = Tag.objects.create(user=self.alice, name='python')

    # ── ACT: we perform what we are testing ──────────────────────────────
    # One call — one action. What exactly are we testing? Only this.
    note = services.create_note(
        user=self.alice, title='Tagged', tag_ids=[tag1.id, tag2.id]
    )

    # ── ASSERT: we check the result ──────────────────────────────────────
    # What must be true after Act? We check specifically.
    note_tags = list(note.tags.all())
    self.assertIn(tag1, note_tags)
    self.assertIn(tag2, note_tags)

docs.title: Rules of a good test
docs.text: Rule Explanation One test — one behavior test_create_note_sets_user ≠ test_create_note_saves_to_db Name = specification test_add_user_to_group_duplicate_returns_false — the name explains everything Independence A test does not depend on the order or on other tests Speed A unit test < 50ms. If it's slow — check whether you're making unnecessary queries Determinism The same test under the same conditions = the same result

How to read a failed test:

File "tests/test_services.py", line 179
 ↑ Where exactly in the file

self.assertFalse(old_default.is_default)
AssertionError: True is not false
 ↑ We expected False, got True
   → The old default was NOT reset
   → The bug is in services.create_notebook()
