docs.title: Class-Based Views (CBV)
docs.text:
Chapter structure: first, complete working FBVs (function-based views) for note CRUD. Then — how duplication appears when Notebook views are added. Then — CBV as an upgrade: the same result, less code.

What changes in the transition: only views.py and urls.py. models, forms, selectors, services, templates — no changes at all.

docs.title: Part 1 — Complete FBV code (working code)
docs.text:
Here is the real working views code for notes. Read it as the "starting point" — everything works here.

# notes_app/views.py — Function-Based Views for notes
from django.shortcuts import render, redirect, get_object_or_404
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.contrib import messages
from django.http import Http404
from django.db.models import Q

from . import forms, services, selectors
from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag


@login_required
def note_list(request):
    # Parse GET parameters for filtering
    search = request.GET.get('q', '').strip()
    tag_id = request.GET.get('tag')
    notebook_id = request.GET.get('notebook')

    # Validate the ids — check access rights
    tag = None
    if tag_id:
        try:
            tag = Tag.objects.get(id=int(tag_id), user=request.user)  # user=! reject other users' tags
        except (Tag.DoesNotExist, ValueError):
            pass

    notebook = None
    if notebook_id:
        try:
            notebook = Notebook.objects.get(id=int(notebook_id), user=request.user)
        except (Notebook.DoesNotExist, ValueError):
            pass

    # Delegate reading to a selector
    notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user, search=search or None, tag=tag, notebook=notebook)
    notebooks = selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user)
    tags = selectors.get_user_tags(request.user)

    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_list.html', {
        'notes': notes,
        'notebooks': notebooks,
        'tags': tags,
        'search': search,
        'active_tag': tag,
        'active_notebook': notebook,
    })


@login_required
def note_detail(request, pk):
    try:
        note = selectors.get_note_detail(request.user, pk)
    except Note.DoesNotExist:
        raise Http404("Нотатку не знайдено")

    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_detail.html', {'note': note})


@login_required
def note_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = forms.NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            tags = form.cleaned_data.get('tags')
            tag_ids = [t.id for t in tags] if tags else None
            note = services.create_note(
                user=request.user,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', 1),
                notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                tag_ids=tag_ids,
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" створено!')
            return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = forms.NoteForm(user=request.user)

    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'title': 'Нова нотатка',
        'action': 'Створити',
    })


@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    # get_object_or_404 — get the note or 404 (Alice cannot see Bob's notes)
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = forms.NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            tags = form.cleaned_data.get('tags')
            tag_ids = [t.id for t in tags] if tags else []
            services.update_note(
                note,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', note.priority),
                notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                is_pinned=form.cleaned_data.get('is_pinned', note.is_pinned),
                tag_ids=tag_ids,
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" оновлено!')
            return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = forms.NoteForm(instance=note, user=request.user)

    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'note': note,
        'title': f'Редагувати: {note.title}',
        'action': 'Зберегти зміни',
    })


@login_required
def note_delete(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        title = note.title
        services.delete_note(note)
        messages.warning(request, f'Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
        return redirect('notes_app:note_list')

    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

# notes_app/urls.py — FBV url config
from django.urls import path
from . import views

app_name = 'notes_app'

urlpatterns = [
    path('notes/', views.note_list, name='note_list'),
    path('notes/new/', views.note_create, name='note_create'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/', views.note_detail, name='note_detail'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/edit/', views.note_edit, name='note_edit'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/delete/', views.note_delete, name='note_delete'),
]

This code works completely. For many projects it is enough. So when does the need for CBV arise?

docs.title: Part 2 — The problem: duplication when adding Notebook views
docs.text:
Let's add CRUD for notebooks. Compare the code:

# Notebook views — the same pattern, again and again:

@login_required
def notebook_list(request):
    notebooks = selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user)
    return render(request, 'notes_app/notebook_list.html', {'notebooks': notebooks})


@login_required
def notebook_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':          # ← the same if POST/else
        form = NotebookForm(request.POST)
        if form.is_valid():               # ← the same is_valid() check
            notebook = services.create_notebook(
                user=request.user,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                color=form.cleaned_data.get('color', '#4A90E2'),
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Записник "{notebook.title}" створено!')
            return redirect('notes_app:notebook_list')
    else:
        form = NotebookForm()

    return render(request, 'notes_app/notebook_form.html', {'form': form})


@login_required
def notebook_edit(request, pk):
    notebook = get_object_or_404(Notebook, pk=pk, user=request.user)  # ← the same auth check!
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NotebookForm(request.POST, instance=notebook)
        if form.is_valid():
            services.update_notebook(notebook, **form.cleaned_data)
            messages.success(request, f'Записник "{notebook.title}" оновлено!')
            return redirect('notes_app:notebook_list')
    else:
        form = NotebookForm(instance=notebook)
    return render(request, 'notes_app/notebook_form.html', {'form': form, 'notebook': notebook})


@login_required
def notebook_delete(request, pk):
    notebook = get_object_or_404(Notebook, pk=pk, user=request.user)  # ← the same thing again!
    if request.method == 'POST':
        services.delete_notebook(notebook)
        messages.warning(request, f'Записник "{notebook.title}" видалено.')
        return redirect('notes_app:notebook_list')
    return render(request, 'notes_app/notebook_confirm_delete.html', {'notebook': notebook})

Repetition table:

Note views        Notebook views    Tag views
─────────────     ──────────────    ─────────
@login_required   @login_required   @login_required   ← 3 times
if method POST    if method POST    if method POST    ← 3 times
is_valid()        is_valid()        is_valid()        ← 3 times
get_object_or_404 get_object_or_404 (forgotten!)      ← a security hole

If you forget get_object_or_404(Notebook, user=request.user) in one place →
  Alice sees/edits Bob's notebooks.

The problem is not the number of lines, it is security. The get_object_or_404(Model, pk=pk, user=request.user) pattern is an access-rights check. If you repeat it by hand 12 times (5 Note + 5 Notebook + Tag + ...), there is a risk of forgetting it in one place.

The solution: CBV with UserQuerySetMixin — the access check is described once.

docs.title: Part 3 — CBV as an upgrade: less code, the same result
What CBVs are and why
docs.text:
FBV (Function-Based Views) — a view as a function:

def note_list(request):
    notes = Note.objects.filter(user=request.user)
    return render(request, 'note_list.html', {'notes': notes})

CBV (Class-Based Views) — a view as a class:

class NoteListView(LoginRequiredMixin, ListView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_list.html'
    context_object_name = 'notes'

docs.title: Why CBV?
docs.text:
Problem with FBV Solution with CBV @login_required has to be put on every function LoginRequiredMixin once in the class Note.objects.filter(user=request.user) is repeated in 5 places UserQuerySetMixin.get_queryset() — once if request.method == 'POST': form = ...; if form.is_valid(): ... — boilerplate code CreateView/UpdateView do this automatically No standard way to extend the logic We override hooks: get_queryset(), form_valid(), get_context_data()

Important: CBVs do not replace the architecture. Selectors/Services stay where they were — only the calls moved from functions into class methods.

docs.title: Why you cannot put a class directly into urls.py
docs.text:
The Django router expects a callable (a function):

# ❌ DOES NOT WORK — NoteListView is a class, not a callable
path('notes/', views.NoteListView, name='note_list')

# ✅ CORRECT — .as_view() returns a callable wrapper function
path('notes/', views.NoteListView.as_view(), name='note_list')

docs.title: What as_view() does
docs.text:
as_view() is a classmethod that Django calls once when the server starts. It returns an ordinary wrapper function view. On every HTTP request this function:

  1. Creates a new instance of the class (a new one every time — thread-safe!)
  2. Copies request, args, kwargs onto the instance
  3. Calls instance.dispatch(request, *args, **kwargs)
# Simplified pseudocode of what as_view() does inside Django:
@classmethod
def as_view(cls, **initkwargs):
    def view(request, *args, **kwargs):
        self = cls(**initkwargs)          # 1. a new instance
        self.request = request            # 2. copy the request
        self.args = args
        self.kwargs = kwargs
        return self.dispatch(request, *args, **kwargs)  # 3. dispatch
    return view

docs.title: What dispatch() does
docs.text:
dispatch() is the main router of a CBV. It looks at the HTTP method of the request and delegates the call to the corresponding method of the class:

# Pseudocode of dispatch() from the base View:
def dispatch(self, request, *args, **kwargs):
    method = request.method.lower()          # 'get', 'post', 'put', ...
    handler = getattr(self, method, None)    # self.get, self.post, ...
    if handler:
        return handler(request, *args, **kwargs)
    return HttpResponseNotAllowed(...)       # 405 Method Not Allowed

docs.title: Sequence diagram: from the browser request to the method
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Б as Browser
    participant U as urls.py
    participant AV as as_view() wrapper
    participant D as dispatch()
    participant M as get() or post()

    Б->>U: GET /notes/
    U->>AV: view(request)
    AV->>AV: self = NoteListView()
    AV->>D: dispatch(request)
    D->>D: method = 'get'
    D->>M: self.get(request)
    M-->>Б: HttpResponse (HTML)

docs.title: Step 2 — Generic Views: the hierarchy
docs.text: Django ships ready-made CBVs for typical CRUD operations — Generic Views.

docs.title: Class hierarchy
docs.text:
graph TD
    V[View] --> TV[TemplateView]
    V --> LV[ListView]
    V --> DV[DetailView]
    V --> FV[FormView]
    FV --> CV[CreateView]
    FV --> UV[UpdateView]
    FV --> DEL[DeleteView]

    classDef step     fill:#eceff1,stroke:#546e7a,stroke-width:1px;
    classDef success  fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32,stroke-width:2px;

    class V,FV step;

docs.title: What each Generic View does automatically
docs.text: Generic View GET POST Key attributes TemplateView renders the template — template_name ListView gets the list via get_queryset(), renders — model, template_name, context_object_name DetailView gets one object via get_object(), renders — model, template_name, context_object_name CreateView renders an empty form validates → form_valid() or form_invalid() model, form_class, template_name UpdateView renders the form with instance=object validates → form_valid() or form_invalid() the same + loads get_object() DeleteView renders the confirmation deletes → success_url model, template_name, success_url

docs.title: Class attributes instead of arguments
docs.text:
In FBVs, parameters were passed into the function or hardcoded inside it. In CBVs we declare them as class attributes:

class NoteListView(LoginRequiredMixin, ListView):
    model = Note                              # ← which model to use
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_list.html'  # ← which template to render
    context_object_name = 'notes'            # ← what to call the list in the template
                                             #   (instead of the default 'object_list')

docs.title: FBV: the @login_required decorator
docs.text:
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required

@login_required
def note_list(request):
    ...

docs.title: CBV: LoginRequiredMixin — first in the list of base classes
docs.text:
from django.contrib.auth.mixins import LoginRequiredMixin

class NoteListView(LoginRequiredMixin, ListView):
    ...

docs.title: Why the order in the parentheses is critical
docs.text:
Python determines the method lookup order through the MRO (Method Resolution Order). When Django calls dispatch(), Python looks it up along the MRO from left to right:

NoteListView → LoginRequiredMixin → ListView → View

LoginRequiredMixin.dispatch() checks authentication first — before ListView.dispatch() does anything at all.

# ✅ CORRECT: LoginRequiredMixin first → the auth check comes FIRST
class NoteListView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, ListView):
    ...

# ❌ WRONG: ListView first → the auth check comes AFTER the data is loaded
class NoteListView(UserQuerySetMixin, ListView, LoginRequiredMixin):
    ...

docs.title: Flowchart: the authentication check
docs.text:
flowchart TD

    R["Request arrived"] --> D["LoginRequiredMixin.dispatch"]

    D --> A{"Is the user authenticated?"}

    A -->|"yes"| C["super dispatch<br>ListView get"]

    A -->|"no"| L["redirect<br>/accounts/login/"]

    C --> T["renders the template"]

    classDef step     fill:#eceff1,stroke:#546e7a,stroke-width:1px;
    classDef decision fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1565c0,stroke-width:2px;
    classDef success  fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32,stroke-width:2px;
    classDef error    fill:#ffebee,stroke:#c62828,stroke-width:3px;

    class A decision;
    class C,T success;
    class L error;

By default the redirect is /accounts/login/?next=/notes/. You can change it via login_url and redirect_field_name on the class.

docs.title: The problem: duplicating the user filter
docs.text:
Without a mixin, every Detail, Update, Delete view has to repeat:

# In NoteDetailView:
queryset = Note.objects.filter(user=self.request.user)

# In NoteUpdateView:
queryset = Note.objects.filter(user=self.request.user)

# In NoteDeleteView:
queryset = Note.objects.filter(user=self.request.user)

This is not just code repetition — it is a security hole: if you forget it in one place, Alice will see Bob's notes.

docs.title: The solution: a custom mixin
docs.text:
class UserQuerySetMixin:
    """
    A mixin for automatically filtering the QuerySet by the current user.
    """
    def get_queryset(self):
        # super().get_queryset() → returns model.objects.all()
        # .filter(user=...) → restrict to this user's objects only
        return super().get_queryset().filter(user=self.request.user)

docs.title: How Django uses get_queryset() for protection
docs.text:
DetailView, UpdateView, DeleteView load the object via get_object():

# Pseudocode of get_object() in DetailView:
def get_object(self, queryset=None):
    queryset = self.get_queryset()        # ← our filtered queryset!
    pk = self.kwargs.get('pk')
    return queryset.get(pk=pk)           # SQL: WHERE id=pk AND user_id=current_user

If Alice tries to open Bob's note (/notes/42/): - get_queryset() returns Note.objects.filter(user=Alice) - get_object() does .get(pk=42) on this queryset - SQL: SELECT * FROM note WHERE id=42 AND user_id=<Alice_id> → nothing found - Django raises Note.DoesNotExist → Http404

Alice sees a 404, not Bob's data.

docs.title: MRO with UserQuerySetMixin
docs.text:
class NoteDetailView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, DetailView):
    ...

# Python MRO:
# NoteDetailView → LoginRequiredMixin → UserQuerySetMixin → DetailView → View
#
# When get_queryset() is called:
#   1. It finds UserQuerySetMixin.get_queryset()
#   2. super().get_queryset() → goes further → DetailView.get_queryset()
#   3. DetailView.get_queryset() → returns Note.objects.all()
#   4. UserQuerySetMixin adds .filter(user=self.request.user)
#   Result: Note.objects.all().filter(user=self.request.user)

docs.title: Step 5 — ListView: a list of notes with filters
docs.text:
class NoteListView(LoginRequiredMixin, ListView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_list.html'
    context_object_name = 'notes'   # instead of the default 'object_list'

docs.title: get_queryset() — which collection to return
docs.text:
In the FBV we read GET parameters directly in the function. In a CBV we do it in get_queryset() via self.request.GET:

def get_queryset(self):
    self._get_filters()       # parse GET params once (cache on self)
    return selectors.get_user_notes(
        self.request.user,
        search=self.search or None,
        tag=self.active_tag,
        notebook=self.active_notebook,
    )

The architecture is preserved: the selector does all the ORM logic. get_queryset() only delegates.

docs.title: get_context_data() — which data to pass to the template
docs.text:
ListView automatically adds to the context: - notes (or object_list) — the result of get_queryset() - page_obj — if there is pagination - is_paginated — a boolean

We extend the context via super():

def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
    self._get_filters()
    ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)   # ← already contains 'notes'!
    ctx['notebooks'] = selectors.get_user_notebooks(self.request.user)
    ctx['tags'] = selectors.get_user_tags(self.request.user)
    ctx['search'] = self.search
    ctx['active_tag'] = self.active_tag
    ctx['active_notebook'] = self.active_notebook
    return ctx

Always call super().get_context_data(**kwargs) and add to the dictionary — do not replace it.

docs.title: _get_filters() — a private helper for DRY
docs.text:
Both methods (get_queryset and get_context_data) need the same GET parameters. To avoid parsing them twice — a private helper with caching on self:

def _get_filters(self):
    if hasattr(self, '_filters_parsed'):   # already parsed earlier
        return
    self._filters_parsed = True

    self.search = self.request.GET.get('q', '').strip()

    tag_id = self.request.GET.get('tag')
    self.active_tag = None
    if tag_id:
        try:
            # check access rights! user=request.user
            self.active_tag = Tag.objects.get(id=int(tag_id), user=self.request.user)
        except (Tag.DoesNotExist, ValueError):
            pass   # invalid id → simply ignore it

docs.title: Step 6 — DetailView: object detail
docs.text:
class NoteDetailView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, DetailView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_detail.html'
    context_object_name = 'note'

docs.title: What DetailView does automatically
docs.text:
1. Reads pk from self.kwargs['pk'] (from the URL pattern <int:pk>)
  2. Calls get_object() → get_queryset().get(pk=pk)
  3. Passes the object to the template as 'note' (our context_object_name)
  4. Renders template_name
  5. If not found → 404 automatically

docs.title: Overriding get_object() for Prefetch
docs.text:
In our project the selector loads the note with Prefetch(to_attr='upcoming_reminders'). So we override get_object() to use the selector instead of the standard queryset.get(pk=pk):

def get_object(self, queryset=None):
    try:
        return selectors.get_note_detail(self.request.user, self.kwargs['pk'])
    except Note.DoesNotExist:
        raise Http404("Нотатку не знайдено")

docs.title: get_context_data() — adding reminders
docs.text:
def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
    ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
    # upcoming_reminders is set via Prefetch(to_attr=) in the selector
    ctx['reminders'] = getattr(self.object, 'upcoming_reminders', [])
    return ctx

self.object is the loaded object (always available after get_object()).

docs.title: Step 7 — CreateView and get_form_kwargs()
docs.text:
class NoteCreateView(LoginRequiredMixin, CreateView):
    model = Note
    form_class = NoteForm
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_form.html'

docs.title: What CreateView does automatically
docs.text:
GET request: 1. get_form() → form_class(**get_form_kwargs()) → an empty form 2. get_context_data() → adds {'form': form} 3. Renders the template

POST request: 1. get_form() → a form with data=request.POST 2. form.is_valid(): - True → calls form_valid(form) - False → calls form_invalid(form) → renders the template with errors

docs.title: The problem: how to pass user= into the form
docs.text: NoteForm.__init__ needs user= to filter the QuerySet for the notebook and tags fields.

docs.title: The solution: get_form_kwargs()
docs.text:
def get_form_kwargs(self):
    kwargs = super().get_form_kwargs()
    # super() returns: {'data': request.POST, 'files': request.FILES, ...}
    kwargs['user'] = self.request.user   # ← add user=
    return kwargs
    # Result: NoteForm(data=POST, files=FILES, user=request.user)

docs.title: get_initial() — initial values for the form
docs.text:
TagCreateView supports ?name=python — it pre-fills the field:

def get_initial(self):
    initial = super().get_initial()
    name = self.request.GET.get('name')
    if name:
        initial['name'] = name
    return initial

get_initial() returns a dictionary of initial values. CreateView passes them into the form as initial=.

docs.title: Step 8 — UpdateView: editing with an instance
docs.text:
class NoteUpdateView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, UpdateView):
    model = Note
    form_class = NoteForm
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_form.html'

docs.title: What UpdateView does automatically (compared with CreateView)
docs.text:
UpdateView does everything CreateView does, plus:

  • Before rendering on GET: loads the existing object via get_object()
  • Passes instance=object into the form → all fields are pre-filled
  • UserQuerySetMixin.get_queryset() → 404 if the object belongs to someone else

docs.title: get_form_kwargs() — passing user=
docs.text:
def get_form_kwargs(self):
    kwargs = super().get_form_kwargs()
    kwargs['user'] = self.request.user
    return kwargs
    # Result: NoteForm(data=POST, instance=note, user=request.user)

docs.title: get_context_data() — breadcrumbs
docs.text:
def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
    ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
    ctx['note'] = self.object           # for breadcrumbs in the template
    ctx['action'] = 'Зберегти зміни'
    ctx['title'] = f'Редагувати: {self.object.title}'
    return ctx

docs.title: Step 9 — DeleteView: safe deletion only via POST
docs.text:
class NoteDeleteView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, DeleteView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html'
    success_url = reverse_lazy('hello_app:note_list')
    context_object_name = 'note'

docs.title: Why DELETE only via POST?
docs.text:
Deleting via GET violates HTTP semantics:

GET /notes/42/delete/   ← Dangerous!
  • The browser may prefetch these URLs — it would delete without a click!
  • A search bot crawls links — it would delete every record!
  • <img src="/notes/42/delete/"> in an email — it would delete on opening!

DeleteView automatically requires POST for the actual deletion: - GET → renders the confirmation page ("Are you sure?") - POST → deletes and redirects

docs.title: form_valid() — the POST confirmation hook
docs.text:
def form_valid(self, form):
    note = self.get_object()
    title = note.title    # save it BEFORE deleting!
    services.delete_note(note)
    messages.warning(self.request, f'Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
    return redirect(self.success_url)

We save title before services.delete_note() — after deletion note.title may be unavailable.

docs.title: Option 1: success_url — a static URL
docs.text:
class NoteDeleteView(..., DeleteView):
    success_url = reverse_lazy('hello_app:note_list')

Why reverse_lazy and not reverse()?

success_url = reverse('hello_app:note_list') is executed when the class is loaded (when Django starts), before the URL patterns are registered. This leads to NoReverseMatch.

reverse_lazy('hello_app:note_list') is executed lazily, only when the attribute is actually needed (during a request). By then the URL patterns are already registered.

docs.title: Option 2: get_success_url() — a dynamic URL
docs.text:
# In TagCreateView: we support the ?next= parameter
def get_success_url(self):
    return self._get_next_url()

def _get_next_url(self):
    return (
        self.request.GET.get('next')     # ?next= in GET
        or self.request.POST.get('next') # next in the POST form
        or 'hello_app:note_create'       # default if there is none
    )

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: success_url get_success_url() When the static URL is known in advance the URL depends on the object or the request Example the list of notebooks the detail of a just-created note reverse_lazy required not needed (called during the request)

docs.title: form_valid() instead of form.save()
docs.text:
Key rule: if you have services.py, never call super().form_valid() in CreateView/UpdateView — inside it there is form.save(), which bypasses your business logic.

class NoteCreateView(LoginRequiredMixin, CreateView):
    ...

    def form_valid(self, form):
        # ❌ WE DO NOT DO THIS: super().form_valid(form) → form.save() is in there!

        # ✅ DELEGATE to a service — transaction.atomic() and business rules live there
        tags = form.cleaned_data.get('tags')
        tag_ids = [t.id for t in tags] if tags else None

        note = services.create_note(
            user=self.request.user,
            title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
            content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
            priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', 1),
            notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
            tag_ids=tag_ids,
        )
        messages.success(self.request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" створено!')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)

docs.title: Full table of hooks
docs.text: Hook Where we override it What for get_queryset() ListView, UserQuerySetMixin which collection to return get_object() NoteDetailView loading with Prefetch via a selector get_context_data() all additional data for the template get_form_kwargs() NoteCreateView, NoteUpdateView pass user= into the form get_initial() TagCreateView initial field values form_valid() all Create/Update/Delete call a service instead of form.save() get_success_url() TagCreateView dynamic redirect after saving

docs.title: Step 12 — CBVs in urls.py
docs.text:
# hello_app/urls.py
from django.urls import path
from . import views

app_name = "hello_app"

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.IndexView.as_view(), name='index'),

    # Notes
    path('notes/', views.NoteListView.as_view(), name='note_list'),
    path('notes/new/', views.NoteCreateView.as_view(), name='note_create'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/', views.NoteDetailView.as_view(), name='note_detail'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/edit/', views.NoteUpdateView.as_view(), name='note_edit'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/delete/', views.NoteDeleteView.as_view(), name='note_delete'),

    # Notebooks
    path('notebooks/', views.NotebookListView.as_view(), name='notebook_list'),
    path('notebooks/new/', views.NotebookCreateView.as_view(), name='notebook_create'),
    path('notebooks/<int:pk>/edit/', views.NotebookUpdateView.as_view(), name='notebook_edit'),
    path('notebooks/<int:pk>/delete/', views.NotebookDeleteView.as_view(), name='notebook_delete'),

]

docs.title: IndexView — a base View without Generic
docs.text:
class IndexView(View):
    """The simplest CBV — the base View."""
    def get(self, request):
        return HttpResponse("Hello, Django ORM!")

The base View does not render a template automatically — you have to implement get() and post() by hand. It suits simple pages or API endpoints.

docs.title: List
docs.text:
# FBV
@login_required
def note_list(request):
    search = request.GET.get('q', '').strip()
    tag_id = request.GET.get('tag')
    tag = None
    if tag_id:
        try:
            tag = Tag.objects.get(id=int(tag_id), user=request.user)
        except (Tag.DoesNotExist, ValueError):
            pass
    notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user, search=search or None, tag=tag)
    notebooks = selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user)
    tags = selectors.get_user_tags(request.user)
    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_list.html', {
        'notes': notes, 'notebooks': notebooks, 'tags': tags, 'search': search,
    })

# CBV — keeps the same logic, but structured
class NoteListView(LoginRequiredMixin, ListView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'notes_app/note_list.html'
    context_object_name = 'notes'

    def _get_filters(self):
        if hasattr(self, '_filters_parsed'):
            return
        self._filters_parsed = True
        self.search = self.request.GET.get('q', '').strip()
        tag_id = self.request.GET.get('tag')
        self.active_tag = None
        if tag_id:
            try:
                self.active_tag = Tag.objects.get(id=int(tag_id), user=self.request.user)
            except (Tag.DoesNotExist, ValueError):
                pass

    def get_queryset(self):
        self._get_filters()
        return selectors.get_user_notes(self.request.user, search=self.search or None, tag=self.active_tag)

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        self._get_filters()
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        ctx['notebooks'] = selectors.get_user_notebooks(self.request.user)
        ctx['tags'] = selectors.get_user_tags(self.request.user)
        ctx['search'] = self.search
        ctx['active_tag'] = self.active_tag
        return ctx

docs.text:
# FBV — 14 lines
@login_required
def note_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            tags = form.cleaned_data.get('tags')
            tag_ids = [t.id for t in tags] if tags else None

# CBV — the same logic, through hooks
class NoteCreateView(LoginRequiredMixin, CreateView):

    def form_valid(self, form):

        note = services.create_note(

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
# FBV — 16 lines
@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            tags = form.cleaned_data.get('tags')
            tag_ids = [t.id for t in tags] if tags else []
            services.update_note(
                note,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', note.priority),
                notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                is_pinned=form.cleaned_data.get('is_pinned', note.is_pinned),
                tag_ids=tag_ids,
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" оновлено!')
            return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(instance=note, user=request.user)
    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_form.html', {'form': form, 'note': note})

# CBV — UserQuerySetMixin automatically ensures a 404 for other users' notes
class NoteUpdateView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, UpdateView):
    model = Note
    form_class = NoteForm
    template_name = 'notes_app/note_form.html'

    def get_form_kwargs(self):
        kwargs = super().get_form_kwargs()
        kwargs['user'] = self.request.user
        return kwargs

    def form_valid(self, form):
        note = self.get_object()
        tags = form.cleaned_data.get('tags')
        tag_ids = [t.id for t in tags] if tags else []
        services.update_note(
            note,
            title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
            content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
            priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', note.priority),
            notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
            is_pinned=form.cleaned_data.get('is_pinned', note.is_pinned),
            tag_ids=tag_ids,
        )
        messages.success(self.request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" оновлено!')
        return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)

    def get_context_data(self, **kwargs):
        ctx = super().get_context_data(**kwargs)
        ctx['title'] = f'Редагувати: {self.object.title}'
        ctx['action'] = 'Зберегти зміни'
        return ctx

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
# FBV
@login_required
def note_delete(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
    if request.method == 'POST':
        title = note.title
        services.delete_note(note)
        messages.warning(request, f'Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
        return redirect('notes_app:note_list')
    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

# CBV
class NoteDeleteView(LoginRequiredMixin, UserQuerySetMixin, DeleteView):
    model = Note
    template_name = 'notes_app/note_confirm_delete.html'
    success_url = reverse_lazy('notes_app:note_list')  # reverse_lazy! (not reverse)
    context_object_name = 'note'

    def form_valid(self, form):
        note = self.get_object()
        title = note.title    # save it BEFORE deleting!
        services.delete_note(note)
        messages.warning(self.request, f'Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
        return redirect(self.success_url)

docs.title: Comparing the approaches
docs.text:
FBV CBV Readability You read from top to bottom — obvious You need to know the hooks and the MRO Duplicating @login_required Repeated on every function LoginRequiredMixin in the base class Access check get_object_or_404(Model, user=...) Repeated in every edit/delete UserQuerySetMixin.get_queryset() — once Testing client.get('/notes/') — simple The same (the URL does not change) When to choose Simple views, 1-2 operations When there are 10+ similar CRUD views

When to switch to CBV: not with the first note. With 3-4 similar CRUD sets, when get_object_or_404(..., user=request.user) is repeated everywhere and there is a risk of forgetting it in one place.

docs.title: What you can do after this step
Design
docs.text:
• [ ] I can describe a domain in words before writing code
  • [ ] I know the 7 steps of the methodology: Domain → Entities → Attributes → Relationships → Normalization → on_delete → Django Model
  • [ ] I understand the difference between OneToOneField, ForeignKey, ManyToManyField
  • [ ] I know where the FK lives (on the "Many" side)

docs.title: Models and migrations
docs.text:

  • [ ] I understand null=True vs blank=True (DB vs form)
  • [ ] I know the migration lifecycle: makemigrations → sqlmigrate → migrate
  • [ ] I never edit a migration that has already been applied
  • [ ] I always give migrations descriptive names (--name)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
• [ ] selectors.py contains only SELECTs (filter, annotate, prefetch_related)

  • [ ] views.py does not contain Model.objects.* directly

docs.title: ORM
docs.text:
• [ ] I understand N+1 and use select_related/prefetch_related

  • [ ] F() — for atomic operations and comparing fields
  • [ ] select_for_update() — for preventing race conditions
  • [ ] transaction.atomic() — for atomic groups of operations
  • [ ] annotate() — for computing in SQL instead of Python

docs.title: CBV
docs.text:

  • [ ] I know why .as_view() is needed in urls.py
  • [ ] I know the MRO order: LoginRequiredMixin FIRST
  • [ ] UserQuerySetMixin — DRY data isolation per user

docs.title: Mistake 1: Starting with models.py
docs.text:
❌ WRONG: we immediately write class Note(models.Model)
✅ CORRECT: first describe the domain in words, then the ER diagram, then the code

docs.title: Mistake 2: A QuerySet in the View
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG:
def note_list(request):
    notes = Note.objects.filter(user=request.user).select_related(...)
    return render(...)

# ✅ CORRECT:
def note_list(request):
    notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user)
    return render(...)

docs.title: Mistake 3: Direct mutation in the View
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG:
def note_create(request):
    if form.is_valid():
        note = form.save()  # bypasses services!

# ✅ CORRECT:
def note_create(request):
    if form.is_valid():
        note = services.create_note(user=request.user, ...)

docs.title: Mistake 4: N+1 when accessing an FK
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG:
notes = Note.objects.all()
for note in notes:
    print(note.notebook.title)  # N+1!

# ✅ CORRECT:
notes = Note.objects.select_related('notebook').all()
for note in notes:
    print(note.notebook.title)  # 1 query!

docs.title: Mistake 5: SET_NULL without null=True
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG:
notebook = models.ForeignKey(Notebook, on_delete=models.SET_NULL)
# Django system check: fields.E320 — SET_NULL requires null=True on the field!

# ✅ CORRECT:
notebook = models.ForeignKey(
    Notebook, on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
    null=True, blank=True,
)

docs.title: Mistake 6: super().form_valid() in a CBV
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG in a CBV with services:
def form_valid(self, form):
    super().form_valid(form)  # form.save() is in there — bypasses services!

# ✅ CORRECT:
def form_valid(self, form):
    note = services.create_note(user=self.request.user, ...)
    return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)

docs.title: Mistake 7: reverse() instead of reverse_lazy() in a class attribute
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG: executed when the class is loaded
class NoteDeleteView(DeleteView):
    success_url = reverse('hello_app:note_list')  # NoReverseMatch!

# ✅ CORRECT: executed lazily during the request
class NoteDeleteView(DeleteView):
    success_url = reverse_lazy('hello_app:note_list')

docs.title: Domain design
docs.text: "Design before code." Mistake #1 is starting with class Note(models.Model) and adding fields "on the fly". A month later, refactoring the schema = a complex migration that is hard to roll back in prod. 30 minutes of design = weeks of saved time.

docs.title: The 7-step methodology
docs.text:
# Step What you do Example 1 DOMAIN Describe in words what you are building "A user has notebooks. Notebooks contain notes. Notes have tags and reminders." 2 ENTITIES Find the nouns in the description User, Notebook, Note, Tag, Reminder, TodoList, ShoppingList 3 ATTRIBUTES What do we know about each entity? Note → title, content, priority, is_pinned, is_archived 4 RELATIONSHIPS How are the entities related? 1:1 User↔Profile · 1:N Notebook→Notes · M:N Note↔Tag 5 NORMALIZATION Remove duplication author_name in Note? — No, only an FK to User 6 on_delete What happens when the parent is deleted? CASCADE / SET_NULL / PROTECT 7 DJANGO MODEL Only now do we write models.py ← A typical mistake: starting here

Anti-pattern. Starting with class Note(models.Model) and adding fields "on the fly". An ER diagram is a contract between you and the database. Break it in code — and you pay with a migration.

docs.title: Where the "truth" lives
docs.text:
Normalization — every fact is stored in exactly one place.

DOMAIN    → "A user writes notes" — business language
SCHEMA    → ER diagram — the structure of tables and relationships
CODE      → models.py — the Python representation of the schema
MIGRATIONS → Git commits for the DB schema
ADMIN     → feedback: you see the structure in the browser

❌ DENORMALIZED SCHEMA (duplication):
NOTE table:
  author_name VARCHAR(150)  ← duplicates the user's name!
  author_email VARCHAR(254) ← and the email too!

Problem:
  1. The user changes their name → all of their notes need an UPDATE
  2. Mismatch: note.author_name ≠ user.username → DATA INCONSISTENCY
  3. Deleting the user → orphan records without an author

✅ NORMALIZED SCHEMA:
NOTE table:
  user_id BIGINT FK → auth_user  ← one fact: this note belongs to the user with this id

The user's name? → note.user.username (JOIN)
The user's email? → note.user.email (JOIN)
One source of truth → no mismatches

docs.title: Step 0 — From domain to schema
docs.text:
Mental model: Database design is not "which table should I add". It is modeling the real world. First you think in business language: "a user can have notebooks, each notebook contains notes, notes can have tags". Then you translate that into data structures. Django models are the last step, not the first.

Where mistakes begin: Most DB schema problems arise because the developer starts writing code right away without thinking about relationships. A month later it turns out a new relationship is needed — and adding it without a massive migration is impossible.

Typical mistake: Starting by writing the model. The correct order: domain → entities → attributes → relationships → normalization → Django model.

docs.title: The design process (the correct order)
docs.text:
1. DOMAIN — describe in words what we are building
   "A user has notebooks. Notebooks contain notes.
    Notes can be in to-do lists. There are reminders with a date."

2. ENTITIES — find the "nouns" in the domain description
   User, Notebook, Note, To-do list, List item,
   Reminder, Shopping list, Item, Tag

3. ATTRIBUTES — for each entity: what do we know about it?
   Note: title, content, created_at, is_pinned, priority

4. RELATIONSHIPS — how are the entities related to each other?
   Note → Notebook: many notes in one notebook (FK)
   Note ↔ Tag: one note, many tags; one tag, many notes (M:N)

5. NORMALIZATION — check: is there duplication?
   If Note has an author_name field — that duplicates User. Replace it with an FK.

6. CHOOSING on_delete — what happens when the parent record is deleted?
   Deleting a Notebook → delete all its notes (CASCADE)?
   Or keep the notes without a notebook (SET_NULL)?

7. DJANGO MODEL — only after all of the above

docs.title: Step 1 — Designing the domain
docs.text: We are building a personal notes manager — like Notion or Evernote, but simplified.

docs.title: What our product should be able to do
docs.text: Feature Description Notebooks Collections of notes (like folders). Each note is in one notebook Notes Text records with a title, content, tags, priority Tags Labels for notes. One note = many tags. One tag = many notes To-do lists A to-do list. Each list has items with a checkbox Shopping lists A list of items with a quantity and whether it was bought Reminders Notifications tied to a note or a date Pinning Notes can be pinned to the top Archive Notes can be hidden without deleting them

docs.title: Analysis of relationships by type
docs.text:
ONE-TO-ONE (1:1) — "one has exactly one":
  User ←→ UserProfile
  (each user has one profile, one profile belongs to one user)

ONE-TO-MANY (1:N) — "one has many":
  User → Notebook          (one user, many notebooks)
  Notebook → Note          (one notebook, many notes)
  User → Note              (a note has an author)
  User → TodoList          (one user, many to-do lists)
  TodoList → TodoItem      (one list, many items)
  User → ShoppingList      (one user, many shopping lists)
  ShoppingList → ShopItem  (one list, many items)
  Note → Reminder          (one note can have several reminders)

MANY-TO-MANY (M:N) — "many related to many":
  Note ↔ Tag  (a note has tags, a tag is in many notes)

docs.title: Where the FK lives — the "Many side" rule
docs.text:
Why: mistake #2 is putting the FK on the "One" side. For example, storing note_ids in Notebook. SQL does not support arrays in a column (1NF). The FK is always on the "Many" side.

Notebook → Note (1:N):

  notebooks:                   notes:
  ┌────┬──────────┐            ┌────┬─────────────┬─────────────┐
  │ id │ title    │            │ id │ title        │ notebook_id │  ← FK here
  ├────┼──────────┤            ├────┼─────────────┼─────────────┤
  │  1 │ Work     │◄───────────│  1 │ Django ORM   │      1      │
  │  2 │ Personal │◄───────────│  2 │ Python tips  │      1      │
  │    │          │◄───────────│  3 │ Soup recipe  │      2      │
  └────┴──────────┘            └────┴─────────────┴─────────────┘

Notebook does NOT store a list of notes.
Note stores a REFERENCE to its notebook (notebook_id=1).

docs.title: 1:1 — OneToOneField
docs.text:
Why: We extend the built-in User without touching its code. All non-standard fields go into UserProfile. This is vertical partitioning: 5 basic fields in User, 20 optional ones in Profile.

class UserProfile(models.Model):
    user = models.OneToOneField(
        User,
        on_delete=models.CASCADE,   # a profile without a user is meaningless → CASCADE
        related_name='profile',     # user.profile — access from User
    )
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=60, blank=True)
    timezone     = models.CharField(max_length=40, default='UTC')
    avatar_url   = models.URLField(blank=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return f'Profile({self.user.username})'

The SQL Django generates: 

CREATE TABLE "notes_app_userprofile" (
    "id"           bigint NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY,
    "user_id"      bigint NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES "auth_user" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
    "display_name" varchar(60) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    "timezone"     varchar(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UTC',
    "avatar_url"   varchar(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

The key word here is UNIQUE. That is what distinguishes 1:1 from 1:N. Without UNIQUE one user could have several profiles.

Access: 

user = User.objects.get(username='alice')
user.profile              # → UserProfile (not a QuerySet! UNIQUE FK → a single object)
user.profile.timezone     # → 'Europe/Kyiv'
user.profile.display_name # → 'Alice'

docs.title: 1:N — ForeignKey
docs.text:
Why: One notebook contains many notes. The FK is always placed on the "Many" side — in Note, not in Notebook. Notebook cannot store a list of note_ids — an SQL column holds a single value, not an array.

class Notebook(models.Model):
    user       = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                                   related_name='notebooks')
    title      = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    color      = models.CharField(max_length=7, default='#6c757d')  # HEX color
    is_default = models.BooleanField(default=False)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title

class Note(models.Model):
    PRIORITY_LOW    = 1
    PRIORITY_MEDIUM = 2
    PRIORITY_HIGH   = 3
    PRIORITY_CHOICES = [
        (PRIORITY_LOW,    'Низький'),
        (PRIORITY_MEDIUM, 'Середній'),
        (PRIORITY_HIGH,   'Високий'),
    ]

    user     = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                                 related_name='notes')
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        Notebook,
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,  # deleting the notebook → the note lives on
        null=True, blank=True,      # null=True is required when on_delete=SET_NULL
        related_name='notes',
    )
    tags = models.ManyToManyField('Tag', blank=True)  # M:N — a separate junction table

    title       = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    content     = models.TextField(blank=True)
    priority    = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(
        choices=PRIORITY_CHOICES, default=PRIORITY_MEDIUM
    )
    is_pinned   = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    is_archived = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at  = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)  # set once on CREATE
    updated_at  = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)      # updated on every SAVE
    views_count = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=0)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['-is_pinned', '-updated_at']  # pinned on top, then by date

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title

Why is notebook SET_NULL and not CASCADE?

A business decision: when a user deletes the "Work" (Робота) notebook, its notes should not disappear — they move to the "no notebook" state. CASCADE would mean losing all the notes together with the notebook.

Access: 

notebook = Notebook.objects.get(title='Робота')
notebook.notes.all()        # → QuerySet[Note] (reverse access via related_name)
notebook.notes.count()      # → 5

note = Note.objects.get(pk=1)
note.notebook               # → Notebook or None (after SET_NULL)
note.notebook.title         # → 'Робота'
note.user.username          # → 'alice'

docs.title: M:N — ManyToManyField
docs.text:
Why: One note can have several tags. One tag can be in several notes. This is an M:N relationship. SQL implements it via a separate junction table — Django creates it automatically.

class Tag(models.Model):
    user  = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                               related_name='tags')
    name  = models.CharField(max_length=50)
    color = models.CharField(max_length=7, default='#6c757d')

    class Meta:
        unique_together = [('user', 'name')]
        # Alice and Bob can both have a 'python' tag — the constraint is on (user_id, name)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name

Django automatically creates the junction table notes_app_note_tags:

CREATE TABLE "notes_app_note_tags" (
    "id"      bigint NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY,
    "note_id" bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES "notes_app_note" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
    "tag_id"  bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES "notes_app_tag" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
    UNIQUE ("note_id", "tag_id")
);

Access: 

note = Note.objects.get(pk=1)
note.tags.all()                      # → QuerySet[Tag]
note.tags.add(tag_py, tag_django)    # INSERT × 2 into the junction table
note.tags.remove(tag_py)             # DELETE from the junction table
note.tags.set([tag_django])          # synchronize — remove extras, add new ones

# Reverse access:
tag = Tag.objects.get(name='python')
tag.note_set.all()                   # → QuerySet[Note] that have this tag
# or via related_name if you set one:
# tags = models.ManyToManyField('Tag', blank=True, related_name='notes')
# tag.notes.all()

docs.title: Step 5 — The on_delete matrix
docs.text:
Why: on_delete is not a technical decision but a business decision. What happens to the data when a related object is deleted? The wrong choice = data loss or orphan records.

Strategy What it does When to choose it Example CASCADE Delete the children automatically A note without an author is meaningless Reminder → Note SET_NULL FK → NULL, the children live on A note can exist without a notebook Note.notebook → Notebook SET_DEFAULT FK → the default value Move to the "default" one Note → DefaultNotebook PROTECT ProtectedError, forbidden Prevent deletion if there are dependents Not built into our project RESTRICT Forbid, but with nuances Complex domains Rarely DO_NOTHING The DB decides by itself → orphans Almost never Dangerous

Notes Platform — the decision table:

Relationship on_delete Rationale UserProfile.user CASCADE A profile without a user makes no sense Notebook.user CASCADE Notebooks belong to the user; deleting the user = deleting everything Note.user CASCADE Notes without an author are meaningless Note.notebook SET_NULL A note can exist without a notebook (it moves to "no folder") Tag.user CASCADE Tags are tied to the user Reminder.note CASCADE A reminder without a note is meaningless TodoItem.todo_list CASCADE An item without a list is not needed ShopItem.shopping_list CASCADE A product without a list is not needed

docs.title: Step 6 — The full models.py code
docs.text:
Why: Only after the design is finished (steps 1-5) do we write code. Every decision above is reflected in one line of models.py.

# notes_app/models.py
from django.db import models
from django.contrib.auth.models import User


class UserProfile(models.Model):
    user         = models.OneToOneField(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                                        related_name='profile')
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=60, blank=True)
    timezone     = models.CharField(max_length=40, default='UTC')
    avatar_url   = models.URLField(blank=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return f'Profile({self.user.username})'


class Tag(models.Model):
    user  = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='tags')
    name  = models.CharField(max_length=50)
    color = models.CharField(max_length=7, default='#6c757d')

    class Meta:
        unique_together = [('user', 'name')]

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name


class Notebook(models.Model):
    user       = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                                   related_name='notebooks')
    title      = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    color      = models.CharField(max_length=7, default='#6c757d')
    is_default = models.BooleanField(default=False)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title


class Note(models.Model):
    PRIORITY_LOW    = 1
    PRIORITY_MEDIUM = 2
    PRIORITY_HIGH   = 3
    PRIORITY_CHOICES = [
        (PRIORITY_LOW,    'Низький'),
        (PRIORITY_MEDIUM, 'Середній'),
        (PRIORITY_HIGH,   'Високий'),
    ]

    user     = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='notes')
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        Notebook, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True,
        related_name='notes',
    )
    tags = models.ManyToManyField(Tag, blank=True)

    title       = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    content     = models.TextField(blank=True)
    priority    = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(
        choices=PRIORITY_CHOICES, default=PRIORITY_MEDIUM,
    )
    is_pinned   = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    is_archived = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at  = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated_at  = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)
    views_count = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=0)
    group       = models.ForeignKey(
        'auth.Group', on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True, related_name='notes',
    )

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['-is_pinned', '-updated_at']

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title


class Reminder(models.Model):
    REPEAT_CHOICES = [
        ('none',    'Одноразово'),
        ('daily',   'Щодня'),
        ('weekly',  'Щотижня'),
        ('monthly', 'Щомісяця'),
    ]

    note           = models.ForeignKey(Note, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                                       related_name='reminders')
    remind_at      = models.DateTimeField()
    message        = models.TextField(blank=True)
    is_sent        = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    repeat_pattern = models.CharField(
        max_length=20, choices=REPEAT_CHOICES, default='none',
    )

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['remind_at']

    def __str__(self):
        return f'Reminder({self.note.title}, {self.remind_at})'


class TodoList(models.Model):
    user         = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                                     related_name='todo_lists')
    title        = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    is_completed = models.BooleanField(default=False)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title


class TodoItem(models.Model):
    todo_list      = models.ForeignKey(TodoList, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                                       related_name='items')
    text           = models.CharField(max_length=500)
    is_done        = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    order_position = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=0)
    due_date       = models.DateField(null=True, blank=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['order_position']

    def __str__(self):
        return self.text


class ShoppingList(models.Model):
    user       = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                                   related_name='shopping_lists')
    title      = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    store_name = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True)
    group      = models.ForeignKey(
        'auth.Group', on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True, related_name='shopping_lists',
    )

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title


class ShopItem(models.Model):
    UNIT_PIECE  = 'шт'
    UNIT_KG     = 'кг'
    UNIT_LITER  = 'л'
    UNIT_GRAM   = 'г'
    UNIT_CHOICES = [
        (UNIT_PIECE, 'Штуки'),
        (UNIT_KG,    'Кілограми'),
        (UNIT_LITER, 'Літри'),
        (UNIT_GRAM,  'Грами'),
    ]

    shopping_list   = models.ForeignKey(ShoppingList, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                                        related_name='items')
    name            = models.CharField(max_length=120)
    quantity        = models.DecimalField(max_digits=8, decimal_places=2, default=1)
    unit            = models.CharField(max_length=5, choices=UNIT_CHOICES,
                                       default=UNIT_PIECE)
    is_purchased    = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    estimated_price = models.DecimalField(max_digits=10, decimal_places=2,
                                          null=True, blank=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name

Why DecimalField and not FloatField for prices and quantities?

# FloatField — IEEE 754 binary floating point
0.1 + 0.2  # → 0.30000000000000004  ← CPU rounding

# DecimalField — decimal arithmetic (Python Decimal)
Decimal('0.1') + Decimal('0.2')  # → Decimal('0.3')  ← exact

Money is always DecimalField. FloatField leads to penny-level discrepancies in calculations.

docs.title: Step 7 — Checking in the Django shell
docs.text:
Why: Before writing views and templates, we check through the shell that the models and relationships work correctly. It is the fastest way to catch design mistakes.

docker compose run --rm web python manage.py shell

from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from notes_app.models import (
    UserProfile, Tag, Notebook, Note, Reminder,
    TodoList, TodoItem, ShoppingList, ShopItem
)

# --- 1:1 OneToOneField ---
user = User.objects.create_user('alice', 'alice@test.com', 'pass123')
profile = UserProfile.objects.create(user=user, display_name='Alice', timezone='Europe/Kyiv')

print(user.profile)            # → Profile(alice)
print(user.profile.timezone)   # → Europe/Kyiv

# --- 1:N ForeignKey ---
notebook = Notebook.objects.create(user=user, title='Робота', is_default=True)
tag_py = Tag.objects.create(user=user, name='python', color='#3776AB')
tag_dj = Tag.objects.create(user=user, name='django', color='#092E20')

note = Note.objects.create(
    user=user, notebook=notebook,
    title='Django ORM', content='QuerySet — лінива оцінка.',
    priority=Note.PRIORITY_HIGH, is_pinned=True,
)

# Reverse access via related_name:
print(notebook.notes.count())  # → 1
print(notebook.notes.all())    # → <QuerySet [<Note: Django ORM>]>

# --- M:N ManyToManyField ---
note.tags.add(tag_py, tag_dj)                         # INSERT × 2 into the junction table
print(note.tags.all())                                 # → <QuerySet [<Tag: python>, <Tag: django>]>
print(note.tags.count())                               # → 2

# The reverse side of M:N:
print(tag_py.note_set.all())                           # → <QuerySet [<Note: Django ORM>]>

# --- Reminder (CASCADE from Note) ---
reminder = Reminder.objects.create(
    note=note,
    remind_at='2026-06-20 09:00:00+00:00',
    message='Завершити розділ про ORM',
)
print(note.reminders.count())   # → 1

# --- TodoList ---
todo = TodoList.objects.create(user=user, title='Вивчити ORM')
TodoItem.objects.bulk_create([
    TodoItem(todo_list=todo, text='Прочитати docs', order_position=1),
    TodoItem(todo_list=todo, text='Зробити shell-демо', order_position=2),
    TodoItem(todo_list=todo, text='Написати тести', order_position=3),
])
print(todo.items.count())       # → 3

# Checking CASCADE: deleting a note → deleting its reminders
note_id = note.pk
note.delete()
print(Reminder.objects.filter(pk=reminder.pk).exists())  # → False (CASCADE worked)

# Checking SET_NULL: deleting a notebook → notebook_id in its notes becomes NULL
note2 = Note.objects.create(user=user, notebook=notebook, title='Нотатка 2', content='')
notebook.delete()
note2.refresh_from_db()
print(note2.notebook)  # → None (SET_NULL worked)

docs.title: ER diagrams and relationship types
docs.text: Three types of relationships between tables. The question "where does the FK live?" is not a technical one, it is an architectural one.

docs.title: 1:1 — OneToOneField
docs.text:
FK + UNIQUE · "user has exactly one profile"

USER                          USER_PROFILE
┌──────────────┬──────────┐   ┌────────────────┬──────────────────┐
│ id  bigint PK│          │──►│ id    bigint PK│                  │
│ username     │          │   │ user_id bigint │ UNIQUE FK        │
└──────────────┴──────────┘   │ display varchar│                  │
                              │ timezone       │                  │
                              └────────────────┴──────────────────┘

class UserProfile(models.Model):
    user = models.OneToOneField(
        User,
        on_delete=models.CASCADE,
        related_name='profile',
    )
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=60, blank=True)
    timezone     = models.CharField(max_length=40, default='UTC')
    avatar_url   = models.URLField(blank=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return f'Profile({self.user.username})'

The SQL Django generates: 

CREATE TABLE "hello_app_userprofile" (
    "id"           bigint NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY,
    "user_id"      bigint NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES "auth_user" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE,
    "display_name" varchar(60) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    "timezone"     varchar(40) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UTC',
    "avatar_url"   varchar(200) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''
);

Reverse — access from User: 

user = User.objects.get(username='alice')
user.profile              # → UserProfile (not a QuerySet! UNIQUE FK → a single object)
user.profile.timezone     # → 'Europe/Kyiv'

Why is this 1:1? An ordinary FK + UNIQUE on the column. The reverse is an attribute (not a QuerySet): user.profile. Useful for vertical partitioning: 5 basic fields in User, 20 optional ones in Profile — we do not clutter the main table.

When to use 1:1? - "Vertical partitioning": 5 basic fields in User, 20 optional ones in Profile - Different access patterns: User changes often, Profile rarely → a separate QuerySet - Different permissions: view_user without view_userprofile

docs.title: 1:N — ForeignKey
docs.text:
FK on the "Many" side · "notebook has many notes"

NOTEBOOK                    NOTE              NOTE              NOTE
┌──────────┬──────────┐     ┌───────────────────────┐
│ id       │ bigint PK│──┬─►│ id          bigint PK │
│ title    │ varchar  │  │  │ notebook_id bigint FK │← the FK is here!
└──────────┴──────────┘  ├─►│ title       varchar   │
                         │  └───────────────────────┘
                         ├─► (another note)
                         └─► (another note)

class Note(models.Model):
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        'Notebook',                  # ← a string avoids circular imports
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,   # Deleting the notebook → NULL (not CASCADE!)
        null=True,                   # NULL is required with SET_NULL
        blank=True,                  # Form: the field is optional
        related_name='notes',        # notebook.notes.all() → QuerySet of notes
    )

Where does the FK live? Always on the Many side. Notebook does not store a list of notes — Note stores notebook_id. This is the physics of SQL: one column = one value.

WRONG way of thinking:         CORRECT way of thinking:
Notebook has a list of notes   Note belongs to Notebook
→ Notebook.notes = [...]      → Note.notebook_id = FK
→ a JOIN will happen           → Notebook.notes.all() = reverse

Notebook does NOT store a list of Note IDs!
That would break the normal form and complicate the JOIN.

Reverse — access from the "One" side: 

notebook = Notebook.objects.get(id=1)
notebook.notes.all()                    # ← related_name='notes' → QuerySet
notebook.notes.filter(is_pinned=True)   # Filter
notebook.notes.count()                  # Count

note = Note.objects.get(id=1)
note.notebook                           # ← FK attr → a Notebook object (or None)
note.notebook_id                        # ← the raw integer FK without a JOIN
note.notebook.title                     # ← JOIN: SELECT ... WHERE notebook_id=...

docs.title: M:N — ManyToManyField
docs.text:
Via a junction table · Django creates it automatically

NOTE                  NOTE_TAGS (junction)    TAG
┌──────────┬──────┐   ┌──────────┬──────────┐  ┌──────────┬──────────┐
│ id       │  PK  │──►│ note_id  │ bigint FK│  │ id       │  PK      │
│ title    │      │   │ tag_id   │ bigint FK│─►│ name     │ varchar  │
└──────────┴──────┘   └──────────┴──────────┘  └──────────┴──────────┘
                       UNIQUE(note_id, tag_id)
                       Django: hello_app_note_tags

class Note(models.Model):
    tags = models.ManyToManyField(
        'Tag',
        blank=True,              # A note can have no tags
        related_name='notes',    # tag.notes.all() → notes with this tag
    )
    # Django automatically creates the junction table: hello_app_note_tags

M:N operations: 

note = Note.objects.get(id=1)
tag_py = Tag.objects.get(name='python')
tag_dj = Tag.objects.get(name='django')

# Add tags
note.tags.add(tag_py, tag_dj)     # INSERT INTO note_tags (note_id, tag_id)

# The full list
note.tags.all()                    # SELECT * FROM tags JOIN note_tags ...

# Remove a specific tag
note.tags.remove(tag_py)           # DELETE FROM note_tags WHERE ...

# Replace all tags
note.tags.set([tag_dj])           # DELETE the old ones + INSERT the new ones

# Clear them all
note.tags.clear()                  # DELETE FROM note_tags WHERE note_id=...

# Reverse — notes with a tag:
tag_py.notes.all()                 # SELECT * FROM notes JOIN note_tags WHERE tag_id=...

A junction = a separate table. There is no magic here — it is an ordinary table with two FKs. Want to add added_at or role to the relationship? Pass through= and describe your own junction model.

docs.title: on_delete — what happens when the parent is deleted?
docs.text:
Mistake: CASCADE as the default for everything → deleting one user can wipe out hundreds of rows. Always choose the strategy deliberately. It is a business decision, not a technical one.

# CASCADE — delete child records together with the parent
class Reminder(models.Model):
    note = models.ForeignKey(Note, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='reminders')
    # Deleting a Note → all Reminders of that Note are deleted
    # Logic: a Reminder without a Note is meaningless → CASCADE is the right choice

# SET_NULL — the FK becomes NULL, the child record stays
class Note(models.Model):
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        Notebook, on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True,  # ← null=True is REQUIRED with SET_NULL
    )
    # Deleting a Notebook → Note.notebook = NULL
    # Logic: the note must be kept! Only the notebook is deleted.

# PROTECT — forbids deletion if there are child records
# (a hypothetical example: in our project Note.tags is M:N, and M:N has no on_delete)
class Note(models.Model):
    category = models.ForeignKey(Category, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    # Deleting a Category → ProtectedError (an exception)
    # Logic: do not allow a category to be deleted while it is in use

# RESTRICT — similar to PROTECT but allows a cascade from a higher level
# Complex hierarchies, rarely used

# SET_DEFAULT — the FK becomes the default value
class Note(models.Model):
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        Notebook, on_delete=models.SET_DEFAULT,
        default=1,  # ← pk of the default notebook
    )

# DO_NOTHING — leaves an orphan record (the FK points to a non-existent id)
# AVOID: leads to IntegrityError or dirty data

docs.title: The on_delete selection matrix
docs.text:
Strategy What it does When to choose it CASCADE Delete the children automatically Reminder → Note: a reminder without a note makes no sense SET_NULL FK → NULL, the children live on Note → Notebook: a note exists without a notebook. The field must be null=True SET_DEFAULT FK → the default value Note → Notebook: move it to the "Default" notebook PROTECT ProtectedError, deletion is forbidden Category (hypothetical): do not allow deleting a category while it is in use RESTRICT Forbid, but allow a cascade from a higher level Complex domains with several levels of ownership DO_NOTHING The DB decides by itself (often = orphan) Almost never. Only if you manage consistency manually (triggers)

Specifically for the Notes Platform:

If you delete... What do we want with the children? on_delete Note Delete the Reminders (they make no sense without the Note) CASCADE Notebook Keep the Notes (the note is more important than the notebook) SET_NULL User Delete all Notes (the content belongs to the user) CASCADE Tag Note.tags is M:N: only the rows in note_tags are deleted, the notes stay — (M:N has no on_delete)

docs.title: Migration Lifecycle — from a model change to ALTER TABLE
Migration Dependency Graph (DAG)
docs.text:
graph TD
    A["auth.0001_initial<br/>CREATE TABLE auth_user"] --> C
    B["hello_app.0001_initial<br/>CREATE TABLE note"] --> C
    C["hello_app.0002_extended<br/>CREATE notebooks, tags…"]
    C --> D["hello_app.0003_add_index<br/>CREATE INDEX"]
    C --> E["hello_app.0004_add_word_count<br/>ADD COLUMN word_count"]
    D --> F["hello_app.0005_constraint<br/>ADD CONSTRAINT CHECK"]
    E --> F

    classDef step     fill:#eceff1,stroke:#546e7a,stroke-width:1px;
    classDef success  fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32,stroke-width:2px;

    class A step;
    class B,C,D,E,F success;

django_migrations is a special log table. migrate applies only the nodes that are not there yet, in the topological order of their dependencies.

docs.title: Key commands
docs.text:
# Generate a migration with a descriptive name
python manage.py makemigrations --name add_word_count_to_note

# Preview the SQL before running it (always do this before migrate!)
python manage.py sqlmigrate hello_app 0003

# Apply all new migrations
python manage.py migrate

# Show the state of all migrations (✓ applied, □ not yet)
python manage.py showmigrations

# Roll back to a specific migration
python manage.py migrate hello_app 0002

docs.title: Migration rules
docs.text: Rule Why ✅ New field: always default= or null=True Without a default, what should be written into existing rows? ✅ Descriptive name --name add_word_count 0003_add_word_count is more readable than 0003_note ✅ Commit migrations to git Otherwise your colleagues cannot update their DB ✅ sqlmigrate before migrate You check the SQL that will be executed ❌ Editing an applied migration Production and dev get out of sync — a disaster ❌ Deleting migrations from git Breaks the dependency graph

docs.title: Step 5 — The migration workflow
docs.text:
Mental model: Migrations are Git for your database schema. Each migration is a "commit" that describes schema changes. Django tracks which migrations have already been applied in the django_migrations table. migrate runs only the new ones.

Common mistake: Editing a migration that has already been applied. If a migration has already been applied in production and you edit it, production and development get out of sync. Changing an applied migration = disaster. If you need a change → create a new migration.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Dev as Developer
    participant Django as Django
    participant DB as Database

    Dev->>Django: We change models.py
    Dev->>Django: python manage.py makemigrations
    Django->>Django: Compares models.py with the last migration state
    Django-->>Dev: Generates 0002_extended_models.py
    Dev->>Django: python manage.py migrate
    Django->>DB: ALTER TABLE / CREATE TABLE (DDL)
    DB-->>Django: OK
    Django->>DB: INSERT INTO django_migrations (app, name)
    Django-->>Dev: Applied 0002_extended_models
# Steps for our project:

# 1. Go to the project folder
cd module_5/lesson_Django_ORM_Database/notes_project

# 2. Check that hello_app is in INSTALLED_APPS
# settings.py → INSTALLED_APPS must contain 'hello_app'

# 3. Generate the first migration
python manage.py makemigrations
# Expected output:
# Migrations for 'hello_app':
#   hello_app/migrations/0001_initial.py
#     - Create model UserProfile, Tag, Notebook, Note, Reminder,
#       TodoList, TodoItem, ShoppingList, ShopItem

# 4. Preview the SQL that will be executed (without running it)
python manage.py sqlmigrate hello_app 0001
# Useful: check column types, FKs, indexes

# 5. Run the migration
python manage.py migrate

# 6. Show the state of all migrations
python manage.py showmigrations

Look at what Django generated:

BEGIN;
CREATE TABLE "hello_app_tag" (
    "id"      bigint NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    "user_id" bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES "auth_user" ("id"),
    "name"    varchar(50) NOT NULL,
    "color"   varchar(7) NOT NULL
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "unique_user_tag" ON "hello_app_tag" ("user_id", "name");
-- ... and so on for every table
COMMIT;

docs.title: When you need a new migration (adding a field)
docs.text:
# Add a new field to Note
class Note(models.Model):
    ...
    word_count = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=0)  # NEW FIELD

python manage.py makemigrations --name add_word_count_to_note
# → hello_app/migrations/0003_add_word_count_to_note.py

python manage.py sqlmigrate hello_app 0003
# ALTER TABLE "hello_app_note" ADD COLUMN "word_count" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0;

python manage.py migrate

docs.title: Testing the models in the Django shell
docs.text:
python manage.py shell

from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from hello_app.models import *

# Create a user
user = User.objects.create_user('alice', 'alice@test.com', 'pass123')

# Profile (OneToOne)
profile = UserProfile.objects.create(user=user, display_name='Alice')
print(user.profile.display_name)  # via related_name

# Notebook
notebook = Notebook.objects.create(user=user, title='Work', is_default=True)

# Tags
tag_py = Tag.objects.create(user=user, name='python', color='#3776AB')
tag_dj = Tag.objects.create(user=user, name='django', color='#092E20')

# A note with tags
note = Note.objects.create(
    user=user, notebook=notebook,
    title='Django ORM', content='QuerySet — lazy evaluation...',
    priority=Note.PRIORITY_HIGH, is_pinned=True
)
note.tags.add(tag_py, tag_dj)  # M:N — INSERT into the junction table

# To-do list
todo = TodoList.objects.create(user=user, title='Learn the ORM')
TodoItem.objects.bulk_create([
    TodoItem(todo_list=todo, text='RELATIONAL_DB_FOUNDATIONS.md', order_position=1),
    TodoItem(todo_list=todo, text='DJANGO_ORM_DEEP.md', order_position=2),
    TodoItem(todo_list=todo, text='Build the project', order_position=3),
])

# Shopping list
shopping = ShoppingList.objects.create(user=user, title='Grocery run')
ShopItem.objects.create(
    shopping_list=shopping, name='Milk',
    quantity=2, unit=ShopItem.UNIT_LITER, estimated_price=45.00
)

print(f"Notes: {user.notes.count()}")
print(f"Tags: {[t.name for t in note.tags.all()]}")

docs.title: Django models
docs.text: After designing the domain (Steps 0–3), it is time to write code. models.py is the Python representation of the ER schema you have already drawn.

docs.title: Step 4 — Writing Django models
docs.text:
hello_app/models.py:

from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.core.validators import MinValueValidator, MaxValueValidator
from django.db import models


class UserProfile(models.Model):
    user         = models.OneToOneField(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='profile')
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=60, blank=True)
    timezone     = models.CharField(max_length=40, default='UTC')
    avatar_url   = models.URLField(blank=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return f'Profile({self.user.username})'


class Tag(models.Model):
    user  = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='tags')
    name  = models.CharField(max_length=50)
    color = models.CharField(max_length=7, default='#6c757d')  # Hex color

    class Meta:
        ordering    = ['name']
        constraints = [
            models.UniqueConstraint(fields=['user', 'name'], name='unique_user_tag'),
        ]

    def __str__(self):
        return f'#{self.name}'


class Notebook(models.Model):
    user       = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='notebooks')
    title      = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    color      = models.CharField(max_length=7, default='#6c757d')
    is_default = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['-is_default', 'title']

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title


class Note(models.Model):
    PRIORITY_LOW    = 1
    PRIORITY_MEDIUM = 2
    PRIORITY_HIGH   = 3
    PRIORITY_CHOICES = [
        (PRIORITY_LOW,    'Низький'),
        (PRIORITY_MEDIUM, 'Середній'),
        (PRIORITY_HIGH,   'Високий'),
    ]

    user     = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='notes')
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        Notebook, on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True, related_name='notes',
    )
    tags = models.ManyToManyField(Tag, blank=True)

    title       = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    content     = models.TextField(blank=True)
    priority    = models.SmallIntegerField(
        choices=PRIORITY_CHOICES, default=PRIORITY_LOW,
        validators=[MinValueValidator(1), MaxValueValidator(3)],
    )
    is_pinned   = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    is_archived = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at  = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated_at  = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)
    views_count = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=0)

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at']

    def __str__(self):
        return f'📌 {self.title}' if self.is_pinned else self.title

PRIORITY_CHOICES in notes_chat_app

This model uses 3 levels (1–3) for the learning project. notes_chat_app (the final project) has 4 levels: PRIORITY_URGENT = 4 («Терміново», "Urgent"), PositiveSmallIntegerField instead of SmallIntegerField, and MaxValueValidator(4). In addition, notes_chat_app.Note has a group = ForeignKey(Group) field for group sharing (added in Step 5 — Authentication and security).

class Reminder(models.Model):

    remind_at = models.DateTimeField()
