    UNIT_LITER  = 'л'

docs.title: Overview of relationships
docs.text:
# Three relationship types in a single Note model:
class Note(models.Model):
    user     = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=CASCADE, related_name='notes')
    # user: FK (required, CASCADE)

    notebook = models.ForeignKey(Notebook, on_delete=SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True)
    # notebook: FK (optional, SET_NULL — a note can exist without a notebook)

    tags = models.ManyToManyField(Tag, blank=True)
    # tags: M:N (Django creates the junction table automatically)

docs.title: QuerySet — lazy objects
docs.text:
# QuerySet is LAZY: SQL is not executed until the data is needed
qs = Note.objects.filter(user=alice)   # ← NOTHING happened in the DB!
qs = qs.filter(is_pinned=True)         # ← Only refining the query
qs = qs.order_by('-priority')          # ← Still nothing in the DB

# SQL IS EXECUTED here — when we iterate, count, convert:
notes = list(qs)           # ← SELECT NOW!
count = qs.count()         # ← SELECT COUNT(*)
first = qs.first()         # ← SELECT ... LIMIT 1
exists = qs.exists()       # ← SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1 (very fast)
for note in qs: ...        # ← SELECT and iteration
note = qs.get(pk=1)        # ← SELECT WHERE pk=1

# ADVANTAGE OF LAZINESS:
# You can pass a QuerySet to a template → SQL runs only during rendering
# You can chain filters: qs.filter(A).filter(B) = one SELECT with two WHERE conditions

docs.title: Filtering — lookups
docs.text:
# Exact equality:
Note.objects.filter(priority=3)
# SQL: WHERE priority = 3

# Comparison:
Note.objects.filter(priority__gt=1)    # greater than → > 1
Note.objects.filter(priority__gte=2)   # greater or equal → >= 2
Note.objects.filter(priority__lt=3)    # less than → < 3
Note.objects.filter(priority__lte=2)   # less or equal → <= 2

# Strings:
Note.objects.filter(title__exact='Test')          # = 'Test' (case-sensitive)
Note.objects.filter(title__iexact='test')          # = 'test' (case-insensitive)
Note.objects.filter(title__contains='Django')      # LIKE '%Django%'
Note.objects.filter(title__icontains='django')     # ILIKE '%django%'
Note.objects.filter(title__startswith='Hello')     # LIKE 'Hello%'
Note.objects.filter(title__endswith='.md')         # LIKE '%.md'

# NULL:
Note.objects.filter(notebook__isnull=True)         # IS NULL
Note.objects.filter(notebook__isnull=False)        # IS NOT NULL

# Lists:
Note.objects.filter(priority__in=[1, 2])           # IN (1, 2)
Note.objects.exclude(priority__in=[3, 4])          # NOT IN (3, 4)

# Dates:
Note.objects.filter(created_at__year=2026)
Note.objects.filter(created_at__date=date(2026, 6, 13))
Note.objects.filter(created_at__gte=datetime(2026, 1, 1))

# FK:
Note.objects.filter(notebook=my_notebook)          # WHERE notebook_id = X
Note.objects.filter(notebook__title='Work')        # JOIN: WHERE notebook.title = 'Work'
Note.objects.filter(notebook__user=request.user)   # 2 JOIN levels

# M:N:
Note.objects.filter(tags=tag_python)               # notes with the python tag
Note.objects.filter(tags__name='python')           # JOIN on Tag
Note.objects.filter(tags__name__icontains='py')    # JOIN + LIKE

docs.title: Q objects — complex conditions
docs.text:
from django.db.models import Q

# OR condition:
Note.objects.filter(Q(title__icontains='django') | Q(content__icontains='django'))
# SQL: WHERE (title ILIKE '%django%' OR content ILIKE '%django%')

# AND (by default, multiple filters = AND):
Note.objects.filter(Q(is_pinned=True) & Q(priority=3))
# SQL: WHERE is_pinned = TRUE AND priority = 3

# NOT:
Note.objects.filter(~Q(is_archived=True))
# SQL: WHERE NOT is_archived = TRUE  (= WHERE is_archived = FALSE)

# Combining:
Note.objects.filter(
    Q(user=alice) | Q(group__in=alice_groups)
).filter(
    is_archived=False
)
# SQL: WHERE (user_id = 1 OR group_id IN (...)) AND is_archived = FALSE

docs.title: Annotations and aggregates
docs.text:
from django.db.models import Count, Avg, Max, Min, Sum, F

# Count — number of related objects
Notebook.objects.annotate(note_count=Count('notes'))
# SQL: SELECT *, COUNT(notes.id) AS note_count FROM notebooks LEFT JOIN notes ...
# notebook.note_count is available on every object

# Filtered Count
Notebook.objects.annotate(
    active_count=Count('notes', filter=Q(notes__is_archived=False))
)

# Aggregate — a single value for the whole QuerySet
Note.objects.aggregate(avg_priority=Avg('priority'))
# → {'avg_priority': 1.8}

Note.objects.filter(user=alice).aggregate(
    total=Count('id'),
    pinned=Count('id', filter=Q(is_pinned=True)),
    max_priority=Max('priority'),
)
# → {'total': 42, 'pinned': 5, 'max_priority': 3}

# F objects — a reference to a field in SQL (without loading into Python)
Note.objects.filter(views_count__gt=F('priority') * 100)
# SQL: WHERE views_count > priority * 100
# Without F: you would have to load all objects into Python and filter in a loop!

# update with F():
Note.objects.all().update(views_count=F('views_count') + 1)
# SQL: UPDATE ... SET views_count = views_count + 1
# An atomic operation! No race condition.

docs.title: values() and values_list()
docs.text:
# Returns dictionaries instead of objects (faster for large QuerySets)
Note.objects.values('title', 'priority')
# → [{'title': 'Test', 'priority': 1}, ...]

# Returns tuples (even faster)
Note.objects.values_list('title', 'priority')
# → [('Test', 1), ('Django', 2), ...]

# flat=True: one column → a flat list
Note.objects.values_list('id', flat=True)
# → [1, 2, 3, 4, ...]

# Save all ids into a list:
note_ids = list(Note.objects.filter(user=alice).values_list('id', flat=True))

docs.title: order_by, distinct, only, defer
docs.text:
# Ordering:
Note.objects.order_by('priority')           # ASC
Note.objects.order_by('-priority')          # DESC
Note.objects.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')  # Multiple

# Remove duplicates (with JOIN):
Note.objects.filter(tags__name='python').distinct()

# Load only certain fields (optimization):
Note.objects.only('id', 'title', 'priority')   # Other fields → an extra SELECT on access
Note.objects.defer('content')                   # All fields EXCEPT content

# Limiting (LIMIT / OFFSET):
Note.objects.all()[:10]                        # LIMIT 10
Note.objects.all()[10:20]                      # LIMIT 10 OFFSET 10
Note.objects.all()[0]                          # LIMIT 1 (= .first() but not None)

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text: Moving from SQLite to PostgreSQL is an important step before production. SQLite is ideal for development, but PostgreSQL provides: concurrent access, extended field types, ACID transactions with isolation levels, and performance with large volumes of data.

docs.title: 10.1 Running PostgreSQL with Docker
docs.text:
# Run with docker-compose:
docker-compose up -d

# Or directly with docker run:
docker run -d \
  --name notes_postgres \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=notes_db \
  -e POSTGRES_USER=notes_user \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=notes_pass \
  -p 5432:5432 \
  postgres:16-alpine

# docker-compose.yml
version: '3.9'
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: notes_db
      POSTGRES_USER: notes_user
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: notes_pass
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
volumes:
  postgres_data:

After switching to PostgreSQL, unique field types become available:

# PostgreSQL only — ArrayField, JSONField with full capabilities
from django.contrib.postgres.fields import ArrayField

    )

# Filtering by JSON/Array:
Note.objects.filter(quick_labels__contains=['python'])
Note.objects.filter(metadata__word_count__gte=100)
Note.objects.filter(metadata__language='uk')

docs.title: QuerySet in depth: N+1, normalization, transactions
docs.text: This section covers three key concepts: database schema normalization, solving the N+1 problem, and atomic operations.

docs.title: Normalization: Before / After
docs.text: "One truth for one fact." Normalization is the process of finding and removing duplication from a relational schema. Goal: every fact is stored in exactly one place.

docs.title: 3NF by example
docs.text:
❌ BEFORE (1NF) — everything in a single employees table:

id name dept_id dept_name location salary 1 Alice 10 Engineering Kyiv 50000 2 Bob 10 Engineering Kyiv 45000 3 Carol 20 Design Lviv 48000 4 Dan 10 Engineering Kyiv 52000 5 Eva 20 Design Lviv 49000

Problem: "Engineering / Kyiv" is repeated 3 times. Moved to Kharkiv? UPDATE 1000 rows. Made a typo in the name? Inconsistency.

--- → 3NF: move it into a separate table ---

✅ AFTER — employees (FK → departments.id):

id name dept_id salary 1 Alice 10 50000 2 Bob 10 45000 3 Carol 20 48000 4 Dan 10 52000 5 Eva 20 49000

✅ departments — one truth:

id name location 10 Engineering Kyiv 20 Design Lviv 
# Django model after normalization:
class Department(models.Model):
    name     = models.CharField(max_length=80)
    location = models.CharField(max_length=80)

class Employee(models.Model):
    name       = models.CharField(max_length=80)
    department = models.ForeignKey(Department, on_delete=models.PROTECT)
    salary     = models.DecimalField(max_digits=10, decimal_places=2)

Moving now: UPDATE departments SET location='Kharkiv' WHERE id=10; 1 row instead of 1000. Inconsistency is impossible.

docs.title: The three normal forms — cheat sheet
docs.text:
Form Rule Violation — example 1NF All values are atomic, no arrays in a cell tags = "python,django,orm" in a single column 2NF All non-key attributes depend on the whole PK In the table (order_id, product_id) → product_name depends only on product_id 3NF No transitive dependencies (A→B→C where B is not a key) employee.dept_name depends on dept_id, not on employee.id

Rule of thumb: if changing one fact requires an UPDATE of > 1 row, the schema is not normalized.

docs.title: The N+1 Problem
docs.text: The most common performance bug in Django: Django makes 1 + N SQL queries instead of 1.

docs.title: Why N+1 happens
docs.text:
N+1 happens precisely because a QuerySet is lazy. The student already knows that for note in notes: materializes a single SELECT. But as soon as note.notebook appears in the template, Django does not know that notebook will be needed for every note, so it runs a separate SELECT for each one:

{% for note in notes %}
    {{ note.notebook.title }}   ← for each note: SELECT FROM notebooks WHERE id=?
{% endfor %}

50 notes → the template "asks for" the notebook 50 times → 51 SQL queries instead of the expected one.

This is not a Django bug — it is a natural consequence of lazy loading. The solution is to tell Django explicitly, in advance, which relationships will be needed.

# 50 notes in the database. Each has a ForeignKey to Notebook.
notes = Note.objects.all()          # Query 1: SELECT * FROM notes  ← 50 rows

for note in notes:
    print(note.notebook.title)       # Query 2, 3, 4, ..., 51!
    # Each note.notebook.title → a SEPARATE SELECT FROM notebooks WHERE id=...
    # 50 notes → 50 extra queries → 51 TOTAL!

docs.title: select_related — solving N+1 for FKs
docs.text:
# ❌ N+1: 100 notes + 100 queries for user + 100 for notebook = 201 queries
notes = Note.objects.filter(is_archived=False)[:100]
for note in notes:
    print(note.user.username, note.notebook.title)  # new SQL for each one!

# ✅ select_related: 1 query with a JOIN
notes = Note.objects.select_related(
    'user', 'notebook'
).filter(is_archived=False)[:100]
for note in notes:
    print(note.user.username, note.notebook.title)  # already in memory

docs.title: How it works inside
docs.text:
# Step 1: The base QuerySet (LAZY — the SQL has not been executed yet!)
qs = Note.objects.filter(user=user, is_archived=archived)
#    SQL so far: WHERE note.user_id=? AND note.is_archived=?
#    But the SQL is NOT executed — Django waits until someone iterates the QuerySet!

# Step 2: select_related('notebook') — join the FK with a single JOIN
qs = qs.select_related('notebook')
#    The SQL becomes: LEFT JOIN hello_app_notebook nb ON note.notebook_id = nb.id
#    Consequence: note.notebook.title → does NOT run a new SELECT (already in memory!)
#
#    WITHOUT select_related: for note in qs: print(note.notebook.title)
#                        → 1 SELECT + N SELECT = the N+1 problem!
#    WITH select_related: 1 SELECT with a JOIN — always!

docs.title: prefetch_related — for M:N and reverse FKs
docs.text:
# ✅ 2 queries: one for notes, one for tags
notes = Note.objects.prefetch_related('tags').all()[:50]
for note in notes:
    print([t.name for t in note.tags.all()])  # already in memory!

docs.title: How it works inside
docs.text:
# Step 3: prefetch_related('tags') — load the M:N relationship
qs = qs.prefetch_related('tags')
#    QUERY 1: SELECT * FROM note WHERE ...
#    QUERY 2: SELECT tag.* ... WHERE note_id IN (1, 2, 3, ...)
#    Python: Django joins them on its own
#    Consequence: note.tags.all() → already in the cache, NOT a new SELECT!

docs.title: Prefetch with a filter (to_attr)
docs.text:
from django.db.models import Prefetch
from django.utils import timezone

notes = Note.objects.prefetch_related(
    'tags',
    Prefetch(
        'reminders',
        queryset=Reminder.objects.filter(
            remind_at__gte=timezone.now()   # only FUTURE reminders
        ).order_by('remind_at'),
        to_attr='upcoming_reminders'  # store them in a SEPARATE attribute!
    )
)

# Why Prefetch with to_attr?
# WITHOUT to_attr:  note.reminders.all()         → NEW QuerySet (another SELECT!)
#              note.reminders.filter(...)      → NEW QuerySet (a different SELECT!)
# WITH to_attr:   note.upcoming_reminders        → list[Reminder] (already in memory!)
#   In the template: {% for r in note.upcoming_reminders %}  ← NO SELECT!

docs.title: Combining select_related and prefetch_related
docs.text:
# A real example: the note_list view
notes = (
    Note.objects
    .select_related('user', 'notebook')     # FK → SQL JOIN (1 query)
    .prefetch_related('tags', 'reminders')  # M:N + reverse FK (2 queries)
    .filter(is_archived=False)
    .order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')
)
# TOTAL: 2 SQL queries for any number of notes ✓
# WITHOUT optimization: 1 + N + N SQL (for N notes)

docs.title: Annotate instead of N queries
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG: N+1!
notebooks = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user)
for nb in notebooks:
    count = nb.notes.filter(is_archived=False).count()  # a separate SELECT!
# 10 notebooks → 11 SQL queries!

# ✅ RIGHT: a single GROUP BY
notebooks = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user).annotate(
    note_count=Count('notes', filter=Q(notes__is_archived=False))
)
# SQL: SELECT nb.*, COUNT(note.id) FILTER (WHERE note.is_archived=FALSE) AS note_count
#      FROM notebook nb LEFT JOIN note ON note.notebook_id=nb.id
#      WHERE nb.user_id=? GROUP BY nb.id
# 1 SQL! nb.note_count → a number, already in memory!

docs.title: Double annotation
docs.text:
TodoList.objects.filter(user=user).annotate(
    total_items=Count('items'),                                    # total items
    done_items=Count('items', filter=Q(items__is_done=True))       # completed
)
# SQL: SELECT todolist.*,
#             COUNT(item.id) AS total_items,
#             COUNT(item.id) FILTER (WHERE item.is_done=TRUE) AS done_items
#      FROM todolist LEFT JOIN todoitem item ON item.todo_list_id = todolist.id
#      WHERE todolist.user_id = ? GROUP BY todolist.id
#
# In the template:
# todo.total_items → 5 (without a single SELECT!)
# todo.done_items  → 3 (without a single SELECT!)
# Progress: 3/5 = 60%

docs.title: How to detect N+1: Django Debug Toolbar
docs.text:
pip install django-debug-toolbar

# settings.py:
INSTALLED_APPS = ['debug_toolbar', ...]
MIDDLEWARE = ['debug_toolbar.middleware.DebugToolbarMiddleware', ...MIDDLEWARE]
INTERNAL_IPS = ['127.0.0.1']

# urls.py:
if settings.DEBUG:
    import debug_toolbar
    urlpatterns = [path('__debug__/', include(debug_toolbar.urls))] + urlpatterns

In the browser → the side panel shows all SQL queries with duplicates highlighted.

docs.title: F() — atomic operations
docs.text:
from django.db.models import F

# ✅ Atomic increment (race-condition safe!)
# UPDATE hello_app_note SET views_count = views_count + 1 WHERE id = 42
Note.objects.filter(pk=42).update(views_count=F('views_count') + 1)

# ✅ Comparing two fields with each other
Note.objects.filter(views_count__gt=F('likes_count'))
# WHERE views_count > likes_count  (comparing COLUMNS, not values)

# ❌ Unsafe with concurrent requests:
note = Note.objects.get(pk=42)
note.views_count += 1   # reads in Python
note.save()             # writes back → race condition!

docs.title: transaction.atomic()
docs.text: An atomic operation: either ALL changes are saved, or NONE.

docs.title: The problem without atomic
docs.text:
def create_note(user, title, tag_ids):
    note = Note.objects.create(user=user, title=title)
    # ← INSERT INTO note → id=42

    # AN ERROR HERE (for example, a tag does not exist):
    tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=user)
    note.tags.set(tags)   # ← An exception because of an invalid tag_id!

    # DATABASE STATE:
    # The Note with id=42 exists (the INSERT already happened)
    # But the tags are not attached
    # AN INCONSISTENT STATE! An "orphan" without tags

docs.title: The solution — transaction.atomic
docs.text:
from django.db import transaction

def create_note(user, title, tag_ids):
    with transaction.atomic():
        note = Note.objects.create(user=user, title=title)
        # ← While inside the atomic block → BEGIN TRANSACTION

        tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=user)
        note.tags.set(tags)
        # ← If there is an exception → ROLLBACK of the whole block
        # The Note is NOT saved in the DB!

    # ← If everything is OK → COMMIT
    return note

docs.title: Nested atomic blocks — savepoints
docs.text:
def complex_operation():
    with transaction.atomic():      # ← BEGIN
        do_operation_1()            # ← INSERT ...

        with transaction.atomic():  # ← SAVEPOINT sp_1
            do_operation_2()        # ← INSERT ...
            # If there is an exception here → ROLLBACK TO sp_1
            # operation_1 is kept!

        do_operation_3()            # ← INSERT ...
    # ← COMMIT (if everything is OK)

docs.title: @transaction.atomic as a decorator
docs.text:
@transaction.atomic
def create_notebook(user, title, is_default=False):
    """
    Business rule: a user has only ONE default notebook.
    These two queries must be atomic:
    1. Reset the previous default
    2. Set the new one
    """
    if is_default:
        Notebook.objects.filter(user=user, is_default=True).update(is_default=False)
        # ← If there is an exception here → there will be no "no default" situation
    return Notebook.objects.create(user=user, title=title, is_default=is_default)
    # ← Both operations succeed, or both are rolled back

docs.title: select_for_update() — preventing race conditions
docs.text:
with transaction.atomic():
    # SELECT ... FOR UPDATE → locks the row until the end of the transaction
    note = Note.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=note_id)
    if not note.is_archived:
        note.is_archived = True
        note.save(update_fields=['is_archived'])
    # COMMIT → the lock is released

# nowait=True: raises DatabaseError instead of waiting if the row is already locked
try:
    note = Note.objects.select_for_update(nowait=True).get(pk=note_id)
except DatabaseError:
    return JsonResponse({'error': 'Ресурс зайнятий, спробуйте пізніше'}, status=409)

docs.title: Why select_for_update is needed for a toggle
docs.text:
# WHY select_for_update()?
# The problem without locking:
#   Thread A: SELECT item WHERE id=5 → is_done=False
#   Thread B: SELECT item WHERE id=5 → is_done=False  (THE SAME VALUE!)
#   Thread A: UPDATE item SET is_done=True
#   Thread B: UPDATE item SET is_done=True  ← both set True!
#   Bug: the second click should have removed the checkmark!

with transaction.atomic():  # select_for_update REQUIRES atomic!
    item = TodoItem.objects.select_for_update().get(
        id=item_id,
        todo_list__user=user  # SECURITY: check access rights through the FK!
    )
    # SQL: SELECT ... FROM todoitem
    #      JOIN todolist ON todoitem.todo_list_id = todolist.id
    #      WHERE todoitem.id=? AND todolist.user_id=?
    #      FOR UPDATE  ← locks the row!

    item.is_done = not item.is_done
    item.save(update_fields=['is_done'])
# COMMIT → releases the row lock

docs.title: Services and Selectors
docs.text: Thin Views · Selectors Read · Services Write Each layer has one responsibility. Breaking this rule is the main cause of the "fat view" anti-pattern.

docs.title: Layer architecture
docs.text:
HTTP REQUEST
     │
     ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  views.py                               │
│  ✓ parses the request                   │
│  ✓ calls a selector / service           │
│  ✓ render / redirect                    │
│  ✗ no QuerySets                         │
└────────────┬───────────────┬────────────┘
             │ READ →        │ WRITE →
             ▼               ▼
┌────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
│  selectors.py      │  │  services.py                 │
│  SELECT only       │  │  CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE    │
│                    │  │                              │
│  get_user_notes()  │  │  create_note()               │
│  get_note_detail() │  │  update_note()               │
│  get_notebooks()   │  │  toggle_todo_item()          │
│  get_reminders()   │  │  mark_reminder_sent()        │
│                    │  │                              │
│  select_related,   │  │  transaction.atomic,         │
│  prefetch_related, │  │  F(), select_for_update      │
│  annotate — here   │  │  — here                      │
└────────┬───────────┘  └───────────┬──────────────────┘
         │ SELECT                   │ INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE
         └──────────┬───────────────┘
                    ▼
             ┌─────────────┐
             │  PostgreSQL │
             │  Database   │
             └─────────────┘

Why separate them? The same query is needed in a View, a Celery task, an API endpoint, a test. Without selectors.py, you copy the QuerySet into 10 places. Change the logic → 10 places to update. With selectors.py → one function that everyone uses.

docs.title: Responsibility matrix
docs.text:
Layer Does Does NOT do models.py Structure · fields · relationships · constraints · indexes Business logic, HTTP selectors.py SELECT QuerySets · annotate · prefetch · filters INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE services.py CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE · transaction · F() · locks HTTP, render, redirect views.py Parse the request · call a selector/service · render QuerySets, business logic forms.py Validating HTTP input · clean_* DB queries (except the queryset for choices) templates/ HTML markup · context from the View Any logic

Check yourself: if you see Note.objects.filter(...) in views.py, that is a signal to move it to selectors.py. If you see an access-permission check condition in a template, that is also a violation.

docs.title: The problem: a "Fat View"
docs.text:
# ❌ ANTI-PATTERN: all the logic in the view
def note_list(request):
    # Does the View know about QuerySet optimization? Not its job!
    notes = Note.objects.filter(
        user=request.user,
        is_archived=False,
    ).select_related('notebook').prefetch_related('tags')

    # Does the View know about business rules? Not its job!
    if request.GET.get('q'):
        notes = notes.filter(
            Q(title__icontains=request.GET['q']) |
            Q(content__icontains=request.GET['q'])
        )

    # If this logic is needed in an API endpoint or a Celery task → do we copy it?!
    return render(request, 'note_list.html', {'notes': notes})

docs.title: READ flow — tracing GET /notes/?q=python
docs.text:
01 │ Browser      │ GET /notes/?q=python
02 │ urls.py      │ match → views.note_list
03 │ views.py     │ search = request.GET['q']
04 │ views.py     │ selectors.get_user_notes(user, search='python')
05 │ selectors.py │ QuerySet.filter().select_related('notebook').prefetch_related('tags')
06 │ ORM          │ SQLCompiler → 2 SQL (note + tags prefetch)
07 │ PostgreSQL   │ executes the plan, returns rows
08 │ ORM          │ ModelIterable → list[Note] with a filled _result_cache
09 │ views.py     │ render('note_list.html', {notes, tags, notebooks})
10 │ Browser      │ 200 OK · HTML

The View stays thin: 3 lines of code (parse + delegate + render). All the complexity lives in selectors.get_user_notes: filters, JOINs, the prefetch cache.

docs.title: WRITE flow — tracing POST /notes/create/
docs.text:
01 │ Browser      │ POST /notes/create/ form=...
02 │ views.py     │ form = NoteForm(POST, user=request.user) · is_valid?
03 │ views.py     │ services.create_note(user, title, tag_ids)
04 │ services.py  │ with transaction.atomic():
05 │ services.py  │ Note.objects.create(...) → BEGIN, INSERT note
06 │ services.py  │ Tag.objects.filter(user=user, id__in=...) · ownership check
07 │ services.py  │ note.tags.set(valid) → INSERT × N into the junction
08 │ PostgreSQL   │ COMMIT · on_commit callbacks
09 │ views.py     │ messages.success(...)  ·  return redirect('note_detail', pk)
10 │ Browser      │ 302 → GET /notes/42/  (PRG pattern: F5 is safe)

PRG (Post / Redirect / Get). A POST does not render — it redirects. F5 repeats the GET, which is safe. Without PRG: F5 = a duplicate record.

Ownership through FK traversal. Tag.objects.filter(user=user, id__in=...) — do not let a user attach someone else's tags to their own note.

docs.text:
# hello_app/selectors.py
"""
Selectors — the data READ layer.
All SELECT queries live here.
Views, Tasks, API — everything uses selectors.
"""
from django.db.models import Count, Q, Prefetch
from django.utils import timezone

from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag, TodoList, TodoItem, ShoppingList, Reminder


def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False, notebook=None, tag=None, search=None):
    """
    The user's note list with filters.
    select_related + prefetch_related — solves the N+1 problem.

    Keyword-only kwargs (after *) — protection against positional arguments:
    get_user_notes(alice, True) → TypeError (unclear that True = archived)
    get_user_notes(alice, archived=True) → OK, explicit
    """
    qs = Note.objects.filter(
        user=user,
        is_archived=archived
    ).select_related(
        'notebook'           # FK → JOIN (1 query instead of N)
    ).prefetch_related(
        'tags'               # M:N → a 2nd query (not N+1)
    )

    if notebook:
        qs = qs.filter(notebook=notebook)

    if tag:
        qs = qs.filter(tags=tag)

    if search:
        qs = qs.filter(
            Q(title__icontains=search) | Q(content__icontains=search)
        )

    return qs.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')
    # Order: pinned first → priority → recently updated


def get_note_detail(user, note_id):
    """
    Note detail — with all its relationships.
    Raises Note.DoesNotExist if not found or not the owner.
    """
    return Note.objects.select_related(
        'notebook', 'user'
    ).prefetch_related(
        'tags',
        Prefetch(
            'reminders',
            queryset=Reminder.objects.filter(
                remind_at__gte=timezone.now()
            ).order_by('remind_at'),
            to_attr='upcoming_reminders'  # store them in a SEPARATE attribute!
        )
    ).get(id=note_id, user=user)


def get_user_notebooks(user):
    """All notebooks with their note counts."""
    return Notebook.objects.filter(user=user).annotate(
        note_count=Count('notes', filter=Q(notes__is_archived=False))
    ).order_by('-is_default', 'title')


def get_user_tags(user):
    """Tags with their note counts."""
    return Tag.objects.filter(user=user).annotate(
        note_count=Count('notes')
    ).order_by('name')


def get_note_for_user(user, pk):
    """
    Returns the note if it belongs to the user, or None.
    Used in a view instead of get_object_or_404 when softer handling is needed.
    """
    return Note.objects.filter(user=user, pk=pk).select_related('notebook').first()


def get_user_todo_lists(user):
    """To-do lists with progress."""
    return TodoList.objects.filter(
        user=user
    ).annotate(
        total_items=Count('items'),
        done_items=Count('items', filter=Q(items__is_done=True))
    ).prefetch_related('items').order_by('is_completed', '-created_at')


def get_pending_reminders():
    """For the Celery worker: reminders that need to be sent."""
    return Reminder.objects.filter(
        is_sent=False,
        remind_at__lte=timezone.now()
    ).select_related('note__user')

# hello_app/services.py
"""
Services — the data WRITE layer.
All the business logic lives here: CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE.
Services may call selectors, but not the other way around.
"""
from django.db import transaction
from django.db.models import F

from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag, TodoItem, Reminder


def create_note(*, user, title, content='', notebook=None, priority=1, tag_ids=None):
    """
    Creates a note with tags atomically.

    transaction.atomic(): either the Note and the tags are saved together, or nothing is.
    Tag protection: filter(user=user) → other users' tags are ignored (Mass Assignment protection).

    Why the asterisk * before the arguments?
    → all arguments are KEYWORD-ONLY (no positional ones after *)
    → call: services.create_note(user=user, title="Test")  ✓
    → call: services.create_note(user, "Test")             ✗ TypeError!
    Why? More readable, fewer mistakes during refactoring.
    """
    with transaction.atomic():  # SQL: BEGIN;
        note = Note.objects.create(
            user=user,
            title=title,
            content=content,
            notebook=notebook,
            priority=priority,
        )
        if tag_ids:
            # Check that the tags belong to this user (security!)
            valid_tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=user)
            # filter(user=user): Protection! The user cannot attach someone else's tags.
            note.tags.set(valid_tags)
        # COMMIT (or ROLLBACK if any operation failed!)

    return note


def update_note(note, *, title=None, content=None, notebook=..., priority=None,
                is_pinned=None, is_archived=None, tag_ids=None):
    """
    Updates only the fields that were passed.
    update_fields → UPDATE only the changed columns (more efficient).

    notebook=... (Ellipsis) = "not passed" (the notebook does not change).
    notebook=None           = "remove the notebook" (SET_NULL).
    notebook=<Notebook>     = "set the notebook".
    Ellipsis distinguishes "not passed" from "passed None".
    """
    changed = []
    if title is not None:
        note.title = title
        changed.append('title')
    if content is not None:
        note.content = content
        changed.append('content')
    if notebook is not ...:              # Ellipsis = sentinel "not passed"
        note.notebook = notebook         # None → SET_NULL; <Notebook> → set it
        changed.append('notebook')
    if priority is not None:
        note.priority = priority
        changed.append('priority')
    if is_pinned is not None:
        note.is_pinned = is_pinned
        changed.append('is_pinned')
    if is_archived is not None:
        note.is_archived = is_archived
        changed.append('is_archived')

    if changed:
        changed.append('updated_at')  # Always update the timestamp
        note.save(update_fields=changed)
        # SQL: UPDATE hello_app_note SET title=..., updated_at=... WHERE id=...
        # NOT: UPDATE hello_app_note SET ... (all fields)

    if tag_ids is not None:
        valid_tags = Tag.objects.filter(id__in=tag_ids, user=note.user)
        note.tags.set(valid_tags)   # DELETE the old ones + INSERT the new ones

    return note


def archive_note(note):
    """Archive a note (not delete it)."""
    Note.objects.filter(pk=note.pk).update(is_archived=True)


def toggle_pin_note(note):
    """Toggles is_pinned and saves it to the DB."""
    note.is_pinned = not note.is_pinned
    note.save(update_fields=['is_pinned', 'updated_at'])
    return note


def delete_note(note):
    """
    Deletes a note.
    CASCADE automatically deletes the related Reminder objects.
    """
    note.delete()


def toggle_todo_item(item_id, *, user):
    """
    Check/uncheck a list item.
    select_for_update() — prevents a race condition on simultaneous clicks.
    """
    with transaction.atomic():
        item = TodoItem.objects.select_for_update().get(
            id=item_id,
            todo_list__user=user   # access-permission check via FK traversal
        )
        # SQL: SELECT ... FROM todoitem
        #      JOIN todolist ON todoitem.todo_list_id = todolist.id
        #      WHERE todoitem.id=? AND todolist.user_id=?
        #      FOR UPDATE  ← locks the row!
        item.is_done = not item.is_done
        item.save(update_fields=['is_done'])
    return item


def mark_reminder_sent(reminder_id):
    """
    Atomically mark a reminder as sent.
    F() + update() — race condition safe.
    """
    Reminder.objects.filter(pk=reminder_id).update(is_sent=True)


def create_tag(*, user, name, color='#808080'):
    """Create a tag with a uniqueness check."""
    tag, created = Tag.objects.get_or_create(
        user=user,
        name=name.lower().strip(),  # normalization: "Python" → "python"
        defaults={'color': color}   # color is set ONLY on CREATE
    )
    return tag, created


@transaction.atomic
def create_notebook(user, title, is_default=False):
    """
    Business rule: a user has ONLY ONE default notebook.
    Atomically reset the old one and set the new one.
    """
    if is_default:
        Notebook.objects.filter(user=user, is_default=True).update(is_default=False)
        # UPDATE all to default=False before creating the new one
    return Notebook.objects.create(user=user, title=title, is_default=is_default)


def complete_todo_list(todo_list):
    """Bulk-mark all items as completed."""
    with transaction.atomic():
        # Step 1: mark the list
        todo_list.is_completed = True
        todo_list.save(update_fields=['is_completed'])

        # Step 2: bulk-mark all items
        todo_list.items.filter(is_done=False).update(is_done=True)
        # SQL: UPDATE todoitem SET is_done=TRUE
        #      WHERE todo_list_id=? AND is_done=FALSE
        #
        # WRONG:
        # for item in todo_list.items.all():
        #     item.is_done = True
        #     item.save()  # N queries instead of 1!
        #
        # RIGHT: .update() → 1 SQL for all rows!

def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
    # Step 1: initialize the parent ModelForm
    super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
    # After super().__init__:

        self.fields['notebook'].queryset = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user)
        # Now the dropdown shows ONLY this user's notebooks!
        self.fields['tags'].queryset = Tag.objects.filter(user=user)
        # Now the checkboxes show ONLY this user's tags!
    else:
        self.fields['notebook'].queryset = Notebook.objects.none()
        self.fields['tags'].queryset = Tag.objects.none()

    self.fields['notebook'].required = False

def clean_name(self):
    # Validation Pipeline:
    # 1. to_python("  Python  ") → str "  Python  "
    # 2. validate("  Python  ") → OK (required, max_length)
    # 3. run_validators → (no custom ones)
    # 4. clean_name(self) ← WE ARE HERE
    #    self.cleaned_data['name'] = "  Python  " (the string that passed validate)

    name = self.cleaned_data['name']
    normalized = name.lower().strip()   # "  Python  " → "python"

    if not normalized:
        raise forms.ValidationError("Назва тегу не може бути порожньою.")

    return normalized  # ← you MUST return it!
    # cleaned_data['name'] = "python" (normalized!)

docs.text:
URL: GET /notes/?q=python&notebook=3&tag=7

from django.contrib import messages
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, redirect, render

from .forms import NoteForm
from .models import Note
from . import selectors, services


@login_required   # ← AnonymousUser → redirect to /accounts/login/?next=...
def note_list(request):
    # Step 1: Read the filters from the URL
    search = request.GET.get('q', '').strip()  # '' if missing
    tag_id = request.GET.get('tag')            # '7' or None

    # Step 2: Convert id → objects (with a permission check!)
    tag = None
    if tag_id:
        try:
            tag = Tag.objects.get(id=int(tag_id), user=request.user)
            #                          ↑                ↑
            #              string→int conversion    only your own tag!
        except (Tag.DoesNotExist, ValueError):
            pass  # invalid id → simply ignore it

    # Step 3: Get the data through a selector
    notes     = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user, search=search or None, tag=tag)
    tags      = selectors.get_user_tags(request.user)
    notebooks = selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user)

    # Step 4: Render (this is where the QuerySet is executed!)
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_list.html', {
        'notes':     notes,
        'tags':      tags,
        'notebooks': notebooks,
        'search':    search,
    })
    # During rendering: {% for note in notes %} → the SQL SELECT is executed!

docs.title: note_create(request) — the PRG pattern
docs.text:
GET  /notes/new/  → show an empty form
POST /notes/new/  → process the form → redirect

@login_required
def note_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        # 1. Bind the POST data to the form (the form becomes "bound")
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)

        # 2. Validation Pipeline:
        #    to_python → validate → run_validators → clean_<field> → clean
        if form.is_valid():
            # 3. Extract tag_ids from the M:N field
            tags = form.cleaned_data.get('tags')   # QuerySet[Tag] or None
            tag_ids = [t.id for t in tags] if tags else None  # [1, 3] or None

            # 4. Business logic → Service (not here in the View!)
            note = services.create_note(
                user     = request.user,
                title    = form.cleaned_data['title'],  # a typed str (validated!)
                content  = form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                notebook = form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                priority = form.cleaned_data.get('priority', 1),
                tag_ids  = tag_ids,
            )

            # 5. PRG: messages + redirect (not render!)
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" створено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
            # HTTP 302 → GET /notes/42/ → safe, F5 does not duplicate!

    else:  # GET
        form = NoteForm(user=request.user)  # an empty form

    # Render for GET and for a POST with errors:
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'title': 'Нова нотатка',
        'action': 'Створити',
    })

@login_required
def note_edit(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
    # pk + user=request.user → 404 if it is someone else's note (IDOR protection)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            services.update_note(
                note,
                title    = form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content  = form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                notebook = form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                priority = form.cleaned_data.get('priority'),
                tag_ids  = [t.id for t in form.cleaned_data.get('tags', [])],
            )
            messages.success(request, 'Нотатку оновлено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(instance=note, user=request.user)

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form, 'note': note, 'title': f'Редагувати: {note.title}'
    })

GET  /notes/42/delete/  → confirmation page
POST /notes/42/delete/  → deletion → redirect

# Why can't GET delete?
# Browsers, bots, antivirus software make GET requests AUTOMATICALLY
# (prefetching links, availability checks, etc.)
# If GET /notes/42/delete/ deleted things → notes would disappear "by themselves"!

@login_required
def note_delete(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
    # SQL: SELECT WHERE id=42 AND user_id=request.user.id
    # 404 if not found → Alice cannot delete Bob's notes!

    if request.method == 'POST':  # the form in the confirmation template
        title = note.title  # save it BEFORE deleting
        services.delete_note(note)
        # CASCADE: deleting a note → automatically deletes its Reminder objects
        messages.warning(request, f'Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_list')

    # GET → show the page with a warning and a confirmation form
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

docs.title: Views in detail — the full HTTP cycle
docs.text: A view is a Python function (or class) that receives an HTTP request and returns an HTTP response. It is the single entry point for every URL in Django.

docs.title: Why views — the HTTP Request/Response cycle
docs.text:
Browser → HTTP Request → Django → View → HTTP Response → Browser

Every click on a link or form submission is an HTTP request. Django matches the URL to a view function through urls.py and passes it the request object. The view processes the request and returns a response.

# The simplest view — takes a request, returns a response
from django.http import HttpResponse

def hello(request):
    return HttpResponse("Hello, Django!")  # 200 OK + text

GET /hello/  →  Django → hello(request)  →  200 OK "Hello, Django!"

But in real applications, a view does more: - Checks authentication (@login_required) - Reads GET/POST parameters - Calls selectors (reading from the DB) and services (changes in the DB) - Renders an HTML template or returns JSON - Redirects after a successful POST (the PRG pattern)

docs.title: The request object — everything that came from the browser
docs.text:
request is an instance of HttpRequest. It contains everything the browser sent:

@login_required
def note_create(request):
    # The HTTP request method:
    request.method        # → 'GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE'

    # The current authenticated user (filled in by AuthMiddleware):
    request.user          # → a User object or AnonymousUser
    request.user.is_authenticated  # → True/False

    # GET parameters (?q=python&tag=5):
    request.GET           # → QueryDict {'q': ['python'], 'tag': ['5']}
    request.GET.get('q', '')  # → 'python' (None if missing)
    request.GET.getlist('ids') # → ['1', '2', '3'] if ids=1&ids=2&ids=3

    # POST parameters (the form body):
    request.POST          # → QueryDict {'title': ['Нотатка'], 'priority': ['2']}
    request.POST.get('title', '')  # → 'Нотатка'

    # Uploaded files:
    request.FILES         # → MultiValueDict {'avatar': [<InMemoryUploadedFile>]}

    # Browser cookies (a dictionary):
    request.COOKIES       # → {'sessionid': 'abc123', 'csrftoken': 'xyz456'}

    # HTTP headers:
    request.headers       # → {'Host': 'localhost', 'Accept': 'text/html', ...}
    request.META.get('HTTP_REFERER', '')  # → URL of the previous page

    # The current URL (without GET parameters):
    request.path          # → '/notes/new/'

    # AJAX check (if fetch/axios sends the header):
    request.headers.get('X-Requested-With') == 'XMLHttpRequest'

Why request.POST and not request.body.decode()?

request.POST is an already parsed QueryDict from an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. request.body is the raw byte string. JSON APIs use json.loads(request.body), but for HTML forms it is always request.POST.

docs.title: render() — an HTML page
docs.text:
from django.shortcuts import render

def note_list(request):
    notes = Note.objects.filter(user=request.user)

    return render(
        request,                        # 1. request (required)
        'notes_app/note_list.html',     # 2. template path
        {'notes': notes, 'count': notes.count()},  # 3. context (a dictionary)
        # status=200,                   # 4. HTTP status (200 by default)
    )

# render() = TemplateResponse:
#   1. Finds the template by its path
#   2. Renders the Django Template with the context
#   3. Returns an HttpResponse with Content-Type: text/html

Check: 

curl -I http://localhost:8001/notes/
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
# Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8

docs.title: redirect() — redirection
docs.text:
from django.shortcuts import redirect

# Redirect by URL name (recommended — does not depend on the actual URL)
return redirect('notes_app:note_list')
# → HTTP/1.1 302 Found + Location: /notes/

# Redirect by URL with arguments:
return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
# → HTTP/1.1 302 Found + Location: /notes/42/

# Redirect by a URL string (hardcoded — not recommended):
return redirect('/notes/')

# Permanent redirect (301, for SEO):
return redirect('notes_app:note_list', permanent=True)
# → HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently

301 vs 302:

Code Name When 302 Found (temporary) After a POST (PRG pattern), after login 301 Moved Permanently The URL has changed permanently (SEO, old links)

The browser caches a 301. If you make a 301 by accident, the browser will cache it forever. In development, always use 302.

docs.title: HttpResponse — an arbitrary response
docs.text:
from django.http import HttpResponse, HttpResponseNotFound, HttpResponseForbidden

# Plain text:
return HttpResponse("OK", status=200)

# JSON (better: JsonResponse):
import json
return HttpResponse(
    json.dumps({'status': 'ok'}),
    content_type='application/json',
    status=200,
)

# 404 manually (better: raise Http404):
return HttpResponseNotFound("Сторінку не знайдено")

# 403 manually:
return HttpResponseForbidden("Доступ заборонено")

docs.title: JsonResponse — a JSON API
docs.text:
from django.http import JsonResponse

def api_notes(request):
    notes = Note.objects.filter(user=request.user).values('id', 'title', 'priority')
    return JsonResponse(
        {'notes': list(notes)},   # ← json.dumps() automatically
        status=200,
    )
# → HTTP/1.1 200 OK + Content-Type: application/json
# → {"notes": [{"id": 1, "title": "Назва", "priority": 2}]}

docs.title: Http404 — page not found
docs.text:
from django.http import Http404

def note_detail(request, pk):
    try:
        note = Note.objects.get(pk=pk, user=request.user)
    except Note.DoesNotExist:
        raise Http404("Нотатку не знайдено")
    # → 404 Not Found + the templates/404.html template

# Or the shortcut — get_object_or_404:
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404
note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
# If the Note does not exist → 404 automatically

docs.title: PRG Pattern — Post/Redirect/Get
docs.text:
The problem without PRG: 

POST /notes/new/ (form)
→ The View saves the note
→ render() 200 OK (HTML with "Saved!")
→ The browser shows the page
→ F5 (refresh)
→ The browser asks: "Resend the POST request?"
→ If "Yes" → the note is created TWICE! A duplicate.

With PRG (Post/Redirect/Get): 

POST /notes/new/ (form)
→ The View saves the note
→ redirect() 302 → /notes/42/   ← REDIRECT after a successful POST!
→ The browser performs GET /notes/42/
→ The View renders the note
→ F5 → repeats GET /notes/42/ → safe


# The PRG pattern — a mandatory standard for forms
@login_required
def note_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = services.create_note(
                user=request.user,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', 2),
                notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                tag_ids=[t.id for t in form.cleaned_data.get('tags', [])],
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" створено!')
            return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)  # ← PRG: redirect!
        # is_valid() = False → fall through → render the form with errors
    else:
        form = NoteForm(user=request.user)  # GET: an empty form

    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'title': 'Нова нотатка',
        'action': 'Створити',
    })

Flow diagram:

GET /notes/new/
    │
    ▼
form = NoteForm(user=request.user)  ← an empty form
    │
    ▼
render(note_form.html, {'form': form})  ← 200 OK

The student fills it in and clicks Submit:

POST /notes/new/
    │
    ▼
form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
    │
    ├── is_valid() = False
    │       │
    │       └── render(note_form.html, {'form': form})  ← 200 OK with errors
    │
    └── is_valid() = True
            │
            ├── services.create_note(...)
            ├── messages.success(...)
            └── redirect('note_detail', pk=...)  ← 302 Found

GET /notes/42/
    │
    ▼
render(note_detail.html, {'note': note})  ← 200 OK

docs.title: get_object_or_404() — safely retrieving an object
docs.text:
from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404

# Basic syntax:
note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)
# SQL: SELECT * FROM note WHERE id=42
# If not found → Http404 (a 404 Not Found page)

# With a permission check (MANDATORY for private data!):
note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
# SQL: SELECT * FROM note WHERE id=42 AND user_id=<current_user_id>
# If Alice requests Bob's note → 404 (not 403!) → Alice does not know whether this note exists at all

Why 404 and not 403 for other users' objects?

403 Forbidden: "you do not have permission"
→ Alice knows that id=42 EXISTS (she just has no access)
→ Information leak: an attacker iterates over ids and learns which ones exist

404 Not Found: "not found"  (but it actually exists, it is just not yours)
→ Alice does not know whether id=42 exists at all
→ No leak of information about other users' data

Syntax variants:

# 1. By pk via a keyword argument:
note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)

# 2. By queryset — more flexible (allows filter, select_related):
note = get_object_or_404(
    Note.objects.select_related('notebook', 'user'),
    pk=pk,
    user=request.user,
)

# 3. With a Q filter (group notes — either mine or shared):
from django.db.models import Q
user_groups = request.user.groups.all()
note = get_object_or_404(
    Note.objects.filter(Q(user=request.user) | Q(group__in=user_groups)),
    pk=pk,
)

docs.title: Messages Framework — one-time messages
docs.text:
Django Messages lets you pass a message through a redirect. The message is stored in the session and displayed once on the next render.

from django.contrib import messages

# Message types:
messages.success(request, 'Нотатку створено!')       # green
messages.error(request, 'Помилка при збереженні.')   # red
messages.warning(request, 'Нотатку видалено.')        # yellow
messages.info(request, 'Для початку — авторизуйся.') # blue

# In the template (base.html or layouts/dashboard.html):

{% if messages %}
{% for message in messages %}
<div class="alert alert-{{ message.tags }} alert-dismissible fade show" role="alert">
    {{ message }}
    <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-bs-dismiss="alert"></button>
</div>
{% endfor %}
{% endif %}

# settings.py — mapping levels to Bootstrap classes:
from django.contrib.messages import constants as messages_constants
MESSAGE_TAGS = {
    messages_constants.DEBUG:   'secondary',
    messages_constants.INFO:    'info',
    messages_constants.SUCCESS: 'success',
    messages_constants.WARNING: 'warning',
    messages_constants.ERROR:   'danger',   # Bootstrap: alert-danger
}

How messages pass through a redirect:

POST /notes/42/delete/
    │
    ├── messages.warning(request, 'Видалено.')   ← stored in the SESSION
    └── redirect('notes_app:note_list')           ← 302

GET /notes/
    │
    ├── Django inserts messages from the SESSION into the context
    └── render(note_list.html)
            │
            └── {% for message in messages %} ← shown ONCE, then deleted

docs.title: @login_required
docs.text:
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required

@login_required
def note_list(request):
    # request.user is guaranteed to be authenticated here
    ...

# What happens if the user is not logged in:
# → redirect '/accounts/login/?next=/notes/'
# After login → redirect back to '/notes/'

# Change the login URL (if it is non-standard):
@login_required(login_url='/auth/login/')
def note_list(request):
    ...

# Or globally in settings.py:
LOGIN_URL = '/accounts/login/'

docs.title: @require_http_methods / @require_POST
docs.text:
from django.views.decorators.http import require_POST, require_GET, require_http_methods

# POST only (for example, for deletion or a toggle):
@login_required
@require_POST
def note_pin(request, pk):
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)
    services.toggle_pin_note(note)
    return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=pk)

# A GET request to this view → 405 Method Not Allowed

# Or with the methods decorator:
@require_http_methods(['GET', 'POST'])
def note_create(request):
    ...
# PUT, DELETE → 405

docs.title: Decorator order
docs.text:
# ❌ WRONG: login_required checks after require_POST
@require_POST
@login_required
def note_delete(request, pk):
    ...

# Anonymous GET → require_POST: 405 (not a 302 to login!)

# ✅ RIGHT: login_required first → checks authentication before the method
@login_required
@require_POST
def note_delete(request, pk):
    ...

# Anonymous GET → login_required: 302 to login ✓

Decorators are applied from the bottom up. @login_required above @require_POST means that login_required runs FIRST when the view is called.

docs.title: The full request → response cycle
docs.text:
Browser: POST /notes/new/

     │
     ▼
1. nginx (reverse proxy)
   → proxies to Django/Uvicorn

     │
     ▼
2. Django Middleware (a chain, ordered as in MIDDLEWARE in settings.py)
   → SecurityMiddleware: checks HTTPS, CSP
   → SessionMiddleware: loads the session from DB/Redis → request.session
   → AuthenticationMiddleware: session → request.user
   → CsrfViewMiddleware: checks csrfmiddlewaretoken
   → MessageMiddleware: loads messages from the session

     │
     ▼
3. URL Router (urls.py)
   → path('notes/new/', views.note_create, name='note_create')
   → calls views.note_create(request)

     │
     ▼
4. View: note_create(request)
   → request.method == 'POST'
   → NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
   → form.is_valid()
   → services.create_note(...)
   → messages.success(request, '...')
   → redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
   → HttpResponse(status=302, Location='/notes/42/')

     │
     ▼
5. Response Middleware (reverse order)
   → MessageMiddleware: saves messages to the session
   → SessionMiddleware: saves the session

     │
     ▼
6. HTTP Response → nginx → browser
   302 Found
   Location: /notes/42/

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text: Error Cause Solution 302 instead of 200 on GET @login_required and the user is not logged in Log in or check request.user.is_authenticated 403 Forbidden on POST CSRF token missing or invalid Add {% csrf_token %} to the form 404 Not Found get_object_or_404 found nothing or the URL is wrong Check the pk and user in the request 405 Method Not Allowed Wrong HTTP method (e.g. GET instead of POST) Check the form's method attribute 500 Internal Server Error An error in the view's Python code Read the stack trace in the Django logs The form is not saved, no redirect is_valid() returns False Temporarily add print(form.errors)

docs.title: Add print for debugging (temporarily)
docs.text:
@login_required
def note_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
        print("POST data:", request.POST)     # ← what came from the browser
        print("Form errors:", form.errors)    # ← why the form is invalid
        if form.is_valid():
            ...

# View in the Docker logs:
docker compose logs -f web
# → POST data: <QueryDict: {'title': [''], 'priority': ['2'], ...}>
# → Form errors: {'title': ['Це поле обов'язкове.']}

docs.title: Check in the Django shell
docs.text:
docker compose exec web python manage.py shell

from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from notes_app.forms import NoteForm

user = User.objects.get(username='demo_alice')

# Simulate is_valid() with POST data:
data = {
    'title': '',        # empty → error
    'priority': '2',
    'csrfmiddlewaretoken': 'fake',  # not checked in the shell
}
form = NoteForm(data, user=user)
print(form.is_valid())   # → False
print(form.errors)       # → {'title': ['Це поле обов'язкове.']}

# A valid POST:
data['title'] = 'Тест'
form = NoteForm(data, user=user)
print(form.is_valid())         # → True
print(form.cleaned_data)       # → {'title': 'Тест', 'priority': 2, ...}

docs.title: Example: full CRUD for tags (a simple case)
docs.text:
Tags are a good example of a minimal view: no complex filters, no M:N relationships in the form.

# notes_app/views.py

@login_required
def tag_list(request):
    tags = selectors.get_user_tags(request.user)
    return render(request, 'notes_app/tag_list.html', {'tags': tags})


@login_required
def tag_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = TagForm(request.POST)
        if form.is_valid():
            tag = services.create_or_get_tag(
                user=request.user,
                name=form.cleaned_data['name'],
                color=form.cleaned_data.get('color', '#6c757d'),
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Тег "{tag.name}" створено.')

            # Support for ?next= — if we came from a note page, go back there
            next_url = request.GET.get('next') or request.POST.get('next')
            return redirect(next_url or 'notes_app:note_list')
    else:
        # Support for ?name=python — pre-fills the field
        initial = {}
        if name := request.GET.get('name'):
            initial['name'] = name
        form = TagForm(initial=initial)

    return render(request, 'notes_app/tag_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'title': 'Новий тег',
    })


@login_required
def tag_delete(request, pk):
    tag = get_object_or_404(Tag, pk=pk, user=request.user)
    if request.method == 'POST':
        name = tag.name
        tag.delete()   # a simple case — there is no services.delete_tag()
        messages.warning(request, f'Тег "{name}" видалено.')
        return redirect('notes_app:tag_list')
    return render(request, 'notes_app/tag_confirm_delete.html', {'tag': tag})

Two interesting patterns:

  1. ?next= for a redirect after an action: 

    <!-- In the note form template — add a tag and come back: -->
<a href="{% url 'notes_app:tag_create' %}?next={{ request.path }}">
    Новий тег
</a>

  2. ?name=python for pre-filling: 

    <!-- Quickly create a tag with a name from the search: -->
<a href="{% url 'notes_app:tag_create' %}?name={{ search }}">
    Створити тег "{{ search }}"
</a>

docs.title: Step 4. Templates and Forms
docs.text:
Tutorial project: crispy_notes — a standalone application on SQLite, without authentication. This is the fourth step of the evolution: we build a SaaS Dashboard with 3-level Template Inheritance, move from hand-written Bootstrap HTML to {% crispy form %}, and implement a Context Processor for the Sidebar.

Prerequisites

Before you start, make sure you have completed:

  • Step 1. Hello Django — the first HttpResponse, URL routing
  • Step 2. Bootstrap Notes — ModelForm, PRG, Bootstrap CRUD

docs.text: This section covers material from django_bootstrap_project — a practical project where Bootstrap is included via a CDN, and Unfold Admin and the Debug Toolbar are configured.

docs.title: Step B1 — Updating settings.py
docs.text:
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    'django.contrib.admin',
    'django.contrib.auth',
    'django.contrib.contenttypes',
    'django.contrib.sessions',
    'django.contrib.messages',
    'django.contrib.staticfiles',
    'django_bootstrap5',         # ← ADD (Bootstrap 5 for forms)
    'debug_toolbar',             # ← ADD (SQL debugger)
    'hello_app',
]

MIDDLEWARE = [
    'debug_toolbar.middleware.DebugToolbarMiddleware',  # ← ADD IT FIRST
    'django.middleware.security.SecurityMiddleware',
    'django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware',
    'django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware',
    'django.middleware.csrf.CsrfViewMiddleware',
    'django.contrib.auth.middleware.AuthenticationMiddleware',
    'django.contrib.messages.middleware.MessageMiddleware',
    'django.middleware.clickjacking.XFrameOptionsMiddleware',
]

# At the end of the file, add:
INTERNAL_IPS = ['127.0.0.1']

# Bootstrap 5 messages integration
from django.contrib.messages import constants as messages
MESSAGE_TAGS = {
    messages.DEBUG:   'secondary',
    messages.INFO:    'info',
    messages.SUCCESS: 'success',
    messages.WARNING: 'warning',
    messages.ERROR:   'danger',
}

What is MESSAGE_TAGS? Django Messages (flash messages after a POST) have their own levels: success, error, and so on. Bootstrap Alert uses alert-success, alert-danger. MESSAGE_TAGS maps one to the other.

docs.title: Step B2 — Updating urls.py
docs.text:
from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import path, include
from debug_toolbar.toolbar import debug_toolbar_urls

urlpatterns = [
    path('admin/', admin.site.urls),
    path('', include('hello_app.urls', namespace='hello_app')),
] + debug_toolbar_urls()

docs.title: Phase C — The full base.html code
docs.text: Django looks for templates in <app>/templates/. Let's create base.html outside hello_app/templates/hello_app/ — directly in hello_app/templates/, so that it is available globally.

docs.text:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="uk">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>{% block title %}Bootstrap Notes{% endblock %}</title>

    <!--
        Bootstrap 5 CSS — we include it in <head>.
        Why: the browser reads CSS before rendering the page body.
        If you include it at the end, you get a "flash of unstyled content".
    -->
    <link rel="stylesheet"
          href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
          integrity="sha384-QWTKZyjpPEjISv5WaRU9OFeRpok6YctnYmDr5pNlyT2bRjXh0JMhjY6hW+ALEwIH"
          crossorigin="anonymous">

    <!-- Bootstrap Icons — a separate icon library -->
    <link rel="stylesheet"
          href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/font/bootstrap-icons.css">

    <!-- A slot for extra CSS on specific pages -->
    {% block extra_css %}{% endblock %}
</head>
<body class="bg-light d-flex flex-column min-vh-100">
<!--
    Sticky Footer — three Bootstrap classes solve the problem of a "floating" footer.
    d-flex flex-column — body becomes a vertical flex container.
    min-vh-100 — body always takes at least 100% of the window height.
    flex-grow-1 on <main> below — main takes all the free space between nav and footer.
-->

    <!--
        NAVBAR — the Bootstrap navigation component.
        navbar-expand-lg: horizontal on large screens, a hamburger on small ones.
    -->
    <nav class="navbar navbar-expand-lg navbar-dark bg-dark shadow-sm">
        <div class="container">

            <!-- Brand — site name / logo -->
            <a class="navbar-brand fw-bold" href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}">
                <i class="bi bi-journal-text me-2"></i>Bootstrap Notes
            </a>

            <!-- Hamburger button for mobile (xs/sm/md) -->
            <button class="navbar-toggler" type="button"
                    data-bs-toggle="collapse"
                    data-bs-target="#navbarNav"
                    aria-controls="navbarNav"
                    aria-expanded="false"
                    aria-label="Відкрити меню">
                <span class="navbar-toggler-icon"></span>
            </button>

            <!-- Navigation links (hidden on mobile) -->
            <div class="collapse navbar-collapse" id="navbarNav">
                <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
                    <li class="nav-item">
                        <a class="nav-link" href="{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}">
                            <i class="bi bi-list-ul me-1"></i>Всі нотатки
                        </a>
                    </li>
                    <li class="nav-item">
                        <a class="nav-link" href="{% url 'hello_app:note_create' %}">
                            <i class="bi bi-plus-circle me-1"></i>Нова нотатка
                        </a>
                    </li>
                </ul>
                <ul class="navbar-nav">
                    <li class="nav-item">
                        <a class="nav-link" href="{% url 'admin:index' %}">
                            <i class="bi bi-gear me-1"></i>Адмін
                        </a>
                    </li>
                </ul>
            </div>

        </div>
    </nav>

    <!-- Main content — flex-grow-1 stretches main between the navbar and the footer -->
    <main class="container my-4 flex-grow-1">

        <!--
            Django Messages → Bootstrap Alerts.
            messages — a Context Processor that is automatically available in all templates.
            message.tags → 'success'/'danger'/'warning' (mapped via MESSAGE_TAGS in settings.py).
        -->
        {% if messages %}
            {% for message in messages %}
            <div class="alert alert-{{ message.tags }} alert-dismissible fade show" role="alert">
                <i class="bi bi-{% if message.tags == 'success' %}check-circle{% elif message.tags == 'danger' %}exclamation-triangle{% else %}info-circle{% endif %} me-2"></i>
                {{ message }}
                <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-bs-dismiss="alert"
                        aria-label="Закрити"></button>
            </div>
            {% endfor %}
        {% endif %}

        {% block content %}{% endblock %}

    </main>

    <!-- Footer -->
    <footer class="bg-dark text-center text-white-50 py-3 mt-5">
        <small>Bootstrap Notes © 2026 — навчальний проєкт</small>
    </footer>

    <!--
        Bootstrap JS Bundle (includes Popper.js).
        defer — loaded after the HTML.
        Why: Modal, Navbar collapse, Toast need JS.
    -->
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js"
            integrity="sha384-YvpcrYf0tY3lHB60NNkmXc4s9bIOgUxi8T/jzmAgD0SnMiKKmFClVgaFa11iGj0E"
            crossorigin="anonymous" defer></script>

    <!-- A slot for page-specific JS -->
    {% block extra_js %}{% endblock %}

</body>
</html>

docs.title: Sticky Footer (the footer is always at the bottom)
docs.text:
Problem: if a page has little content (for example, 1–2 notes or an empty list), the footer "hangs" in the middle of the page, with empty background below it.

Solution — a Sticky Footer with Bootstrap Flexbox:

<!-- BEFORE: -->
<body class="bg-light">
    ...
    <main class="container my-4">

<!-- AFTER: -->
<body class="bg-light d-flex flex-column min-vh-100">
    ...
    <main class="container my-4 flex-grow-1">
Class Where What it does d-flex <body> Turns body into a flex container flex-column <body> Flex direction: vertical (navbar → main → footer) min-vh-100 <body> Body takes at least 100% of the window height (100vh) flex-grow-1 <main> Main stretches across all the free space between the navbar and the footer

Visual diagram:

┌────────────────────── body (min-vh-100) ──────────────────────┐
│  <nav>        — fixed height                                  │
│  <main>       — flex-grow-1: takes everything that is left ↕↕↕│
│  <footer>     — fixed height, always at the bottom            │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% load django_bootstrap5 %}

{% block title %}Мої нотатки — Bootstrap Notes{% endblock %}

{% block content %}

<div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-4">
    <div>
        <h1 class="h2 mb-1">
            <i class="bi bi-journal-text me-2 text-primary"></i>
            Мої нотатки
        </h1>
        <p class="text-muted mb-0">
            {{ notes|length }} нотаток
        </p>
    </div>

    <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_create' %}" class="btn btn-primary">
        <i class="bi bi-plus-lg me-1"></i>
        Нова нотатка
    </a>
</div>

{% if notes %}

    <!--
        Bootstrap Grid:
        row-cols-1 — one column on small screens;
        row-cols-md-2 — two columns on medium screens;
        row-cols-lg-3 — three columns on large screens;
        g-4 — gaps between the cards.
    -->
    <div class="row row-cols-1 row-cols-md-2 row-cols-lg-3 g-4">

        {% for note in notes %}
        <div class="col">

            <!--
                Card — a Bootstrap component for a single note.
                h-100 makes cards the same height within a row.
                shadow-sm adds a light shadow.
            -->
            <div class="card h-100 shadow-sm">

                <div class="card-body">
                    <h5 class="card-title">
                        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_detail' pk=note.pk %}"
                           class="text-decoration-none text-dark">
                            {{ note.title }}
                        </a>
                    </h5>

                    {% if note.content %}
                    <p class="card-text text-muted small">
                        {{ note.content|truncatechars:100 }}
                    </p>
                    {% else %}
                    <p class="card-text text-muted small fst-italic">
                        Зміст відсутній.
                    </p>
                    {% endif %}

                </div>

                <div class="card-footer bg-transparent d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center">
                    <small class="text-muted">
                        <i class="bi bi-clock me-1"></i>
                        {{ note.created_at|timesince }} тому
                    </small>

                    <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm">
                        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_edit' pk=note.pk %}"
                           class="btn btn-outline-secondary"
                           title="Редагувати">
                            <i class="bi bi-pencil"></i>
                        </a>

                        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_delete' pk=note.pk %}"
                           class="btn btn-outline-danger"
                           title="Видалити">
                            <i class="bi bi-trash"></i>
                        </a>
                    </div>
                </div>

            </div>
        </div>
        {% endfor %}

    </div>

{% else %}

    <div class="text-center py-5">
        <i class="bi bi-journal-x display-1 text-muted d-block mb-3"></i>
        <h4 class="text-muted">Ще немає нотаток</h4>
        <p class="text-muted">Створіть першу нотатку і вона з'явиться тут.</p>
        <a href="{% url 'hello_app:note_create' %}" class="btn btn-primary mt-2">
            <i class="bi bi-plus-lg me-1"></i>Створити нотатку
        </a>
    </div>

{% endif %}

{% endblock %}

from django import forms
from .models import Note


class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    """
    ModelForm — automatically generates form fields from the Note model.
    Django takes field types from the model and generates the matching HTML inputs.
    CharField(max_length=200) → <input type="text" maxlength="200">
    TextField → <textarea>
    """

    class Meta:
        model = Note
        fields = ['title', 'content']  # which fields to include in the form
        widgets = {
            # Add the Bootstrap class='form-control' to every field
            # Without it, Django renders bare HTML without Bootstrap styles
            'title': forms.TextInput(attrs={
                'class': 'form-control',
                'placeholder': 'Введіть назву нотатки...',
                'autofocus': True,
            }),
            'content': forms.Textarea(attrs={
                'class': 'form-control',
                'rows': 6,
                'placeholder': 'Текст нотатки...',
            }),
        }
        labels = {
            'title': 'Заголовок',
            'content': 'Зміст',
        }

docs.text:
from django.shortcuts import render, redirect, get_object_or_404
from django.contrib import messages   # ← Django Messages

from .models import Note
from .forms import NoteForm           # ← our form


def index(request):
    """Redirect from / to /notes/."""
    return redirect('hello_app:note_list')


def note_list(request):
    """List of all notes."""
    notes = Note.objects.all()
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_list.html', {'notes': notes})


def note_detail(request, pk):
    """
    Note detail.
    get_object_or_404: if a note with this pk does not exist → returns 404 (not 500).
    """
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)
    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_detail.html', {'note': note})


def note_create(request):
    """
    The PRG (Post/Redirect/Get) pattern:
    GET  → show an empty form
    POST → process, save → redirect to the list (so that F5 does not duplicate)
    """
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = form.save()
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" успішно створено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_list')
    else:
        form = NoteForm()

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'action': 'Створити',
        'title': 'Нова нотатка',
    })


def note_edit(request, pk):
    """Editing a note — the same PRG, but the form is initialized with instance=note."""
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, instance=note)
        if form.is_valid():
            form.save()
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" оновлено!')
            return redirect('hello_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(instance=note)  # instance fills the form with the current data

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_form.html', {
        'form': form,
        'note': note,
        'action': 'Зберегти зміни',
        'title': f'Редагувати: {note.title}',
    })


def note_delete(request, pk):
    """
    Deletion via POST (not GET!).
    GET → confirmation page.
    POST → delete → redirect.
    """
    note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk)

    if request.method == 'POST':
        title = note.title
        note.delete()
        messages.warning(request, f'Нотатку "{title}" видалено.')
        return redirect('hello_app:note_list')

    return render(request, 'hello_app/note_confirm_delete.html', {'note': note})

docs.text:
from django.urls import path
from . import views

app_name = 'hello_app'

urlpatterns = [
    path('', views.index, name='index'),
    path('notes/', views.note_list, name='note_list'),
    path('notes/new/', views.note_create, name='note_create'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/', views.note_detail, name='note_detail'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/edit/', views.note_edit, name='note_edit'),
    path('notes/<int:pk>/delete/', views.note_delete, name='note_delete'),
]

What is <int:pk>? A path converter — captures an integer from the URL and passes it to the view as the pk argument. /notes/42/ → pk=42 → Note.objects.get(pk=42).

{% extends 'base.html' %}

{% load django_bootstrap5 %}

{% block title %}{{ title }} — Bootstrap Notes{% endblock %}

{% block content %}

<div class="row justify-content-center">
    <div class="col-12 col-md-8 col-lg-6">

        <div class="card shadow-sm">
            <div class="card-header">
                <h1 class="h4 mb-0">
                    <i class="bi bi-{% if note %}pencil{% else %}plus-circle{% endif %} me-2"></i>
                    {{ title }}
                </h1>
            </div>

            <div class="card-body">
                <!--
                    {% csrf_token %} — MANDATORY in every POST form!
                    Without it, Django returns 403 Forbidden.
                    CSRF: Cross-Site Request Forgery protection.
                -->
                <form method="post" novalidate>
                    {% csrf_token %}

                    {% for field in form %}
                    <div class="mb-3">
                        <label for="{{ field.id_for_label }}" class="form-label fw-semibold">
                            {{ field.label }}
                            {% if field.field.required %}
                                <span class="text-danger" title="Обов'язкове поле">*</span>
                            {% endif %}
                        </label>

                        {{ field }}

                        {% if field.help_text %}
                            <div class="form-text text-muted">{{ field.help_text }}</div>
                        {% endif %}

                        {% for error in field.errors %}
                            <div class="invalid-feedback d-block">
                                <i class="bi bi-exclamation-circle me-1"></i>{{ error }}
                            </div>
                        {% endfor %}
                    </div>
                    {% endfor %}

                    <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center pt-2">
                        <a href="{% if note %}{% url 'hello_app:note_detail' pk=note.pk %}{% else %}{% url 'hello_app:note_list' %}{% endif %}"
                           class="btn btn-outline-secondary">
                            <i class="bi bi-x-lg me-1"></i>Скасувати
                        </a>
                        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">
                            <i class="bi bi-check-lg me-1"></i>{{ action }}
                        </button>
                    </div>
                </form>
            </div>
        </div>

    </div>
</div>

{% endblock %}

Option 2 — automatic rendering with django-bootstrap5:

Instead of the manual {% for field in form %} loop, you can write a single line: 

{% load django_bootstrap5 %}
{% bootstrap_form form %}
The django-bootstrap5 package automatically adds all the Bootstrap classes, labels, and errors.
